# Tool Reference

This page lists ue-mcp's own category tools and actions. For the official Unreal tools (UE 5.8+) that ue-mcp wraps (surfaced inside these same categories), see [Native Tools](native-tools.md).

UE-MCP exposes **<!-- count:tools -->31<!-- /count --> category tools** covering **<!-- count:actions -->3707+<!-- /count --> actions**, plus a `flow` tool for running multi-step YAML workflows. Every category tool takes an `action` parameter that selects the operation and an `args` object holding that action's parameters: `level(action="place_actor", args={actorClass: "PointLight"})`. Under the default `micro` [context strategy](configuration.md#context-strategy-full-lean-micro) the same call goes through the gateway: `tools(action="call", category="level", method="place_actor", args={...})`.

!!! tip "First call in any session"
    Start with `project(action="get_status")` to check the connection, then `level(action="get_outliner")` or `asset(action="list")` to explore.

!!! info "How to read this page"
    Each row gives an action's signature, the same line the server advertises, and its description. In a signature `?` marks an optional parameter, `a|b` is one parameter with `b` an accepted alias, `one(a; b+c)` means exactly one of the groups and `any(a; b)` at least one. A type follows a colon, and no type means a string: `s` string, `n` number, `i` integer, `b` boolean, `o` object, `v` `{x,y,z}`, `r` `{pitch,yaw,roll}`, `c` `{r,g,b,a?}`, `ref` an asset path or `{refPath}`, `*` any JSON, `[t]` an array of `t`, `t/u` either type. For each parameter's description, nested fields and defaults, call `project(action="describe_action", args={name: "level.place_actor"})`.

### Parameters every category tool accepts

These parameters sit beside `action` and `args` on every category tool. Dispatch reads them and strips them before the call reaches the bridge, so they never collide with an action's own parameters. While the server drives more than one editor, `editor` (which editor runs the call) is added the same way.

| Parameter | Type | What it does |
|-----------|------|--------------|
| `select` | string or string list | Keep only these result fields. |
| `omit` | string or string list | Drop these result fields. Runs after `select`. |
| `timeoutMs` | integer, 1 to 3600000 | How long to wait for this one call. |

Results can also carry `fieldsNotFound`, `paramsNotForwarded`, `paramsNotRead` and `pathsRepaired`, described below.

#### `select` and `omit`

Use them to cut a large result, such as `level(get_component_tree)` on a character or `asset(bulk_read_properties)` across a library, down to the fields you need. Both take dotted paths and traverse arrays:

```
level(action="get_outliner", select="actors.name")
level(action="get_component_tree", args={actorLabel: "BP_Hero"}, select=["components.name", "components.class"])
level(action="get_component_tree", args={actorLabel: "BP_Hero"}, omit="components.materials")
```

`components.name` keeps the name of every component in the array. `components[].name` means the same thing. Two paths into the same array produce one array of two-key objects.

A path that matches nothing is listed in `fieldsNotFound`, beside `available`, the result's own top-level keys. If no path matched at all, the filter is not applied and the full result comes back with the same report. A list sent JSON-encoded as text (`"[\"a\",\"b\"]"`) or a quoted path (`"\"a\""`) is read as the paths it encodes.

#### Parameters that went nowhere

A parameter the action does not use is reported, not silently dropped:

- `paramsNotForwarded` lists keys you sent that the action never passes to the editor. With `UE_MCP_STRICT_PARAMS=1` the call is refused instead and nothing reaches the editor.
- `paramsNotRead` lists keys that reached the editor and that the handler never read.

Either field means the call ran without that parameter. Check the spelling against the action's `Params:` list.

In a `Params:` list, `name (or other)` means `other` is an alias the editor renames to `name` before the handler runs. Send one of the two. If both are sent, the alias is ignored and comes back in `paramsNotRead`.

#### `timeoutMs`

How long to wait for this call, in milliseconds. The default is 30 seconds, or longer for actions the editor allows longer. Raise it for a large batch, or for an editor busy compiling shaders.

A timeout does not mean the call did not happen. The request was sent; only the wait ended. Read the state back before retrying.

#### `pathsRepaired`

The server replaces backslashes with forward slashes in any parameter whose name ends in `Path`, `Paths`, `Dir`, `Directory`, `File` or `Folder`, including every element of a list such as `assetPaths`. Each repair is reported on the result:

```json
{
  "pathsRepaired": {
    "note": "Backslashes were replaced with forward slashes in these parameters. Unreal addresses content with forward slashes; send them that way to avoid the repair.",
    "repairs": [{ "param": "assetPath", "from": "\\Game\\UI\\WBP_Menu", "to": "/Game/UI/WBP_Menu" }]
  }
}
```

A UNC path (`\\server\share\x`) is left alone. A Windows drive path (`C:\Users\name`) is repaired, because Node, UBT and Unreal's file APIs all accept forward slashes. The field appears only on an object result where something was repaired.

### Property paths

Every action that reads or writes one reflected property takes a path to it, and they all resolve it the same way, so a path that reads is a path that writes:

- `asset`: `read_properties`, `get_properties`, `set_property` and `append_array_elements` (`propertyName`), and the keys of each item's `properties` in `bulk_set_properties`
- `editor`: `get_property`, `set_property`, `set_object_property` and the `propertyNames` of `describe_object`
- `reflection`: `reflect_instance` (`propertyPath`)

Other actions that take a dotted property name, such as PCG node settings, behavior tree node properties and world partition settings, go through the same resolver and accept the same segments.

| Segment | Means |
|---------|-------|
| `Presentation` | A property, or a field of the struct the path is in. A struct is entered in place, an object reference (an instanced subobject) is followed, and an `FInstancedStruct` is entered through its payload. |
| `Rules[1]` | Element 1 of an array, or of a C-style fixed array. |
| `WeaponProfiles[WeaponId=SGK_Stone_Axe]` | The one element whose `WeaponId` is `SGK_Stone_Axe`. |

One field of one array entry is one call:

```
asset(action="get_properties", args={assetPath: "/Game/Data/DA_Weapons",
  propertyName: "WeaponProfiles[WeaponId=SGK_Stone_Axe].Presentation.MeshOffset.Scale3D",
  valueFormat: "json"})
asset(action="set_property", args={assetPath: "/Game/Data/DA_Weapons",
  propertyName: "WeaponProfiles[WeaponId=SGK_Stone_Axe].Presentation.MeshOffset.Scale3D",
  value: {X: 1.25, Y: 1.25, Z: 1.25}})
```

**What can be a key.** A field directly on the element: a name, string, text (its display string), enum (`Primary`, or `ESlot::Primary`), integer, bool (`true` or `false`, any case) or gameplay tag (the tag name). Floats and structs are refused, because an exact float match is not a way to name something. The element can be a struct, an `FInstancedStruct` (the key is read off each payload, and an element whose payload has no such field is passed over) or an instanced object (the key is read off each object).

**Exactly one element must match.** The comparison is exact and case-sensitive. When nothing matches, the error lists the key values that are there (the first 20, then how many more) and points out a value that differs only in case. When several match, the error gives their indices and asks for one of them by index. Neither case writes anything.

**Writing a value with `]` in it.** Quote it: `Rows[Label="a]b"]`. Inside the quotes `\"` and `\\` are escapes. A `.` inside the brackets never splits the path, quoted or not, so `Rows[Label=Sword.Long].Damage` works as written. Selectors nest: `OpStack[Name=Jump].Elements[Id=3].Value`.

**Maps and sets.** Their entries are not addressable by path. Read or write the whole `TMap` (`...Presentation.HolsterSlotOffsets`), which `get_properties` with `valueFormat="json"` returns as JSON and `set_property` takes back in the same form. A key selector on a map or set is refused with that advice.

**What comes back.** An action that resolved a key also returns `indexedPath`: the same path with each key replaced by the index it matched (`WeaponProfiles[12].Presentation.MeshOffset.Scale3D`). Rollback records use that form, so an inverse still names the right element after a write that changed its key. `bulk_set_properties` matches every key once, during preflight, against the asset as it was before the batch, so one item can rename an element's key and set its other fields by the old key in the same call.

A keyed write is the same write as its indexed form: the same `Modify`, `PostEditChange` and dirty package, and the action's own `save` flag decides whether it reaches disk.

Something in brackets that is neither a number nor `Field=Value` is refused.

### Dialog handling modes

A modal dialog blocks Unreal's game thread. While one is up, every action is refused with `dialogBlocking: true`, `refusedMethod`, `dialogMode`, `dialogTitle`, `dialogMessage` and `buttons`. The same refusal applies on every route to that editor: an MCP tool call, a flow step, the HTTP flow surface and a plugin guard task. The gate is per editor, so a modal in one project does not refuse calls to another.

These stay reachable while a dialog is up: `editor(list_dialogs)`, `editor(respond_to_dialog)`, `editor(list_windows)`, `editor(press_window_button)`, `editor(close_window)`, `editor(get_dialog_policy)`, `editor(get_engine_state)` and `project(get_status)`. A successful result taken while a modal is up is stamped `editorBlockedByDialog` with the dialog's title and message. Everything else is refused, including `start_editor`, `stop_editor`, `restart_editor`, `set_dialog_policy` and `clear_dialog_policy`.

The **dialog handling mode** decides who answers.

| Mode | What happens to a blocking dialog |
|------|-----------------------------------|
| `interactive` | You get an elicitation form with the dialog's buttons as choices, plus "leave it open". The button you pick is pressed and the blocked call then runs. Decline and you get the refusal. A dialog too long for a form is returned in full on the first refused call (`dialogPhase: "relay"`) and the form appears on the next. Default when your client advertises elicitation. |
| `auto` | The refusal lists each button with the `editor(respond_to_dialog)` call that presses it, under `choices`. The agent picks one. Applies only when you set it. |
| `defer` | The refusal names the dialog and its buttons but not the calls that press them. Answer it in the Unreal Editor window. Default when your client does not advertise elicitation. |

The press actions (`respond_to_dialog`, `press_window_button`, `close_window`) are accepted only in `auto`. Under `interactive` and `defer` they are refused, because the answer belongs to the person.

**Policies.** `editor(set_dialog_policy)` arms a pattern in advance. A dialog matching an armed policy is answered immediately under every mode. There are no built-in policies. `editor(start_editor)` takes `dialogPolicy` for prompts raised during startup, before the bridge can answer.

**Setting the mode.** Highest wins:

1. `UE_MCP_DIALOG_MODE=interactive|auto|defer` in the server's environment. A value that names no mode is ignored, and the result says so.
2. `dialog.mode` for this project in `~/.ue-mcp/state.json`, set with `npx ue-mcp dialog mode <mode> --editor <name>`.
3. `dialog.mode` for this user in `~/.ue-mcp/state.json`, set with `npx ue-mcp dialog mode <mode>`.
4. The default: `interactive` when the client advertises elicitation, otherwise `defer`. The default is never `auto`.

`npx ue-mcp dialog mode` with no value prints the effective mode and where it came from, and `npx ue-mcp dialog mode default` clears the preference. Do not hand-edit `~/.ue-mcp/state.json`. The mode is not read from `ue-mcp.yml`, because whether someone is at the keyboard is a property of your machine, not project policy. It is read per call, so a change applies without a restart.

## project

*Project status and editor connection: get_status (is the editor connected?), set_project (switch/redirect the bridge to another .uproject), get_info. Also config INI files, module load state, and C++ source inspection. Call project(get_status) first in any session.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `get_status()` | Check server mode and editor connection. pluginStale is the primary staleness verdict: from the running plugin's own handler list when it published one (pluginStaleSource 'parity'), else from build timestamps ('build-timestamps'). pluginBuildStale reports the compiled bridge being older than its source, read from disk. deployedPlugin is what the binary that answered says about itself: when it was built, and how many methods this server advertises that it does not register, which is what 'Unknown method' on a real action means. answeringPid is the editor process the bridge is connected to; projectEditors and projectEditorsWarning appear when several editor processes (headless included) hold the project, and every response then carries the answering pid. unrealMcpServer appears when Epic's own Unreal MCP server (UE 5.8+) is set to start with this project's editor, with its URL and where that came from, because it then runs beside ue-mcp. Params: `none (#785, #1002, #1021, #1150, #1826)` |
| `set_project(projectPath)` | Switch project: moves both path resolution and the editor connection to the new .uproject. Params: `projectPath` |
| `list_editors()` | List every editor session this server drives: name, project, bridge port, whether the socket is connected, whether anything is answering on that port, and which session untargeted calls fall through to. Params: `none (#817)` |
| `use_editor(editorTarget)` | Make one editor session the default target for untargeted calls. Does not change the session set and never touches any editor process. Params: `editorTarget (session name, project name, or .uproject path) (#817)` |
| `add_editor(projectPath, editorName?, start?:b, timeout?:n)` | Register another project as an addressable editor session, with its own bridge connection and port. Optionally launch its editor. Every category then accepts editor="<name>" to run a call there. Params: `projectPath, editorName? (defaults to the project name), start? (launch the editor and wait for it to be ready), timeout? (seconds, default 300) (#817)` |
| `drop_editor(editorTarget)` | Forget an editor session and close its bridge socket. The editor process is LEFT RUNNING and untouched - this detaches, it does not stop anything (use editor(stop_editor) for that). Params: `editorTarget (#817)` |
| `get_info()` | Read .uproject file details. Params: `none` |
| `read_config(configName)` | Read INI config. Params: `configName (e.g. 'Engine', 'Game')` |
| `search_config(query)` | Search INI files. Params: `query` |
| `list_config_tags()` | Extract gameplay tags from config. Params: `none` |
| `resolve_setting(configName, key, section, platform?)` | Final value of one ini key as the editor reads it, through Unreal's whole config hierarchy (engine Base.ini, Base<Category>.ini, the engine platform file, the project's Default<Category>.ini and platform file, then Saved/Config/<Platform>Editor), with +, -, ., ! array operations applied. Returns value (a string, a list for an array key, null when unset), setBy (layer, file, line, text) and the layers read. No editor needed. Params: `configName (category, e.g. 'Engine', 'Game', 'Input'), section, key, platform? (default this machine's: Windows, Mac or Linux)` |
| `explain_setting(configName, key, section, platform?)` | Every config layer that touches one ini key, lowest first, with the lines it applies (+, -, ., ! array operations included) and the value after each, then the final value. The layers are resolve_setting's. No editor needed. Params: `configName (category, e.g. 'Engine'), section, key, platform?` |
| `diff_config_from_default(configName, includeUser?:b, platform?)` | The ini keys the project changes from the engine's defaults for one category: every key whose final value through the project (and, by default, the per-user Saved) layers differs from the value the engine layers alone give. Each change has section, key, engineValue, value and setBy. No editor needed. Params: `configName (category, e.g. 'Engine'), platform?, includeUser? (default true: include Saved/Config/<Platform>Editor)` |
| `read_cpp_header(headerPath)` | Parse a .h file. Params: `headerPath` |
| `read_module(moduleName)` | Read module source. Params: `moduleName` |
| `list_modules()` | List C++ modules. Params: `none` |
| `search_cpp(query, directory?)` | Search .h/.cpp files. Params: `query, directory?` |
| `read_engine_header(headerPath)` | Parse a .h file from the engine source tree. Params: `headerPath (relative to Engine/Source, or absolute)` |
| `find_engine_symbol(symbol, maxResults?:n)` | Grep engine headers for a symbol. Params: `symbol, maxResults?` |
| `list_engine_modules()` | List modules in Engine/Source/Runtime. Params: `none` |
| `search_engine_cpp(query, maxResults?:n, subdirectory?, tree?)` | Search engine .h/.cpp/.inl files across Runtime/Editor/Developer/Plugins. Params: `query, tree? (Runtime\|Editor\|Developer\|Plugins\|all - default Runtime), subdirectory?, maxResults? (default 500)` |
| `search_tools(query, limit?:n)` | Search every ue-mcp tool + action by keyword or task INTENT (a synonym layer maps 'screenshot'->capture_scene_png, 'tile a texture'->the texture-bomb flow, etc.) and return ranked matches (tool, action, description, score). The first step before editor(execute_python); most tasks already have a dedicated action. Params: `query (space-separated keywords/intent), limit? (default 20) (#704)` |
| `describe_action(name, category?)` | Return the live parameter schema for one action: every parameter it accepts, with type, required/optional, description, allowed values and default, plus the bridge method it dispatches to. search_tools finds an action by keyword and hands back only prose; this answers what to actually pass, so the first call is the right one. name takes 'tool.action' (asset.set_property) or a bare action name, which reports every category providing it. A name that does not resolve comes back with the closest spellings rather than a bare failure. Reads the graph THIS editor advertises, so injected Epic and plugin actions are included. Each action also reports class: read (observes), mutate (changes the editor, its project on disk, or its process) or unknown (decided by a parameter, so gated like mutate) - MCP's own readOnlyHint is per tool, and every tool here is a category holding both, so a harness that gates writes reads it from here. Params: `name (required), category? (return every action of one category instead of one action)` |
| `list_available_actions(category?, includeNames?:b, state?)` | Report which actions this server can serve RIGHT NOW and why the rest cannot. With no editor attached the surface is advertised in full but most of it cannot run, and this is the line between the two halves: an action either runs in this Node process (availability 'always') or dispatches to a bridge method only a running editor answers (availability 'editor', with bridgeMethod naming it). The offline half is the engine symbol index and the C++ correctness checks, the project config, source and file readers, the surface introspection, and the process lifecycle actions that start, stop and build. An action contributed by a plugin whose route is undeclared reports 'unknown' and should be treated as needing an editor. Counts come back by default, per category as well as overall; includeNames=true adds the actions themselves, and category narrows the whole report to one. With an editor attached everything is available and the classification still answers the question worth asking then, which is what keeps working once the editor is stopped for a rebuild. Params: `category?, includeNames? (default false), state? (available\|blocked\|all, default available)` |
| `list_categories()` | Every category with what is turned on in it: ue-mcp's own actions (native) and the actions wrapping Unreal's toolsets (epic), each with its action count, plus the Unreal toolsets the category maps to and, with an editor attached, which of them its Toolset Registry has on. With no editor, the toolsets the project's setting file blocks. Params: `none` |
| `set_category_enabled(category, enabled:b, scope?)` | Turn a category on or off for this project, live: the surface is rebuilt and clients get tools/list_changed. scope 'native' is ue-mcp's own actions, 'epic' is the actions wrapping Unreal's toolsets AND those toolsets in the editor's Toolset Registry (changed live through the bridge, or in the project's setting file when no editor runs; refused when an editor runs but its bridge does not answer), 'all' (default) is both. Written to `disable:` in ue-mcp.yml. A call to an action turned off is refused naming this action. project and epic keep their own actions (only scope 'epic' applies to them). Params: `category, enabled (bool), scope? (all\|native\|epic, default all)` |
| `set_toolset_enabled(enabled:b, toolsets:s/[s])` | Turn Unreal toolsets on or off in the editor's Toolset Registry by name, which is what Epic's own MCP server and the AI Assistant read too. Live through the bridge when the editor answers; written to the project's setting file when no editor runs (UE 5.9 Config/DefaultGame.ini, UE 5.8 the per-user EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini), applied at its next start; refused when an editor runs but its bridge does not answer. The ue-mcp surface is not changed: set_category_enabled with scope 'epic' does both. Params: `toolsets (names, as epic(list_toolsets) gives them), enabled (bool)` |
| `acquire_lease(paths:s/[s], ttlSeconds?:n)` | Claim assets for this session so another agent on the same editor cannot change them until the lease is released, runs out, or this session ends. A path another session holds refuses the whole request, naming the holder and when its lease runs out. Calling again renews. A folder path with a trailing slash covers every asset under it. Off when ue-mcp.yml sets leases.mode: off. Params: `paths (asset paths), ttlSeconds? (default from leases.ttlSeconds, 600; max 86400)` |
| `release_lease(paths?:s/[s])` | Release this session's leases: the paths named, or every lease it holds in this editor when none are. Only the holder can release a lease; another session's runs out on its own or when that session ends. Params: `paths?` |
| `list_leases()` | Every live asset lease on this server, which session holds each and when it runs out, plus the lease mode and whether calls take leases implicitly right now. Params: `none` |
| `list_content_assets(contentPath?, maxResults?:n, namePattern?, recursive?:b)` | List the project's assets from the package files on DISK, which is the one asset query that works with no editor running. Takes a mount path (/Game, /Game/Characters, or a plugin's /MyPlugin) and resolves it through the same mount table the live path uses, so an offline listing names assets exactly as the editor would. It answers existence, layout, size and modified time, and it deliberately does not answer class, registry tags or dependencies: those live in the editor's asset registry and are not in the file, so asset(list) and asset(search) remain the answer once an editor is up. maxResults stops the walk rather than trimming the result, and truncated says when it did. Params: `contentPath? (default /Game), recursive? (default true), namePattern? (case-insensitive substring of the asset name), maxResults? (default 1000)` |
| `check_install(projectPath?, skipToolchain?:b)` | Answer whether this project can run the bridge at all, from disk, with no editor running and nothing compiled. Reports the project kind (a project declaring no native modules of its own is Blueprint-only, which is NOT a blocker: UnrealBuildTool writes temporary target and module files under Intermediate/Source/ and compiles the plugin against them), the engine that will be used and where it was resolved from, whether the plugin is deployed, enabled in the .uproject, compiled and up to date with its source, and whether this machine has the C++ toolchain Unreal needs. Every problem carries a stable code, what is wrong and the exact fix, and nextSteps is those fixes in order. Read-only: it never deploys, enables or builds anything. Params: `projectPath? (default the loaded project), skipToolchain? (skip the toolchain probe, which shells out to vswhere or the compiler)` |
| `execute_python_report()` | Measurement for #704: reads this session's execute_python calls and, for each, runs its taskSummary back through search_tools to flag calls that OVERLAPPED an existing dedicated action ('you used Python for X, but tool Y does X'). Returns totalCalls, overlapping[] and an overlapRate. Params: `none (#704)` |
| `list_files(directory, extensions?:s/[s], maxResults?:n, namePattern?, recursive?:b)` | List files on disk under a directory, optionally filtered by extension(s) and by name. Runs in the MCP server process (no editor round-trip). Params: `directory (inside the project: absolute, or relative to the project dir), extensions? (e.g. ['png','exr'] or 'png'), namePattern? (case-insensitive substring of the file name; maxResults counts matches, so a name search over a large tree is not cut short by files that do not match), recursive? (default false), maxResults? (default 1000) (#608)` |
| `set_config(configName\|configFile?, section, key, value)` | Write to INI. Params: `configName? (or configFile), section, key, value` |
| `set_developer_setting(settingsClass, propertyName, settingValue:*, persist?:{default,user})` | Set a UPROPERTY(Config) value on a settings class default object (a UDeveloperSettings subclass or any config= class) and save it the way the Project Settings dialog does: PostEditChangeProperty on the default object, then UpdateSinglePropertyInConfigFile into Default<Config>.ini (TryUpdateDefaultConfigFile for a container), or the per-user config with persist=user. The ini is the one the class names, never a caller path. Unlike set_config, the settings object sees the change and the value survives a restart; unlike editor(set_object_property), it is saved. Returns configFile, section, key and the iniLines now on disk. Read the current value with editor(get_property) on the class path. Params: `settingsClass, propertyName, settingValue, persist?` |
| `get_maps_settings()` | Read Project Settings > Maps & Modes: default GameMode, server GameMode, GameInstance class, game/server/editor startup/transition maps. settings is the live value in the editor, stored is what DefaultEngine.ini holds (null when the file has no entry) (#1566). Params: `none` |
| `set_maps_settings(any(globalDefaultGameMode; globalDefaultServerGameMode; gameInstanceClass; gameDefaultMap; serverDefaultMap; editorStartupMap; transitionMap))` | Write Project Settings > Maps & Modes. Classes accept a /Script path, short name or Blueprint asset path and must derive from GameModeBase or GameInstance; maps must be existing world assets; an empty string clears. Every value is validated before any is written. Updates the live settings object and DefaultEngine.ini, then returns settings, stored (read back from the file) and persisted per write. For any other Project Settings page, editor(set_property) on the settings class path persists a config property the same way (#1566). Params: `at least one of globalDefaultGameMode/globalDefaultServerGameMode/gameInstanceClass/gameDefaultMap/serverDefaultMap/editorStartupMap/transitionMap` |
| `build(clean?:b, configuration?, platform?)` | Build the project's C++ out of process with UnrealBuildTool. Works with the editor STOPPED, which a full rebuild requires (UBT cannot link while an editor holds the module DLLs). Blocks until the build finishes and returns the compiler output. A link that fails because another process holds an output open names the file and the holder under lockedOutputs, with the remedy in the message. Params: `configuration? (default Development), platform? (default the host platform), clean? (#958)` |
| `generate_project_files()` | Generate IDE project files (Visual Studio, Xcode, etc.). Params: `none` |
| `create_cpp_class(className, parentClass?, moduleName?, classDomain?, subPath?)` | Create a new native UCLASS in a project module. Uses the same engine template path as File → New C++ Class. Writes .h + .cpp; returns both paths plus needsEditorRestart (true unless Live Coding successfully hot-reloaded). Params: `className, parentClass?, moduleName?, classDomain?, subPath?` |
| `list_project_modules(cursor?, limit?:n)` | List native modules in the current project (name, host type, source path), in the .uproject's own declaration order. Feed moduleName from here into create_cpp_class. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `list_loaded_modules(filter?, loadedOnly?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | Deprecated address, removed in the next release: use reflection(list_loaded_modules). Enumerate modules with runtime load state. filter is a case-insensitive substring; loadedOnly defaults to false. Returns modules[{name, loaded, gameModule}] + totalLoaded/totalModules (#689). Params: `filter?, loadedOnly?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `is_module_loaded(moduleName\|module)` | Deprecated address, removed in the next release: use reflection(is_module_loaded). Report whether a named module is currently loaded (#689). Params: `moduleName (or module)` |
| `list_available_plugins(filter?, pluginCategory?, enabledOnly?:b, cursor?, limit?:n)` | List every plugin installed in this engine or project, sorted by name, with its category, version, type, whether it is enabled in THIS editor session, whether it is enabled by default, and the .uproject's current reference to it under projectReference {present, enabled}. Those two disagree after enable_plugin until the editor restarts, which is the point of reporting both. Params: `filter?, pluginCategory?, enabledOnly?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `enable_plugin(pluginName)` | Enable a plugin in the .uproject. Plugin enablement is neither a UPROPERTY nor an INI key, it is a JSON array in the .uproject read once at startup, so set_config cannot reach it and without this a plugin-gated capability stays permanently unreachable through the bridge. Idempotent: a plugin already enabled, or enabled by default with no entry, reports existed and writes nothing. The change is a file change, so modules, classes, content and settings appear only after editor(restart_editor), which the result says. Only the plugin's entry in the on-disk .uproject Plugins array is patched; every other field, including a Modules edit made while the editor runs, is left as the file has it (#1248). Params: `pluginName` |
| `disable_plugin(pluginName, removeReference?:b)` | Disable a plugin in the .uproject. removeReference deletes the entry outright instead of writing an explicit disable, which is the difference between handing a default-on plugin back to its default and overriding it, and the two are not the same file. Idempotent against whichever of the two was asked for. Refuses to disable the bridge itself, since that would leave no way to undo it. Patches only that entry of the on-disk .uproject (#1248). Takes effect on the next editor start. Params: `pluginName, removeReference?` |
| `live_coding_compile(wait?:b)` | Trigger a Live Coding compile (Windows only). Hot-patches method bodies of existing UCLASSes without editor restart - the fast inner loop for UFUNCTION implementations. Does NOT reliably register brand-new UCLASSes; use build_project + editor restart for those. Params: `wait?` |
| `live_coding_status()` | Report Live Coding availability/state (available, started, enabledForSession, compiling). Helps choose between live_coding_compile and build_project. Params: `none` |
| `resolve_collision_profile(profileName, channel?, includeAllChannels?:b)` | Read one collision profile's resolved per-channel responses: collisionEnabled, objectType, and every channel with Block/Overlap/Ignore. This is the project-side half of blueprint(get_component_collision) (#925): a component's ResponseArray only lists the channels it OVERRIDES, so the profile is where an inherited response actually comes from. Project trace and object channels appear under their configured names, with enumName (ECC_GameTraceChannel1) alongside so a caller can key on something stable. By default the eight engine channels plus every channel the project configured are returned; includeAllChannels=true adds the unused slots. channel narrows it to one. A profile that does not exist lists the ones that do. Params: `profileName, channel?, includeAllChannels?` |
| `write_cpp_file(content, path)` | Write a .h / .cpp / .inl file under the project's Source/ tree. Used to append UPROPERTYs/UFUNCTIONs or method bodies after create_cpp_class. Writes are scoped to Source/ for safety. Params: `path (relative to Source/ or absolute within Source/), content (full file contents)` |
| `read_cpp_source(sourcePath)` | Read a .cpp file from the project Source/ tree. Companion to read_cpp_header for round-trip edits. Params: `sourcePath (relative to Source/ or absolute)` |
| `write_source_file(content, fileName, module, visibility)` | Write a .h/.cpp/.inl into a named module's Public/Private folder (resolves the module dir for you, including plugin modules under Plugins/*/Source/ that write_cpp_file refuses). After a new file, build_project + restart; after a body edit, live_coding_compile. Params: `module (module name, default the project's primary module), visibility (Public\|Private, default Private), fileName, content` |
| `read_source_file(fileName, module, visibility?)` | Read a .h/.cpp/.inl from a named module's folder (companion to write_source_file; resolves plugin modules too). With no visibility it tries Public then Private then the module root. Params: `module, visibility?, fileName` |
| `build_engine_index(refresh?:b)` | Build or refresh the engine symbol index that verify_symbols, lint_cpp_header and suggest_build_deps read. Scans roughly 31,000 headers across Runtime, Editor, Developer and the includable half of Engine/Plugins, and records for each symbol the header that declares it, the module that owns it, its signature and any UE_DEPRECATED. The result is cached per engine under the user directory and shared by every project on that engine, so this is a one-time cost per engine install: expect several minutes cold (first touch of each file goes through the virus scanner on Windows) and a few seconds warm. The other actions build it on demand, so this is only needed to refresh after an engine upgrade or to pay the cost deliberately. Params: `refresh? (rebuild even when a valid cache exists)` |
| `verify_symbols(names:s/[s])` | Check that engine symbols exist BEFORE writing C++ that uses them, and get back what you need to write it: the header to #include, the owning module for Build.cs, the exact declaration, the base class, and any UE_DEPRECATED with its version and message. Accepts a qualified 'UGameplayStatics::GetPlayerPawn' as well as a bare type name, and covers plugin modules (GameplayAbilities, Niagara, PCG, EnhancedInput) as well as the engine. A name that does not resolve comes back with close spellings; a member miss on a class that does exist says so, which separates a misspelled method from a misspelled class. The aggregate includes[] and modules[] are the whole edit you need to make. Builds the index on first use, which can take several minutes on a cold filesystem. Params: `names (string[] or comma-separated string, max 200)` |
| `suggest_build_deps(names:s/[s], buildCsPath?, modulePath?)` | Given the engine symbols a module uses, report which modules its Build.cs has to depend on and which of those it does not list yet, plus the AddRange line to paste. Core and CoreUObject are omitted because every module already has them. buildCsPath defaults to the Build.cs owning modulePath, or the project's first module. Pair with add_module_dependency, which performs the edit. Params: `names (string[] or comma-separated string), buildCsPath? (absolute), modulePath? (a file or directory whose owning Build.cs to use)` |
| `find_example_usage(symbol, limit?:n, trees?:s/[s])` | Find real call sites for an engine symbol in the engine's own .cpp files, which answers 'how is this actually used' with code that compiles. Better than a signature for anything with a non-obvious calling convention. Searches sources rather than headers on purpose: a header gives the declaration, which verify_symbols already returns. An engine installed from the Epic launcher ships headers WITHOUT .cpp sources, so on those there are no engine call sites to find; the result says so via engineSourcesAvailable and falls back to inline code in headers and to this project's own Source tree, rather than returning an empty list that reads as 'nothing uses this'. Params: `symbol (bare or Class::Member), limit? (default 10), trees? (Runtime\|Editor\|Developer, default Runtime)` |
| `class_hierarchy(symbol, depth?:n, direction?, limit?:n)` | Report what a class derives from and what derives from it, which is the question behind 'what should I subclass' and 'what already does this'. Ancestors are the full chain up to the root, nearest parent first; descendants default to the direct subclasses only, because every transitive subclass of UObject is tens of thousands of names. Every node carries its module, its include and whether it crosses a module boundary from the queried class, since crossing one is what forces a Build.cs dependency; crossModuleDependencies is that list on its own. Reads the engine symbol index and no files, so it is fast once the index exists, and builds it on first use, which can take several minutes on a cold filesystem. A base the index cannot resolve (a template, a macro-generated type) stops the walk and is reported as unresolvedAncestor rather than silently ending the chain. Params: `symbol (class or struct name, prefix optional), direction? (ancestors\|descendants\|both, default both), depth? (generations of descendants, default 1), limit? (max descendants, default 100)` |
| `find_references(symbol, includeProject?:b, limit?:n, trees?:s/[s])` | Find every line in the engine tree that names a symbol, which answers 'how is this woven into the engine' and 'what would break if this changed'. Broader than find_callers on purpose: a reference is a member declaration, a UPROPERTY type, a cast, a template argument or a call, and both headers and .cpp files are searched. Comment lines and preprocessor lines are skipped, since neither is a use. Each site reports its file, line, text and owning module. An engine installed from the Epic launcher ships headers WITHOUT .cpp sources, so engineSourcesAvailable says whether implementation files could be searched at all and the note says what was searched instead. Scans files rather than the index, so a rare name on a cold filesystem is slow. Params: `symbol (bare or Class::Member), limit? (max sites, default 40), trees? (Runtime\|Editor\|Developer\|Plugins\|all, default Runtime), includeProject? (also search this project's Source and Plugins, default true)` |
| `find_callers(symbol, includeProject?:b, limit?:n, trees?:s/[s])` | Find who calls a function, and from which enclosing function, which is how to see the conventions around a call before writing one: what is checked first, what is passed, what is done with the result. Searches .cpp bodies first, since a mention in a header is usually a declaration rather than a call, and excludes the function's own definition. Each site reports file, line, text, module and, for a site in a .cpp, the Class::Method it sits inside. An engine installed from the Epic launcher ships headers WITHOUT .cpp sources, so on those there are no engine call sites to find: engineSourcesAvailable reports that and the search falls back to inline code in headers and to this project's own Source tree, rather than returning an empty list that reads as 'nothing calls this'. Params: `symbol (bare or Class::Method), limit? (max sites, default 25), trees? (Runtime\|Editor\|Developer\|Plugins\|all, default Runtime), includeProject? (also search this project's Source and Plugins, default true)` |
| `find_callees(symbol, limit?:n, trees?:s/[s])` | Report what a function calls, by reading its body and looking every called name back up in the engine index. Answers 'what does doing this properly actually involve': the result carries each callee's module and include, and modules[] is the Build.cs cost of writing code that does the same thing. The body is found via the index, which keeps the search to the owning class's module rather than the whole tree, and the definition it read is reported with its file and line range. An engine installed from the Epic launcher ships headers WITHOUT .cpp sources, so only functions whose body is inline in a header can be read there; engineSourcesAvailable and the note say so instead of returning an empty list. Builds the index on first use. Params: `symbol (Class::Method, or a bare exported free function), limit? (max callees, default 100), trees? (which trees to test for sources, default Runtime)` |
| `symbol_context(symbol, contextAfter?:n, contextBefore?:n)` | Return the lines of engine source around a declaration, so the API surrounding a symbol can be read without opening the file: the sibling overloads, the UPROPERTY above it, the comment saying which of three similar methods to call. verify_symbols returns the declaration line alone, which is the signature and nothing else; this is that line in its neighbourhood. Accepts Class::Member as well as a bare type and resolves both exactly as verify_symbols does. When the declaration opens a body that closes inside the window the result ends at the closing brace instead of mid-type, and reports bodyEndLine. Builds the index on first use, which can take several minutes on a cold filesystem. Params: `symbol (bare or Class::Member), contextBefore? (lines before the declaration, default 8), contextAfter? (lines after, default 40)` |
| `lint_cpp_header(path, buildCsPath?)` | Check a header you just wrote against the engine it has to build against, and report what the compiler would before the compiler runs. Covers the structural mistakes that produce baffling Unreal build errors (a reflected type with no .generated.h include, a .generated.h that is not last, a UCLASS or USTRUCT with no GENERATED_BODY, no #pragma once) and the engine-facing ones (a symbol that does not exist, one used without its include, one whose module is missing from Build.cs, one the engine deprecated). A forward declaration counts as satisfying an include, since in a header it usually is. Run this after write_cpp_file and before build_project. Params: `path (absolute, or relative to the project Source/), buildCsPath? (defaults to the owning module's)` |
| `add_module_dependency(dependency, moduleName, access?)` | Add a module to a target module's Build.cs dependency array. Params: `moduleName (the Build.cs to edit - must exist in the project), dependency (module name to add, e.g. 'UMG'), access? ('public'\|'private', default 'private')` |
| `add_cpp_member(declaration, headerPath, memberName, access?)` | Append a UPROPERTY/UFUNCTION declaration to an existing UCLASS header inside the access specifier you choose. Idempotent: if a declaration containing the same memberName is already present, returns existed:true. Params: `headerPath (relative to Source/ or absolute), declaration (full multi-line UPROPERTY(...) / UFUNCTION(...) block plus its single-line member or function signature), memberName (the identifier the declaration introduces - used for idempotency), access? ('public'\|'protected'\|'private', default 'public')` |
| `list_localization_cultures()` | Report the project's cultures: the editor's current culture, language and locale, the game's native culture and the cultures it has compiled localization for, CulturesToStage from the packaging settings, and every project localization target with its native culture and supported cultures. Params: `none` |
| `list_localization_targets(includeEngineTargets?:b)` | List the project's localization targets (includeEngineTargets adds the engine's): name, guid, cultures with word counts, nativeCulture, what each gathers from (packages with include/exclude paths, source files with search directories, metadata), conflict status, and its files (gather and compile configs, manifest, an archive and a LocRes per culture, each with exists, bytes and modified). Every row is valid set_localization_target input. Params: `includeEngineTargets?` |
| `set_localization_target(target, cultures?:[s], nativeCulture?, gatherFromPackages?:b, includePaths?:[s], excludePaths?:[s], gatherFromTextFiles?:b, searchDirectories?:[s])` | Create or change a project localization target: cultures (replaces the list), nativeCulture, gatherFromPackages with includePaths/excludePaths (wildcards relative to the project root, e.g. Content/UI/*), gatherFromTextFiles with searchDirectories. A new target gathers nothing until told what to. Written to DefaultEditor.ini as Project Settings would. A call that changes nothing reports unchanged; the rollback removes a created target or restores the previous settings. Params: `target, cultures?, nativeCulture?, gatherFromPackages?, includePaths?, excludePaths?, gatherFromTextFiles?, searchDirectories?` |
| `remove_localization_target(target, deleteFiles?:b)` | Remove a project localization target; deleteFiles also deletes its configs, manifest, archives and LocRes. The rollback recreates its settings (not deleted files). Removing one that is not there reports alreadyRemoved. Params: `target, deleteFiles?` |
| `gather_localization_target(target)` | Gather text for one localization target: writes its gather config and runs the GatherText commandlet in a separate process, as the Localization Dashboard's Gather Text does, then answers with the exit code, the error lines, a log tail and the target's refreshed files and word counts. A second gather or compile while one runs is refused. Params: `target` |
| `compile_localization_target(target, culture?)` | Compile one localization target's archives into LocRes files (culture narrows it to one), through the GatherText commandlet as the Localization Dashboard's Compile Text does, then refreshes the editor's loaded localization. Answers with the exit code, error lines, a log tail and the target's files. Params: `target, culture?` |
| `epic_compile_live_coding()` | [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Triggers a Live Coding compile and returns a pending result that resolves once the compile finishes. Live Coding must be enabled in Editor Preferences. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_create_directory(path)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Creates a directory and any missing parents. A directory that already exists is a success. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path` |
| `epic_delete_file(path)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Deletes one file. Directories are rejected. Recursive deletion is unavailable. Source-controlled files are marked for deletion when source control is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path` |
| `epic_discover_tests(bForceRediscover?:b)` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Initialize automation worker discovery and load the test list. Must be called once before ListTests or RunTests. Takes several seconds as it discovers the local automation worker and enumerates all registered tests. Returns an async result that completes with true when tests are available, or an error if discovery fails. Params: `bForceRediscover?` |
| `epic_download_url(url, destinationPath, bOverwrite:b)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Downloads an HTTPS URL to a file. Redirects are not followed. Responses above 1 GiB are rejected. Local, private, and selected special-use addresses are rejected. Only HTTP 200 responses succeed. Host resolution and the HTTP request each time out after 30 seconds. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `url, destinationPath, bOverwrite` |
| `epic_edit_text_by_anchor(path, anchorText, newText, editMode)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Edits the unique occurrence of a piece of text. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected. Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. AnchorText is matched exactly first. If that fails, LF and CRLF variants are tried. NewText uses the file's existing line ending. Replace changes the anchor text itself. InsertBefore and InsertAfter insert whole lines and preserve the anchor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, anchorText, newText, editMode` |
| `epic_edit_text_by_line_range(path, firstLine:i, lastLine:i, newText, editMode)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Edits an inclusive range of one-based lines. Source files and results above 1 MiB are rejected. Big-endian UTF-16 files are rejected. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Lines outside the range remain unchanged, including their line endings. NewText uses the file's existing line ending. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, firstLine, lastLine, newText, editMode` |
| `epic_enable_live_coding()` | [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Call before CompileLiveCoding on a session launched with Live Coding off; starts the Broker/Agent. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_section_property_values(containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertyNames:[s])` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns the current values of the specified properties as a JSON object. Params: `containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertyNames` |
| `epic_get_section_schema(containerName, categoryName, sectionName)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns a JSON Schema describing the user-visible properties of a settings section. The schema maps each property name to its type, description, and constraints. A section that uses a custom widget has no settings object and so no schema. Params: `containerName, categoryName, sectionName` |
| `epic_get_supported_platforms()` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns the platforms the project declares support for in its .uproject file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_test_results()` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get detailed results for the current or most recent test run. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_test_status()` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get a lightweight status snapshot of the automation controller. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Params: `none` |
| `epic_is_live_coding_ready()` | [Epic LiveCodingToolset.LiveCodingToolset] Poll before calling CompileLiveCoding to avoid blocking on the Broker's initial module load. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_available_platforms()` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the platforms a project can declare support for, the choices in the Project Settings Supported Platforms section. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_categories(containerName)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all categories within a settings container, sorted alphabetically. Params: `containerName` |
| `epic_list_containers()` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all known settings containers, sorted alphabetically. Common containers are "Editor" and "Project". Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_directory(path, firstEntry?:i, maximumEntries?:i)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Lists a range from the immediate contents of a directory. Directories with more than 100000 immediate entries are rejected before filtering or range selection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, firstEntry?, maximumEntries?` |
| `epic_list_sections(containerName, categoryName)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all sections within a settings category, sorted alphabetically. Params: `containerName, categoryName` |
| `epic_list_tests(nameFilter?, tagFilter?, limit?:i)` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] List available automation tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Params: `nameFilter?, tagFilter?, limit?` |
| `epic_read_text_file(path, firstLine?:i, maximumLines?:i, continuationCursor?, maximumResponseCharacters?:i)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Reads lines or fragments without line numbers, budgeting the complete JSON response for EDA. Decode Contents once as JSON when ContentsEncoding is "json-string" to recover NUL and U+FFFE/U+FFFF without transport substitution. Oversized lines are returned in character-aligned fragments. Pass NextCursor to continue without losing text. Supports UTF-8 and byte-order-marked UTF-16. Legacy single-byte text is not supported on all platforms. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, firstLine?, maximumLines?, continuationCursor?, maximumResponseCharacters?` |
| `epic_reset_section_to_defaults(containerName, categoryName, sectionName)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Resets the settings in a section to their default values. Project sections saved to a Default*.ini cannot be reset, matching the Settings editor. Params: `containerName, categoryName, sectionName` |
| `epic_resolve_path(path)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Resolves a native path, Unreal virtual-content path, or plugin path that the plugin manager finds to an absolute native path. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path` |
| `epic_run_tests(testNames:[s])` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run a set of automation tests by name. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Starts executing the specified tests and returns an async result that completes with a summary when all tests finish. Params: `testNames` |
| `epic_run_tests_by_filter(filterExpression)` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run automation tests selected by a filter expression. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Much faster than RunTests when targeting a large batch because the engine narrows the report tree in a single pass instead of running a per-leaf membership check against the requested name list. Filter syntax (multiple expressions joined by '+'): "StartsWith:System.Engine" prefix match against the full test path "^Foo" prefix anchor (equivalent to StartsWith:) "Bar$" suffix anchor "Substring" bare token matches anywhere in the path "Group:Smoke" expand a named group from AutomationControllerSettings ini Groups Returns an async result that completes with the same summary shape as RunTests. Params: `filterExpression` |
| `epic_save_section(containerName, categoryName, sectionName)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Saves the settings in a section. The default config file is checked out first when source control is enabled. Params: `containerName, categoryName, sectionName` |
| `epic_search_settings(query)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Finds settings by the label shown in the Settings editor, the property name, the tooltip, or the console variable the property is bound to, across every container. Every word in the query must match, ignoring case. A section whose own name matches is returned with an empty PropertyName. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `query` |
| `epic_set_section_properties(containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertiesJson)` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Sets one or more properties on a settings section from a JSON object and saves. PropertiesJson must be a JSON object mapping property names to new values, in the same format returned by GetSectionPropertyValues. If any value is rejected, none are applied and nothing is saved. The default config file is checked out first when source control is enabled. Params: `containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertiesJson` |
| `epic_set_supported_platforms(platforms:[s])` | [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Replaces the platforms the project declares support for and saves the .uproject file, checking it out first when source control is enabled. Packaging, running or cooking for a platform not in the list warns. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `platforms` |
| `epic_stop_tests()` | [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Stop all currently running tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. If a RunTests async result is pending, it will be completed with an error. Params: `none` |
| `epic_write_text_file(path, contents, bOverwrite:b)` | [Epic FileSystemToolset.FileSystemToolset] Writes a complete UTF-8 text file and creates missing parent directories. Existing read-only files are checked out through source control before replacement. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, contents, bOverwrite` |

---

## asset

*Asset management: list, search, read, CRUD, import meshes/textures, datatables, stringtables.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list(directory?, classFilter\|typeFilter?, recursive?:b, cursor?, limit\|maxResults?:i, offset?:n, classPaths?:[s], recursiveClasses?:b, nameRegex?, regexIgnoreCase?:b, skeletonPath?, includeMetadata?:b)` | List assets through the Asset Registry, including mounted plugin roots. Filter by classPaths (including subclasses), classFilter, nameRegex and skeletonPath. includeMetadata adds animation skeleton and playLength in seconds from registry tags without loading assets. Cursor-paginated with totalMatched, hasMore and nextCursor; maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit. Params: `directory?, classFilter? (or typeFilter), recursive?, cursor?, limit? (or maxResults), offset?, classPaths?, recursiveClasses?, nameRegex?, regexIgnoreCase?, skeletonPath?, includeMetadata?` |
| `search(query, classFilter?, cursor?, directory?, limit?:i, maxResults?:i, searchAll?:b)` | Search by name/class/path. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit and sizes the page when limit is omitted. With extra content roots configured and no directory, this searches each root and pages ONE ROOT AT A TIME, so a cursor has to be passed back together with the directory it came from. classFilter (alias typeFilter) keeps only assets whose class name contains it, case-insensitive, as list_assets does. Params: `query, directory?, classFilter?, maxResults?, searchAll?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `read(assetPath\|path)` | Read asset via reflection. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `read_properties(assetPath\|path, propertyName?, includeValues?:b, valueFormat?, expandDepth?:i, expandExternal?:b, maxExpandedObjects?:i)` | Read asset properties with values. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO (#568). propertyName accepts dotted/indexed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects (e.g. `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field`), and keyed paths that pick the one array element whose field equals a value (`Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`, reported back as indexedPath and resolvedPropertyName); landing on an array of subobjects also lists each element's index+class (#527). expandDepth inlines the properties of subobjects OWNED by this asset, so a data asset's nested payload comes back in ONE call instead of a reference you have to chase (#755); references to OTHER assets are marked expandable rather than followed, unless expandExternal=true. Capped by maxExpandedObjects with expansionTruncated reported. Find an array element by field value in a data asset without reading the whole array, e.g. `Profiles[Id=Primary].Presentation.Mesh` reads exactly one matching element. A nested key such as `[Meta.Id=Foo]` also works; no match or several matches are refused with the count and sample values. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName?, includeValues?, valueFormat?, expandDepth?, expandExternal?, maxExpandedObjects?` |
| `list_properties(assetPath\|path, propertyName?, includeValues?:b, valueFormat?, expandDepth?:i, expandExternal?:b, maxExpandedObjects?:i)` | List reflected properties on any asset. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName?, includeValues?, valueFormat?, expandDepth?, expandExternal?, maxExpandedObjects?` |
| `get_properties(assetPath\|path, propertyName?, includeValues?:b, valueFormat?, expandDepth?:i, expandExternal?:b, maxExpandedObjects?:i)` | Read property values on any asset; the same read as read_properties with includeValues on by default. propertyName accepts dotted/indexed/keyed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects, so one leaf of one element reads without dumping the array: `Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`. valueFormat='json' returns structured values. resolvedPropertyName reports the numeric path matched; indexedPath is also returned for keyed paths. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName?, includeValues?, valueFormat?, expandDepth?, expandExternal?, maxExpandedObjects?` |
| `duplicate(sourcePath, destinationPath, onConflict?)` | Duplicate any asset, including an Enhanced Input InputAction with independent copies of its instanced triggers, modifiers and PlayerMappableKeySettings. sourcePath and destinationPath name the assets; onConflict=error refuses an existing destination. Verify with gameplay(read_input_action). Rollback deletes the copy. Params: `sourcePath, destinationPath, onConflict?` |
| `rename(sourcePath?, destinationPath?, assetPath?, newName?, force?:b)` | Rename asset: pass assetPath and newName, or sourcePath and destinationPath. World Partition levels are detected and their __ExternalActors__/__ExternalObjects__ packages migrate atomically alongside the .umap, source-side redirectors get fixed up, and the active editor world is swapped to blank if it matches the source (#409). Refuses if any package is dirty - save first. If a prior rename left externals orphaned at the old path, re-running reconciles them. Rollback descriptor is emitted even on partial failure so the inverse rename can recover. `force=true` lets the call merge into a destination with pre-existing externals (used by rollback). For batches of 3+ scene-referenced non-world assets use bulk_rename instead. Params: `sourcePath?, destinationPath?, assetPath?, newName?, force?` |
| `bulk_rename(renames:[o])` | Batched rename using IAssetTools::RenameAssets. Each renames[] item is exactly one of {sourcePath, destinationPath (full package path with the asset name)}, {assetPath, newName} or {sourcePath, newPackagePath, newName}; an unknown or mixed key, or a destinationPath naming an existing folder, refuses the whole batch with invalidItems before anything moves (#1291). It runs as a single transaction with one redirector-fixup pass (matches Content Browser drag). Use this over looped rename for scene-referenced assets. World assets are rejected (status=rejected_world); use rename_asset which handles WP externals atomically (#409). The fix-up pass cannot see a referencer that is not loaded, so each renamed item reports redirectorLeft and the result carries redirectorsLeft/redirectorsRemoved plus redirectorPackages, which feeds straight into fixup_redirectors (#908). A batch that would leave another object of a multi-object package at the old path is refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind and splitPackages naming each one; nothing moves (#1137). Params: `renames` |
| `fixup_redirectors(paths:[s], dryRun?:b, save?:b, allowProjectWide?:b, deleteRedirectors?:b)` | Clean up ObjectRedirectors left at the old paths after a move, bounded to exactly the packages you name. Preflights each redirector, its destination, and its hard AND soft referencers, then reports packagesToLoad/packagesToSave before touching anything; dryRun=true stops there. The real run loads only those referencers (a soft reference in an unloaded package is what the rename's own fix-up pass misses), rewrites them, saves them, RE-QUERIES the asset registry, and deletes a redirector only when nothing references it any more, reporting kept vs deleted per package with the referencers that survived. Naming a whole content root is refused unless allowProjectWide=true, so this can never turn into a project-wide resave. Protected mounts are refused outright. Runs unattended: it never calls the editor's interactive fix-up, so no 'No referencing assets found' message or Redirector Update Report modal can block it, and the result summarises fixed (redirectors whose referencers were all repointed), deleted, and noReferencers (#1266). dryRun is the way to preview; save=false repoints the referencers in memory without writing them and keeps every redirector they reference (#908). deleteRedirectors=false saves the repointed referencers and keeps the redirector stubs, reported as kept (#1828). Params: `paths, dryRun?, save?, allowProjectWide?, deleteRedirectors?` |
| `move(sourcePath?, destinationPath?, assetPath?, newName?, force?:b)` | Move asset: pass sourcePath and destinationPath. The same call as rename. Params: `sourcePath?, destinationPath?, assetPath?, newName?, force?` |
| `delete(assetPath\|path, force?:b)` | Delete asset. force defaults to false and is a REAL guard: the bridge asks the Asset Registry for referencers first and refuses with success=false, reason='has_referencers' and the full referencers list rather than destroying an asset other packages point at (#976). force=true takes the force-delete path, which also auto-closes open asset editors (#278). On a delete the editor attempted and could not finish, the reason is open_in_editor / has_referencers / in_memory_referenced / package_read_only / package_dirty / unknown, with referencers, inMemoryReferencers, packageReadOnly and packageDirty diagnostics (#601). Params: `assetPath (or path), force?` |
| `delete_batch(assetPaths\|paths:[s], force?:b)` | Batch-delete assets. Per-path status is deleted \| absent \| protected \| refused \| failed, plus reason+referencers on refused and failed entries. A referenced asset is refused per entry with force=false and the rest of the batch still runs, so one guarded asset never hides behind a bare failed count (#976, #278). Result carries deleted/absent/refused/failed/protected/total. Params: `assetPaths (or paths), force?` |
| `create_data_asset(name, className\|class, packagePath?, properties?:o, onConflict?)` | Create UDataAsset instance of custom class. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix (UMyConfig and MyConfig both resolve), a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name; a failed lookup lists the spellings tried and the closest matches (#823). Params: `name, className (or class), packagePath?, properties?, onConflict?` |
| `create_asset_by_class(name, className\|class, packagePath?, properties?:o, onConflict?)` | Create an asset of ANY concrete UObject class (not just UDataAsset) - physical-material subclasses, curves, settings objects. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix, a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name (#823). Actors/components and specialized assets (Blueprint/Material) have dedicated actions (#726). Params: `name, className (or class), packagePath?, properties?, onConflict?` |
| `read_graph(assetPath\|path, graphName?, includePins?:b, maxNodes?:n)` | Read the NODE GRAPH of any EdGraph-backed asset: every graph in it, every node, and every node's pins with what each pin is connected to. Reflection cannot reach topology: UEdGraphNode declares its Pins array with no UPROPERTY, and UEdGraphPin is a plain class rather than a UObject, so no set_property, reflect_instance or find_object can read, break or make a connection (#1059). For the EdGraph types with no category of their own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them. A Blueprint, a PCG graph or a Material is REFUSED here and pointed at blueprint(read_graph) / blueprint(get_connections) / pcg(read_graph) / material(read_graph), which own those types and address them in their own terms. Each node reports name, path, class, title, position and comment; each pin reports name, pinId, direction, type, defaultValue and linkedTo[] naming the node and pin at the other end. Node settings themselves are read with reflection(action='reflect_instance') on the node path this returns, which already works; this reports what that cannot see. connectionCount is per graph and counts each wire once; nodesReported is how many nodes this call emitted, which maxNodes can cut below a graph's own nodeCount. A node reported with hasNoPins is broken: AllocateDefaultPins never ran for it, so it can never be wired and the editor cannot draw it. Each node also reports nodeGuid. To change the graph use connect_graph_pins, disconnect_graph_pins, add_graph_node and remove_graph_node, which go through the graph's own schema. An asset with no graph answers with an empty list and says so rather than failing. Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, includePins?, maxNodes?` |
| `connect_graph_pins(assetPath\|path, graphName?, sourceNode?, sourcePinId?, sourcePin?, sourcePinDirection?, targetNode?, targetPinId?, targetPin?, targetPinDirection?, save?:b)` | Connect two pins in any EdGraph-backed asset with no category of its own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them, through the graph's own schema (TryCreateConnection), so the graph type's rules decide what is legal. A refusal returns the schema's own message with reason='schema_disallowed'. Address each end by node (nodeGuid, node path, name or unique title from read_graph) and pinId, which is the reliable form because pin names repeat on some node types; pin name plus direction also works. A pinId alone needs no node. brokenLinks lists any link the schema replaced. Rollback: disconnect_graph_pins. A Blueprint, Material or PCG graph is refused and pointed at its own category. Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, sourceNode?, sourcePinId?, sourcePin?, sourcePinDirection?, targetNode?, targetPinId?, targetPin?, targetPinDirection?, save?` |
| `disconnect_graph_pins(assetPath\|path, graphName?, sourceNode?, sourcePinId?, sourcePin?, sourcePinDirection?, targetNode?, targetPinId?, targetPin?, targetPinDirection?, save?:b)` | Break links in an EdGraph-backed asset through its schema. With a target pin, breaks that one link (BreakSinglePinLink); without one, breaks every link on the source pin (BreakPinLinks). Pins are addressed as in connect_graph_pins. A link that does not exist is reported with wasConnected=false and nothing changes. Rollback: connect_graph_pins when exactly one link was broken; otherwise brokenLinks names each one. Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, sourceNode?, sourcePinId?, sourcePin?, sourcePinDirection?, targetNode?, targetPinId?, targetPin?, targetPinDirection?, save?` |
| `add_graph_node(assetPath\|path, graphName?, nodeClass?, actionName?, spawnMode?, posX?:n, posY?:n, save?:b)` | Add a node to an EdGraph-backed asset's graph through the schema's own node action, so its pins are allocated and it is parented to the graph. nodeClass is the class the action spawns (a CustomizableObjectNode class for Mutable, a SoundNode class for a SoundCue); actionName picks a menu entry by name ('category\|name' also works) when several actions spawn the same class. When nothing matches, the error lists availableActions. spawnMode=direct constructs nodeClass itself (CreateNewGuid, PostPlacedNewNode, AllocateDefaultPins), and auto does that only for a schema that publishes no node actions. Returns nodeGuid, nodePath and every pin with its pinId. Rollback: remove_graph_node. Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, nodeClass?, actionName?, spawnMode?, posX?, posY?, save?` |
| `remove_graph_node(assetPath\|path, graphName?, node, save?:b)` | Remove a node from an EdGraph-backed asset's graph: the schema breaks its links, then the node is destroyed. A node the graph type forbids deleting (a root or output node) is refused. brokenLinks names every link it had so they can be re-made. Rollback: add_graph_node with the same class and position when exactly one schema action spawns it (lossy: a fresh default node); otherwise rollbackPossible=false. Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, node, save?` |
| `create_customizable_object(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, save?:b)` | Create a Mutable CustomizableObject through Mutable's own factory, so it holds its Source graph with the Base Object node and can be authored with add_graph_node and connect_graph_pins at once. An asset made with create_asset_by_class has no graph. Returns objectPath, graphName, rootNode (nodeGuid and pins with pinIds) and every graph node. onConflict=skip returns an existing CustomizableObject as existed; error refuses. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the plugin is off. Rollback: delete_asset. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, save?` |
| `compile_customizable_object(assetPath\|path, optimizationLevel?, textureCompression?)` | Compile a Mutable CustomizableObject synchronously, without saving or gathering references, and report the outcome: state, compiled, and the LogMutable errors and warnings the compile wrote. A failed compile returns success=false with the first error. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the Mutable plugin is not enabled. Params: `assetPath (or path), optimizationLevel?, textureCompression?` |
| `create_subobject(assetPath\|path, className, name, properties?:o, outer?, onConflict?, save?:b)` | Create a named subobject OWNED by an existing asset, inside that asset's package, and return its object path for later property writes. This is the missing half of editing a data asset whose payload is named subobjects referenced from a struct array: set_property, bulk_set_properties and append_array_elements can edit the entries, and this makes a new one. Component classes are accepted, unlike create_asset_by_class; Actors are refused because they are spawned into a level. className takes a /Script/Module.Class path, which is how you name a plugin class the Python `unreal` module never exposes. The new object is created RF_Standalone and the package is saved in the same call, so it survives the garbage collection that used to eat a fresh object within one call and is reachable by path from the next one. properties are applied to a throwaway instance first, so a bad path or value creates nothing. outer='asset' (default) gives '<asset>.<name>'; outer='package' puts it beside the asset in the package (#975). Params: `assetPath (or path), className, name, properties?, outer?, onConflict?, save?` |
| `bulk_upsert_data_assets(items:[o], onConflict?, dryRun?:b, save?:b)` | Create or update up to 500 UDataAsset instances in ONE call. Every descriptor is first applied to a transient copy, so a bad class, property path, or value rejects the whole batch before a package is touched; nothing is half-written by a typo. Per-item status is created \| updated \| unchanged \| skipped \| failed (dryRun reports wouldCreate \| wouldUpdate \| wouldRemainUnchanged \| wouldSkip), each with its own error when it failed. Replaying the same request returns unchanged, and only changed packages are saved. Emits a rollback descriptor that restores prior values and deletes what it created. Params: `items, onConflict?, dryRun?, save?` |
| `save(assetPath\|path?, assetPaths?:[s], force?:b)` | Save one asset, exactly the packages named by assetPaths, or every dirty asset under /Game when both are omitted. assetPaths resolves each asset, object or package path to its loaded package (naming a World Partition actor names its external package), refuses the whole call before writing anything if one names nothing in memory, and reports each package as saved, notDirty or failed with a reason; no other package is written. The save-everything form refuses a call carrying any key it does not take, so a misspelt selector cannot widen it. force=true saves regardless of the dirty flag - several edits (OFPA level actors, some subsystem property writes) never mark their package dirty, so a dirty-only save skipped them and still reported success. Returns the package name plus on-disk file path, size and mtime so the write can be verified rather than trusted (#768). A failed save returns the engine's reason in error and saveDiagnostics, and when the engine refused a reference to a private object, illegalReference names that object, the object and property holding it, and how to clear it (#1120). Params: `assetPath? (or path), assetPaths?, force?` |
| `save_all_dirty(saveMapPackages?:b, saveContentPackages?:b)` | Flush every dirty package to disk in one call. Reports the packages it attempted, which ones reached disk (with file path, size and mtime) and which are still dirty afterwards, because a bare savedAll boolean has come back true while packages were never written (#768). Params: `saveMapPackages?, saveContentPackages?` |
| `read_mesh_materials(assetPath, lodIndex?:i)` | Read every mesh material slot, effective shading properties through instance overrides, parent chain, LOD section-to-slot mappings and Nanite state. Read-only. Params: `assetPath, lodIndex?` |
| `set_mesh_material(assetPath\|path, materialPath, slotIndex?:n)` | Assign material to static mesh slot. Params: `assetPath (or path), materialPath, slotIndex?` |
| `set_mesh_materials_batch(assignments:[o], save?:b, dryRun?:b, continueOnError?:b)` | Assign materials across many meshes and slots in one call, so an N mesh x M slot kit costs one round trip instead of N*M. StaticMesh and SkeletalMesh both work. Address a slot by slotName (survives a reimport reordering slot indices) or by slotIndex (default 0); passing both is rejected when they disagree. Every submitted assignment returns its own index/ok/status/error, status being ok\|updated\|unchanged\|invalid\|protected\|duplicate\|not_found\|slot_not_found\|failed\|skipped. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a mesh is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the assignments that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Each mesh is written and saved once no matter how many of its slots the batch names, and the rollback payload restores only the writes that landed (#822). Params: `assignments, save?, dryRun?, continueOnError?` |
| `recenter_pivot(one(assetPath\|path; assetPaths:[s]))` | Move static mesh pivot to geometry center. With assetPaths, the first mesh sets the reference pivot for all of them. Params: `assetPath (or path) OR assetPaths` |
