| `import_static_mesh(filePath\|filename, name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, combineMeshes?:b, importMaterials?:b, importTextures?:b, generateLightmapUVs?:b, importUniformScale?:n)` | Import from FBX, OBJ, or GLB/glTF (glTF routes through Interchange) (#549). importUniformScale=100 fixes metre-authored FBX (#687). Params: `filePath (or filename), name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), combineMeshes?, importMaterials?, importTextures?, generateLightmapUVs?, importUniformScale?` |
| `import_skeletal_mesh(filePath\|filename, name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, skeletonPath?, importMaterials?:b, importTextures?:b, importUniformScale?:n, importMorphTargets?:b, createPhysicsAsset?:b, replaceExisting?:b, importer?:{auto,interchange,legacy}, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Import skeletal meshes with scale, replacement, target skeleton or a new skeleton, and optional material/texture import. importer=interchange supplies an explicit pipeline stack so UE 5.8 applies the settings; auto selects it on 5.8 and later. Legacy uses FbxImportUI. dryRun validates first; save defaults false. Returns importedAssets, meshes with bounds, material slots, skeleton and sockets, plus boxExtent, morphTargets and numLODs. Import changes may require backup restoration. Params: `filePath (or filename), name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), skeletonPath?, importMaterials?, importTextures?, importUniformScale?, importMorphTargets?, createPhysicsAsset?, replaceExisting?, importer?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `import_animation(one(filePath\|filename; filePaths:[s]), name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, skeletonPath, importCustomAttribute?:b, removeRedundantKeys?:b, importSettings?:o)` | Import anim from FBX. importSettings sets any FbxAnimSequenceImportData or FbxImportUI field by UPROPERTY name or dotted path, e.g. {bSnapToClosestFrameBoundary: true} for clips whose length is not frame-aligned; a bool may drop its b prefix. An unknown key fails before anything is imported (#1134). filePaths imports a batch of FBX files into one folder with the same settings, one row per file under files. animations reads back each imported AnimSequence: path, playLength, numberOfFrames, numberOfKeys, frameRate, boneTrackCount, curveCount, enableRootMotion, and hasRootMotion with rootTravel from the root bone track (#1228). Params: `filePath (or filename) OR filePaths, name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), skeletonPath, importCustomAttribute?, removeRedundantKeys?, importSettings?` |
| `import_file(filePath\|filename, packagePath\|destinationPath, name\|assetName?, factoryClass?, factoryProperties?:o, replaceExisting?:b, save?:b, automated?:b)` | Import any source file through a chosen factory, unattended. factoryClass names a UFactory subclass by name or /Script path, including one a plugin ships (resolved at runtime; omit it to let the editor pick by extension). factoryProperties sets that factory's properties by UPROPERTY name or dotted path before the import runs, which is how a factory that raises its own options dialog is told to use the supplied options instead, since unattended mode cancels the dialog and the import with it. The file extension is checked against the factory's formats first. An unknown property fails before anything is imported (#1096). Imported assets are saved by default and imported[] reports saved, saveError or dirtyNotSaved per asset; save=false leaves them dirty (#1280). Params: `filePath (or filename), packagePath (or destinationPath), name? (or assetName), factoryClass?, factoryProperties?, replaceExisting?, save?, automated?` |
| `import_font(filePath\|filename, name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, onConflict?, hinting?, loadingPolicy?, createFont?:b)` | Import a .ttf/.otf (or .ttc/.otc collection) as a FontFace asset, with no import dialog. hinting and loadingPolicy set the face's own options; createFont=true also makes <name>_Font, a runtime Font whose Default typeface is this face. Returns path and the subFaces the file holds. onConflict: skip (default) \| error \| replace (reimport the bytes) (#1377). Params: `filePath (or filename), name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), onConflict?, hinting?, loadingPolicy?, createFont?` |
| `create_font(name, packagePath?, fontFaces:[s], typefaceNames?:[s], onConflict?)` | Create a runtime Font (composite font) whose default typeface has one entry per FontFace: fontFaces[] are FontFace asset paths and typefaceNames[] their entry names in the same order (Regular, Bold, Italic). This is the FTypefaceEntry/FFontData write Python cannot make. onConflict=update rewrites an existing font's default typeface and reports previousTypefaces (#1377). Params: `name, packagePath?, fontFaces, typefaceNames?, onConflict?` |
| `import_texture(filePath\|filename, name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, sRGB?:b, compressionSettings?, lodGroup?, neverStream?:b, noCompression?:b, noAlpha?:b)` | Import image. sRGB/compressionSettings/lodGroup/neverStream are applied at import time (folded in, no second call needed) (#661). Params: `filePath (or filename), name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), sRGB?, compressionSettings?, lodGroup?, neverStream?, noCompression?, noAlpha?` |
| `create_render_target_2d(name, packagePath?, width?:i, height?:i, format?, clearColor?:o, generateMips?:b, targetGamma?:n, onConflict?)` | Create and persist a TextureRenderTarget2D asset. Render format is applied before resource initialization. Params: `name, packagePath?, width?, height?, format?, clearColor?, generateMips?, targetGamma?, onConflict?` |
| `generate_skeletal_mesh_lods(one(assetPath; assetPaths:[s]; directory), recursive?:b, lodCount:i, trianglePercentages?:[n], regenerateImported?:b, skipExisting?:b, dryRun?:b, save?:b)` | Generate auto-reduced LODs on one SkeletalMesh, a list, or every SkeletalMesh in a folder, through the engine's RegenerateLOD (#1372). lodCount counts LOD 0; trianglePercentages gives each later LOD its triangle percentage of LOD 0, otherwise the engine's reduction settings apply. Idempotent: a mesh already at lodCount is skipped unless skipExisting=false, and a mesh with more LODs is never trimmed. Imported LODs are kept unless regenerateImported=true. dryRun reports without changing anything. Each mesh row lists every LOD with triangles, vertices, generated and trianglePercentage. Params: `assetPath OR assetPaths OR directory, recursive?, lodCount, trianglePercentages?, regenerateImported?, skipExisting?, dryRun?, save?` |
| `read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings(assetPath, lodIndex?:i, allLods?:b)` | Read a SkeletalMesh's per-LOD FSkeletalMeshBuildSettings without changing anything. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings (identical on a read), beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}, where each settings object carries bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bComputeWeightedNormals, bRemoveDegenerates, bUseHighPrecisionTangentBasis, bUseHighPrecisionSkinWeights, bUseFullPrecisionUVs, bUseBackwardsCompatibleF16TruncUVs, bOptimizeForInstancing, thresholdPosition, thresholdTangentNormal, thresholdUV, morphThresholdPosition and boneInfluenceLimit. Params: `assetPath, lodIndex?, allLods?` |
| `set_skeletal_mesh_optimize_for_instancing(assetPath, enabled:b, lodIndex?:i, allLods?:b)` | Write bOptimizeForInstancing on a SkeletalMesh's LOD build settings, which reorders the skin data so instanced draws of the mesh batch. Only LODs whose current value differs are touched, and the asset is only rebuilt and saved when at least one changes, so a call that asks for the value already set is a no-op. Read the current state with read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings first. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings, beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}. Params: `assetPath, enabled, lodIndex?, allLods?` |
| `get_static_mesh_build_settings(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i)` | Read a StaticMesh source model's FMeshBuildSettings (bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bRemoveDegenerates, bGenerateLightmapUVs, BuildScale3D and every other field) by its engine property name. lodIndex picks the source model (default 0). Returns settings and sourceModelCount. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?` |
| `set_static_mesh_build_settings(assetPath\|path, settings:o, lodIndex?:i, save?:b)` | Write FMeshBuildSettings fields on a StaticMesh source model, then rebuild and save it. settings is keyed by engine property name, e.g. {bRecomputeNormals: true}; an unknown name or wrong type refuses the whole call before anything changes. A call that changes nothing skips the rebuild. Returns previous and settings, and rolls back to the previous values. BuildScale3D scales only the render vertices: the editor keeps taking bounds from the unscaled source geometry, so a non-unit BuildScale3D also returns bounds, renderBounds, boundsMatchRender and a warning. To resize a mesh use scale_mesh_geometry. Params: `assetPath (or path), settings, lodIndex?, save?` |
| `scale_mesh_geometry(assetPath\|path, factor:n/v, pivot?:v, outputPath?, scaleSockets?:b, scaleCollision?:b, save?:b)` | Bake a scale into a StaticMesh's geometry: every source LOD and the hi-res source are transformed (normals and tangents corrected), then render data and bounds are rebuilt, so get_mesh_bounds, actor bounds and the rendered size all follow. factor is a number or {x, y, z}, every component above 0; pivot is the mesh-space point that stays fixed (default origin). Sockets and simple collision move with the geometry unless scaleSockets or scaleCollision is false; a rotated box, sphere or capsule under a non-uniform scale is fitted and counted in collision.approximated. outputPath scales a copy and leaves assetPath untouched. Returns previousBounds, bounds, lods[], socketsScaled and collision. In place, rolls back with the inverse scale; with outputPath, by deleting the copy. Params: `assetPath (or path), factor, pivot?, outputPath?, scaleSockets?, scaleCollision?, save?` |
| `read_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights(assetPath, vertexIndices:[i], lodIndex?:i, profileName?)` | Read existing per-vertex skin influences from one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile. The caller must name 1-256 source MeshDescription vertex IDs, so a read cannot dump a whole mesh. Each influence returns boneName, boneIndex, normalized weight and exact uint16 rawWeight. Render data may use 8-bit weights unless high-precision skin weights are enabled. Generated LODs without source geometry are refused. Params: `assetPath, vertexIndices, lodIndex?, profileName?` |
| `read_skeletal_mesh_bone_vertex_bounds(assetPath, boneNames?:[s], minWeight?:n, lodIndex?:i, profileName?)` | Measure where each bone's skinned vertices sit on one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile, so physics bodies, sockets and hit volumes can be sized from the mesh instead of guessed. By default each source vertex counts once, for its dominant bone; minWeight counts it for every bone weighing at least that much. boneNames limits the report to those bones (a named bone with no vertices comes back with vertexCount 0); omitted, every bone that owns a vertex is listed. Each bone returns boneName, boneIndex, parentName, vertexCount, bindPose (its component-space reference transform), componentSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bind pose and boneSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bone's own bind-pose frame, the frame a physics body on that bone uses. Also returns vertexCount, unweightedVertexCount and, with minWeight, belowThresholdVertexCount. Read-only. Params: `assetPath, boneNames?, minWeight?, lodIndex?, profileName?` |
| `read_skeletal_mesh_vertices(assetPath, boneNames?:[s], includeChildBones?:b, minWeight?:n, box?:o, include?:[s], offset?:n, limit?:i, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?, lodIndex?:i, profileName?)` | Read source vertices of one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile in bulk, to analyse a part before moving or reweighting it. Select with boneNames (vertices weighted to any of those bones, includeChildBones adds the bones below them, minWeight sets the least summed weight on them), box {min, max} in the component-space bind pose, both, or neither for every vertex. include picks positions, weights and triangles (default positions and weights). Each vertex returns vertexIndex (the source ID read_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights and set_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights take), position, influences [{boneName, boneIndex, weight}] and, with boneNames, selectedWeight. triangles lists each triangle whose three corners are selected, with triangleIndex, vertexIndices and polygonGroup, once across pages. Pages with offset and limit (default 2000, at most 20000) and returns hasMore and nextOffset; dumpToFile writes the whole selection to outputPath (default under Saved/UE_MCP/SkeletalMeshVertices) and returns only the summary. Always returns vertexCount, selectedVertexCount and selectedBounds. Read-only. Params: `assetPath, boneNames?, includeChildBones?, minWeight?, box?, include?, offset?, limit?, dumpToFile?, outputPath?, lodIndex?, profileName?` |
| `set_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights(assetPath, edits:[o], lodIndex?:i, profileName?, restoreRawWeights?:b)` | Replace skin influences on explicitly selected source MeshDescription vertices in one existing SkeletalMesh LOD/profile. The complete batch is validated before mutation: invalid or duplicate vertices/bones, non-finite/negative/out-of-range weights and all-zero sets fail without a write. Unreal's FBoneWeights normalizes, quantizes to uint16 source weights and prunes ordinary edits to its influence limit; actual before/after values are read back. Other source vertices and source profiles are untouched. Rebuilding may refresh derived render data and dependent generated LODs. A changed mesh is rebuilt and saved; an identical request is a no-op. Rollback payloads use restoreRawWeights with exact uint16 rawWeight values. Params: `assetPath, edits, lodIndex?, profileName?, restoreRawWeights?` |
| `transform_skinned_part(assetPath, boneName, any(translation:v; rotation:r), space?:{bone,component}, moveBone?:b, lods?:[i], dryRun?:b, save?:b)` | Move one rigid part of a SkeletalMesh with its bone: the bone's reference pose and every source vertex skinned to it or to a bone below it, in every LOD, by translation and/or rotation about the bone's origin. space picks the axes: bone (its bind-pose frame, default) or component. A vertex moves by its weight on those bones. Every LOD is read and checked before anything is written, so the edit is all-or-nothing: a LOD without source geometry that is not generated, bones that differ from the reference skeleton, or no LOD 0 vertex on the part refuse the call. A LOD with no vertex on the part is reported with verticesMoved 0, not refused. Vertices move in place in each LOD's source geometry, so hard edges and imported normals are kept (turned with the part on a rotation) whatever the LOD's recompute settings; generated LODs follow their base LOD. Returns per LOD verticesMoved, fullyWeighted, partiallyWeighted, and after the rebuild renderVerticesMoved, maxRenderPositionErrorCm and maxRenderNormalChangeDegrees against where the move should put each drawn vertex. dryRun reports the same plan without writing. Rolls back with the inverse move when every moved vertex moved rigidly. Params: `assetPath, boneName, at least one of translation/rotation, space?, moveBone?, lods?, dryRun?, save?` |
| `read_cloth_data(skeletalMeshPath\|assetPath)` | Read Chaos cloth data on a skeletal mesh: per clothing asset, its configs (reflected properties), LOD count, and per-LOD point-weight-map summary (name, target, vertex count, min/max - including the MaxDistances mask). Also reports which render sections each clothing asset is bound to (boundSections, bound), every section of every LOD (sections: lodIndex, sectionIndex, materialIndex, usesCloth, clothingAsset, assetLodIndex) and unboundClothingAssets: an asset bound to no section never simulates (#595/#1139). Params: `skeletalMeshPath (or assetPath)` |
| `bind_cloth_to_section(skeletalMeshPath\|assetPath, lodIndex:i, sectionIndex:i, clothingAsset?, assetLodIndex?:i)` | Bind a clothing asset to one render section so it simulates, as the skeletal mesh editor's section clothing dropdown does. Whatever the section was bound to is unbound first. lodIndex and sectionIndex are validated against the mesh, assetLodIndex against the clothing asset. Saves the mesh; rolls back to the previous binding (#1139). Params: `skeletalMeshPath (or assetPath), lodIndex, sectionIndex, clothingAsset?, assetLodIndex?` |
| `unbind_cloth_from_section(skeletalMeshPath\|assetPath, lodIndex:i, sectionIndex:i, clothingAsset?)` | Remove the clothing asset bound to one render section. The engine unbinds per LOD, so other sections of that LOD bound to the same asset are released too and listed in releasedSections. A section with no binding is a no-op. Saves the mesh; rolls back by rebinding (#1139). Params: `skeletalMeshPath (or assetPath), lodIndex, sectionIndex, clothingAsset?` |
| `set_cloth_config(skeletalMeshPath\|assetPath, properties:o, clothingAsset?, configType?)` | Set properties on a clothing asset's Chaos cloth config via reflection (#595). Params: `skeletalMeshPath (or assetPath), properties, clothingAsset?, configType?` |
| `export_texture(assetPath\|path, outputPath\|filePath, inline?:b/i)` | Export a Texture2D to a PNG on disk (for inspection or external diffing) (#697). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `assetPath (or path), outputPath (or filePath)` |
| `compare_textures(assetPathA\|a, assetPathB\|b)` | Compare two Texture2D assets by dimensions, pixel format, and source-content identity (FTextureSource id) - tells you whether an authored texture actually changed without offline pixel-diffing (#697). Params: `assetPathA (or a), assetPathB (or b)` |
| `import_texture_batch(items:[o], packagePath?, save?:b, automated?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Batch import PNGs and other images with per-file preset=normal\|masks\|color and settings. Normal maps use linear Normalmap compression without green flip; packed masks use linear Masks; color uses sRGB. Per-file lodGroup, maxTextureSize, compressionSettings, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel override presets. All entries preflight before import; dryRun writes nothing. Saves after applying settings and returns per-item importedAssets, readBack and saved. Rollback deletes new textures only; replaced pixels require a backup. Params: `items, packagePath?, save?, automated?, dryRun?` |
| `reimport(assetPath\|path, filePath\|filename?, preserveSettings?:b, save?:b)` | Reimport an imported asset from its source file, or from filePath, which is recorded as its new source. A texture keeps its settings: compression, LOD group, sRGB, NeverStream, max size, mip generation, filter and addressing are read before the reimport and any the reimport changed are put back (preserveSettings=false skips that). For a texture the response carries settingsBefore, settingsAfter, restoredSettings (what the reimport changed and was undone) and sourceSizeBefore/sourceSizeAfter, the source pixel dimensions. The package is left dirty and unsaved unless save=true; packageDirty reports it. Params: `assetPath (or path), filePath? (or filename), preserveSettings?, save?` |
| `read_datatable(assetPath\|path, rowFilter?, rowNames?:[s], columns?:[s], outputPath?)` | Read DataTable rows as structured JSON (struct fields come back as objects). rowNames returns exactly the named rows in the order given, matched like FindRow (case-insensitive), and lists names the table lacks in missingRowNames instead of failing; rowFilter is a substring match instead. columns narrows each row to its Name and the named top-level row-struct fields, which is how one field is read across every row of a wide table; an unknown name is refused with the row struct's field list, and the response echoes the resolved columns. A large table overflows the response inline: pass outputPath to write the rows (after rowNames, rowFilter and columns) to a file as a JSON array instead. The response then carries outputPath (resolved absolute path), rowCount, bytes, rowStruct and totalRowCount, with no rows or rowNames. A relative outputPath resolves under the project's Saved/, missing folders are created and an existing file is overwritten. Params: `assetPath (or path), rowFilter?, rowNames?, columns?, outputPath?` |
| `create_datatable(name, rowStruct, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create DataTable. Params: `name, rowStruct, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `reimport_datatable(assetPath\|path, jsonPath?, jsonString?)` | Reimport DataTable from JSON. Params: `assetPath (or path), jsonPath?, jsonString?` |
| `clone_datatable_rows(assetPath\|path, clones:[o], save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Clone DataTable rows in one call: clones=[{sourceRow, rowName, overrides?}]. Copies native row memory before applying nested or dotted struct overrides, preserving omitted fields and references. All source rows must exist and all destination names must be unused; the full batch is validated before mutation. dryRun returns proposedRows; writes return rows with fields read back, clonedCount, rowCount, saved and persisted. Uses one editor undo transaction; rollback removes the cloned rows with the same save policy and is marked lossy because row change hook side effects cannot be reversed. Params: `assetPath (or path), clones, save?, dryRun?` |
| `set_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, rowName, row\|fields\|data:o)` | Append or overwrite a single DataTable row. row carries row-struct fields, and a partial update merges with the existing row. Idempotent; rollback restores the prior row (#437). Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName, row (or fields, or data)` |
| `add_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, rowName, row\|fields\|data:o)` | Alias for set_datatable_row (#437). Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName, row (or fields, or data)` |
| `update_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, rowName, row\|fields\|data:o)` | Alias for set_datatable_row; partial update merges with existing row (#437). Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName, row (or fields, or data)` |
| `remove_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, one(rowName; rowNames:[s]), save?:b)` | Remove a DataTable row with rowName, or several with rowNames in one transaction. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when all selected rows are absent. save defaults to true; save=false keeps removal in memory, including clone_datatable_rows rollback. Batch or unsaved removal uses editor undo to restore row values; the original single saved removal returns its set_datatable_row inverse. Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName OR rowNames, save?` |
| `get_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, rowName)` | Read one DataTable row's fields without dumping the whole table (#535). Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName` |
| `set_datatable_cell(assetPath\|path, rowName, fieldName, value:*)` | Write a single field on a single existing row (merges, leaves other cells untouched). Errors if the row doesn't exist (#535). Params: `assetPath (or path), rowName, fieldName, value` |
| `set_datatable_cells(assetPath\|path, cells:[o], dryRun?:b, save?:b)` | Write many cells across many existing rows in one call, such as relabelling one column on every row. Every cell is validated first (the row exists, the column is a top-level field, the value parses as set_datatable_cell parses it); if any fails, nothing is written and errors[] lists each failing cell. The rest apply in one undo transaction with one Modify/PostEditChange, then every row is re-exported and compared with the export taken before: touched rows may differ only in the requested fields and every other row must be identical, or the write is rolled back and the offending row and field named. Reports changedCells, unchangedCells (already equal), rowsTouched and verified. dryRun validates and reports without writing; save defaults to false; rollback restores the prior values. Params: `assetPath (or path), cells, dryRun?, save?` |
| `rename_datatable_row(assetPath\|path, oldName\|rowName, newName)` | Rename a row key, preserving its values (#535). Params: `assetPath (or path), oldName (or rowName), newName` |

The other channels are left alone. Returns the stored keys and an exact rollback (#1687). Params: `assetPath (or path), channel?, channelName?, keys, save?` |

| `get_texture_info(one(assetPath\|path; assetPaths:[s]))` | Read one texture or many via assetPaths: dimensions, MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream, flipGreenChannel, mip count and pixel format. Params: `assetPath (or path) OR assetPaths` |
| `set_texture_settings(one(assetPath\|path; assetPaths:[s]), preset?:{normal,masks,color}, settings?:o, compressionSettings?, lodGroup?, sRGB?:b, neverStream?:b, flipGreenChannel?:b, maxTextureSize?:i(0..32768), save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Set one texture or many via assetPaths, with preset=normal\|masks\|color and explicit settings. Supports MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings including Masks, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel. Validates every texture before mutation; dryRun previews, save defaults false. Returns previousSettings and readBack per texture, saved, and a rollback restoring the previous settings. Params: `assetPath (or path) OR assetPaths, preset?, settings?, compressionSettings?, lodGroup?, sRGB?, neverStream?, flipGreenChannel?, maxTextureSize?, save?, dryRun?` |

Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, widgetName?` |

Same addressing as get_text_localization. A Widget Blueprint is compiled; the asset is saved. The rollback restores the previous namespace, key and source, or string table reference. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, widgetName?, namespace?, key?, sourceString?, stringTableId?, stringTableKey?` |
| `import_stringtable(assetPath\|path, filePath\|filename\|csvPath)` | Import StringTable entries from CSV. Params: `assetPath (or path), filePath (or filename, or csvPath)` |
| `import_stringtable_csv(assetPath\|path, csvPath\|filePath, expectedKeys?:[s], requireExactKeys?:b, replaceExisting?:b, save?:b)` | Import or refresh a String Table from a CSV that is the canonical source, using Unreal's own String Table CSV importer. The CSV is parsed into a throwaway table and checked against expectedKeys FIRST, so a malformed file or a key set that does not match leaves the asset untouched and comes back with missingKeys/unexpectedKeys instead. replaceExisting=true prunes entries the CSV no longer carries, which is what makes the CSV canonical rather than additive; the prune runs after a successful merge so a bad parse can never empty the table. Returns addedKeys, updatedKeys, removedKeys, entry counts and an explicit persisted/saved plus persistError, so a write that did not reach disk is never reported as a success. A relative csvPath is read against the project directory (#978). Params: `assetPath (or path), csvPath (or filePath), expectedKeys?, requireExactKeys?, replaceExisting?, save?` |

Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted. Params: `imcPath (or mappingContext, or assetPath), inputActionPath (or inputAction), key, save?` |
| `remove_input_mapping(imcPath\|mappingContext\|assetPath, mappingIndex?:n, inputActionPath\|inputAction?, key?, save?:b)` | Remove an IMC key mapping. Same as gameplay(remove_imc_mapping) (#525). Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted. Params: `imcPath (or mappingContext, or assetPath), mappingIndex?, inputActionPath? (or inputAction), key?, save?` |

SkeletalMesh writes mesh-local sockets by default; pass a Skeleton asset path to edit skeleton-level sockets. Idempotent on socket name; pass onConflict='update' to overwrite an existing socket's transform with the supplied relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale (#412). Params: `assetPath, socketName, boneName?, relativeLocation?, relativeRotation?, relativeScale?, onConflict?` |
| `remove_socket(assetPath, socketName)` | Remove socket by name. Params: `assetPath, socketName` |
| `list_sockets(assetPath)` | List sockets on a mesh (StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh). SkeletalMesh results include mesh-local sockets plus assigned Skeleton sockets, each with source='mesh' or source='skeleton'. Every skeletal socket also carries componentTransform {location, rotation, scale}: its transform in component space at the reference pose (the SkeletalMesh's pose for a mesh, including its Skeleton's sockets; the Skeleton's own for a Skeleton asset, named in componentTransformPose), so no actor is needed to see where a socket sits. A socket whose bone is missing from that skeleton returns componentTransformError instead. Params: `assetPath` |
| `set_socket_transform(assetPath, socketName, relativeLocation?:v, relativeRotation?:r, relativeScale?:v)` | Update an existing socket's relative transform on StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. Pass any subset of relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale; omitted fields stay at their current values. Errors if the socket does not exist (use add_socket to create). Common after FBX import when SOCKET_* empties land with scale=(100,100,100) (#412). Params: `assetPath, socketName, relativeLocation?, relativeRotation?, relativeScale?` |
| `set_property(assetPath\|path, propertyName, value:*, save?:b)` | Assign a different skeleton to an existing SkeletalMesh with propertyName=Skeleton and value set to the skeleton object path; save controls persistence. Use edit_collection_entry to clone a keyed array element or patch one TMap entry. Set a UPROPERTY on any loaded asset (Material, DataAsset, DataTable, SubsurfaceProfile, etc.) using a dotted path. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO so you can author its defaults + Instanced sub-object arrays (#568). Walks nested structs, array elements by index (`Rules[1]`) or by key (`Rules[Id=Axe]`: exactly one element's Id must equal Axe, else the error lists the ids), and instanced subobjects internally - no more read-modify-write copies (e.g. `settings.mean_free_path_distance` on a UMaterial, or `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field` on a config asset #527). Value goes through MCPJsonProperty::SetJsonOnProperty so JSON null clears object refs, structs accept {x,y,z}, arrays/maps round-trip. TMap values take { "Key": value } or, for struct keys, [{ key: {...}, value: ... }]; a write that cannot store every entry fails and leaves the old value untouched (#820). The write is saved to the package by default and the result reports persisted plus the package name; a write that could not reach disk (save=false, a protected mount, a read-only file, a refused save) comes back with persisted=false and persistError naming the reason instead of a bare success that reverts on the next editor start (#931) (#420). With save=false, nested array field writes stay in memory, leave the package dirty, and support editor undo; rollback restores the old value with the same save option. An Instanced or EditInlineNew object property takes {instanceClass, properties}: a new subobject of that class is created with the owning object as its outer and its fields set from properties, e.g. RootMotionModifier = {instanceClass: "RootMotionModifier_Scale", properties: {Scale: {x:0,y:0,z:0}}} (#1292). An array of structs is written whole or per element (PropTypes[1].Modes = [{Key, DisplayName, bInCycle}, ...]); struct members match by C++ name, display name, or the Python spelling (display_name, in_cycle) (#1370). For example, `Profiles[Id=Primary].Presentation.Mesh` sets a field on the array element whose Id equals Primary. resolvedPropertyName and the rollback carry the numeric index matched, even when the write changes the key itself. A nested key such as `[Meta.Id=Foo]` also works. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, value, save?` |
| `edit_collection_entry(assetPath\|path, propertyName, entryKey:*, keyField?, newKey?:*, overrides?:o, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Update or clone one struct array element or TMap entry on a data asset, selected by entryKey. Arrays also need keyField (for example WeaponId); maps use their actual reflected key type. newKey clones to an unused key, while omitting it patches the existing entry. overrides accepts nested objects and dotted struct fields, preserving omitted fields. Validates before mutation; duplicate or missing keys fail. dryRun returns proposedValue; writes return value read back, count, saved and persisted. Rollback restores the whole collection, so replay before further collection edits. Instanced subobject cloning is refused. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, entryKey, keyField?, newKey?, overrides?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `append_array_elements(assetPath\|path, propertyName, elements:[*], unique?:b, save?:b)` | Append one or more JSON values to a reflected TArray without replacing existing entries. Supports dotted property paths plus native and user-defined USTRUCT elements. All elements are validated before mutation; returns appended indices and rollback data. The append is saved to the package by default and reports persisted / persistError the same way set_property does (#931); rollback preserves the same save option, so an unsaved append can be restored without writing to disk. Keyed paths such as `Profiles[Id=Foo].Items` select one nested array; resolvedPropertyName and the rollback use its numeric path. unique=true skips a value the array already holds (or an earlier element of the batch adds), compared the way the property type compares, and reports skippedElements; when every value is present nothing is written or saved (#1659). The response carries value, the array read back. Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, elements, unique?, save?` |
| `remove_array_elements(assetPath\|path, propertyName, one(indices:[i]; elements:[*]), save?:b)` | Remove elements from a reflected TArray by indices (each must exist) or by elements (every entry matching one of the values goes), keeping the order of the rest. Supports dotted and keyed property paths. Validates before mutation; returns removedIndices, previousValue and value read back, saves by default with persisted / persistError like set_property, and a rollback that restores the whole array with the same save option. A value that matches nothing removes nothing and writes nothing (#1659). Params: `assetPath (or path), propertyName, indices OR elements, save?` |
| `bulk_set_properties(items:[o], save?:b, dryRun?:b, continueOnError?:b)` | Set dotted UPROPERTY paths (indexed `Rules[1].X` or keyed `Rules[Id=Axe].X`, keys matched once in preflight) on as many as 500 assets in one preflighted batch. Every asset, path, and value is validated before anything is mutated, and every submitted item comes back with its own ok/status/error, so a bad path in item 300 never hides the other 499 verdicts. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a single UObject is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the items that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Returns per-property readback, aggregate counts, targeted save results, and a replayable rollback payload covering only the writes that landed. Each property readback reports resolvedPropertyName; apply and rollback use the numeric path matched during preflight. Params: `items, save?, dryRun?, continueOnError?` |
| `bulk_read_properties(propertyNames:[s], one(assetPaths:[s]; directory), recursive?:b, classNames?:[s], matchSubclasses?:b, where?:[o], whereMode?, suspectOnly?:b, groupBy?, countBy?:[s], sampleLimit?:i, countOnly?:b, limit?:i, startIndex?:i, maxAssets?:i, outputPath?)` | Read the SAME properties off many assets in one call, filtered and aggregated in the editor. read_properties answers one asset per call, which turns a library-wide question (concurrency settings across 582 sound assets, cull distances across 201 foliage types) into a loop. Select with assetPaths or with directory narrowed by classNames; propertyNames accepts dotted paths into nested structs (e.g. 'CullDistance.Max') and array elements by index or by field value (e.g. 'Profiles[Id=Foo].Mesh'; each row's resolvedPropertyNames gives the index matched and missingReasons says why a selector matched no element or several), and a Blueprint path reads its generated-class CDO. Predicates, groupBy and countBy all evaluate here: filtering happens before anything crosses the wire, with the same operators as level(query_components). Absent and null are reported separately, because 'this class has no such property' and 'this property is unset' are different findings; suspect is true for either, and suspectOnly returns just those rows. Never writes, and reports dirtiedPackages (#909). Params: `propertyNames, assetPaths OR directory, recursive?, classNames?, matchSubclasses?, where?, whereMode?, suspectOnly?, groupBy?, countBy?, sampleLimit?, countOnly?, limit?, startIndex?, maxAssets?, outputPath?` |
| `set_texture_settings_by_type(groups:o)` | Apply the canonical (compressionSettings, sRGB, LOD group) combo to every texture in each group: normal -> Normalmap, grayscale -> Grayscale, baseColor -> Default sRGB, hdr -> HDR (#421). Params: `groups` |
| `create_interchange_pipeline(one(assetPath; name), packagePath?, meshType?, options?:o, onConflict?)` | One-call factory for a UInterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline asset with the 15-property mesh-import boilerplate already applied (RecomputeNormals=false, MikkTSpace=true, HighPrecisionTangents=true, BuildNanite=false, CreatePhysicsAsset=false, etc.) (#421). Params: `assetPath OR name, packagePath?, meshType?, options?, onConflict?` |
| `reload_package(assetPath\|path)` | Force reload an asset package from disk. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `health_check(assetPath\|path)` | Diagnose stuck-unloadable asset. Returns onDisk/inRegistry/isLoaded/canLoad/isStuck flags so an agent can detect the half-shutdown state where load returns null but the file exists (#279). Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `force_reload(one(assetPath\|path; assetPaths:[s]), discardUnsaved?:b)` | Aggressive reload from disk: closes open editors, reloads the package (rebuilding a Blueprint's class and CDO so container properties come back fresh, not just scalars), and reports objectReplaced. Refuses a dirty package unless discardUnsaved=true, and fails loudly when the editor would not release the old object rather than serving stale values (#279/#820). assetPaths reloads up to 500 assets in one pass, so a material and its instances are re-read together; the whole set is validated first (a missing or unsaved package refuses the call before anything is released) and each asset reports under results (#1645). Params: `assetPath (or path) OR assetPaths, discardUnsaved?` |
| `export(assetPath\|path, outputPath, format?, dryRun?:b, replaceExisting?:b)` | Export static or skeletal meshes to FBX, Texture2D to PNG, or MaterialInstance parameters to JSON for a DCC round-trip. Material JSON includes parent lineage, scalar/vector/texture overrides and resolved parameter values. DataTable and CompositeDataTable require .json or .csv; format overrides their serializer. Relative outputPath resolves against the project directory; missing folders are created. replaceExisting defaults true; dryRun writes no file. Returns outputPath, assetClass, bytes, and material readBack or table rowCount. Overwritten files require a backup. Params: `assetPath (or path), outputPath, format?, dryRun?, replaceExisting?` |
| `search_fts(query, classFilter?, cursor?, limit\|maxResults?:i)` | Ranked asset search (token-scored over name/class/path). Every match is scored and the ranked list is paged, so the top page is a page rather than the whole answer. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit. Params: `query, classFilter?, cursor?, limit? (or maxResults)` |
| `reindex_fts(directory?)` | Rescan a content path so newly added assets on disk become searchable by search_fts. Params: `directory?` |
| `quick_search(query, refreshFiles?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | Keystroke-speed ranked search over assets, actors in the open level, and files under Source/ and Config/. Every word must match a name, class or path token (exact, prefix, substring, or the letters of the name in order). A leading BP_, M_, DT_ (any short prefix ending in _) keeps names with that prefix; actor:, asset: or file: keeps one kind. Each row has kind, path, name, class, a one-line summary and score; assets also carry objectPath. Assets come from an in-memory index kept current by Asset Registry add, rename and delete events, so no reindex is needed. Returns totalMatched, matchedByKind, indexedAssets, scannedActors, indexedFiles and elapsedMs; paged with cursor and limit. Params: `query, refreshFiles?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `semantic_search(query, limit?:i, directory?, maxDistance?:n)` | Natural-language asset search through Epic's Semantic Search plugin (UE 5.8+, experimental, off by default): the query is embedded by the configured provider (Loci or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and matched against the plugin's hybrid vector and keyword index. Returns results ranked by score, each with objectPath, name, class, vectorDistance and keywordScore. directory narrows to one folder; maxDistance overrides the plugin's VectorDistanceCutoff. Refuses with semantic_search_provider_not_configured, naming what is missing, when no provider can answer; check semantic_search_status first. Params: `query, limit?, directory?, maxDistance?` |
| `semantic_search_status()` | Report whether Epic's Semantic Search can answer: pluginLoaded, provider and providerConfigured (with providerNote saying what is missing), providerRegistered, embeddingDimension, initialized, indexingInProgress, indexedPaths, and index stats (vectorCount, keywordCount, supportedAssetCount, failedCount, indexing). available=false with errorCode and reason when it cannot. Never errors. Params: `none` |
| `semantic_search_index(assetPaths?:[s], force?:b)` | Queue assets for Semantic Search's index: assetPaths (object or package paths) indexes those, otherwise every asset in the plugin's indexed folders, and force=true clears the index and rebuilds every embedding. Returns at once with started, queuedAssetCount and the index stats; indexing runs in the background (watch semantic_search_status). Requires a configured provider, like semantic_search. Params: `assetPaths?, force?` |
| `get_referencers(packages\|assetPaths?:[s], packagePath\|assetPath?, includeDetails?:b, maxDepth?:i(1..8), includeMeshInfo?:b)` | Batch reverse dependency lookup for packages (or one packagePath). includeDetails follows Blueprint referencers up to maxDepth and reports maps, external actor packages, Blueprint paths and one shortest route per package. includeMeshInfo adds bounds, material slots, skeleton, sockets and static mesh collision setup. Returns referencersByPackage and detailsByPackage. Uses saved registry references; runtime-only and unsaved references are outside its scope. Params: `packages? (or assetPaths), packagePath? (or assetPath), includeDetails?, maxDepth?, includeMeshInfo?` |
| `get_dependencies(packages\|assetPaths?:[s], packagePath\|assetPath?, hard?:b, soft?:b)` | Forward dependency lookup (what packages this asset references) (#588). Returns {dependenciesByPackage, totalDependencies}. Params: `packages? (or assetPaths), packagePath? (or assetPath), hard?, soft?` |
| `list_skeleton_bones(assetPath\|path, includeTransforms?:b, limit?:i, offset?:n, includeBones?:b)` | List bones (names + rest-pose local and component-space transforms) from a SkeletalMesh or Skeleton asset, no live actor needed (#593). Returns {bones, boneCount, sourceKind, scaleSummary}. scaleSummary covers every bone whatever the page: bonesWithNonUnitLocalScale, min/maxComponentScale, rootScale and up to 32 scaledBones. limit pages the bones and offset starts the page; nextOffset is set while more remain. includeBones=false returns the summary alone (#1201). Params: `assetPath (or path), includeTransforms?, limit?, offset?, includeBones?` |
| `get_primary_asset_ids(type?, maxResults?:i)` | Enumerate AssetManager-registered FPrimaryAssetIds (verify a primary-asset registration) (#579). Returns {primaryAssetIds:[{primaryAssetId, type, name, assetPath}], count, total}. Params: `type?, maxResults?` |
| `set_sk_material_slots(assetPath\|path, slots:[o])` | Set materials on a USkeletalMesh by slot name or slotIndex (bypasses the blueprint override-materials path that UE's ICH silently reverts). Params: `assetPath (or path), slots` |
| `diagnose_registry(path, recursive?:b, reconcile?:b)` | Scan a content path and compare disk vs AssetRegistry (including in-memory pending-kill entries). Returns onDiskCount, inMemoryIncludedCount, ghostCount and paths. Params: `path, recursive?, reconcile?` |
| `get_mesh_bounds(assetPath)` | Get StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh bounding box. Returns min, max, boxExtent, boxCenter, meshKind (#193/#351). Params: `assetPath` |
| `get_mesh_info(assetPath)` | One-call static or skeletal mesh summary: boundsOrigin, boundsExtent, materialSlots (index, slotName, materialPath, isDefaultFallback), sockets (mesh and skeleton sockets), socketCount, skeletonPath, LOD/vertex counts and heightM. Params: `assetPath` |
| `read_import_sources(assetPath\|path)` | Read AssetImportData source filenames on an imported asset (StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture, Animation, etc.). Returns sources[] of {relativeFilename, absolutePath, timestamp, fileHash, displayLabelName} (#270). Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `get_mesh_collision(assetPath)` | Inspect StaticMesh collision setup. Returns collisionTraceFlag, hasSimple/ComplexCollision, element counts (#177). Params: `assetPath` |
| `get_static_mesh_geometry(assetPath\|path, geometrySource:{sourceModel,renderData}, lodIndex?:i, elementType?:{vertices,corners,triangles}, elementOffset?:i(0..1000000), pageSize?:i(1..512), snapshotId?, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?)` | Capture immutable StaticMesh geometry from an explicit sourceModel or renderData LOD. Page vertices, corners and oriented triangles with all UV channels, normals, tangents, binormal signs, RGBA and material groups; loose vertices and corners are retained. Source data is unbuilt; Nanite render data is its fallback LOD, never cluster geometry. First call returns snapshotId and contentRevision; reuse snapshotId for every table/page. Cached pages describe capturedUtc, not current asset state; omit the ID at offset 0 for a fresh capture after edits. No silent recapture on expiry. Maximum 512 elements per page, 128 MiB per capture, 4 captures/256 MiB cached, 300 seconds idle lifetime. Includes capture-time build, Nanite, collision and material metadata. dumpToFile streams the complete snapshot in one call to a new JSON file (1 GiB export cap), returning only a receipt; outputPath follows the Saved/ dump convention and existing destinations are refused. Omit paging parameters for export. Params: `assetPath (or path), geometrySource, lodIndex?, elementType?, elementOffset?, pageSize?, snapshotId?, dumpToFile?, outputPath?` |
| `get_mesh_geometry(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, sectionIndex?:i, include?:[s], uvChannel?:i, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?)` | Read actual vertex data off a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh: per-section positions, uvs, normals and triangle indices, from the engine's render data (no ProceduralMeshComponent plugin needed). Triangle indices are section-local, so they index that section's own positions array; add baseVertexIndex for LOD-global indices. Over 20000 vertices inline is refused - pass dumpToFile to write the full data to a JSON file instead, or narrow with sectionIndex (#948/#926/#953). Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, sectionIndex?, include?, uvChannel?, dumpToFile?, outputPath?` |
| `measure_mesh_geometry(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, sectionIndex?:i)` | Measure a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, dimensions, surfaceArea, volume, triangleCount, vertexCount, isClosed, isManifold, boundaryEdgeCount, nonManifoldEdgeCount. surfaceArea and volume are NAMED fields, never a positional pair (the engine's get_mesh_volume_area returns them in the order opposite to its name, #938). Vertices are welded by position before topology analysis so a UV seam does not read as a hole (#938/#953). Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, sectionIndex?` |
| `read_uv_channels(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, channels?:[n], includeIslands?:b, includeOverlap?:b, rasterSize?:n)` | Report every UV channel of a StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, UV area, unit-square coverage, overlap fraction and the triangles involved, island count, degenerate islands, seam edges, out-of-range and flipped triangles, plus which channel LightMapCoordinateIndex points at and the LOD's lightmap build settings. This is the verification half of the UV surface: every other UV action reports the same channel block after it writes, so a change can be checked rather than trusted. Overlap and coverage are RASTERISED at rasterSize rather than tested exactly, and the result says so via overlapMethod. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, channels?, includeIslands?, includeOverlap?, rasterSize?` |
| `set_uv_channel_count(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, op?, channelCount?:n, count?:n, channel?:n, fromChannel?:n, toChannel?:n, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Add, remove, resize or copy a UV channel. Channel count is a mesh-description attribute with no UPROPERTY, so asset(set_property) cannot reach it. Setting the count it already has returns existed=true and skips the rebuild. Growing has an exact inverse and the rollback restores it; remove and copy-over-existing DESTROY coordinates, so those report rollbackRestoresChannelCountOnly rather than pretending the undo is complete. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, op?, channelCount?, count?, channel?, fromChannel?, toChannel?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `unwrap_uvs(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, channel?:n, method?, pack?:b, textureResolution?:n, maxIterations?:n, initialPatchCount?:n, islandSource?, projectionTransform?:o, preserveVertexOrder?:b, backupToChannel?:n, save?:b, dryRun?:b, rasterSize?:n)` | Auto-unwrap and pack islands into one channel via Geometry Script, adding the channel if it does not exist. It converts the LOD to a DynamicMesh and back, so the WHOLE LOD is rewritten rather than only its UVs; the result says so. Pass backupToChannel for a lossless rollback, otherwise only the channel count is restorable. Without the Geometry Script plugin it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable instead of failing opaquely. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, channel?, method?, pack?, textureResolution?, maxIterations?, initialPatchCount?, islandSource?, projectionTransform?, preserveVertexOrder?, backupToChannel?, save?, dryRun?, rasterSize?` |
| `transform_uvs(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, channel?:n, translate?:o, scale?:o, rotate?:n, origin?:o, flipU?:b, flipV?:b, order?, selection?:o, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | One action for every UV transform: the whole channel, chosen islands, triangles facing a direction, or one material slot, plus flips. The filter is the only thing that varies, so the maths lives in one place rather than in four near-identical actions. Edits the mesh description directly, touching nothing but the UV channel, and emits an EXACT inverse as its rollback. A zero scale component is refused because it has no inverse; an identity transform returns existed=true without rebuilding. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, channel?, translate?, scale?, rotate?, origin?, flipU?, flipV?, order?, selection?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `generate_lightmap_uvs(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, enable?:b, sourceChannel?:n, destinationChannel?:n, minLightmapResolution?:n, lightmapResolution?:n, setLightmapCoordinateIndex?:b, force?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b, rasterSize?:n)` | Apply the lightmap build settings AND run UStaticMesh::Build AND read the result back. Deliberately not a setter: bGenerateLightmapUVs, SrcLightmapIndex, DstLightmapIndex and LightMapCoordinateIndex are plain UPROPERTYs that asset(set_property) already writes, and writing them does NOTHING until the mesh rebuilds. That rebuild is the whole point. Returns the channel the build actually produced with its overlap and island report, and fails loudly when the channel did not appear. StaticMesh only. Rollback restores the settings, not the generated coordinates. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, enable?, sourceChannel?, destinationChannel?, minLightmapResolution?, lightmapResolution?, setLightmapCoordinateIndex?, force?, save?, dryRun?, rasterSize?` |
| `export_uv_layout(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, channel?:n, outputPath?, imageSize?:n, showIslands?:b, showOverlaps?:b, showGrid?:b, inline?:b/i)` | Render one UV channel to a PNG under Saved/UVLayouts: white wireframe, one hue per island, red where two triangles share a texel, yellow unit-square border. Returns the file path plus the same channel statistics read_uv_channels reports, so the picture and the numbers describe the same rasterisation. Use it to SEE why a lightmap bake is wrong instead of inferring it from counts. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, channel?, outputPath?, imageSize?, showIslands?, showOverlaps?, showGrid?` |
| `check_uvs(assetPath\|path, lodIndex?:i, requireLightmapChannel?:b, maxOverlapFraction?:n, rasterSize?:n)` | One-call UV health report, the same idiom as measure_mesh_geometry. Flags a missing lightmap channel, a LightMapCoordinateIndex that disagrees with the build's DstLightmapIndex, overlap in the lightmap channel over budget, lightmap UVs outside 0..1, empty or degenerate channels and islands, and flipped triangles, each with a severity and the action that fixes it. Out-of-range UVs OUTSIDE the lightmap channel are reported as info rather than a fault, because tiling is legitimate there. Params: `assetPath (or path), lodIndex?, requireLightmapChannel?, maxOverlapFraction?, rasterSize?` |
| `apply_mesh_simplify(assetPath\|path, simplifyMode?, triangleCount?:i, vertexCount?:i, tolerance?:n, edgeLength?:n, angleThreshold?:n, method?, allowSeamCollapse?:b, preserveVertexPositions?:b, autoCompact?:b, outputPath?, inPlace?:b, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?:b, copyCollisionFromSource?:b, nanite?, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, removeDegenerates?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Reduce a StaticMesh's triangle count while keeping its silhouette, through Geometry Script. Nine strategies because 'simplify' means different things: a target triangleCount or vertexCount, a geometric tolerance (the furthest the surface may drift), an edgeLength, a fast cluster-based edgeLength, a structural collapse of coplanar regions (planar) or of PolyGroup faces (polygroup), and the editor's own reducer (editorTriangleCount, editorVertexCount). NOT reachable through asset(set_property): a StaticMesh's LOD reduction settings build a NEW LOD, they never rewrite LOD 0's source geometry, and no UPROPERTY means 'collapse this mesh to 500 triangles'. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default (outputPath, or '<assetPath>_Simplified'), whose rollback is a complete delete; inPlace=true overwrites the source and reports that its edit has no inverse, with backupPath as the escape. Idempotent: a mesh already at or under the target reports changed=false and is not rewritten. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin, and without it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable. Params: `assetPath (or path), simplifyMode?, triangleCount?, vertexCount?, tolerance?, edgeLength?, angleThreshold?, method?, allowSeamCollapse?, preserveVertexPositions?, autoCompact?, outputPath?, inPlace?, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?, copyCollisionFromSource?, nanite?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, removeDegenerates?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `apply_mesh_remesh(assetPath\|path, remeshMode?, targetType?, targetTriangleCount?:i, targetEdgeLength?:n, smoothingType?, smoothingRate?:n, boundaryConstraint?, iterations?:i, discardAttributes?:b, reprojectToInputMesh?:b, relativeDensity?:n, outputPath?, inPlace?:b, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?:b, copyCollisionFromSource?:b, nanite?, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, removeDegenerates?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Rebuild a StaticMesh's triangulation at a uniform or adaptive density. Different from apply_mesh_simplify: simplify only removes triangles, remesh splits AND collapses AND flips edges to reach an even edge length, which is what a mesh needs before deformation, baking, or a convex decomposition that would otherwise follow the original triangulation's bias. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Remeshed'). Deliberately NOT idempotent and says so in repeatIsIdempotent: remeshing a remeshed mesh keeps moving vertices, so a repeat is a second edit rather than a no-op, which is why the separate-output default matters here more than anywhere else. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin. Params: `assetPath (or path), remeshMode?, targetType?, targetTriangleCount?, targetEdgeLength?, smoothingType?, smoothingRate?, boundaryConstraint?, iterations?, discardAttributes?, reprojectToInputMesh?, relativeDensity?, outputPath?, inPlace?, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?, copyCollisionFromSource?, nanite?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, removeDegenerates?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `apply_mesh_mirror(assetPath\|path, axis?, planeOrigin?:v, planeNormal?:v, applyPlaneCut?:b, flipCutSide?:b, weldAlongPlane?:b, outputPath?, inPlace?:b, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?:b, copyCollisionFromSource?:b, nanite?, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, removeDegenerates?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Reflect a StaticMesh across a plane, optionally cutting away the far side first and welding the seam. This is the 'model half of it and mirror' workflow, and it is real geometry rather than a negative component scale, which inverts the winding and lights wrong; no UPROPERTY on a StaticMesh mirrors its source geometry. Name the plane with axis=x\|y\|z through planeOrigin, or axis=custom with an explicit planeNormal. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Mirrored'). NOT idempotent and says so: mirroring a mirrored mesh doubles it again rather than returning the original. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin. Params: `assetPath (or path), axis?, planeOrigin?, planeNormal?, applyPlaneCut?, flipCutSide?, weldAlongPlane?, outputPath?, inPlace?, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?, copyCollisionFromSource?, nanite?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, removeDegenerates?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `apply_mesh_hole_fill(assetPath\|path, fillMethod?, weldFirst?:b, weldTolerance?:n, removeDegenerateFirst?:b, deleteIsolatedTriangles?:b, outputPath?, inPlace?:b, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?:b, copyCollisionFromSource?:b, nanite?, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, removeDegenerates?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Close every open boundary loop on a StaticMesh so it becomes watertight, which is what a boolean, a voxel operation, a convex decomposition and a physics conversion all require and the most common reason those fail. WELDS FIRST by default: a great many 'holes' are not holes but duplicated vertices along a seam that no fill can close, and running the fill alone on such a mesh reports zero holes filled while the mesh stays open. Genuinely idempotent: a mesh with nothing left to fill reports existed=true and is not rewritten. Reports filledHoles, failedHoleFills, weldedOpenEdges and the before/after open-border-edge counts, so 'watertight now' can be verified rather than assumed. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin. Params: `assetPath (or path), fillMethod?, weldFirst?, weldTolerance?, removeDegenerateFirst?, deleteIsolatedTriangles?, outputPath?, inPlace?, backupPath?, lodType?, lodIndex?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?, copyCollisionFromSource?, nanite?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, removeDegenerates?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `generate_mesh_collision(assetPath\|path, op?, method?, maxConvexHulls?:i, hullTargetFaceCount?:i, maxShapeCount?:i, minThickness?:n, autoDetectSpheres?:b, autoDetectBoxes?:b, autoDetectCapsules?:b, simplifyHulls?:b, removeFullyContainedShapes?:b, decompositionErrorTolerance?:n, decompositionSearchFactor?:n, sweptHullAxis?, markAsCustomized?:b, weldFirst?:b, weldTolerance?:n, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Build simple collision shapes for a StaticMesh from its own geometry, or clear them. Eight solver methods from axis-aligned boxes to a full convex decomposition, plus BoundingBox (one box fitted to the whole mesh). Coincident edges are welded first (weldFirst), so a mesh of unwelded faces fits as one island instead of one shape per face. Writing collision refreshes physics only and never rebuilds render data; the result's renderData reports that the mesh is still drawable and repairs it when it is not. NOT reachable through asset(set_property): UBodySetup AggGeom is a UPROPERTY, but what has to go into it is the OUTPUT of a decomposition solver running over the mesh, and there is no value a caller could supply; the shape count and trace flag stay ordinary property writes and asset(get_mesh_collision) is still the read half. Idempotent: generation from the same mesh with the same options is deterministic, so a repeat reports changed=false without rewriting the asset, compared by a structural signature (shape counts per kind, hull vertex counts, trace flag) rather than byte-for-byte. op='clear' is the remove half and needs no plugin at all. A generation that produces zero shapes is reported as a failure naming apply_mesh_hole_fill, not as a success that quietly left the mesh with no collision. Params: `assetPath (or path), op?, method?, maxConvexHulls?, hullTargetFaceCount?, maxShapeCount?, minThickness?, autoDetectSpheres?, autoDetectBoxes?, autoDetectCapsules?, simplifyHulls?, removeFullyContainedShapes?, decompositionErrorTolerance?, decompositionSearchFactor?, sweptHullAxis?, markAsCustomized?, weldFirst?, weldTolerance?, lodType?, lodIndex?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `apply_mesh_fracture(assetPath\|path, pattern?, axis?, pieces?:i, gridX?:i, gridY?:i, gridZ?:i, planeCount?:i, seed?:i, jitter?:n, gapWidth?:n, fillHoles?:b, minPieceTriangles?:i, outputBasePath?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?:b, nanite?, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | Cut a StaticMesh with planes and write each resulting piece out as its own StaticMesh asset, ready to be placed, simulated or destroyed individually. Three patterns: slice (parallel cuts along one axis), grid (cuts along all three) and random (seeded planes through the bounds). WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not Chaos destruction and produces no UGeometryCollection, because every engine entry point for that carries no UFUNCTION and reflection cannot reach it; the result says so in producesGeometryCollection=false rather than leaving it to be discovered. The source asset is never modified, so the rollback is an exact delete of the pieces it wrote. Seeded, therefore repeatable: onConflict='error' (the default) refuses rather than writing over pieces already there. dryRun lists the cut planes and every path it would write. Params: `assetPath (or path), pattern?, axis?, pieces?, gridX?, gridY?, gridZ?, planeCount?, seed?, jitter?, gapWidth?, fillHoles?, minPieceTriangles?, outputBasePath?, onConflict?, copyMaterialsFromSource?, nanite?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, lodType?, lodIndex?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `audit_hygiene(directory?, directories?:[s], recursive?:b, maxAssets?:i, maxIssues?:i, checks?:[s], classNames?:[s], excludePaths?:[s], keepPaths?:[s], duplicateMethod?, namingRules?:[o], namingRuleMode?, includeWorlds?:b, ignoreRedirectorReferencers?:b)` | One read-only sweep answering the questions a project accumulates answers to and never gets asked: what nothing references (unreferenced), what references nothing (brokenReferences), what exists twice (duplicates), what breaks the naming convention (naming), and what renames left behind (redirectors). asset(get_referencers) and asset(get_dependencies) answer the first two for ONE named package; this is the project-wide form, which is the one an agent needs. The unreferenced section carries a caveat to read before acting on it: an asset loaded by name from an INI setting, from C++ with a hardcoded path, or from a soft reference resolved at runtime has no package dependency and appears there while being very much in use, so treat it as candidates to review rather than a delete list. Maps, World Partition external actors and Asset Manager primary assets are already excluded for that reason. Duplicate detection by content matches class, file size and saved package hash, which finds a file copied verbatim but NOT a copy saved under a different name (the name is inside the file); duplicateMethod='name' is what catches an asset imported twice into two folders. Naming rules match on the asset's class name, so WidgetBlueprint and AnimBlueprint carry their own prefixes rather than inheriting Blueprint's, and the effective table comes back in rulesApplied. Counts are always complete; only the listings are capped by maxIssues. Params: `directory?, directories?, recursive?, maxAssets?, maxIssues?, checks?, classNames?, excludePaths?, keepPaths?, duplicateMethod?, namingRules?, namingRuleMode?, includeWorlds?, ignoreRedirectorReferencers?` |
| `bulk_fix_hygiene(fix, assetPaths?:[s], directory?, directories?:[s], recursive?:b, maxAssets?:i, classNames?:[s], excludePaths?:[s], keepPaths?:[s], namingRules?:[o], namingRuleMode?, unreferencedAction?, quarantineFolder?, ignoreRedirectorReferencers?:b, maxFixes?:i, continueOnError?:b, save?:b, dryRun?:b)` | The batched fix-up for the two audit_hygiene findings a machine can act on without deciding something a person should: a name that breaks the convention (fix='naming') and an asset nothing references (fix='unreferenced'). Same preflight shape as bulk_set_properties: every candidate is validated, every candidate gets a status back including the rejected ones, and a failed preflight aborts before anything is touched unless continueOnError. THREE SAFETY RULES that are not the shape: dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and the dry run names every asset with its exact destination; fix='unreferenced' MOVES assets into quarantineFolder by default rather than deleting them, and that move has an exact inverse this call emits as its rollback; and findings are recomputed here rather than taken from an audit, so an asset that gained a referencer since then is skipped with the referencer named. maxFixes caps the batch far below the audit's scan ceiling. Worlds are refused outright, because moving one without migrating its external-actor packages in the same batch orphans every actor in the level; use asset(rename). fix='redirectors' is refused too and points at asset(fixup_redirectors), which already does it properly. Params: `fix, assetPaths?, directory?, directories?, recursive?, maxAssets?, classNames?, excludePaths?, keepPaths?, namingRules?, namingRuleMode?, unreferencedAction?, quarantineFolder?, ignoreRedirectorReferencers?, maxFixes?, continueOnError?, save?, dryRun?` |
| `mesh_boolean(operation, targetPath, toolPath, outputPath?, inPlace?:b, targetTransform?:o, toolTransform?:o, lodType?, lodIndex?:i, fillHoles?:b, simplifyOutput?:b, simplifyPlanarTolerance?:n, allowEmptyResult?:b, recomputeNormals?:b, recomputeTangents?:b, removeDegenerates?:b, copyCollisionFromTarget?:b, copyMaterialsFromTarget?:b, nanite?, onConflict?, dryRun?:b, save?:b)` | Boolean CSG between two StaticMeshes: union, subtract, intersect, trimInside, trimOutside, newPolyGroupInside, newPolyGroupOutside. The target is the mesh being cut and the tool is what cuts it, each placed by its own optional transform. Writes to a SEPARATE output asset by default (outputPath, or '<targetPath>_<Operation>' when omitted); inPlace=true opts into overwriting the target and is the only destructive form. An existing outputPath is refused unless onConflict='replace'. An empty result is refused and nothing is written unless allowEmptyResult=true, because two meshes that never overlap otherwise report success having deleted everything. Returns triangle and vertex counts for both inputs and the result, plus the written asset's triangles, vertices, LOD count, material slots and bounds, so the operation can be verified rather than trusted. dryRun runs the boolean and reports those counts without writing. Materials and simple collision are copied from the target by default. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin: without it the call returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable, rather than failing opaquely (#916). Params: `operation, targetPath, toolPath, outputPath?, inPlace?, targetTransform?, toolTransform?, lodType?, lodIndex?, fillHoles?, simplifyOutput?, simplifyPlanarTolerance?, allowEmptyResult?, recomputeNormals?, recomputeTangents?, removeDegenerates?, copyCollisionFromTarget?, copyMaterialsFromTarget?, nanite?, onConflict?, dryRun?, save?` |
| `migrate(destinationContentDir, allowDirty?:b, one(assetPaths:[s]; assetPath), dryRun?:b, includeDependencies?:b, onConflict?)` | Copy assets and their dependencies into ANOTHER project's Content directory - the scripted form of the content browser's Migrate (#760). destinationContentDir is the TARGET project's Content folder. While this server drives more than one editor, a 'toEditor' parameter is offered as well: name the destination editor and its Content folder is resolved for you and its asset registry rescanned afterwards, so the assets are visible there without a manual rescan (#817). The call runs in the editor holding the SOURCE assets, so it pushes assets out of the project it is attached to. Unsaved or never-saved assets are refused, because migrate copies files and would otherwise silently omit your edits. Every asset is resolved before anything is copied, and the destination is checked for the packages afterwards rather than reporting success on the call returning. Params: `assetPaths (string[]) or assetPath, toEditor OR destinationContentDir, includeDependencies? (default true), onConflict? (skip\|overwrite, default skip), allowDirty?, dryRun?` |

Refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind, before anything moves, when a package in the folder holds an object the move would leave at the old path (#1137) (#192). Params: `sourcePath, destinationPath` |

A World Partition map's __ExternalActors__ and __ExternalObjects__ packages for the folder go with it and are counted in externalPackagesDeleted; packages still loaded are kept and reported. Per-path status (deleted/absent/failed) with reason (invalid_path/protected_path/not_empty/delete_failed) and a sample of contained assets on not_empty entries. Params: `path?, paths?, force?` |

| `edit_user_defined_struct(assetPath\|path, op, fieldName?, fieldGuid?, newDisplayName?, type?)` | Author a UserDefinedStruct content asset. op=add_field appends a member (pass fieldName for its display name; type accepts scalars, structs, enums, object refs and containers such as struct:/Game/S.S[], TArray<int>, Set<Name>, Map<Name,int>, and a field typeSpec from list_struct_fields round-trips). op=rename_field sets a new newDisplayName on the member resolved by fieldGuid or fieldName - the member GUID is preserved so existing Blueprint pins and DataTable rows survive. op=set_field_type changes a member's type. op=remove_field deletes it. add_field, set_field_type and remove_field recompile every loaded Blueprint whose class holds the struct, reinstancing its live instances, and list them in dependentsRecompiled. Native structs are not editable (#735). Params: `assetPath (or path), op, fieldName?, fieldGuid?, newDisplayName?, type?` |

| `diff(assetPath\|path, otherPath)` | Semantic structural diff between two assets, dispatching on the asset's class. Blueprints: parent class, variables, functions, components, per-graph node and connection deltas. Skeleton and SkeletalMesh: raw bone additions and removals, reparenting (bone, fromParent, toParent), raw-index changes (bone, fromIndex, toIndex), and declared virtual-bone additions and removals, with hierarchyCompatible and editorCompatible reported SEPARATELY. That separation is the point: it answers whether two skeletons are bone-compatible enough to register as Compatible Skeletons or whether a retarget is required, because appending bones (virtual ones especially) leaves the shared hierarchy intact while reparenting an existing bone does not (#879). Deliberately OUT of scope and reported as such: reference-pose transforms (referencePoseCompared=false), export names (exportNamesCompared=false), sockets and retarget sources; structureScope spells the boundary out in the result. Both paths must be the same class. Other asset types report that diffing is not supported yet rather than failing opaquely. Params: `assetPath (or path), otherPath` |

Params: `assetPath, graphName?, format?, focus?, depth?, maxNodes?, outputPath?` |
