| `epic_trace_world(start:o, end:o)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools] Traces a line through the world and returns the distance to the first hit. Params: `start, end` |
| `epic_unload_actors(actors:[o])` | [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Unloads previously loaded World Partition actors from the editor. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `actors` |
| `epic_unload_level_instance(levelInstance:ref)` | [Epic EditorToolset.LevelToolset] Unloads a level instance's level. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `levelInstance` |
| `epic_update_annotation(id, prompt?, group?:i)` | [Epic UnrealCanvasAnnotationsEditor.UnrealCanvasSpatialAnnotationToolset] Changes an existing annotation's prompt and/or colour group. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `id, prompt?, group?` |

---

## material

*Materials: create, read, parameters, shading, textures, and graph authoring (expression nodes, connections).*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `insert_expression_between(materialPath, one(targetExpression; property), targetInput?, expressionType, inputForUpstream?, properties?:o)` | Insert an expression between an existing source and an expression input or material property. Preserves the source output and masks. Named inputs include MakeMaterialAttributes and SetMaterialAttributes. Repeating the same target, type and upstream input reports existed. Returns previousSource, expressionName and rollback restoring the original wire. Dirties the material; save explicitly. Params: `materialPath, targetExpression OR property, targetInput?, expressionType, inputForUpstream?, properties?` |
| `restore_expression_insertion(materialPath, expressionName, insertion:o, previousSource:o)` | Apply an insert_expression_between rollback record: restore the exact previous source and masks and remove the inserted node. Refuses if the target changed or another wire now uses that node. Params: `materialPath, expressionName, insertion, previousSource` |
| `read_summary(materialPath, classes?:[s], parameterNames?:[s], propertyChain?:o)` | Read class counts and only nodes matching classes and parameterNames, with parameter names and groups. Without filters returns counts only. propertyChain traces one material property or named expression input upstream with a depth limit and a 2000 node cap; reports truncation. Read-only. Params: `materialPath, classes?, parameterNames?, propertyChain?` |
| `read(assetPath\|path\|materialPath)` | Read material structure. Accepts a Material or a MaterialInstance; an instance answers with its lineage, shading setup and resolved parameters instead of a graph (#952). Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath)` |
| `list_parameters(assetPath\|path\|materialPath)` | List a material's parameters. On a MaterialInstance each entry carries the resolved value, the parent's defaultValue and whether this instance overrides it (#952). Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath)` |
| `set_parameter(assetPath\|path, parameterName, parameterType?, any(value:*; color\|colour:c; texturePath), association?)` | Set parameter on MaterialInstance. parameterType (scalar\|vector\|texture) is auto-detected when omitted. A vector/colour value may be passed as value OR color, shaped {r,g,b,a}, [r,g,b,a] or '(R=..,G=..,B=..,A=..)'. Saves the instance and returns readBack + saved so a set/verify round trip needs no second call (#952). Params: `assetPath (or path), parameterName, parameterType?, at least one of value/color (or colour)/texturePath, association?` |
| `read_instance(one(assetPath\|path\|materialPath; assetPaths:[s]; actorLabel; actorPath), overridesOnly?:b, componentName?, slotIndex?:i, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Read any MaterialInstance (Constant or Dynamic): parentChain up to the base material, the overrides it holds, and the effective scalar/vector/texture parameter values it renders with (value, parent defaultValue, overridden). To read the material actually on a placed component, including a transient MaterialInstanceDynamic created at runtime, pass actorLabel or actorPath instead of assetPath; world defaults to auto (PIE when running, else editor) (#1114). assetPaths reads several instances in one call into instances[], each with requestedPath, parentChain and its scalar/vector/texture overrides; a path that is not a MaterialInstance fails that row and the call names it. overridesOnly=true leaves out the effective value of every parameter, which keeps a palette read across many instances small (#1183). Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath) OR assetPaths OR actorLabel OR actorPath, overridesOnly?, componentName?, slotIndex?, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `read_mpc(assetPath\|path, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Read a MaterialParameterCollection: every scalar and vector parameter with its stored defaultValue and id. Pass world to also read the live collection instance in that world (liveValue, differsFromDefault), which is what materials sample and what Blueprint writes change (#1116). Params: `assetPath (or path), world?, pieInstance?` |
| `set_instance_parent(assetPath\|path\|materialPath, newParentPath\|parentPath)` | Set a MaterialInstanceConstant parent. Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath), newParentPath (or parentPath)` |
| `batch_set_instances(instances:[o])` | Assign texture, scalar and vector tint/scale parameters to material instances in one batch. Batch reparent + reassign parameters across many Material Instances in one call. Returns per-instance results (#594). Params: `instances` |
| `clear_instance_parameters(assetPath\|path\|materialPath)` | Clear all MaterialInstanceConstant parameter overrides. Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath)` |
| `list_static_switches(assetPath\|path\|materialPath)` | List static switch parameters on a Material or MaterialInstance. Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath)` |
| `set_static_switch(assetPath\|path\|materialPath, parameterName, value:*, association?, parameterIndex?:n)` | Set a MaterialInstanceConstant static switch parameter. value is a boolean. Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath), parameterName, value, association?, parameterIndex?` |
| `set_expression_value(one(materialPath\|path\|assetPath; functionPath\|materialFunctionPath), expressionIndex:n, value?:*, color\|colour?:c, x?:n, y?:n, parameterName?, texturePath?, uTiling?:n, vTiling?:n, coordinateIndex?:i, propertyName?)` | Set a value on an expression node. Common typed knobs: value (constant/param default), texturePath (TextureSample/TextureSampleParameter2D default texture). Constant2Vector/3Vector/4Vector and VectorParameter all take value (or color) as {r,g,b,a}, {x,y,z,w}, [r,g,b,a] or '(R=..,G=..)'; Constant2Vector reads the first two components (#979). Saves the material and reports saved. A TextureCoordinate node takes uTiling, vTiling and coordinateIndex, which are separate top-level keys rather than anything inside `value`. For any OTHER UPROPERTY on the expression (e.g. SamplerType, SamplerSource, Group), pass propertyName + value to hit the generic reflection setter. Reports previousValue and rolls back to it where the previous value can be expressed in this action's own vocabulary. Pass functionPath instead of materialPath to edit a node inside a MaterialFunction (index from list_function_expressions); the function is then updated so every material using it recompiles (#1138, #663). Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath) OR functionPath (or materialFunctionPath), expressionIndex, value?, color? (or colour), x?, y?, parameterName?, texturePath?, uTiling?, vTiling?, coordinateIndex?, propertyName?` |
| `set_custom_expression(one(materialPath\|path\|assetPath; functionPath\|materialFunctionPath), expressionIndex:n, code?, inputs?:[s], outputType?, description?)` | Read/write a MaterialExpressionCustom (HLSL) node: code, named inputs[] (rebuilds input pins; wire them with connect_expressions targetInput=<name>), outputType (float1\|float2\|float3\|float4\|materialAttributes), description. Omit code/inputs to read. Add the node first via add_expression expressionType=Custom, or add_function_expression inside a MaterialFunction (then pass functionPath, #1138) (#617). Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath) OR functionPath (or materialFunctionPath), expressionIndex, code?, inputs?, outputType?, description?` |
| `disconnect_property(materialPath\|assetPath, property)` | Disconnect a material property input. Params: `materialPath (or assetPath), property` |
| `create_instance(parentPath, name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create an instance of a parameterized master material, then assign BaseColor, Normal and packed RMA textures with set_parameter or batch_set_instances. Create material instance. Idempotent by path: an existing instance is reported rather than replaced. Params: `parentPath, name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `create(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create material. Idempotent by path: an existing material is reported rather than replaced. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `create_function(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, description?)` | Create a MaterialFunction asset (#463). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, description?` |
| `add_function_expression(functionPath\|materialFunctionPath, expressionType, positionX?:n, positionY?:n, inputName?, inputType?, outputName?, name?)` | Add an expression node to a MaterialFunction graph. inputName and inputType apply to a FunctionInput, outputName to a FunctionOutput (#463). name labels any node, so connect_function_expressions can address it by that name. Params: `functionPath (or materialFunctionPath), expressionType, positionX?, positionY?, inputName?, inputType?, outputName?, name?` |
| `connect_function_expressions(functionPath\|materialFunctionPath, sourceExpression, sourceOutput?, targetExpression, targetInput?)` | Wire two expressions inside a MaterialFunction; each expression is named or indexed. The result lists sourceOutputs (the source node's output names by index; an empty name is the default output an omitted sourceOutput selects) and connectedOutputName (#463). Params: `functionPath (or materialFunctionPath), sourceExpression, sourceOutput?, targetExpression, targetInput?` |
| `list_function_expressions(functionPath\|materialFunctionPath)` | List expression nodes inside a MaterialFunction (#463). Params: `functionPath (or materialFunctionPath)` |
| `build_material(one(materialPath\|assetPath; name), packagePath?, textures?:o, textureParameters?:b/o, parameters?:[o], nodes?:[o], connections?:[o], propertyConnections?:[o], instances?:[o], samplerTypes?:o, clearExisting?:b, assignToMesh\|meshPath?, meshSlots?:[*])` | Build a PBR material from a texture set in one call: creates a TextureSample per entry, picks each sampler type FROM THE TEXTURE (a virtual/UDIM texture silently loses its material connection on recompile unless it samples through the Virtual* variant), wires them, recompiles, saves, and reports which connections survived the recompile. name (+ packagePath) creates the material; materialPath builds into an existing one. assignToMesh puts the result on a StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh (#946). A parameterized master and its instances in the same call (#1229): textureParameters=true makes the samples TextureSampleParameter2D nodes named after their keys; parameters[] adds scalar/vector/texture parameter nodes {name, type, default?, group?}; nodes/connections/propertyConnections add math nodes exactly as build_graph does, where a connection can name a texture key (orm), a parameter name (Tint) or a node; instances[] creates one MaterialInstanceConstant per piece {name, parameters: {Tint: {r,g,b}, ORM: '/Game/T_Piece_ORM'}, assignToMesh, slotName} and assigns it to that slot. textures is optional when parameters or nodes say what to build. Params: `materialPath (or assetPath) OR name, packagePath?, textures?, textureParameters?, parameters?, nodes?, connections?, propertyConnections?, instances?, samplerTypes?, clearExisting?, assignToMesh? (or meshPath), meshSlots?` |
| `create_simple(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, baseColor?:c, metallic?:n, specular?:n, roughness?:n, emissive?:n, usages?:[s])` | Single-call simple material with optional constants and usages[] (e.g. InstancedStaticMeshes, Nanite, NiagaraSprites). Recompiles + saves in one shot (#225). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, baseColor?, metallic?, specular?, roughness?, emissive?, usages?` |
| `get_usage(assetPath\|path)` | Read the EMaterialUsage flags on a material. `usages[]` carries every flag this engine build defines with its `enabled` state and the bUsedWith* `propertyName` behind it, and `enabled[]` is just the ones that are on. Pass a material INSTANCE and the flags come from the base material it resolves to, which is the shader map it renders through: `materialPath` names that material and `inherited` is true (#1004). Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `set_usage(assetPath\|path\|materialPath, any(usages:[s]; usage))` | Turn on EMaterialUsage flag(s) for a material, then recompile and save. Flag names come from this engine own EMaterialUsage reflection, so every usage the build defines is accepted (VolumetricCloud, Voxels, MeshDeformer and the rest included) and `unknown` names only what it truly could not resolve. This only ever turns flags ON: it routes each one through UMaterial::SetMaterialUsage, which is an ensure rather than a write, so a replay also repairs a material whose bit is set but whose shaders were never built. `applied` names the flags this call turned on and `alreadySet` those that were on already. To CLEAR a flag, write its reflected property with editor(set_property): every usage this action recognises is backed by a bUsedWith* UPROPERTY on the material, and the response returns the exact {objectPath, propertyName, value} arguments per flag under `clearCalls`. Clearing a flag does not discard the shader permutations that were compiled for it (#225). Params: `assetPath (or path, or materialPath), at least one of usages/usage` |
| `set_shading_model(assetPath\|path, shadingModel)` | Set shading model. Params: `assetPath (or path), shadingModel` |
| `set_blend_mode(assetPath\|path, blendMode)` | Set blend mode. Params: `assetPath (or path), blendMode` |
| `set_domain(assetPath\|path, materialDomain\|domain)` | Set material domain. Required for post-process / decal / UI authoring (#299/#356). Params: `assetPath (or path), materialDomain (or domain)` |
| `set_base_color(assetPath\|path, color:c)` | Set base color. Params: `assetPath (or path), color` |
| `connect_texture(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, texturePath, property\|materialProperty?)` | Connect texture to property. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), texturePath, property? (or materialProperty)` |
| `add_expression(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, expressionType, name\|expressionName?, parameterName?, group?, sortPriority?:n, defaultValue?:n/o, value?:*, channels?:o, properties?:o, positionX?:n, positionY?:n)` | Author parameterized master materials with TextureSampleParameter2D (BaseColor, Normal, packed RMA), ScalarParameter, VectorParameter (tint), TextureCoordinate and Multiply nodes. parameterName names texture/scalar/vector parameters; set_expression_value assigns default textures and SamplerType. Add expression node (#318). properties sets any other UPROPERTY on it in the same call, e.g. {ConstB: 12.92} on Divide, {ConstExponent: 2.4} on Power (#1461). Returns expressionIndex, the node's position as set_expression_value and set_custom_expression take it, and expressionName, its unique engine name. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), expressionType, name? (or expressionName), parameterName?, group?, sortPriority?, defaultValue?, value?, channels?, properties?, positionX?, positionY?` |
| `connect_expressions(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, sourceExpression, sourceOutput?, targetExpression, targetInput?)` | Wire two expressions. sourceOutput and targetInput take a pin name or an index; a single-input node such as Sine, ComponentMask or BlackBody takes targetInput Input (or 0), and the graph editor's short labels (UVs, Tex, Exp) are accepted too. An unknown pin fails and lists the node's pins by index. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), sourceExpression, sourceOutput?, targetExpression, targetInput?` |
| `connect_to_property(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, expressionName, outputName?, property)` | Wire expression to material output. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), expressionName, outputName?, property` |
| `list_expressions(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, includeInputs?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List expression nodes, in the material's own stored order, which is what nodeId indexes into. Set includeInputs to include each node's input wiring (default false). Paged with cursor/limit. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), includeInputs?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `read_graph(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, expressionIndex?:n, cursor?, limit?:i)` | Read the stored material expression graph without creating an editor graph. Returns the same paged expressions as list_expressions, with inputs carrying inputIndex, inputName, connectedExpressionIndex, connectedOutputIndex, connectedExpressionClass and connectedExpressionDescription, plus every root material input under connections (expressionIndex, outputIndex, expressionClass, expressionDescription; null when disconnected). MaterialAttributes is listed only when the material uses material attributes. Pass expressionIndex (a nodeId) to read just that node and the source expressions its inputs link to, unpaged. A Custom node's row also carries custom {code, description, outputType, inputNames, additionalOutputs, additionalDefines, includeFilePaths}, so the whole graph, HLSL included, can be checked against source in one read (#1645). Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), expressionIndex?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `delete_expression(one(materialPath\|path\|assetPath; functionPath\|materialFunctionPath), expressionName)` | Remove expression. expressionName matches a description, class, parameter name, FunctionInput/FunctionOutput name, index or engine name. Pass functionPath instead of materialPath to remove it from a MaterialFunction (#1138). Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath) OR functionPath (or materialFunctionPath), expressionName` |
| `list_expression_types(cursor?, limit?:i)` | List available expression types, in the curated order they are grouped in. Paged with cursor/limit. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `recompile(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, recompileChildren?:b)` | Recompile material. Pass recompileChildren=true to cascade to every MaterialInstanceConstant whose parent chain reaches this material (#421). Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), recompileChildren?` |
| `duplicate(sourcePath, destinationPath)` | Duplicate material asset. Params: `sourcePath, destinationPath` |
| `validate(assetPath\|materialPath)` | Validate material graph - find orphans, broken refs. An orphan is a node no material output or custom output node reaches; delete_orphans removes exactly those. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath)` |
| `delete_orphans(assetPath\|materialPath, dryRun?:b)` | Delete every expression no material output or custom output node reaches (the orphans validate reports), then recompile and save. dryRun=true lists them without deleting. Returns orphans[] and deletedCount. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath), dryRun?` |
| `get_shader_stats(assetPath\|materialPath)` | Shader compile stats, sampler+param counts. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath)` |
| `export_graph(assetPath\|materialPath)` | Export material graph as JSON in build_graph's shape: nodes[], connections[] and propertyConnections[], so the result imports back. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath)` |
| `import_graph(assetPath\|materialPath, nodes:[o], connections?:[o], propertyConnections?:[o], removeExpressions?:[s])` | build_graph under another name: adds the nodes, connections and propertyConnections it is given (an export_graph result imports as is). Params: `assetPath (or materialPath), nodes, connections?, propertyConnections?, removeExpressions?` |
| `build_graph(assetPath\|materialPath, nodes:[o], connections?:[o], propertyConnections?:[o], removeExpressions?:[s])` | Add a whole node graph in one call. nodes[]: {name, class, posX?, posY?, parameterName?, group?, defaultValue?, value?, channels?, texturePath?, properties?:{UPROPERTY: value}}; name is yours and becomes the node description. connections[]: {from, fromOutput?, to, toInput?} between node names (or expressions already in the material), pins by name or index; a single-input node such as Sine takes toInput Input. propertyConnections[]: {property, from, output?}. removeExpressions[]: existing expressions to delete once the new nodes are wired, so a Custom node is replaced in one call (#1461). Every class, property and pin is checked first and a failure keeps nothing. Returns nodes[] mapping each name to its expressionName and expressionIndex. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath), nodes, connections?, propertyConnections?, removeExpressions?` |
| `render_preview(assetPath\|materialPath, outputPath, width?:n, height?:n, inline?:b/i)` | Render preview PNG. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `assetPath (or materialPath), outputPath, width?, height?` |
| `begin_transaction(label?)` | Begin undo transaction. Params: `label?` |
| `end_transaction()` | End undo transaction. Params: `none` |
| `create_rvt(name, packagePath?, materialType?, onConflict?)` | Create a RuntimeVirtualTexture asset. materialType is validated against RuntimeVirtualTexture::IsMaterialTypeSupported, which is the reason it is a parameter rather than a follow-up property write: a project can disable individual material types to cut shader permutations, and set_property would happily store one that then compiles to nothing. Everything else (tileCount, tileSize, tileBorderSize, compression, adaptive/private/packed page table, continuous update, LOD group) is a plain UPROPERTY: write it with asset(set_property) at the returned objectPath. Reads back the DERIVED layout - size, pageTableSize, layer count and per-layer pixel format and colour space - which no property read produces. Idempotent by path; rollback deletes the asset. Params: `name, packagePath?, materialType?, onConflict?` |
| `read_rvt(rvtPath\|assetPath)` | Read a RuntimeVirtualTexture and its whole reference graph: the derived layout (size, pageTableSize, per-layer pixel format, sRGB and YCoCg), every volume bound to it with its transform, every primitive and landscape that writes into it, and every material sample node that reads it. problems[] names the failures that otherwise only show up visually - no volume (so no world bounds), no writer (so every page renders empty), a disabled material type, and the classic one: a sample node whose materialType disagrees with the asset, which decodes the wrong channels and still compiles. level(get_runtime_virtual_texture_summary) answers the level-side question; this answers the asset-side one. Params: `rvtPath (or assetPath)` |
| `add_rvt_volume(rvtPath\|assetPath, actorLabel?, boundsMode?, boundsAlignActor?)` | Spawn the RuntimeVirtualTextureVolume that gives an RVT its world bounds, bind the asset through the engine's SetVirtualTexture (which re-registers the render state, unlike a raw property write), and fit the volume to what actually writes into the texture. An unfitted volume sits at the origin at unit scale and renders a 100cm cube of the world, so the fit is the point. Idempotent BY BINDING rather than by label: two volumes on one RVT is a real misconfiguration (one wins, the other renders nothing) and an existing binding is reported rather than duplicated. When nothing writes into the RVT yet there is nothing to fit to, and the response says so in boundsFitNote rather than reporting a fit that did not happen. Rollback deletes the actor. Params: `rvtPath (or assetPath), actorLabel?, boundsMode?, boundsAlignActor?` |
| `set_rvt_volume_bounds(one(rvtPath\|assetPath; actorLabel; actorPath), boundsMode?, boundsAlignActor?)` | Refit an RVT volume to the world, which is the Set Bounds button and is not a property write: it DERIVES a transform from what is in the level. boundsMode='writers' covers every primitive whose RuntimeVirtualTextures array names this RVT; boundsMode='alignActor' matches one actor's box and rotation, which is what a landscape wants because the volume's axes have to be the terrain's axes. The volume's own local extent is read back through CalcBounds and solved against the target box rather than assumed to be a unit cube, so the fit survives engine changes. Honest limitation: it does NOT perform the landscape texel snap (that lives in a module the bridge does not link) and says so when bSnapBoundsToLandscape is set. Rollback restores the previous transform exactly. Params: `rvtPath (or assetPath) OR actorLabel OR actorPath, boundsMode?, boundsAlignActor?` |
| `add_rvt_sampler(materialPath\|assetPath, rvtPath, expressionName?, connectOutputs?:b, positionX?:n, positionY?:n, recompile?:b)` | Add or rebind the RuntimeVirtualTextureSample node that READS an RVT in a material, then call the engine's InitVirtualTextureDependentSettings, which is the one step add_expression + set_expression_value cannot do: it copies the asset's material type and packed/adaptive page-table flags onto the node and rebuilds its output pins. Setting VirtualTexture alone leaves those stale, which compiles cleanly and decodes the wrong channels. Optionally connects each output pin to the material property of the same name and reports the pins that have no counterpart (WorldHeight, Mask, Mask4, Displacement) rather than dropping them silently. Idempotent by expressionName. MipValueMode, TextureAddressMode and bEnableFeedback stay editor(set_property) territory at the returned expressionObjectPath. Params: `materialPath (or assetPath), rvtPath, expressionName?, connectOutputs?, positionX?, positionY?, recompile?` |
| `add_rvt_output(materialPath\|assetPath, expressionName?, mirrorProperties?:b, positionX?:n, positionY?:n, recompile?:b)` | Add the RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput node that makes a material WRITE into an RVT, and mirror the material's existing BaseColor / Normal / Roughness / Specular / Opacity connections into it, which by hand is one connect_expressions call per channel with each source expression and output index looked up by eye. Reads the node's inputs by NAME through the same GetInput/GetInputName pair connect_expressions uses, so a channel added by an engine version is picked up rather than mis-wired. Inputs with no material counterpart are reported with the call that wires them. Idempotent by expressionName. Note this does not choose WHICH RVT: that is the primitive's RuntimeVirtualTextures array (assign_rvt_to_landscape, or editor(set_property) on a mesh component). Params: `materialPath (or assetPath), expressionName?, mirrorProperties?, positionX?, positionY?, recompile?` |
| `assign_rvt_to_landscape(one(actorLabel; actorPath), rvtPaths?:[s], rvtPath?, assignMode?)` | Assign RVTs to a landscape across EVERY proxy that shares its ULandscapeInfo, not just the actor named. A streaming or World Partition landscape is many ALandscapeStreamingProxy actors, and writing RuntimeVirtualTextures on one of them with set_property leaves the rest rendering nothing into the RVT, which is invisible until the pages come back empty. Also calls PostEditChange plus MarkComponentsRenderStateDirty per proxy, without which the change does not take effect, and checks the two things that make an assignment useless anyway: a landscape material with no RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput node, and an RVT whose material type is disabled for the project. assignMode='set' with an empty list clears the assignment. Rollback replays the named landscape's previous list, with previousPerProxy carrying the exact per-proxy state. Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, rvtPaths?, rvtPath?, assignMode?` |
| `create_designer(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create a Material Designer material: a DynamicMaterialInstance asset WITH its Material Designer model, through the plugin's own DynamicMaterialInstanceFactory (asset(create_asset_by_class) leaves the model empty). Seeds a Base Color slot when the new model has none, requests a build and saves. Returns path, modelPath, slotCount and a delete_asset rollback. Needs the Material Designer plugin (#1131). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `read_designer(one(assetPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, slotIndex?:i, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?:n, designerSlot?:n/s, layerIndex?:i, maxDepth?:i)` | Read a Material Designer (DynamicMaterial) model: material settings (domain, blend mode, shading model, flags), materialProperties with their enabled state and designerSlot, and every slot's layer stack. Each layer carries name, bEnabled, MaterialProperty, blendMode, effectStack and its stages (stageType Base or Mask) with sources, inputs, sub-stages, values, texture UVs and text renderers described recursively; every component reports objectPath, componentPath and writableProperties for set_designer_value. Target a Motion Design shape with actorLabel/actorPath (the first material slot holding a DynamicMaterialInstance, or componentName?/slotIndex?/slotName?), or pass assetPath (a DynamicMaterialInstance, a DynamicMaterialModel, or any object inside one). designerSlot and layerIndex narrow the read. Needs the Material Designer plugin (#1131). Params: `assetPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, slotIndex?, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?, designerSlot?, layerIndex?, maxDepth?` |
| `set_designer_value(propertyName, value:*, one(objectPath; componentPath; layerIndex:i; layerName), stage?, assetPath?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, slotIndex?:i, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?:n, designerSlot?:n/s, rebuild?:b)` | Set one property on a Material Designer component (a layer, stage, value, texture UV, text renderer, the editor-only data's settings) by reflection. Uses the component's own setter when it has one (SetValue, SetOffset, SetTiling, SetText, SetEnabled, SetLayerName) so the model updates the way the Material Designer UI does; otherwise writes the property, calls PostEditChangeProperty and Update, and requests a material build. Address the component by objectPath or componentPath (both reported by read_designer), or by designerSlot? + layerIndex/layerName (+ stage? base\|mask\|index); componentPath and the layer forms also need assetPath or actorLabel/actorPath. Returns previousValue and a rollback (#1131). Params: `propertyName, value, objectPath OR componentPath OR layerIndex OR layerName, stage?, assetPath?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, slotIndex?, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?, designerSlot?, rebuild?` |
| `add_designer_layer(one(assetPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, slotIndex?:i, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?:n, designerSlot?:n/s, materialProperty?, layerName?)` | Add a default layer to a Material Designer slot through UDMMaterialSlot::AddDefaultLayer, optionally naming it, then request a material build. Returns the new layer as read_designer describes it; its stages are then set with set_designer_value. designerSlot defaults to the slot mapped to materialProperty (#1131). Params: `assetPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, slotIndex?, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?, designerSlot?, materialProperty?, layerName?` |
| `remove_designer_layer(one(objectPath; assetPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, slotIndex?:i, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?:n, designerSlot?:n/s, layerIndex?:i, layerName?)` | Remove a layer from a Material Designer slot through UDMMaterialSlot::RemoveLayer, after CanRemoveLayer agrees (a slot keeps its base layer). Address it by objectPath, or by layerIndex or layerName in a target's slot. Runs in an editor transaction; the rollback is one editor undo (#1131). Params: `objectPath OR assetPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, slotIndex?, slotName?, world?, pieInstance?, designerSlot?, layerIndex?, layerName?` |
| `diagram(one(assetPath; materialPath), depth?:i, focus?, format?, maxNodes?:i, outputPath?)` | Draw a material's expression graph as a left-to-right flowchart into the material output: parameters marked, every wire labelled with the input it feeds (and the output index when not the first), each root input (BaseColor, Roughness, ...) labelled on its wire into the output node. Node ids are expr:<nodeId>, the index the other material actions take. format: mermaid (default; Mermaid text), svg (an image file drawn by ue-mcp, its path returned), png (the same image rasterised, returned inline as image content and written to a file), json (the normalised nodes and edges). focus: a node title, id or state name to centre on, with depth hops either way (default 3). maxNodes caps the drawing (default 80, max 500); what is cut is named in a note node and in notes. outputPath: where svg, png or mermaid is written (default <Project>/Saved/UE_MCP/Diagrams/). Params: `assetPath (or materialPath), format?, focus?, depth?, maxNodes?, outputPath?` |
| `epic_add_expression(material_or_function:ref, expression_class:ref, x?:i, y?:i)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Adds a new expression node to a Material or MaterialFunction graph. Use list_expression_classes to discover available types. Params: `material_or_function, expression_class, x?, y?` |
| `epic_clear_parameters(instance:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Clears all parameter overrides on a material instance, reverting to parent defaults. Params: `instance` |
| `epic_connect_expressions(from_expression:ref, from_output_name, to_expression:ref, to_input_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Connects an expression node's output pin to another expression node's input pin. Params: `from_expression, from_output_name, to_expression, to_input_name` |
| `epic_connect_to_output(expression:ref, output_name, material_property)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Connects an expression node's output to one of the material's output properties. Params: `expression, output_name, material_property` |
| `epic_create(folder_path, asset_name, parent:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Creates a new MaterialInstanceConstant asset derived from a parent material. Material instances expose the parent's parameters without triggering a full shader recompile when parameter values change. Params: `folder_path, asset_name, parent` |
| `epic_create_function(folder_path, asset_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty MaterialFunction asset. Params: `folder_path, asset_name` |
| `epic_create_material(folder_path, asset_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty Material asset. Warning: Each new Material increases shader compile times. Prefer creating a MaterialInstance from an existing Material where possible. Params: `folder_path, asset_name` |
| `epic_create_parameter_collection(folder_path, asset_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Creates a new empty MaterialParameterCollection (MPC) asset. An MPC holds named Scalar and Vector parameters with default values that materials can reference at runtime without recompiling shaders. Params: `folder_path, asset_name` |
| `epic_delete_expression(material_or_function:ref, expression:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Removes an expression node from a Material or MaterialFunction graph. Params: `material_or_function, expression` |
| `epic_delete_parameter_group(material_or_function:ref, group_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Removes a parameter group, ungrouping all parameters that belong to it. The parameter expressions themselves are not deleted - only their group assignment is cleared. Params: `material_or_function, group_name` |
| `epic_delete_unused_expressions(material:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Deletes all expression nodes not connected to any material output. Useful for cleaning up a material graph after reorganising or after the AI has added experimental nodes that were later abandoned. Params: `material` |
| `epic_diff(oldAssetPath, newAssetPath)` | [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialInstanceToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two MaterialInstanceConstant assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `oldAssetPath, newAssetPath` |
| `epic_diff_function(oldAssetPath, newAssetPath)` | [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two MaterialFunction assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `oldAssetPath, newAssetPath` |
| `epic_diff_material(oldAssetPath, newAssetPath)` | [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns a human-readable text diff between two Material assets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `oldAssetPath, newAssetPath` |
| `epic_disconnect_expressions(to_expression:ref, to_input_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Disconnects the input pin of an expression node, removing whatever is connected to it. Params: `to_expression, to_input_name` |
| `epic_disconnect_from_output(material:ref, material_property)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Disconnects the expression currently connected to a material output property. Params: `material, material_property` |
| `epic_get_expression_input_names(expression:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the names of all input pins on a material expression node. Use these names as to_input_name when calling connect_expressions. Params: `expression` |
| `epic_get_expression_inputs(material_or_function:ref, expression:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the current wiring of each input pin on a material expression. Use after building or modifying a graph to verify the wiring matches expectations. Params: `material_or_function, expression` |
| `epic_get_expression_output_names(expression:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the names of all output pins on a material expression node. Use these names as from_output_name when calling connect_expressions or connect_to_output. The empty string represents the default (first) output of nodes that expose only an unnamed output. Params: `expression` |
| `epic_get_expressions(material_or_function:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns all expression nodes in a Material or MaterialFunction graph. Params: `material_or_function` |
| `epic_get_property_input(material:ref, material_property)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the expression and output pin feeding a material output property. Use to inspect what drives MP_EmissiveColor, MP_Opacity, MP_BaseColor, etc. Params: `material, material_property` |
| `epic_get_referencing_materials(material_function:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns asset data for all Materials that reference this MaterialFunction. Params: `material_function` |
| `epic_get_scalar_parameter(instance:ref, name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the current value of a scalar parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name` |
| `epic_get_static_switch_parameter(instance:ref, name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the value of a static switch parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name` |
| `epic_get_statistics(material:ref)` | [Epic EditorToolset.MaterialToolset] Returns compiled shader statistics for a Material or MaterialInstance on the current shader platform: instruction counts, texture-sample counts, and sampler usage. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `material` |
| `epic_get_texture_parameter(instance:ref, name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the texture assigned to a texture parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name` |
| `epic_get_vector_parameter(instance:ref, name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Gets the current value of a vector parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name` |
| `epic_layout_expressions(material_or_function:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Automatically arranges all expression nodes in a Material or MaterialFunction graph. Params: `material_or_function` |
| `epic_list_expression_classes(material_or_function:ref, search)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns MaterialExpression subclasses valid for the given context. Use the results with add_expression. Pass a search string to filter by name, e.g. 'Multiply' or 'Parameter'. Params: `material_or_function, search` |
| `epic_list_parameter_groups(material_or_function:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Returns the unique parameter group names defined in a Material or MaterialFunction. Parameters are organised into groups in the Material Instance editor. This returns the distinct set of group names found across all parameter expressions in the graph. The empty string represents parameters that have not been assigned to a named group. Params: `material_or_function` |
| `epic_list_parameters(material:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Returns all parameters exposed by a material or instance, with their names and types. Params: `material` |
| `epic_recompile(material_or_function:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Recompiles a Material or MaterialFunction after edits. For Materials, raises if the shader fails to compile. For MaterialFunctions, also recompiles any Materials that reference the function. Call this once after a set of graph modifications is complete - after adding or deleting expressions, making connections, or changing expression properties such as parameter names or default values. Params: `material_or_function` |
| `epic_rename_parameter_group(material_or_function:ref, old_name, new_name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools] Renames a parameter group across all parameter expressions in a Material or MaterialFunction. All parameters currently in old_name will be moved to new_name. If new_name already exists, the parameters are merged into it. Params: `material_or_function, old_name, new_name` |
| `epic_set_parameter_override(instance:ref, name, override:b)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Enables or disables a parameter override on a material instance. Enabling sets the override to the current effective value. Disabling reverts to the parent. For non-static parameter types, disabling also discards the prior override value; re-enabling later restores the parent value, not the prior override. Static switches and static component masks preserve their value across toggle. Params: `instance, name, override` |
| `epic_set_parent(instance:ref, parent:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Changes the parent of a material instance. Params: `instance, parent` |
| `epic_set_scalar_parameter(instance:ref, name, value:n)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a scalar parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name, value` |
| `epic_set_static_switch_parameter(instance:ref, name, value:b)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a static switch parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name, value` |
| `epic_set_texture_parameter(instance:ref, name, value:ref)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Assigns a texture to a texture parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name, value` |
| `epic_set_vector_parameter(instance:ref, name, value:o)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools] Sets the value of a vector parameter on a material instance. Params: `instance, name, value` |

---

## animation

*Animation assets, skeletons, montages, blendspaces, anim blueprints, physics assets.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `read_anim_blueprint(assetPath\|path)` | Read AnimBP structure. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `read_montage(assetPath\|path)` | Read montage: sections, slot tracks and notifies. Each notify and notify state carries objectPath (the placed instance) and properties (its editable reflected properties as export text), so an existing one can be edited in place with editor(set_property, objectPath, propertyName, value). notifyStates lists the windowed notifies the way add_notify_state reports them. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `read_sequence(assetPath\|path?, assetPaths?:[s], directory?, recursive?:b, nameFilter?, fields?:[s], cursor?, limit?:i)` | Read anim sequence: length, rate scale, frames, root motion, curves and notifies. Each notify carries triggerTime and duration in seconds, trackIndex and trackName, and for a notify state its notifyStateClass and endTime. Resolves the same path forms asset(read) does. Batch: pass assetPaths (up to 1000) or directory (with recursive? and nameFilter?, a case-insensitive substring or * ? wildcard on the asset name) instead of assetPath to get one row per sequence in 'sequences', paged (default 50, max 200). A sequence that fails to load is its own row with success false and error; the call still succeeds and reports failedCount. Also reports interpolation (linear\|step), retargetSource (the skeleton's named retarget pose, empty for none) and retargetSourceAsset (the mesh whose pose the clip's bone lengths are retargeted from, empty for none). fields selects the columns (assetPath is always kept); batch rows default to name, sequenceLength, rateScale, numberOfFrames, samplingFrameRate, rootMotionEnabled, notifyCount. Params: `assetPath? (or path), assetPaths?, directory?, recursive?, nameFilter?, fields?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `scan_animation_tracks(directory?, recursive?:b, assetPaths?:[s], skeletonPath?, targetTrackCount?:n, includeTrackNames?:b)` | Scan AnimSequence bone-track counts. Params: `directory?, recursive?, assetPaths?, skeletonPath?, targetTrackCount?, includeTrackNames?` |
| `read_blendspace(assetPath\|path)` | Read blendspace. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `add_blend_sample(assetPath\|path, animation, position?:o, x?:n, y?:n)` | Append a sample to a BlendSpace (#248). Params: `assetPath (or path), animation, position?, x?, y?` |
| `set_blend_sample(assetPath\|path, sampleIndex:i, any(position:o; x:n; y:n; animation; rateScale:n))` | Move an existing BlendSpace sample, swap its animation (#272), or set its per-sample rateScale (#1663). Runs ResampleData and PostEditChange, so the grid is rebuilt; read_blendspace reports each sample's rateScale. Params: `assetPath (or path), sampleIndex, at least one of position/x/y/animation/rateScale` |
| `list(directory?, recursive?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List anim assets (AnimSequence, AnimMontage, AnimBlueprint, BlendSpace). directory scopes the read to one folder and is now honoured; it was advertised and ignored, so a scoped call used to get the whole project back. Params: `directory?, recursive?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `create_montage(name, animSequencePath, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create montage. Params: `name, animSequencePath, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `author_montages_batch(items:[o])` | Batch-author montages in one call: idempotent create, slot name, blend/rate/length properties, sections and notifies, then save. Every item reports success plus the failing stage (validate\|create\|slot\|properties\|sections\|notifies\|save) and error, so one bad item does not hide the rest. Newly created montages come back as a delete_asset_batch rollback. Each montage still holds the single segment create_montage builds. Params: `items` |
| `create_anim_blueprint(name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, parentClass?, onConflict?)` | Create AnimBP. Params: `name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, parentClass?, onConflict?` |
| `create_blendspace(name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, axisHorizontal?, axisVertical?, horizontalMin?:n, horizontalMax?:n, verticalMin?:n, verticalMax?:n, onConflict?)` | Create blendspace (2D). Params: `name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, axisHorizontal?, axisVertical?, horizontalMin?, horizontalMax?, verticalMin?, verticalMax?, onConflict?` |
| `create_blendspace_1d(name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, axisName?, axisMin?:n, axisMax?:n, gridNum?:n, onConflict?)` | Create BlendSpace1D (#459). Params: `name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, axisName?, axisMin?, axisMax?, gridNum?, onConflict?` |
| `populate_blendspace(assetPath\|path, axis?:o, axisIndex?:i, blendspaceAxes?:[o], axisHorizontal?, horizontalMin?:n, horizontalMax?:n, gridNumHorizontal?:i, axisVertical?, verticalMin?:n, verticalMax?:n, gridNumVertical?:i, samples?:[o], clearExisting?:b)` | One-call axis params + samples authoring for BlendSpace 1D/2D. Axis params come from axis (with axisIndex), the per-axis blendspaceAxes list, or the flat create_blendspace keys (#459). Params: `assetPath (or path), axis?, axisIndex?, blendspaceAxes?, axisHorizontal?, horizontalMin?, horizontalMax?, gridNumHorizontal?, axisVertical?, verticalMin?, verticalMax?, gridNumVertical?, samples?, clearExisting?` |
| `add_notify(assetPath\|path, notifyName, triggerTime:n, notifyClass?, notifyProperties?:o, branchingPoint?:b)` | Add notify. For PlayMontageNotify the notifyName is also written onto the spawned notify object so OnPlayMontageNotifyBegin broadcasts it (not 'None'), and montage branching-point markers refresh (#528/#880). On a montage the PlayMontageNotify classes are added as BRANCHING POINT notifies, which is the only tick type UAnimNotify_PlayMontageNotify::BranchingPointNotify runs at, so OnPlayMontageNotifyBegin broadcasts without a montage reload; pass branchingPoint to force it either way, and read branchingPointMarkerCount in the response to see what the montage cached. notifyProperties writes EditAnywhere fields onto the spawned notify object and therefore requires a notifyClass that resolves. Params: `assetPath (or path), notifyName, triggerTime, notifyClass?, notifyProperties?, branchingPoint?` |
| `remove_notify(assetPath\|path, notifyName?, notifyClass?)` | Remove notify(s) by name and/or class (#471). Pass at least one of notifyName/notifyClass; both filters AND. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true if no match. Params: `assetPath (or path), notifyName?, notifyClass?` |
| `get_skeleton_info(assetPath\|path)` | Read a skeleton from a SkeletalMesh or the Skeleton asset itself: bones (name, index, parentIndex), virtualBones (name, sourceBone, targetBone) and slotGroups (name, slots). Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `list_sockets(assetPath\|path)` | List sockets. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `list_skeletal_meshes(directory?, recursive?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List skeletal meshes. directory scopes the read to one folder and is now honoured; it was advertised and ignored, so a scoped call used to get the whole project back. Params: `directory?, recursive?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_physics_asset(assetPath\|path)` | Read physics asset. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `get_physics_asset_constraints(assetPath\|path, boneName?, limit?:i)` | Read every constraint template of a PhysicsAsset: constraintName, bone1 (child) and bone2 (parent); linear x/y/z motion and limit; swing1/swing2/twist motion (Free\|Limited\|Locked) with limit degrees; per-limit soft flag, stiffness and damping; whether the linear and angular drives are enabled; parentDominates and disableCollision; and frame1/frame2, the constraint frame's position and rotation in each body's space. get_physics_asset lists only body bone names and asset(read_properties) shows ConstraintSetup as opaque object paths, so diagnosing a contorted ragdoll used to need Python. Pass the PhysicsAsset path, or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. boneName keeps the constraints touching one bone; limit caps the rows and total still counts every match. Also reports bodyCount, constraintCount and the preview skeletal mesh path. Params: `assetPath (or path), boneName?, limit?` |
| `set_physics_asset_constraint_limits(assetPath\|path, constraintNames?:[s], swing1Motion?, swing2Motion?, twistMotion?, swing1LimitDegrees?:n, swing2LimitDegrees?:n, twistLimitDegrees?:n, swingSoft?:b, twistSoft?:b, constraints?:[o], save?:b)` | Write the angular limits of a PhysicsAsset's constraint templates: swing1/swing2/twist motion (Free\|Limited\|Locked), limit degrees (0 to 180), and whether the cone and twist limits are soft or hard. Shared values go to constraintNames, or every constraint when it is omitted; constraints[] carries per-joint values and is applied after them. A degree value is written only where that axis is Limited, so locked and free axes keep theirs and are listed in skippedLimits. Each template's serialized profile is updated, so the edit survives a save. Unknown names are refused before anything changes. Pass the PhysicsAsset or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. Saves by default (save=false to skip) and returns a rollback that restores every touched constraint. Params: `assetPath (or path), constraintNames?, swing1Motion?, swing2Motion?, twistMotion?, swing1LimitDegrees?, swing2LimitDegrees?, twistLimitDegrees?, swingSoft?, twistSoft?, constraints?, save?` |
| `set_physics_asset_body_material(assetPath\|path, any(physicalMaterialPath; bodies:[o]), boneNames?:[s], save?:b)` | Set the simple-collision PhysicalMaterial of a PhysicsAsset's bodies. physicalMaterialPath goes to boneNames, or every body when it is omitted; bodies[] carries per-bone materials and is applied after it. An empty path clears the override. Unknown bones and a path that is not a PhysicalMaterial are refused before anything changes. Pass the PhysicsAsset or the SkeletalMesh it is assigned to. Saves by default (save=false to skip) and returns a rollback that restores each body's previous material. Params: `assetPath (or path), at least one of physicalMaterialPath/bodies, boneNames?, save?` |
| `create_sequence(name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, numFrames?:n, frameRate?:n, onConflict?)` | Create blank AnimSequence. Params: `name, skeletonPath, packagePath?, numFrames?, frameRate?, onConflict?` |
| `set_bone_keyframes(assetPath\|path, boneName, keyframes:[o])` | Set bone transform keyframes. Params: `assetPath (or path), boneName, keyframes` |
| `bake_keyframes_batch(assetPath\|path, tracks:[o], save?:b)` | Bake per-bone keyframe arrays for many bones into an AnimSequence in one call. Auto-creates each bone track first (set_bone_keyframes silently leaves a T-pose if the track is missing), wraps the batch in one transaction, and raises if any bone fails instead of reporting hollow success (#540). Params: `assetPath (or path), tracks, save?` |
| `reverse_sequence(sourcePath, destinationPath?, name?, packagePath?, inPlace?:b, cycleOffsetFrames?:i, cycleOffsetSeconds?:n, onConflict?)` | Create a time-reversed copy of an AnimSequence, or reverse it in place with inPlace=true. Bone tracks are rewritten through the animation data controller, float and transform curves are mirrored with their tangents, notifies move to length - time (a notify state to length - time - duration) and sync markers mirror the same way. A blendspace sample with RateScale -1 is not a substitute: it freezes under the non-legacy sample length calculation. cycleOffsetFrames or cycleOffsetSeconds (rounded to whole frames) then rotates the reversed loop so it starts that far in; the last key is rewritten to repeat the new first key. The destination is destinationPath, or name (default <Source>_Reversed) in packagePath (default the source's folder). onConflict=skip (default) returns an existing destination untouched, error refuses; it never overwrites. Returns path, numFrames, numKeys, frameRate, the applied cycle offset, reversed counts {boneTracks, floatCurves, transformCurves, notifies, notifyStates, syncMarkers}, and a delete_asset rollback, or for inPlace a reverse_sequence replay that restores it (#1162). Params: `sourcePath, destinationPath?, name?, packagePath?, inPlace?, cycleOffsetFrames?, cycleOffsetSeconds?, onConflict?` |
| `get_bone_transforms(skeletonPath\|assetPath\|path, boneNames?:[s], space?)` | Read reference pose transforms for one, many, or ALL bones. Omit boneNames to return every bone with index/parentIndex/location/rotation/scale; rotation is a quaternion {x,y,z,w}. With boneNames, returns only the named bones (#245). space=component composes the parent chain. A SkeletalMesh path reads the mesh's own bind pose, a Skeleton path the Skeleton's; poseSource and poseSourcePath say which was read (#1451). Params: `skeletonPath (or assetPath, or path), boneNames?, space?` |
| `inspect_anim_nodes(assetPath\|path, graphName?, nodeClass?)` | Deep-dump the FAnimNode_* struct of anim graph nodes (PoseDriver PoseTargets/PoseAsset/RBF params/source bones, etc.) that read_anim_graph omits because it skips the 'Node' property (#657). Params: `assetPath (or path), graphName?, nodeClass?` |
| `compare_curves_to_morph_targets(animPath\|assetPath, skeletalMeshPath\|meshPath)` | Compare an AnimSequence/PoseAsset's curve names against a SkeletalMesh's morph target names. Returns curves[], morphTargets[], matched[], curvesWithoutMorph[], morphsWithoutCurve[] - verify authored curves drive morphs without Python (#656). Params: `animPath (or assetPath), skeletalMeshPath (or meshPath)` |
| `set_montage_sequence(assetPath\|path, animSequencePath, slotIndex?:n, segmentIndex?:n)` | Replace the animation sequence in a montage slot. With segmentIndex, replaces only that one segment; without it, replaces every segment in the slot (#626). Params: `assetPath (or path), animSequencePath, slotIndex?, segmentIndex?` |
| `set_montage_properties(assetPath\|path, sequenceLength?:n, rateScale?:n, blendIn?:n, blendOut?:n)` | Set montage properties. Params: `assetPath (or path), sequenceLength?, rateScale?, blendIn?, blendOut?` |
| `create_state_machine(assetPath\|path, name?, graphName?)` | Create state machine in AnimBP. Params: `assetPath (or path), name?, graphName?` |
| `add_state(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, stateName, onConflict?)` | Add state to a state machine. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, stateName, onConflict?` |
| `add_transition(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, fromState, toState, blendDuration?:n, blendLogic?)` | Add directed transition between states. blendDuration and blendLogic are applied to the new transition as set_transition_blend applies them, and the result echoes the effective blendDuration and blendLogic. An existing transition is returned unchanged, with a warning when the requested blend differs. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, fromState, toState, blendDuration?, blendLogic?` |
| `set_state_animation(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, stateName, animAssetPath)` | Assign anim asset to state. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, stateName, animAssetPath` |
| `set_transition_blend(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, fromState, toState, blendDuration?:n, blendLogic?)` | Set blend type/duration on transition. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, fromState, toState, blendDuration?, blendLogic?` |
| `set_transition_condition(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, variableName, transitionGuid?, fromState?, toState?, negate?:b)` | Set a transition's 'can enter transition' condition from a bool variable, keyed by transition (not graph name - every rule graph is named 'Transition' so blueprint graph tools can only reach the first). Wires VariableGet(bool) -> bCanEnterTransition, replacing any prior condition. Identify the transition by transitionGuid (from add_transition/read_state_machine) OR fromState+toState (#707). Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, variableName, transitionGuid?, fromState?, toState?, negate?` |
| `read_state_machine(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName)` | Read state machine topology. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName` |
| `set_state_machine_entry(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName, stateName?)` | Point the state machine's ENTRY node at a state, which is the only thing that gives a machine an initial state. create_state_machine and add_state never wired it, so a machine authored through the bridge compiled with no entry and produced the reference pose at runtime. There is no property behind this: it is the pin link from UAnimationStateMachineGraph::EntryNode to the state's input pin. An omitted or empty stateName clears the link instead, so set and clear are one pair. Reports previousEntryState, and unchanged=true on a replay. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName, stateName` |

Address it by transitionGuid (from add_transition or read_state_machine) or by fromState plus toState, which can match several and removes all of them. | `remove_state_machine(assetPath\|path, stateMachineName)` | Remove a state machine node and everything inside it: its states, its transitions, each of their bound graphs, and the machine's own graph. Leaving a bound graph behind after its node is gone is what makes the next compile assert, so the teardown is explicit rather than left to the node. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the machine is not there. Params: `assetPath (or path), stateMachineName` |

Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when there is no such curve, and the miss lists the curves that do exist. Params: `assetPath (or path), curveName` |

Registers the modifier on the sequence so it re-applies on reimport. props sets the modifier's EditAnywhere fields (e.g. DistanceCurveModifier: {CurveName, Axis:'XY'\|'X'\|..., bStopAtEnd, StopSpeedThreshold, SampleRate}). | `list_montage_segments(assetPath\|path, slotName?)` | List every slot's segments on a montage so a caller can address them by index: animation path, startPos/endPos trim, playRate, loopCount, track position and length per segment, plus the sections with the slot and segment each one links to (#826). Baseline first: before this call, reuse or create a Control Rig for the target character, bind/import the exact target skeleton, add the intended controls, author Forward Solve, add Backward/Inverse Solve, verify it with read_control_rig_hierarchy/read_control_rig_graph, and pass an unchanged source round-trip. For a new baseline, the Unreal 5.8 ControlRig toolset (wrapped on this category, or through epic(call_tool)) creates the rig, imports the skeleton bones, adds controls and adds a backward solve graph; a newly created rig alone is not usable. There is no silent fallback to raw bone-key authoring. rigMode='fk' uses UFKControlRig only when generated FK controls are sufficient; rigMode='asset' requires the verified controlRigPath and rejects rigs without inverse execution. bindingTag is the stable natural key for replay. onConflict is skip\|error (default error); existing sessions are never modified. layered defaults false. startFrame is inclusive and endFrame is exclusive. Returns the resolved bindingTag/binding GUID, rig, frame range, controls and created/existed status. Read transform, bool, float/scale-float, and integer/enum controls from a Control Rig editing session without changing editor state; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no silent fallback. Scalar samples return value instead of transform. Control metadata includes native controlType, animatable, and enum path/options where applicable. Returns session identity, layered mode, range/rate, filtered control metadata, and requested frame samples. Params: `sequencePath, bindingTag, controlNames?, frame?, frames?, space?` |

Capture current live local UControlRig values without opening, scrubbing, refreshing, or evaluating Sequencer; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no silent fallback. The addressed LevelSequence must already be focused. Omit controlNames to capture the current Control Rig selection. Returns an immutable captureVersion=1 snapshot with sequence, binding, track, section, rig-object, current-frame, selection, control-type, and typed-value identity for later propagate_pose validation. Params: `sequencePath, bindingTag, controlNames?` |
| `apply_control_rig_edits(sequencePath, bindingTag, operations:[o<op>])` | UE 5.8+. Apply typed Control Rig edits in one transaction; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines. There is no silent fallback to raw bone tracks. set_keys writes strictly ordered full per-frame transforms from normalized quaternions and preserves shortest-arc quaternion continuity. A set operation writes one full absolute transform at frame or frames. An offset operation applies translation/rotation/scale deltas across an inclusive frame range with optional edge blends. propagate_pose validates caller-held baseline and accepted live snapshots from the same session, exact rig instance, frame, and complete control set, then keys only controls whose values changed across each control's explicit original donorFrames. Snapshot selection is provenance metadata; the explicit propagation controls are authoritative. mode='fixed' copies the accepted changed channels; mode='local_delta' preserves donor motion while applying the captured local delta. Bool, enum, and int controls support fixed only. contact_lock densely constrains a translatable driver control, or an optional driven bone/socket reference, to a fixed component-space target with smooth edge blends and optional pole/control stabilization. Driver and stabilizer keys are read back transactionally. A drivenReference or targetReference contact returns verification='bake_and_analyze_required' without passed=true; bake it and analyze every constrained frame before accepting the bone/socket result. set_bool, set_float, and set_int key matching scalar controls; enum controls use set_int with one of the integer values reported in enumOptions. Sequencer's current interpolation mode is retained. Operations are keyed in order, each sampled after the ones before it land, so batched control offsets compose like separate calls: a component-space offset on a child adds to an earlier offset on its parent. Contacts using targetReference, or drivenReference without the FK rotation-chain solver, require a fresh session without earlier rig edits because those references sample the source animation; bake prior edits and begin a new session first. They must also be first in the batch, otherwise contact_lock_reference_batch_unsupported refuses it. Final readback checks stored control/driver poses; it does not re-evaluate target-reference motion after later edits. Driven contacts also check their final FK end-control or asset-driver pose before saving; bone/socket results still require bake and analysis. Returns per-operation counts, affected controls/frames and changedChannels; a failed key/readback batch is undone. Params: `sequencePath, bindingTag, operations` |
| `bake_control_rig_edit(sequencePath, bindingTag, outputAssetPath, frameRate?:n, reduceKeys?:=false, tolerance?:n, createLink?:=false, onConflict?, setRetargetSourceAsset?:b, interpolation?:{linear,step}, curveInterpolation?:{linear,constant,cubic}, recordInWorldSpace?:b, evaluateAllSkeletalMeshComponents?:b, exportTransforms?:b, exportMorphTargets?:b, exportAttributeCurves?:b, exportMaterialCurves?:b, skipCurvesWithZeroValue?:b, includeAnimationNames?:[s], excludeAnimationNames?:[s], removeExcludedCurves?:b, warmUpFrames?:i(0..100000), delayBeforeStart?:i(0..100000), bakeTimecode?:b, timecodeRate?:n, startFrame?:i, endFrame?:i)` | UE 5.8+. Bake the evaluated Control Rig session to a new AnimSequence asset; native returns unsupported_engine_version on older engines and has no raw-track fallback. The source LevelSequence remains unchanged. outputAssetPath is the output natural key; onConflict is skip\|error (default error), never overwrite. Key reduction and Sequencer links are not supported yet, so reduceKeys/createLink must be false or omitted. The output names the bound mesh as its retarget source asset unless setRetargetSourceAsset=false, so a mesh whose proportions differ from the skeleton's reference pose is not retargeted twice on playback. interpolation defaults to the session source clip's, so a Step clip bakes as Step. Takes the rest of the Sequencer bake options (curves, world space, include/exclude names, warm-up, delay, timecode, custom startFrame/endFrame). Returns output asset metadata, frame/rate counts, retargetSourceAsset, interpolation, status, and delete-created-asset rollback. Params: `sequencePath, bindingTag, outputAssetPath, frameRate?, reduceKeys?, tolerance?, createLink?, onConflict?, setRetargetSourceAsset?, interpolation?, curveInterpolation?, recordInWorldSpace?, evaluateAllSkeletalMeshComponents?, exportTransforms?, exportMorphTargets?, exportAttributeCurves?, exportMaterialCurves?, skipCurvesWithZeroValue?, includeAnimationNames?, excludeAnimationNames?, removeExcludedCurves?, warmUpFrames?, delayBeforeStart?, bakeTimecode?, timecodeRate?, startFrame?, endFrame?` |

Bake one skeletal mesh binding of any LevelSequence to a new AnimSequence with the full set of Sequencer bake options, which the engine's own anim sequence export tool does not take. Pick the binding with exactly one of bindingTag, bindingGuid or bindingName. setRetargetSourceAsset defaults true: the output names the bound mesh as its retarget source asset, so its recorded bone lengths are not retargeted again on playback. interpolation is linear\|step (default linear). The LevelSequence is never modified; onConflict is skip\|error (default error), never overwrite. Returns output asset metadata, frame/rate counts, retargetSourceAsset, interpolation and delete-created-asset rollback. Samples an AnimSequence and reports deterministic numeric motion diagnostics without Python or viewport inference. Returns source/rate/range metadata, sampled local/component transforms, root-motion and continuity metrics, and any written analysis artifacts. facingBones samples the component-space vector from boneA to boneB at every sampled frame, rotates it into the root bone's frame, and reports its yaw per sample (facingYawDegrees; 0 is root +X, 90 is root +Y) and over the clip in summary.facing: averageYawDegrees (circular mean), minYawDegrees, maxYawDegrees, spreadDegrees, resultantLength and degenerateSampleCount for samples where the vector is vertical. Configure an existing IK Retargeter through UIKRetargeterController with the correct default-op and per-op rig assignment order, auto/manual chain mappings, named pose authoring, processor validation, native readback, transaction rollback, and checked save; older engines return unsupported_engine_version. With easeToSource the keys ease from that composed pose at frame 0 to the named source's pose at the last frame (linear or smooth); otherwise every key holds the composed pose. Every sequence, bone and donor is validated before anything is written. Each row reports frame 0 of every written track before and after as quaternions. Params: `assetPaths, trackOps, save?` |

Otherwise the action refuses to repurpose it. If either save fails, it restores and saves the mesh's previous skeleton reference, then deletes the new skeleton when safe; an incomplete cleanup returns a machine-readable recovery descriptor. | `epic_create_condition_endpoint(sequence:ref, conditionHost:ref, functionName, rowIndex?:i)` | [Epic AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset] Create a Director Blueprint Condition function endpoint on the sequence's Director Blueprint and bind it to a director-blueprint condition on the given host (a section, a whole track, or a single track row), so the host only evaluates at runtime when the function returns true. If the host has no condition, a Director Blueprint Condition is created on it; if it already has one, that condition is reused. A host carrying a different condition type (e.g. a platform or group condition) is rejected - clear it first via MovieSceneConditionExtensions.ClearSectionCondition or ClearTrackCondition. Generates a function graph named after FunctionName whose entry node takes an FMovieSceneConditionContext and returns a bool. The body is left empty by design - author it via BlueprintToolset, then call BlueprintToolset.CompileBlueprint on the Director BP so the condition's CompiledFunctionName is populated; without that the condition is skipped at runtime. The returned UK2Node_FunctionEntry is the new function's entry node. Scope, CheckFrequency, bEditorForceTrue and payload variables are EditAnywhere on the condition; set them via set_editor_property on the condition UObject, obtained from the native accessor (e.g. section.get_section_condition()). Retrieve the condition object before editing its properties; a class-path string is not an object reference. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `sequence, conditionHost, functionName, rowIndex?` |

| `epic_create_dynamic_binding_resolver(sequence:ref, binding:o, functionName)` | [Epic AnimationAssistantToolset.SequencerDirectorToolset] Create a dynamic-binding resolver function endpoint on the sequence's Director Blueprint and wire it to the binding's FMovieSceneDynamicBinding so the binding is resolved at runtime by the generated function. Generates a function graph named after FunctionName whose entry node returns a FMovieSceneDynamicBindingResolveResult. The function body is left empty by design - callers author it via BlueprintToolset (e.g. drop a "GetPlayerPawn" node, connect its return to the entry's Object pin via a MakeStruct FMovieSceneDynamicBindingResolveResult). The returned UK2Node_FunctionEntry is the entry-point node of the new function graph; pass it by name lookup to BlueprintToolset calls that take node references. | `epic_replace_control_rig(inControlRigTrack:ref, newControlRig:ref)` | [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Replace the Control Rig on the track with a new Control Rig. Note it will now be owned by the track. When the track's sequence is focused in Sequencer, a rig with no bound object is bound to the track's skeletal mesh and initialized, and the new rig replaces the old one in Sequencer and Animation Mode, so setting its values keys it. The new rig is constructed with the track's settings and rotation order overrides, and the controls selected on the old rig are selected on it. One undoable step. Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the rig is already on it or on another track, one is layered and the other is not, or the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig's asset (as in UEFN). ReplaceControlRigFromReference creates the new rig from a Control Rig class or asset. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `inControlRigTrack, newControlRig` |
| `epic_replace_control_rig_from_reference(inTrack:ref, inRef:o)` | [Epic ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary] Replace the Control Rig on a Control Rig track with a new rig created from a Control Rig class or asset, as FindOrCreateControlRigTrackFromReference creates one. Keys on controls the new rig also has are kept, a layered track stays layered, an FK rig keeps the old FK rig's apply mode, and the track is renamed after the new rig when it comes from a different class or asset. The new rig is constructed with the track's settings and rotation order overrides, and the controls selected on the old rig are selected on it. When the track's sequence is focused in Sequencer, the new rig is bound to the track's skeletal mesh and replaces the old one in Sequencer and Animation Mode, so it can be read and keyed at once. One undoable step. Raises a script error if the track is not a writable Control Rig track, the reference is not a Control Rig class or asset, the track is layered and the new rig is not an FK rig and has no backwards solve event, or the editor's asset reference filter refuses a reference from the track's sequence to the rig (as in UEFN). With bKeepOrientation the actors orbit the pivot and keep their rotation and scale, as Shift does in the tool. Keys the actors in one undoable step. An actor that cannot be keyed (not bound in the sequence, or its Transform track has no Absolute section) is skipped and the reason is logged as an error. Raises when the sequence is not focused or is read-only, Actors or Frames is empty, an actor is null, or no actor can be keyed; nothing is keyed then. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. At every frame a control's new world transform is World * Pivot^-1 * Delta * Pivot: Delta is applied in the pivot's space, so a 90 degree yaw turns the controls about the pivot's up axis. Controls are keyed with SetControlRigWorldTransforms, so constraints and spaces are compensated. Raises a script error if the sequence is not focused, a control does not exist, Frames is empty, or PivotObject names more than one object. Every control is checked for being driven by the rig at the first frame before any is keyed; if keying still fails partway, the controls keyed before the failure stay keyed, in the call's single transaction, so one undo reverts the whole call. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `levelSequence, controlRig, controlNames, frames, delta, pivotObject, pivotTransform, timeUnit?` |
