---

## landscape

*Landscape terrain: info, layers, sculpting, weight painting, materials, splines, proxies.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `get_info()` | Get landscape setup. Params: `none` |
| `list_layers()` | List paint layers. Params: `none` |
| `sample(x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?, layerName?, includeLayers?:b)` | Read the surface height AND every paint-layer weight at one world XY. Height and weights come from the landscape's own height and weight data (the merged result of every edit layer), the same data landscape(paint_layer) writes, so they are exact and do not depend on built collision. Layers come back with weight (0..1), weight255 (the weightmap byte the editor shows), the LayerInfo path and its physical material, plus dominantLayer and totalWeight - which is what makes reading a paint weight one call instead of rendering the weightmap to a render target and reading that back. Also returns quad, quadExtent and inBounds, so a zero weight OFF the landscape reads as out of bounds rather than as a measured zero, and traceHeight/normal from a confirmation collision trace (absent when collision is unbuilt or the proxy is streamed out). Position accepts x + y, point {x, y}, or worldX + worldY (#939). Params: `x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, layerName?, includeLayers?` |
| `sculpt(center:o, radius?:n, mode?, amount?:n, falloff?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, maxVertices?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Raise, lower or flatten terrain with a circular brush. mode=raise\|lower\|flatten; amount is world centimetres at full strength (raise/lower), and flatten pulls toward the height under the brush centre. falloff (0..1) is the smoothstepped soft edge. Runs in one transaction and leaves the level dirty and unsaved. Writes into an edit layer (editLayer by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0) - required on UE 5.8, where a write without one is regenerated away by the layer system. Idempotent: a brush that rounds to the height already there reports unchanged=true and updated=false rather than claiming it moved ground. The rollback record carries the exact previous heights over the brush rectangle and replays through set_height_region; above rollbackMaxVertices the response says rollbackOmitted with the reason instead of a record that would restore part of the footprint (#742). Params: `center, radius?, mode?, amount?, falloff?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, maxVertices?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `paint_layer(layerName, center:o, radius?:n, strength?:n, falloff?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, maxVertices?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Paint a weight layer with a circular brush. The layer must already have a LayerInfo on this landscape (see add_layer_info) - an unregistered name errors and lists the layers that ARE registered instead of silently painting nothing. Weights are written as given - the engine no longer renormalises other layers for you, so set them explicitly if they must sum to 1. Writes into an edit layer (editLayer by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0). Idempotent: a brush that changes no weight reports unchanged=true. The rollback record carries the exact previous weights over the brush rectangle and replays through set_layer_weight_region, with the same rollbackOmitted cap as the region writes (#742). Params: `layerName, center, radius?, strength?, falloff?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, maxVertices?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `list_edit_layers(actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | List the landscape's edit layers by name, in stack order, with guid, visible, locked, heightmapAlpha and weightmapAlpha. These names are what sculpt, paint_layer and the region writes take as editLayer (#1156). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `merge_edit_layers(actorLabel?, actorPath?, updateNow?:b)` | Re-merge every edit layer into the landscape's final height and weight maps (ALandscape::ForceLayersFullUpdate), then run the update immediately unless updateNow=false. Use after edits that leave the merged result stale. Changes no authored value, so there is no rollback (#1156). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, updateNow?` |
| `list_splines()` | Read every landscape spline network: controlPoints (name, path, location and rotation in world space, halfWidth, sideFalloff, endFalloff, layerName, raiseTerrain, lowerTerrain, connectedSegments, and the owner actor) and segments (start and end points, tangent lengths, layer, raise/lower flags, meshes, meshComponentCount, length). Covers splines on landscape actors and proxies and on World Partition LandscapeSplineActors. x/y/z on a point are its location in spline space, as before. Params: `none` |
| `create_spline_point(location:v, rotation?:r, halfWidth?:n, sideFalloff?:n, endFalloff?:n, layerName?, raiseTerrain?:b, lowerTerrain?:b, name?, ownerPath?, newSplineActor?:b, onConflict?, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Add a landscape spline control point at a world location, with optional rotation, halfWidth, sideFalloff, endFalloff, paint layerName and raiseTerrain/lowerTerrain. On a single landscape it goes into the landscape's own splines component; on a World Partition map it goes into a new LandscapeSplineActor, as the Landscape Mode spline tool does, unless ownerPath names an existing owner. Pass ownerPath (returned as ownerPath) to keep later points in the same network, since a segment only joins points of one owner. name makes the create idempotent. Rolls back through delete_spline_point. Params: `location, rotation?, halfWidth?, sideFalloff?, endFalloff?, layerName?, raiseTerrain?, lowerTerrain?, name?, ownerPath?, newSplineActor?, onConflict?, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `update_spline_point(controlPoint, location?:v, rotation?:r, halfWidth?:n, sideFalloff?:n, endFalloff?:n, layerName?, raiseTerrain?:b, lowerTerrain?:b, autoRotate?:b)` | Move a landscape spline control point or change its rotation, halfWidth, falloffs, paint layer or raise/lower flags. Moving a connected point recomputes its rotation from its segments unless rotation is passed or autoRotate is false. Reports unchanged when nothing moved, and the rollback restores every previous value. Params: `controlPoint, location?, rotation?, halfWidth?, sideFalloff?, endFalloff?, layerName?, raiseTerrain?, lowerTerrain?, autoRotate?` |
| `delete_spline_point(controlPoint)` | Delete a landscape spline control point and every segment connected to it. Idempotent: a point that is not there reports alreadyDeleted. A point with no segments rolls back through create_spline_point with its name and settings; one with segments says why it has no rollback. Params: `controlPoint` |
| `connect_spline_points(startPoint, endPoint, startTangentLength?:n, endTangentLength?:n, layerName?, raiseTerrain?:b, lowerTerrain?:b, meshes?:[o], collisionProfile?, castShadow?:b, autoRotate?:b, name?)` | Join two control points of the same spline owner with a segment. Tangent lengths default to the distance between the points; layerName, raiseTerrain, lowerTerrain, meshes, collisionProfile and castShadow set the segment in the same call. Points already joined report existed. Rolls back through delete_spline_segment. Params: `startPoint, endPoint, startTangentLength?, endTangentLength?, layerName?, raiseTerrain?, lowerTerrain?, meshes?, collisionProfile?, castShadow?, autoRotate?, name?` |
| `update_spline_segment(segment, startTangentLength?:n, endTangentLength?:n, layerName?, raiseTerrain?:b, lowerTerrain?:b)` | Change a landscape spline segment's tangent lengths, paint layer or raise/lower flags. Reports unchanged when nothing changed; the rollback restores the previous values. Params: `segment, startTangentLength?, endTangentLength?, layerName?, raiseTerrain?, lowerTerrain?` |
| `set_spline_segment_meshes(segment, meshes?:[o], collisionProfile?, castShadow?:b)` | Set the meshes a landscape spline segment deforms along itself (mesh, scale, forwardAxis, upAxis, materialOverrides, centerH, scaleToWidth per entry), its collisionProfile and castShadow. meshes replaces the whole list, and an empty list clears it. Returns meshComponentCount, the spline mesh components the segment built. The rollback restores the previous list. Params: `segment, meshes?, collisionProfile?, castShadow?` |
| `delete_spline_segment(segment)` | Delete one landscape spline segment; its control points stay. Idempotent. Rolls back through connect_spline_points with the segment's tangents, layer, flags and meshes. Params: `segment` |
| `apply_splines(actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, updateNow?:b)` | Apply the landscape's splines to its terrain: raise and lower the heights under each segment and paint each segment's layer. A landscape with a reserved splines edit layer is written there, regenerated from the splines each time; otherwise the deformation goes into editLayer (by name, else editLayerIndex, default 0) and stays when the splines change. The edit layers merge now unless updateNow is false; read the result back with get_height_at_point after merge_edit_layers, since the merge finishes on the GPU. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, updateNow?` |
| `get_component(componentIndex?:i)` | Inspect component. Params: `componentIndex?` |
| `set_material(materialPath\|path\|assetPath, landscapeName?)` | Set landscape material. Params: `materialPath (or path, or assetPath), landscapeName?` |
| `add_layer_info(layerName, landscapeName?, packagePath?)` | Register paint layer (creates LayerInfo asset + binds to active landscape). Idempotent: a layer already registered reports existed and emits no record, so a replay cannot delete a layer it did not create. Rolls back through remove_layer on the parent Landscape actor, which un-registers the layer; marked lossy when the LayerInfo ASSET was created here, because remove_layer deliberately leaves it on disk. Params: `layerName, landscapeName?, packagePath?` |
| `create_layer_info(layerName, name?, packagePath?, onConflict?, physMaterial?, hardness?:n)` | Standalone LayerInfo asset creation - no landscape required (#251). Params: `layerName, name?, packagePath?, onConflict?, physMaterial?, hardness?` |
| `create(location?:v, scale?:v, componentCountX?:i, componentCountY?:i, subsectionSizeQuads?:i, numSubsections?:i, heightOffset?:i, label?)` | Spawn a new ALandscape with a flat heightmap. Defaults match the Editor's Landscape Mode 'create new' (8x8 components, 63 quads/subsection, 2 subsections/component = 1016x1016 quads) (#303). Params: `location?, scale?, componentCountX?, componentCountY?, subsectionSizeQuads?, numSubsections?, heightOffset?, label?` |
| `get_material_usage_summary()` | Per-proxy summary: landscape/hole material paths + component/grass/nanite counts (#150). Params: `none` |
| `list_proxies(cursor?, limit?:i)` | Enumerate loaded World Partition LandscapeStreamingProxy actors with per-proxy objectPath and worldBounds (origin/extent), sorted by object path, plus loadedProxies + parentLandscapes counts. Unloaded proxies are not spawned as actors, so only loaded ones appear - use this to confirm a proxy is streamed in before trusting a layer/height readback (#733). Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `find_proxy_at(worldX:n, worldY:n)` | Resolve which loaded LandscapeStreamingProxy covers a world X/Y. Returns found/loaded + label, or loaded:false when the covering proxy is streamed out (so a 0-weight readback there is ambiguous, not real) (#733). Params: `worldX, worldY` |
| `get_height_region(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, includeHeights?:b, encoding?, arrayEncodingLimit?:i)` | Read the raw uint16 heights over a rectangle of landscape vertices, with min/max/mean reported in raw units AND in world Z so the numbers mean something without a second call. Heights come back as a plain array below arrayEncodingLimit and as a little-endian base64 blob above it, and that blob feeds straight back into set_height_region, so a read-modify-write round trip needs no reformatting. Reports hasUnloadedComponentsInRegion, because on a World Partition map an unloaded component reads as absent rather than as flat ground. Reads the merged surface unless editLayer or editLayerIndex names one, in which case it reads that layer's own contribution. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, includeHeights?, encoding?, arrayEncodingLimit?` |
| `set_height_region(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, heightsBase64?, heights?:[n], height?:n, rawHeight?:n, heightSpace?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Write heights over a rectangle of landscape vertices. Accepts heightsBase64 (the blob get_height_region hands back), heights as one number per vertex row-major from (minX,minY), or height / rawHeight to fill the whole rectangle with one value; heightSpace picks whether the numbers are raw uint16 (32768 = the actor's own Z) or world centimetres. Idempotent: a write that changes nothing reports unchanged true and updated false rather than claiming an edit. The rollback record carries the exact previous heights, and when the rectangle is above rollbackMaxVertices the response says rollbackOmitted with the reason instead of emitting a record that would restore only part of it. Requires an edit layer, since a write with none is regenerated away by the layer system. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, heightsBase64?, heights?, height?, rawHeight?, heightSpace?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `get_height_at_point(x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i)` | Surface height under one world XY, as both the raw uint16 and the world Z, plus the landscape vertex it was read at. Reads the nearest vertex rather than interpolating, so it can differ from a physics trace by up to half a quad of slope, and it says so. Position accepts x + y, point {x, y}, or worldX + worldY. Params: `x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?` |
| `get_normal_at_point(x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | World-space surface normal under one world XY, computed by central difference over the neighbouring vertices in world centimetres and rotated into world space, so a non-uniform landscape scale is accounted for. Returns the normal, the slope in degrees and the vertex it was read at. Params: `x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `get_slope_at_point(x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Slope under one world XY in degrees from horizontal, in radians, and as a grade percentage, plus the downhill direction as a unit vector. The downhill direction is what routes a road or a river; a slope number alone never is. Params: `x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `get_slope_map(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, includeSlopes?:b, arrayEncodingLimit?:i)` | Per-vertex slope in degrees over a rectangle, plus min/max/mean and a fixed nine-bucket ten-degree histogram. The buckets are fixed on purpose: they are what a caller reasons about (anything under 15 degrees is buildable) and a configurable bin count would make two runs incomparable. The per-vertex array is returned below arrayEncodingLimit and omitted with a reason above it. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, includeSlopes?, arrayEncodingLimit?` |
| `sculpt_region(operator, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, amount?:n, strength?:n, falloff?:n, sharpness?:n, shape?, targetHeight?:n, flattenTo?, iterations?:i, steps?:i, ridgeAngle?:n, rimPosition?:n, rimRatio?:n, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Apply one shaping operator over a rectangle: raise, lower, flatten, smooth, mountain, valley, ridge, plateau, crater or terrace. One action rather than ten, because the region resolution, falloff, strength blend, previous-height capture and rollback record are identical for every shape and only the per-vertex kernel differs. amount is world centimetres at full strength, shape picks a radial (ellipse) or edge-relative (rect) falloff, and sharpness controls how peaked the dome operators are. flatten and plateau take targetHeight in world Z, or flattenTo as mean / center / min / max; smooth takes iterations; terrace takes steps; ridge takes ridgeAngle in degrees; crater takes rimPosition and rimRatio. Reports verticesClampedToHeightRange when the shape ran past the uint16 range, since that is a flat-topped mountain rather than a failure. With more than one edit layer it shapes the merged terrain and writes only the change into editLayer, scaled by that layer's heightmap alpha; terrainBefore/terrainAfter report the ground, heightBefore/heightAfter the layer. Params: `operator, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, amount?, strength?, falloff?, sharpness?, shape?, targetHeight?, flattenTo?, iterations?, steps?, ridgeAngle?, rimPosition?, rimRatio?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `apply_erosion(actorLabel?, actorPath?, erosionType?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, iterations?:i, maxWork?:i, talusAngle?:n, strength?:n, rainAmount?:n, evaporation?:n, sedimentCapacity?:n, erosionRate?:n, depositionRate?:n, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Run hydraulic or thermal erosion over a rectangle. Hydraulic rains on every vertex, routes water to lower four-neighbours, carries sediment to capacity and deposits the rest, then re-deposits whatever is still suspended so the pass does not quietly remove material every run; thermal slumps anything steeper than talusAngle toward it. This is a CPU grid model over the region on the game thread, not the Landscape Mode erosion tool, and the response says so. Cost is vertices times iterations and is refused above maxWork rather than blocking the editor for an unbounded time. With more than one edit layer it shapes the merged terrain and writes only the change into editLayer, scaled by that layer's heightmap alpha; terrainBefore/terrainAfter report the ground, heightBefore/heightAfter the layer. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, erosionType?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, iterations?, maxWork?, talusAngle?, strength?, rainAmount?, evaporation?, sedimentCapacity?, erosionRate?, depositionRate?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `import_heightmap(filePath\|sourcePath, actorLabel?, actorPath?, format?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, width?:i, height?:n, resample?:b, minHeight?:n, maxHeight?:n, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Write a 16-bit heightmap file into a region of the landscape. format is png16 (16-bit greyscale PNG) or raw16 (headerless little-endian uint16), inferred from the extension when omitted; an 8-bit image is refused with its real format rather than stretched, because a 256-step heightmap terraces visibly. A raw16 file carries no dimensions, so width and height are required for it. When the image and the region disagree the call refuses and prints the region that WOULD fit, unless resample is true, which bilinearly fits it and says detail was averaged away. minHeight and maxHeight remap the image's 0 and 65535 onto a world Z band, which is the control a heightmap authored elsewhere actually needs. A relative filePath resolves under the project's Saved directory. Params: `filePath (or sourcePath), actorLabel?, actorPath?, format?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, width?, height?, resample?, minHeight?, maxHeight?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `export_heightmap(filePath\|outputPath, actorLabel?, actorPath?, format?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, overwrite?:b)` | Write a region's heights out as a 16-bit greyscale PNG or a headerless little-endian uint16 file, for inspection or for a round trip through an external terrain tool. Reports the exact byte count, the region and the height range in raw units and world Z, so the file can be re-imported at the right scale. Exports the merged surface unless editLayer or editLayerIndex names one. No inverse is emitted: the bridge has no delete-file method, and overwriting a file whose previous contents were never read is not undoable, so the response says rollbackOmitted with which of the two cases applied. Params: `filePath (or outputPath), actorLabel?, actorPath?, format?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, overwrite?` |
| `analyze_terrain(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, histogramBins?:i, slopeThresholdDegrees?:n)` | Height and slope distribution over a region, plus largestFlatArea: the biggest axis-aligned rectangle whose every vertex is within slopeThresholdDegrees, in quad indices AND world coordinates with its mean Z. That last part is the answer to where a building fits, which a flat-vertex COUNT never is - ten thousand scattered flat vertices and one flat plateau report the same number. The height histogram takes histogramBins; the slope histogram is fixed at nine ten-degree bands so two runs stay comparable. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, histogramBins?, slopeThresholdDegrees?` |
| `get_layer_weight_region(layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, includeWeights?:b, encoding?, arrayEncodingLimit?:i)` | Read one paint layer's 0..255 weights over a rectangle, with min/max/mean and the painted vertex count and fraction. An unregistered layerName is refused with the layers that ARE registered, so a typo and a landscape whose material never declared the layer read differently. Weights come back as an array below arrayEncodingLimit and as base64 above it, in the exact form set_layer_weight_region takes back. Params: `layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, includeWeights?, encoding?, arrayEncodingLimit?` |
| `set_layer_weight_region(layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, maxVertices?:i, weightsBase64?, weights?:[n], weight?:n, strength?:n, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Write one paint layer's weights over a rectangle. Accepts weightsBase64 (one uint8 per vertex, the form the getter returns), weights as one number per vertex, or weight / strength as a single 0..1 fraction to fill the rectangle. Idempotent, with the same unchanged/updated reporting as set_height_region, and the rollback record carries the exact previous weights up to rollbackMaxVertices. Weights are written as given: the engine no longer renormalises the other layers for you, so set them explicitly if they must sum to 1. Params: `layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, maxVertices?, weightsBase64?, weights?, weight?, strength?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `layer_exists(layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Is this paint layer registered on the landscape, and does it have a LayerInfo asset to store weights in? Returns exists, hasLayerInfo, its layerInfoPath, and the full layer list. The two flags are separate because a material can declare a layer that has no LayerInfo assigned, which looks present and fails every paint. Params: `layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `add_layer(layerName, landscapeName?, packagePath?)` | Register a paint layer on the landscape, creating the ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset that its weight data needs and binding it. The counterpart to remove_layer, and the same handler add_layer_info calls. Idempotent: a layer already registered is reported with its existing asset path rather than duplicated. Params: `layerName, landscapeName?, packagePath?` |
| `remove_layer(layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Unregister a paint layer and drop its weight data across every component of the landscape. Idempotent: removing a layer that is not there reports alreadyAbsent with the layers that are, rather than failing. NOT undoable through the bridge - the weights are destroyed without being read back first, and the response says so with the reason, so export them with get_layer_weight_region first if they matter. The ULandscapeLayerInfoObject asset itself is left on disk, so add_layer brings the layer back empty. Params: `layerName, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `get_holes(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, maxVertices?:i, includeMask?:b, arrayEncodingLimit?:i, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i)` | Read the landscape visibility mask over a rectangle or at a single world XY, as booleans plus the hole vertex count and fraction. A vertex counts as a hole once its visibility weight passes the engine's own two-thirds threshold, so this action and the renderer agree about what a hole is. A hole only renders, and only stops collision, if the landscape material routes a Landscape Visibility Mask node into opacity mask. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, maxVertices?, includeMask?, arrayEncodingLimit?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?` |
| `set_holes(actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?:o, space?, center?:o, radius?:n, x?:n, y?:n, point?:o, worldX?:n, worldY?:n, maxVertices?:i, hole?:b, holes?:[b], weightsBase64?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?:i, rollbackMaxVertices?:i)` | Punch or fill the landscape visibility mask over a rectangle or at a single world XY. Accepts hole as a single boolean for the whole target, holes as one boolean per vertex, or weightsBase64 to restore exact previous visibility weights (which is the form its own rollback record carries). Unlike every other region action this one does NOT default to the whole landscape when no target is given: that would punch the entire terrain into a hole on a call that forgot a parameter, so it refuses instead. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, region?, space?, center?, radius?, x?, y?, point?, worldX?, worldY?, maxVertices?, hole?, holes?, weightsBase64?, editLayer?, editLayerIndex?, rollbackMaxVertices?` |
| `plan_real_world(minElevationMeters:n, maxElevationMeters:n, realWorldSizeMeters?:o, boundsLatLon?:o, sourcePath\|filePath?, format?, width?:i, height?:n, metersPerQuad?:n, elevationEncoding?, verticalExaggeration?:n, maxComponents?:i, location?:v)` | Turn a real-world extent plus a heightmap file into the exact landscape(create) and landscape(import_heightmap) parameters that reproduce it in engine at true scale. Creates nothing: it is arithmetic against engine invariants a caller cannot restate correctly by hand, namely that a landscape's vertex count is componentCount x subsectionSizeQuads x numSubsections + 1 with subsectionSizeQuads restricted to 7/15/31/63/127/255, and that its uint16 heights only mean metres through the actor's Z scale. Size the tile with realWorldSizeMeters {x,y}, or with boundsLatLon {minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon} which is projected on a local tangent plane at the box centre latitude (an approximation, not a datum reprojection, and the response says so). minElevationMeters and maxElevationMeters state what the image's value range means; elevationEncoding full spans 0..65535 across that band, data measures the image's own range and needs sourcePath. Returns the chosen resolution, every legal alternative with its error, the resulting metres per quad, the vertical precision in centimetres, and warnings for resampling, anisotropy, quantisation and exaggeration. Fetching DEM tiles over the network is deliberately NOT part of this: provider APIs, keys and licences change independently of the engine, so that half belongs in a plugin. Params: `minElevationMeters, maxElevationMeters, realWorldSizeMeters?, boundsLatLon?, sourcePath? (or filePath), format?, width?, height?, metersPerQuad?, elevationEncoding?, verticalExaggeration?, maxComponents?, location?` |
| `project_geo_coordinates(boundsLatLon:o, points:[o], actorLabel?, actorPath?, northAt?, sampleHeight?:b)` | Convert between latitude/longitude and a landscape's world space, in both directions, against the same boundsLatLon the landscape was planned for. Each entry in points is either {lat, lon}, answered with the world X/Y and the sampled surface Z so the point lands ON the terrain, or {x, y}, answered with the geographic coordinate that world position corresponds to - which is what turns analyze_terrain's largestFlatArea back into a real place. northAt says which end of the landscape's Y axis is north, defaulting to minY because a DEM raster's first row is its northern edge and that is how import_heightmap lays one down; getting it wrong mirrors every placement about the middle of the map and nothing about the result looks wrong. Params: `boundsLatLon, points, actorLabel?, actorPath?, northAt?, sampleHeight?` |
| `refresh_physical_material_collision(actorLabels?:[s], guids?:[s], bounds?:o, maxActors?:i, save?:=false)` | UE 5.8+: safely refresh physical-material collision data in memory on loaded World Partition LandscapeStreamingProxy actors after a LayerInfo PhysMaterial change. Requires complete registered collision coverage and no pending landscape edit-layer work. Preserves and verifies every raw, complex-live, and simple-live height sample, builds material data before one collision recreation, and fails the whole matched batch on any unsafe result. Filters combine: actorLabels[], guids[], and bounds {min,max}; omitting them targets every loaded proxy up to maxActors (default 256, hard max 1024). Unloaded proxies are untouched; pin them first with level(load_actor_descs). Refuses PIE/SIE and non-World-Partition maps. Persistence is deliberately unsupported because Landscape PreSave can mutate edit-layer collision data; this action never saves packages, and save accepts only false. No inverse: this recomputes derived collision and physical-material data from weightmaps it never writes, so nothing restores the previous build and the response says rollbackPossible=false. Returns loaded/matched/refreshed/failed counts and exact affected package paths. Params: `actorLabels?, guids?, bounds?, maxActors?, save?` |

---

## pcg

*Procedural Content Generation: graphs, nodes, connections, execution, volumes.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_graphs(cursor?, limit?:i)` | List PCG graphs, sorted by object path. Lists the whole project; page through it with cursor/limit. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `read_graph(assetPath\|path)` | Read graph structure: every node with its name, title, inputPins and outputPins (the pin labels connect_nodes takes), the graph's inputNode and outputNode, and edges. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `read_node_settings(assetPath\|path, nodeName)` | Read node settings. An instanced subobject (a spawner's MeshSelectorParameters or InstanceDataPackerParameters) is expanded under instanced {class, properties}, and a weighted mesh selector also lists meshEntries [{mesh, weight, materialOverrides}] (#1303). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName` |
| `get_components()` | List PCG components in level. Params: `none` |
| `get_component_details(one(actorLabel; actorPath))` | Inspect PCG component (#983). Reports blueprintOwned with a warning when the Blueprint's construction script builds the component (edits on the placed actor can be lost on reconstruction; use set_component_parameters with blueprintPath), isGenerating, isCleaningUp, generated, partitioned (with local component counts) and lastRun {id, state generating\|generated\|cancelled\|cleaned\|not_started, startedUtc, finishedUtc}; to wait for a run, use wait_for_generation or wait=true on execute. Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath` |
| `create_graph(name, packagePath\|path?, onConflict?)` | Create graph in packagePath (or path), default /Game/PCG. Idempotent by path: an existing graph is reported rather than replaced. Params: `name, packagePath? (or path), onConflict?` |
| `add_node(assetPath\|path, nodeType, posX?:n, posY?:n, name?)` | Add node. The engine assigns its name unless name is given; either way nodeName in the result is what connect_nodes and remove_node take. A name already in the graph with the same class is reported as existed; another class is refused (#1331). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeType, posX?, posY?, name?` |
| `connect_nodes(assetPath\|path, sourceNode\|sourceNodeName, sourcePin\|sourcePinLabel?, targetNode\|targetNodeName, targetPin\|targetPinLabel?)` | Wire nodes. Returns edgeVerified=true after confirming the UPCGEdge persisted; surfaces an error if AddEdge succeeded but no edge object was instantiated (#304). A pin label the node does not have is refused with reason pin_not_found and validPins, the labels it does have. An edge the graph refuses says why: connectionResult (InvalidNode, InvalidPin, IncompatibleTypes, RequiresFilter, RequiresConversion, CycleDetected) and connectionReason; validate_edge asks the same question without connecting (#1828). Params: `assetPath (or path), sourceNode (or sourceNodeName), sourcePin? (or sourcePinLabel), targetNode (or targetNodeName), targetPin? (or targetPinLabel)` |
| `validate_edge(assetPath\|path, sourceNode\|sourceNodeName, sourcePin\|sourcePinLabel?, targetNode\|targetNodeName, targetPin\|targetPinLabel?)` | Ask whether an edge can be added without touching the graph (UPCGGraph::ValidateEdge on UE 5.9, the same node, pin, cycle and type checks before it). Pins default as connect_nodes defaults them. Returns valid, connectionResult (Success, InvalidNode, InvalidPin, IncompatibleTypes, RequiresFilter, RequiresConversion, CycleDetected), reason and alreadyConnected (#1828). Params: `assetPath (or path), sourceNode (or sourceNodeName), sourcePin? (or sourcePinLabel), targetNode (or targetNodeName), targetPin? (or targetPinLabel)` |
| `get_custom_hlsl(assetPath\|path, nodeName)` | Read a Custom HLSL node's kernel: sourceText, functionsText, the generated declarationsText, and readOnly with kernelSourceOverride when a compute source asset supplies the kernel (#1828). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName` |
| `set_custom_hlsl(assetPath\|path, nodeName, any(sourceText; functionsText))` | Write a Custom HLSL node's sourceText and/or functionsText, as the HLSL Source Editor does (UPCGCustomHLSLSettings::SetSourceText and SetFunctionsText on UE 5.9). Refused while a Kernel Source Override makes the node read-only. Saves the graph; returns the node's pins as they now stand, and the rollback writes the previous text (#1828). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName, at least one of sourceText/functionsText` |
| `disconnect_nodes(assetPath\|path, sourceNode\|sourceNodeName, targetNode\|targetNodeName, sourcePin\|sourcePinLabel?, targetPin\|targetPinLabel?)` | Remove a wired edge between two PCG nodes. Omitted pins match any pin; a pin label the node does not have is refused with validPins. Returns removedEdges count (#346). Params: `assetPath (or path), sourceNode (or sourceNodeName), targetNode (or targetNodeName), sourcePin? (or sourcePinLabel), targetPin? (or targetPinLabel)` |
| `set_node_settings(assetPath\|path, nodeName, one(settings:o; propertyName+propertyValue))` | Set node params. Pass a settings object of {propertyPath: value} (dotted paths and nested structs supported), or propertyName + propertyValue for a single write. Reports previousProperties and rolls back to them. Writing a spawner's MeshSelectorType or InstanceDataPackerType recreates its selector or packer (listed in recreatedInstancedParameters). Fields of an instanced subobject the node owns are written with a dotted key (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName) or a field object ({MeshSelectorParameters: {AttributeName: 'Mesh'}}), in the same call as the type that selects its class; a path for an instanced subobject, or a dotted key into an object the node does not own, is refused. Addresses the graph's DefaultInputNode and DefaultOutputNode too: writing their Pins changes the graph's own pins and those of every Subgraph node calling it. An attribute selector (TargetAttribute, InputSource1, OutputTarget...) takes the PCG editor's syntax as a string: MyAttr, $Density, @Last, $Position.Z (#1275); a selector given as an object replaces the whole selector, so fields left out (ExtraNames) reset. Returns resolvedSelectors with each written selector as stored, and removedEdges for edges a pin-changing write dropped, with a warning (#1298). readBack holds each written property as stored; struct text that left fields out (which keep their old values) adds a warning naming the property (#1299). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName, settings OR propertyName + propertyValue` |
| `set_static_mesh_spawner_meshes(assetPath\|path, nodeName, entries:[o], replace?:b)` | Populate weighted MeshEntries on a PCGStaticMeshSpawner node (#145). entries=[{mesh, weight?}]; replace defaults to true. Refuses a selector the node's settings do not own; reports selectorOuterIsSettings. Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName, entries, replace?` |
| `remove_node(assetPath\|path, nodeName)` | Remove node. The graph's input and output nodes are refused. Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName` |
| `unwrap_instance_nodes(assetPath\|path, nodeName?)` | Give instance nodes (UPCGSettingsInstance wrappers, read-only in the PCG editor's details panel) their own settings object, keeping every value and edge. Settings from a shared asset are copied into the node. Nodes that already own their settings are left alone. Omit nodeName for every node in the graph (#1087). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName?` |
| `execute(one(actorLabel; actorPath), seed?:i, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)` | Regenerate PCG. A seed is written to the component before generating, and the old one reported back as previousSeed (#983). Returns at once with runId, or with wait=true only once that run finishes, adding wait {state generated\|cancelled\|cleaned\|not_started\|timed_out, durationMs}; a timed-out wait is a warning, not a failure (#1365). When Generate defers its start to a later tick, the run follows that generation (lastRun.deferredStart) instead of settling as not_started; a run that started nothing reports alreadyGenerated, lastFinishUtc and a note saying the output was already up to date. Refused with generation_in_progress while a run is active. Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, seed?, wait?, timeoutSeconds?` |
| `force_regenerate(one(actorLabel; actorPath), wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)` | Force a stuck PCG component to regenerate (clears graph ref, re-sets, cleanup+generate) (#146/#983). Cancels active generation before resetting; returns runId like execute, including when the component was busy, and takes wait=true the same way (#1365). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, wait?, timeoutSeconds?` |
| `get_generation_state(one(actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?)` | One poll of a PCG component's generation: busy (generating, cleaning up, or local components generating), finishCount and lastFinishState for generations that ended since the bridge started watching the component (whoever started them), and lastRun. wait_for_generation polls this for you (#1365). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?` |
| `wait_for_generation(actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, graceSeconds?:n, runId?:n, timeoutSeconds?:n)` | Block until a PCG component's generation finishes, for a run started by anything (execute, the editor, a project function that defers to the next tick), polling get_generation_state with backoff. With runId, waits for that run; without, for the generation in flight, or one that starts within graceSeconds (default 2), else returns state idle. Partitioned components finish when their local components do. Returns state generated\|cancelled\|cleaned\|not_started\|idle\|timed_out, durationMs, polls and lastRun; timed_out fails the call (#1365). With runId, a not_started run is final only after graceSeconds, since Generate can defer its start; not_started adds alreadyGenerated and lastFinishUtc. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, runId?, timeoutSeconds?, graceSeconds?` |
| `cleanup(one(actorLabel; actorPath), removeComponents?:b)` | Cleanup a PCG component (remove spawned content) (#146). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, removeComponents?` |
| `toggle_graph(one(actorLabel; actorPath), graphPath?)` | Toggle a PCG component's graph assignment to force reinit (no generate) (#146). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, graphPath?` |
| `add_volume(graphPath?, location?:v, transform?:o, extent?:v, label?, onConflict?)` | Place PCG volume. Idempotent by editor label when one is given. transform {location, rotation, scale\|scale3D} is honoured; reports the placed location, rotation, scale, extent and scaledExtent. Params: `graphPath?, location?, transform?, extent?, label?, onConflict?` |
| `import_graph(assetPath\|path, nodes:[o], connections?:[o], replace?:b, removeNodes?:[s], removeConnections?:[o])` | Bulk-author a PCG graph from JSON: nodes=[{name,class,posX?,posY?,settings?,subgraph?:{path,parameters}}], connections=[{from,fromPin?,to,toPin?}], replace defaults to false. Without replace, a name the graph already has is that node: the same class updates it in place (counted in nodesUpdated and listed in updatedNodes) and edges naming it land on it; another class, or a name given twice, refuses the call before anything changes (#1262). removeNodes and removeConnections run first, without replace. The rollback of an import without replace removes the nodes it created, cuts the edges it added and restores the values it overwrote; only replace=true carries a full graph snapshot (#1331). One call replaces N add_node + M connect_nodes + K set_node_settings (#213). A path for an instanced subobject is refused before anything changes, while its fields are written as set_node_settings writes them (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName or a field object); failed nodes, settings or connections make the result a failure; name-collision warnings are informational. Attribute selectors in settings take the PCG editor's syntax as a string ($Position.Z, @Last). A Get Graph Parameter node (PCGUserParameterGetSettings) takes parameter: '<name>' and binds to that graph parameter; export_graph emits it the same way (#1264). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodes, connections?, replace?, removeNodes?, removeConnections?` |
| `export_graph(assetPath\|path, includeSettings?:b)` | Export a PCG graph as JSON; includeSettings defaults to true. Each node carries inputPins and outputPins, its pin labels; import_graph ignores them. Round-trip safe with import_graph (#213). Subgraph assignments and parameter overrides are preserved as subgraph {path,parameters}; other instanced subobjects (a spawner's mesh selector) are left out and listed in omittedInstancedProperties. Attribute selectors export in editor syntax ("$Position.Z"), extra names included (#1267). Params: `assetPath (or path), includeSettings?` |
| `export_level_to_asset(levelPath, assetPath?, assetName?, save?:b)` | Export a saved level to a PCG data asset (a PCG Assembly), the Content Browser's 'Create PCG Assets from Level(s)' without its dialog. Default name <LevelName>_PCG beside the level; an existing asset is overwritten. assetPath takes the asset's own path (object path, or an existing asset's package path) as well as a folder for assetName, and an existing asset of another class is refused (#1296). Reports points per output pin (Root, Points). UE 5.5+ (#1244). Params: `levelPath, assetPath?, assetName?, save?` |
| `update_level_assets(assetPaths:[s], save?:b)` | Re-export PCG data assets from the levels they were exported from ('Update PCG Assets'). Reports points per output pin. UE 5.5+ (#1244). Params: `assetPaths, save?` |
| `set_subgraph(assetPath\|path, nodeName, subgraphPath)` | Point a Subgraph node at a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance through the engine's SetSubgraph, so its pins and user-parameter bag are built (a write to SubgraphInstance.Graph builds pins but no parameters). "" clears it. Returns the node's pins and every parameter with its value and override state (#1253). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName, subgraphPath` |
| `set_subgraph_parameters(assetPath\|path, nodeName, parameters:o)` | Override a Subgraph node's user parameters: parameters={name: value}; null clears an override. A name the subgraph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1253). Params: `assetPath (or path), nodeName, parameters` |
| `set_graph_pins(assetPath\|path, side, pins:[o], mode?)` | Add, update, replace or remove the graph's own pins on its input or output node (side), matched by label: append (default) adds a pin or updates the one with that label, replace makes the pins exactly the list, remove deletes the labels given. Fields left out keep an existing pin's values, so its edges stay wired. Every Subgraph node calling the graph gets the same pins. Returns the resulting pins and removedEdges for edges a removed or retyped pin dropped. Rolls back to the previous Pins through set_node_settings (#1318). Params: `assetPath (or path), side, pins, mode?` |
| `set_graph_parameters(assetPath\|path, any(graphParameters:[o]; removeParameters:[s]))` | Add, change, retype or remove a graph's user parameters (the Graph Parameters a Get Graph Parameter node and a Subgraph or Graph Instance override read). graphParameters=[{name, type?, typeObject?, default?}]: a new name needs a type; an existing one keeps its type unless another is given; default is JSON or export text. removeParameters=[names]. Every entry is checked on a scratch copy first, so one bad entry refuses the call with nothing changed. Returns the parameters and previousParameters; the rollback removes what was added and restores changed defaults (#1264). Params: `assetPath (or path), at least one of graphParameters/removeParameters` |
| `create_graph_instance(name, graphPath, packagePath?, overrides?:o, onConflict?)` | Create a PCG Graph Instance asset running graphPath, with optional parameter overrides={name: value}; an override for a name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, sets none and fails with the asset path in createdWithoutOverrides. Idempotent by path. Returns every parameter with its value and override state (#1264). Params: `name, graphPath, packagePath?, overrides?, onConflict?` |
| `set_graph_instance_overrides(assetPath\|path, overrides:o)` | Set a PCG Graph Instance asset's parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}; null clears one. A name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1264). Params: `assetPath (or path), overrides` |
| `set_component_graph(one(blueprintPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, graphPath)` | Assign a PCG graph to a PCGComponent through UPCGComponent::SetGraph, on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath; compiled and saved, so every placed instance rebuilds with it) or on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath). graphPath is a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance; "" clears it. componentName picks one when there are several. On a placed actor whose Blueprint's construction script builds the component, the call reruns the construction script and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction if the assignment did not survive. Returns graph, previousGraph and the new graph's parameters with their override state; rolls back to the previous graph (lossy when the component held overrides). Params: `blueprintPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, graphPath` |
| `get_component_parameters(one(blueprintPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?)` | Read a PCG component's graph and each graph parameter's value and override state ({name, type, value, overridden}), on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath) or on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath). componentName picks one when there are several. A placed actor's component that its Blueprint's construction script builds reports blueprintOwned and a warning: values written to the placed actor can be discarded on reconstruction, so write them to the Blueprint. Params: `blueprintPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?` |
| `set_component_parameters(one(blueprintPath; actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, overrides:o)` | Set a PCG component's graph parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}, null clears one. With blueprintPath it writes the Blueprint's component template (a child Blueprint gets its own override of an inherited one), compiles and saves, so every reconstruction keeps the overrides; this is the write for a PCGComponent inside a Blueprint actor. With actorLabel or actorPath it writes the placed component; when the Blueprint's construction script builds that component, the call reruns the construction script as the editor does and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction, naming the lost overrides and the Blueprint write to use, if they did not survive (persistedThroughReconstruction). A name the graph does not declare or a value of the wrong type refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and every parameter's value and override state, and rolls back to the previous values. Params: `blueprintPath OR actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, overrides` |
| `read_generated_output(one(actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, pin?, attributes?:[s], offset?:i, limit?:i, nodeName?, graphPath?, includeLocalComponents?:b)` | Read the data a PCG component generated, for any actor's PCG components (not only PCGVolumes): per tagged data its pin, tags, dataClass, kind (points \| attributeSet \| other), count, and a page of entries with the requested attributes (selectors such as $Position, $Density, $Position.Z or a metadata attribute; default the point properties plus every metadata attribute). offset/limit page the entries, and nextOffset says there are more. A partitioned component's local components are read too. Each component row also lists what the graph spawned, which a spawner does not hand to the output node: spawnedComponents [{name, class, owner, mesh, instanceCount}], spawnedInstanceCount and spawnedActors, with totals spawnedComponentCount and spawnedInstanceCount on the result. With nodeName it reads that node's output from the component's inspection instead (UE 5.8+): the first call turns inspection on and asks for a regenerate, later calls return each execution stack's data (#1309). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, pin?, attributes?, offset?, limit?, nodeName?, graphPath?, includeLocalComponents?` |
