## foliage

*Foliage instances, types, procedural spawners, sampling and settings. Every FoliageType tunable (Density, Radius, ScaleX/Y/Z, AlignToNormal, GroundSlopeAngle, CullDistance, CastShadow) is a plain property: use set_settings, batch_set_settings_where or asset(set_property), not a typed action. Grass on landscape layers is authored elsewhere and deliberately has no action here: material(add_expression, expressionType="LandscapeGrassOutput") adds the slot node, material(list_expressions) reads it back, asset(create_asset_by_class, className="LandscapeGrassType") makes the grass type, and asset(set_property) fills its GrassVarieties.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_types(cursor?, limit?:i)` | List foliage types in the level, one row per type per InstancedFoliageActor (foliageActorPath says which), sorted by that pair. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_settings(foliageTypePath\|foliageTypeName)` | Read foliage type settings. Params: `foliageTypePath (or foliageTypeName)` |
| `sample(center:v, radius?:n)` | Count instances per foliage type inside a sphere. Params: `center, radius?` |
| `create_type(meshPath, name?, packagePath?, onConflict?, settings?:o)` | Create foliage type from mesh. Params: `meshPath, name?, packagePath?, onConflict?, settings?` |
| `set_settings(foliageTypePath\|foliageTypeName, settings:o)` | Modify ONE foliage type's settings. For the same edit across every type matching a condition, use batch_set_settings_where instead of calling this in a loop. Params: `foliageTypePath (or foliageTypeName), settings` |
| `batch_set_settings_where(settings:o, where:[o], whereMode?, foliageTypePaths?:[s], directory?, recursive?:b, fromLevel?:b, propertyNames?:[s], dryRun?:b, save?:b, maxTypes?:i)` | Write settings to every FoliageType whose CURRENT property values match a predicate, with the predicate evaluated in the editor. set_settings is one asset per call and cannot express a condition at all, so 'include_in_hlod=false on every type whose cull distance is set' meant reading 201 assets out, computing the 36 matches client-side, and writing them back one at a time. Candidates come from foliageTypePaths[] (explicit), directory (scan FoliageType assets) or fromLevel=true (types placed in the open level). Predicate fields read the asset's own properties by dotted path, so CullDistance.Max works and a bare name is treated the same as props.<name>; operators are the same vocabulary as level(query_components). dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE because this writes to many assets at once, and the preview still resolves every setting path so an unwritable property is reported before the commit. Written values are read back rather than echoed, so a value the property coerced is visible. The inverse is asset(bulk_set_properties) carrying the previous value of every property on every type written, which is the only action that takes DIFFERENT values per asset - two matched types can have had different previous values for the same setting. It is marked lossy when a matched FoliageType lives inside a level rather than as an asset (no assetPath addresses it), and omitted entirely above that action's 500-item batch limit, with the reason stated rather than a record that would restore part of the write. Pass one of foliageTypePaths, directory or fromLevel (#988). Params: `settings, where, whereMode?, foliageTypePaths?, directory?, recursive?, fromLevel?, propertyNames?, dryRun?, save?, maxTypes?` |
| `add_instances(foliageTypePath, transforms?:[o], center?:v, radius?:n, count?:i, seed?:i, projectToGround?:b, traceUp?:n, traceDown?:n, applyTypeRules?:b, skipCollision?:b)` | PAINT foliage into the open level. Nothing else on this surface could place a single instance, so create_type produced an asset that never appeared anywhere. Two modes: transforms[] places each entry exactly, center+radius+count scatters uniformly over a disc. Each candidate is traced onto the geometry beneath it (projectToGround, default true) and then run through the FoliageType's OWN placement rules (applyTypeRules, default true) so the random scale between ScaleX/Y/Z, the random yaw and pitch, align-to-normal within AlignMaxAngle, the Z offset and the CollisionWithWorld test all apply - which is what makes a painted instance behave like one painted by hand. A candidate that hits nothing, or that the type's ground-slope or height range rejects, is reported in skippedCandidates with the reason rather than silently dropped. The type is added to the level's palette if it is not there already. Returns the InstancedFoliageActor it wrote to, and rolls back by removing exactly the transforms it placed. Each transforms entry is {location, rotation?, scale?}. Params: `foliageTypePath, transforms?, center?, radius?, count?, seed?, projectToGround?, traceUp?, traceDown?, applyTypeRules?, skipCollision?` |
| `remove_instances(foliageTypePath, instanceIndices?:[i], transforms?:[o], center?:v, radius?:n, all?:b, matchTolerance?:n, actorPath?, dryRun?:b)` | Remove foliage instances by index, by exact transform, inside a sphere, or all of a type. The rollback captures each removed instance's world transform and replays it as an add, so this is recoverable up to 2000 instances; the base component an instance was painted onto is not restored. dryRun reports what would go without touching anything. Scope to one InstancedFoliageActor with actorPath when a World Partition map holds the same type on several. Params: `foliageTypePath, instanceIndices?, transforms?, center?, radius?, all?, matchTolerance?, actorPath?, dryRun?` |
| `get_instances(foliageTypePath?, center?:v, radius?:n, limit?:i, startIndex?:i, includeTransforms?:b)` | Read placed foliage instances with their world transforms, paged. sample only ever returned counts, so there was no way to verify a paint or find what to remove. Filter by type and/or by a sphere; index is the position inside the named actor's info for that type, which is exactly what remove_instances takes. Params: `foliageTypePath?, center?, radius?, limit?, startIndex?, includeTransforms?` |
| `add_type_to_level(foliageTypePath)` | Put a FoliageType asset into the open level's palette, allocating the instanced component that holds its instances. create_type only makes the asset; until this runs the type is invisible to the level and to the foliage editor. Idempotent: a type already in the level reports existed and allocates nothing. Params: `foliageTypePath` |
| `remove_type_from_level(foliageTypePath, force?:b)` | Take a FoliageType out of the open level's palette. REFUSES while the type still has instances unless force=true, because removing it destroys them and their transforms are not captured - remove them first with remove_instances, whose rollback does capture them. The FoliageType asset itself is untouched; asset(delete) deletes it. Params: `foliageTypePath, force?` |
| `read_spawner(spawnerPath)` | Read a ProceduralFoliageSpawner: its tile settings, the foliage types it will spawn resolved to real asset paths, and every volume in the open level bound to it with its bounds and whether it has produced anything. The volume half is the part nobody can read off the asset and the usual reason a simulation appears to do nothing. Returns objectPath for the scalar tunables, which are plain properties. Params: `spawnerPath` |
| `set_spawner_types(spawnerPath, foliageTypePaths:[s], mode?, save?:b)` | Set which foliage types a ProceduralFoliageSpawner spawns. This needs an action rather than a property write: FoliageTypes is a private array whose element object pointer is private too, and every write has to be followed by RefreshInstance or the cached type the simulation actually reads stays stale. Validates every path before writing anything, reports unchanged when the list already matched, reads the result back rather than echoing it, and rolls back to the previous list. Params: `spawnerPath, foliageTypePaths, mode?, save?` |
| `simulate_procedural(actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?, clearExisting?:b, skipCollision?:b)` | Run the procedural foliage simulation and place what it generates. Address one volume with actorLabel or actorPath, or every volume in the open level bound to one spawner with spawnerPath. Validates every target first (spawner set, type list non-empty, volume bounds non-zero) so a half-simulated set of volumes is not possible, then generates desired instances and traces and places each one under the same type rules as add_instances. Reports generated, placed and skipped per volume. Place the volume itself with level(spawn_volume, volumeType="ProceduralFoliageVolume"), which builds the cube brush a bare spawn leaves empty. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?, clearExisting?, skipCollision?` |
| `clear_procedural(actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?)` | Remove every instance a procedural foliage component spawned, matched on the component's own procedural GUID so hand-painted instances of the same type are left alone. Pass one of actorLabel, actorPath or spawnerPath. Reports alreadyRemoved when the component had produced nothing. The inverse re-runs the simulation, which reproduces the cleared content only while the spawner's seed, tile settings and type list are unchanged. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, spawnerPath?` |

---

## niagara

*Niagara VFX: systems, emitters, spawning, parameters, and graph authoring.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list(cursor?, limit?:i)` | List Niagara assets: every NiagaraSystem and NiagaraEmitter as one row tagged with its `type`, sorted by object path within each type, plus systemCount/emitterCount for the whole listing. Lists the whole project; page through it with cursor/limit. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_info(assetPath\|path\|systemPath)` | Inspect system. Params: `assetPath (or path, or systemPath)` |
| `list_dynamic_inputs(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, stackContext?, moduleName?)` | Report the authored override map per module: which inputs carry a plain value, which are wired to a dynamic-input script, and which hold an inline HLSL expression, with nested dynamic inputs one level down under nestedOverrides. This is a graph walk, so no property read produces it. Pair with list_module_inputs, which shows the inputs that have no override at all. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?, stackContext?, moduleName?` |
| `set_dynamic_input(systemPath\|assetPath, stackContext, moduleName, inputName, dynamicInputScript, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Wire a dynamic-input NiagaraScript into a module input's override pin, creating the pin if needed and replacing whatever was there. A dynamic input is a graph node, not a property, so set_property cannot do this. Returns dynamicInputName, which is the module name to pass to set_module_input when setting the dynamic input's OWN inputs. Errors list the module's real input names and the modules present. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stackContext, moduleName, inputName, dynamicInputScript, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `remove_dynamic_input(systemPath\|assetPath, stackContext, moduleName, inputName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Unwire a dynamic input, delete the nodes that fed only it, and drop the override pin so the module's own default comes back. An input with no dynamic input returns alreadyRemoved rather than an error, so a rollback replays safely. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stackContext, moduleName, inputName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `add_simulation_stage(systemPath\|assetPath, stageName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, enabled?:b)` | Create a simulation stage on an emitter: the stage object AND the backing NiagaraScript, its output node with a fresh usage id, and a parameter-map input node, so the stage actually compiles. set_property cannot create a graph, which is why this is a handler. Returns simulationStageObjectPath; set IterationSource, NumIterations, ExecuteBehavior and the ElementCount bindings on it with asset(set_property). Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stageName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, enabled?` |
| `remove_simulation_stage(systemPath\|assetPath, stageName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Remove a simulation stage, its script, and the graph nodes that fed only its output node, leaving nodes shared with another stack alone. A missing stage returns alreadyRemoved with the stages that do exist. Reports removedModules, which the rollback cannot restore, rather than pretending the undo is complete. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stageName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `add_event_handler(systemPath\|assetPath, eventName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, sourceEmitterId?)` | Create an event handler on an emitter, with its event script, output node and usage id, so the handler's struct fields point at something real. Returns eventHandlerPropertyPath; set ExecutionMode, SpawnNumber and MaxEventsPerFrame through asset(set_property) on emitterObjectPath with that prefix. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), eventName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, sourceEmitterId?` |
| `remove_event_handler(systemPath\|assetPath, eventName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Remove an event handler by its script's usage id and delete the graph chain that fed only it. A missing handler returns alreadyRemoved listing the handlers present. Echoes the ExecutionMode and SpawnNumber the rollback will not restore. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), eventName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `get_custom_hlsl(one(scriptPath; systemPath), stackContext?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, nodeIndex?:i)` | Read every CustomHLSL node in a graph: the source body, and the pins Niagara parsed out of it. Omit nodeIndex to list them all. This is what makes HLSL iterable rather than write-once, since nothing else can read the body back. stackContext and the emitter apply when addressing a system. Params: `scriptPath OR systemPath, stackContext?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, nodeIndex?` |
| `set_custom_hlsl(hlsl, one(scriptPath; systemPath), stackContext?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, nodeIndex?:i)` | Overwrite a CustomHLSL node's body and reconstruct the node, so the returned pins are the ones the new source actually declares. A bare property write would leave stale pins and an uncompiled script, which is why this is a handler. A body identical to the current one returns alreadySet and skips the recompile. stackContext and the emitter apply when addressing a system. Params: `hlsl, scriptPath OR systemPath, stackContext?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, nodeIndex?` |
| `remove_module(systemPath\|assetPath, stackContext, moduleName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Remove a module from an emitter stack: unwire its node group, close the parameter-map chain over the gap, and delete the module with its override node and dynamic inputs. add_module had no inverse below UE 5.8, where only the Epic toolset covers this. Returns remainingModules in stack order and echoes the removedOverrides the rollback will not restore. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stackContext, moduleName, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `set_module_enabled(systemPath\|assetPath, stackContext, moduleName, enabled:b, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Enable or disable a module in place. A disabled module keeps its node, its inputs and its stack position and is skipped at compile time, which makes this the reversible way to test whether a module is causing a behaviour. Already in that state returns alreadySet. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), stackContext, moduleName, enabled, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `compile(systemPath\|assetPath, force?:b, includeGpuShaders?:b)` | Force a real compile of a system and report what the translator said, per script: scriptName, usage, status (NCS_UpToDate \| NCS_UpToDateWithWarnings \| NCS_Error \| ...), errorMsg and every compile event with its severity and the node and pin guid that produced it, plus a top-level compiled boolean and a flat errors[]. This is the assertion a graph edit has to survive. validate answers whether the system EMITS, which a malformed script can still pass, and get_compiled_hlsl returns success without compiling anything at all on a CPU-sim emitter. The call blocks until the compile settles, because an asynchronous one hands back the previous compile's status. force (default true) recompiles even when nothing looks dirty, which is the case a graph edit that left change tracking untouched produces. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), force?, includeGpuShaders?` |
| `validate(systemPath\|assetPath)` | Verify gate: does this system actually emit? Reports per emitter whether it is enabled and has a spawn module + an enabled renderer. valid=false means empty shell. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath)` |
| `spawn(systemPath\|assetPath, location?:v, rotation?:r, label?, scaleX?:n, scaleY?:n, scaleZ?:n, autoDestroy?:b)` | Spawn VFX on a new NiagaraActor host of its own, never on an existing actor. The rollback deletes that host by actorPath and nothing else. Scale is three separate keys, scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ, not a vector object; autoDestroy=true destroys the host when the system finishes (default false). spawn_actor is the same host without scale or autoDestroy. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), location?, rotation?, label?, scaleX?, scaleY?, scaleZ?, autoDestroy?` |
| `spawn_actor(systemPath\|assetPath, location?:v, rotation?:r, label?, activate?:b)` | Spawn a PERSISTENT, labeled NiagaraActor in the editor world (findable, re-activatable, survives capture - unlike spawn). Assigns the system and activates unless activate=false (#537). Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), location?, rotation?, label?, activate?` |
| `reactivate(one(actorLabel; actorPath))` | Reset + reactivate the NiagaraComponent on a placed actor (replay a burst before capturing) (#537/#983). Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath` |
| `set_parameter(one(actorLabel; actorPath), parameterName, parameterType?, one(value:*; valueX:n+valueY:n+valueZ:n))` | Set a user parameter on the NiagaraComponent of a placed actor. parameterType selects how the value is read: float, int and bool take `value`; vector takes valueX/valueY/valueZ, which are separate keys rather than a `value` object because that is what the handler reads. Reports previousValue and rolls back to it. Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, parameterName, parameterType?, value OR valueX + valueY + valueZ` |
| `create(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create system. Idempotent by path: an existing system is reported rather than replaced. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `create_emitter(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, templatePath?, inherit?:b)` | Create a Niagara emitter asset. templatePath copies an existing emitter as the starting point (the content browser's create-from-template path); omit it for the default empty emitter with the standard modules and a sprite renderer. inherit=true makes it a child that tracks the template instead, which then refuses local edits to inherited modules. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, templatePath?, inherit?` |
| `add_emitter(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterPath)` | Add emitter to system. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterPath` |
| `remove_emitter(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Remove an emitter from a system (CRUD delete), addressed by emitterName or emitterIndex. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `list_emitters(systemPath\|assetPath)` | List emitters in system. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath)` |
| `set_emitter_property(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, propertyName, value:*)` | Set emitter property. propertyName 'enabled' toggles the emitter and 'name' renames it (its Emitter.* parameters follow; the result's newEmitterName is the name it landed on); anything else is an FVersionedNiagaraEmitterData property. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, propertyName, value` |
| `list_modules(pathFilter?, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List Niagara module scripts, sorted by object path. pathFilter narrows the whole set rather than only the first page, which is what it always claimed to do. Params: `pathFilter?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_emitter_info(one(assetPath; systemPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Inspect an emitter: a standalone emitter asset by assetPath, or an emitter inside a system by systemPath plus emitterName or emitterIndex. Returns sim target, renderers, every emitter-data property with its value, and the module stack per context. Module input values such as SpawnRate or the EmitterState loop settings come from list_module_inputs. Params: `assetPath OR systemPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `list_renderers(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | List renderers on an emitter. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `add_renderer(systemPath\|assetPath, rendererType, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Add renderer (sprite/mesh/ribbon or full class). Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), rendererType, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `remove_renderer(systemPath\|assetPath, rendererIndex:i, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Remove renderer by index. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), rendererIndex, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `set_renderer_property(systemPath\|assetPath, rendererIndex?:i, propertyName, value:*, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Set any renderer property. Bools, numbers and strings are taken directly; object properties (a sprite/mesh renderer's Material, the mesh on a mesh renderer) take an asset path and are class-checked; structs, enums, names and arrays go through the shared JSON property setter, so there is no longer a type whitelist to fall off (#783). Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), rendererIndex?, propertyName, value, emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `inspect_data_interfaces(systemPath\|assetPath)` | List user-scope data interfaces. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath)` |
| `create_system_from_spec(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, emitters?:[o])` | Declaratively create a system + emitters: emitters=[{path}]. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, emitters?` |
| `get_compiled_hlsl(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n)` | Read GPU compute script info for an emitter. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?` |
| `list_system_parameters(systemPath\|assetPath)` | List user-exposed system parameters. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath)` |
| `list_module_inputs(systemPath\|assetPath, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, stackContext?, moduleName?)` | List an emitter's modules in stack order (stackContext, stackIndex, moduleName, enabled) with the inputs you can actually SET - Spawn Rate, Lifetime, Colour, Sprite Size - each with its name, qualifiedName, type, a settable flag, its current value and valueSource: local (authored on this emitter), moduleDefault (the module script's default), or linked (driven by a dynamic input, described by list_dynamic_inputs). Compile-time switches and enums are reported separately under switchPins; note that 'inputs' now means override-map inputs, NOT the function-call node pins it meant before (those are switchPins) (#784). Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), emitterName?, emitterIndex?, stackContext?, moduleName?` |
| `set_module_input(systemPath\|assetPath, moduleName, inputName, value:*, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, stackContext?)` | Set a module input value. Override-map-bound inputs (the numeric/colour values that matter) are written through the stack override map, the same path the Niagara stack editor uses; others fall back to the pin default. Reports writePath ('overrideMap'\|'pinDefault'). On the overrideMap path previousValue cannot be read back (NiagaraEditor does not export the binder's reader), so it reports '(unread: override map)' and NO rollback is offered - re-set the value explicitly instead. The pinDefault path reports a real previousValue and is rollback-safe (#769). value accepts a scalar, [x,y,z], {x,y,z[,w]} or {r,g,b[,a]} (alpha defaults to 1); anything the input's type cannot parse is REJECTED rather than written, including gapped component objects and non-finite numbers. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), moduleName, inputName, value, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, stackContext?` |
| `add_module(systemPath\|assetPath, moduleScript, stackContext, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, targetIndex?:i)` | Add a stock /Niagara/Modules script to an emitter stack (the modules that make an emitter actually do anything). Then set_module_input to tune it. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), moduleScript, stackContext, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, targetIndex?` |
| `list_static_switches(systemPath\|assetPath, moduleName?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, stackContext?)` | List static switch inputs on a module. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), moduleName?, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, stackContext?` |
| `set_static_switch(systemPath\|assetPath, moduleName, switchName, value:*, emitterName?, emitterIndex?:n, stackContext?)` | Set static switch value on a module's function call node. Params: `systemPath (or assetPath), moduleName, switchName, value, emitterName?, emitterIndex?, stackContext?` |
| `create_module_from_hlsl(name, hlsl, packagePath?, onConflict?, inputs?:[o], outputs?:[o])` | Create a NiagaraScript module backed by a custom HLSL node. inputs/outputs are [{name,type}]. Params: `name, hlsl, packagePath?, onConflict?, inputs?, outputs?` |
| `create_scratch_module(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, inputs?:[o], outputs?:[o])` | Create empty Niagara scratch module. inputs/outputs are [{name,type}] (#185). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, inputs?, outputs?` |
| `capture_sim_cache(one(actorLabel; actorPath), componentName?, frames?:i, advanceSimulation?:b, tickDelta?:n, attributeCaptureMode?, explicitAttributes?:[s], world?, pieInstance?:i)` | Record per-frame particle attributes off a placed actor's NiagaraComponent into an in-memory NiagaraSimCache, GPU emitters included, in the editor world or PIE. Returns simCachePath, frames, and per emitter its numInstancesPerFrame and attributeNames (bare names: Position, Velocity, Age). frames > 1 advances the simulation one tickDelta between frames. The component must be active. Read the values with read_sim_cache. Params: `actorLabel OR actorPath, componentName?, frames?, advanceSimulation?, tickDelta?, attributeCaptureMode?, explicitAttributes?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `read_sim_cache(simCachePath, emitterName?, attributes?:[s], frameIndex?:i, limit?:i, summarize?:b)` | Read particle attributes from a captured sim cache frame. Returns numInstances for the frame and the emitter layout; per attribute found, count, components, the first `limit` values and per-component min/max/avg over every instance. Names may be bare (Age) or qualified (Particles.Age). A name not in the layout fails the call and names the readable ones; an attribute in the layout on a zero-instance frame reports count 0 with a note, so an empty frame and a wrong name never look the same. Params: `simCachePath, emitterName?, attributes?, frameIndex?, limit?, summarize?` |
| `batch(ops:[o])` | Run a sequence of niagara operations against the bridge in order. Fails fast on the first error (returns results up to that point + error). Params: `ops:[{action, params}] where action is any niagara subaction listed above` |
| `epic_add_emitter(system:ref, templateEmitter:ref, emitterName)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds an emitter to a Niagara System. The new emitter will be based on the template emitter, inheriting its configuration and modules. Returns the full emitter topology (no input values - call GetEmitterInputValues for values). Params: `system, templateEmitter, emitterName` |
| `epic_add_module(moduleLocationRef:o, moduleAsset:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a module to a script stack. The module will be inserted into the specified script's execution stack. Returns the module topology with all inputs walked (no input values - call GetModuleInputValues for values). Params: `moduleLocationRef, moduleAsset` |
| `epic_add_renderer(newRendererLocation:o, rendererClass:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a renderer to an emitter. Creates a new renderer of the specified type and adds it to the emitter's renderer list. Returns an FNiagaraExt_RendererRef with the new renderer's Index and RendererClass, usable directly with SetRendererData / GetRendererData without a follow-up topology call. Params: `newRendererLocation, rendererClass` |
| `epic_add_set_parameter_entry(moduleRef:o, entry:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a single parameter to an existing SetParameters module. The module referenced by ModuleRef must be a SetParameters (UNiagaraNodeAssignment) module. Use bIsSetParametersModule in the module topology to confirm before calling. Params: `moduleRef, entry` |
| `epic_add_set_parameters_module(moduleLocationRef:o, parameters:[o])` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds a SetParameters module to a script stack. Unlike AddModule which requires a script asset, a SetParameters module dynamically assigns values to named parameters and generates its own internal script. Use this when you need to set one or more particle/emitter/system parameters directly in the stack. Params: `moduleLocationRef, parameters` |
| `epic_add_user_variables(system:ref, variablesToAdd:[o])` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Adds or updates user variables on a system. If a variable with the same name already exists, it will be replaced with the new definition. Params: `system, variablesToAdd` |
| `epic_apply_stack_issue_fix(system:ref, issueId, fixId)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Applies a Fix-style stack issue fix identified by IssueId and FixId. Link-style fixes are rejected. The fix is undoable via the editor undo stack. Applying a fix may trigger a recompile; the result waits for that compile to complete so post-fix state is valid. Params: `system, issueId, fixId` |
| `epic_construct_niagara_bpwrapper_from_component(newAssetPath, component:ref, parentClass:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Blueprint] Creates a Blueprint actor wrapper from a Niagara Component. This generates a new Blueprint actor and preserves all component property values and user variable overrides. Params: `newAssetPath, component, parentClass` |
| `epic_construct_niagara_bpwrapper_from_system(newAssetPath, system:ref, parentClass:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Blueprint] Creates a Blueprint actor wrapper around a Niagara System. This generates a new Blueprint actor with a Niagara component configured to use the specified system. Params: `newAssetPath, system, parentClass` |
| `epic_create_niagara_system(assetName, assetPath, templateSystem:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Creates a new Niagara System asset. The new system will be based on the template system, inheriting its configuration and emitters. Params: `assetName, assetPath, templateSystem` |
| `epic_find_niagara_scripts(folderPath, name, usages:[s], visibilities:[s], moduleUsageBitmask?:i, bRecursive:b, bIncludeDeprecated:b, supportedUsages?:[s])` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Searches for UNiagaraScript assets matching the given filters. Params: `folderPath, name, usages, visibilities, moduleUsageBitmask?, bRecursive, bIncludeDeprecated, supportedUsages?` |
| `epic_get_asset_discovery_info()` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Returns the project's configured asset discovery groups. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_available_dynamic_inputs(type:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all available Dynamic Input Module assets compatible with the given type. Dynamic inputs provide procedural value generation for module parameters. Params: `type` |
| `epic_get_data_interface_schema(dataInterfaceClass:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for a specific Data Interface class. Describes all available properties and their types for the given data interface type. Params: `dataInterfaceClass` |
| `epic_get_dynamic_input_chain(stackInputRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the full recursive chain for a dynamic input: topology metadata and resolved values at every level. The starting input must have value mode Dynamic; an error is surfaced otherwise. The schema expands one full level and emits a typed recursion stub at deeper levels; the wire format recurses to arbitrary depth matching the underlying chain. Params: `stackInputRef` |
| `epic_get_dynamic_input_schema(dynamicInputReference?:o, stackInputRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a dynamic input module in the stack. Describes the inputs and configuration for a procedural value generator. Params: `dynamicInputReference?, stackInputRef?` |
| `epic_get_dynamic_input_schema_from_asset(dynamicInputAsset:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a dynamic input asset. Standalone function that doesn't require a system context - useful for browsing available dynamic inputs. Params: `dynamicInputAsset` |
| `epic_get_emitter_data(emitterRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns emitter property values as a single JSON-string blob in PropertyValues. The blob contains the full FVersionedNiagaraEmitterData (SimTarget, bLocalSpace, RandomSeed, FixedBounds, etc.) - fields use C++ PascalCase, must be parsed to read individual values. For typed access to common metadata (SimTarget, EmitterName, bEnabled, RendererClasses) prefer GetEmitterSummary - it returns those as named fields directly and avoids a JSON parse step. Use this endpoint when you need the full property set or a less-common field. Params: `emitterRef` |
| `epic_get_emitter_input_values(emitterRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all resolved input values for every module across all four emitter script stacks. One FNiagaraExt_ModuleInputValues entry per module, each carrying all its resolved input values. Call this in parallel with GetEmitterTopology to get both structure and values in two passes. Params: `emitterRef` |
| `epic_get_emitter_schema()` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for Niagara Emitter. Describes all available properties and their types that can be set on a Niagara Emitter. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_emitter_summary(emitterRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns lightweight emitter metadata: name, enabled state, sim target, renderer classes. Use this when you only need to check metadata without walking the full emitter structure. Params: `emitterRef` |
| `epic_get_emitter_topology(emitterRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns full emitter topology: four script stacks with all modules and inputs, renderer references. All fields always populated. The returned topology carries no input values; call GetEmitterInputValues in parallel. Params: `emitterRef` |
| `epic_get_module_input_values(moduleRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns resolved input values for a single module. Use when you need values for one specific module without walking the whole emitter. Params: `moduleRef` |
| `epic_get_module_schema(moduleReference?:o, moduleRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a module and all its inputs. Call this after seeing a module in topology to understand what inputs it exposes. Params: `moduleReference?, moduleRef?` |
| `epic_get_module_schema_from_asset(moduleAsset:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a module asset. Standalone function that doesn't require a system context - useful for browsing available modules. Params: `moduleAsset` |
| `epic_get_module_topology(moduleRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns module topology: metadata and all inputs (name/type/visibility only, no values). All fields always populated. Params: `moduleRef` |
| `epic_get_niagara_script_digest(objectPath)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Returns the decoded asset-registry tag metadata for a Niagara script asset. Params: `objectPath` |
| `epic_get_renderer_data(rendererRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns renderer property values. Retrieves the current values of all configurable renderer properties. Params: `rendererRef` |
| `epic_get_renderer_schema(rendererClass:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for a specific Renderer class. Describes all available properties and their types for the given renderer type. Params: `rendererClass` |
| `epic_get_script_stack_input_values(scriptRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all resolved input values for every module in the given script stack. One FNiagaraExt_ModuleInputValues entry per module. Params: `scriptRef` |
| `epic_get_script_stack_topology(scriptRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns script stack topology: all modules and their inputs in execution order. All fields always populated. Params: `scriptRef` |
| `epic_get_stack_input_data(stackInputRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the value of a stack module input. Retrieves the current value and configuration for a specific module input parameter. Params: `stackInputRef` |
| `epic_get_stack_input_schema(inputReference?:o, stackInputRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns schema for a single module input in the stack. Describes the type, metadata, and configuration options for a specific input parameter. Params: `inputReference?, stackInputRef?` |
| `epic_get_stack_input_topology(stackInputRef:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns stack input topology: name, type, visibility, editability. No value payload. For the resolved value call GetStackInputData. For a dynamic-input chain call GetDynamicInputChain. Params: `stackInputRef` |
| `epic_get_stack_issues(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all stack issues (errors, warnings, info) from the Niagara module stack, including dismissed ones. Waits for any in-flight compile to complete before collecting. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_system_compile_state(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the current compile state of a Niagara System: aggregate status, per-script compile events, and summary flags. Waits for any in-flight compile to complete before collecting. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_system_data(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns system property values. Retrieves the current values of all configurable system-level properties. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_system_dependencies(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns the four Used* sets (renderers, data interfaces, modules, dynamic inputs) gathered across all emitters and system scripts. These sets are not included in topology structs; call this endpoint separately when needed. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_system_schema()` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns property schema for Niagara System. Describes all available properties and their types that can be set on a Niagara System. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_system_summary(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns lightweight system metadata: name, user variables, and one summary entry per emitter. Use this for first contact with an unfamiliar system. For full structural detail call GetEmitterTopology per emitter. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_user_variables(component:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Returns all user variable values currently set on the component. This retrieves the current values of all user-exposed parameters that can be overridden at the component level. Params: `component` |
| `epic_get_user_variables__niagara_toolset_system(system:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Returns all user variables defined on the system. User variables are parameters exposed for external control and can be overridden per component instance. Params: `system` |
| `epic_get_variable(component:ref, var:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Gets the current value of a specific user variable on the component. This retrieves the current value of a user-exposed parameter, including any component-level overrides. Params: `component, var` |
| `epic_remove_emitter(emitterToRemove?:o, emitterRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes an emitter from a system. Deletes the specified emitter and all its associated scripts, modules, and renderers. Params: `emitterToRemove?, emitterRef?` |
| `epic_remove_module(moduleToRemove?:o, moduleRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a module from a script stack. Deletes the specified module and all its inputs from the script's execution stack. Params: `moduleToRemove?, moduleRef?` |
| `epic_remove_renderer(rendererToRemove?:o, rendererRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a renderer from an emitter. Deletes the specified renderer from the emitter's renderer list. Params: `rendererToRemove?, rendererRef?` |
| `epic_remove_set_parameter_entry(moduleRef:o, parameterName)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes a parameter from an existing SetParameters module by name. The module referenced by ModuleRef must be a SetParameters (UNiagaraNodeAssignment) module. Use bIsSetParametersModule in the module topology to confirm before calling. Params: `moduleRef, parameterName` |
| `epic_remove_user_variables(system:ref, variablesToRemove:[o])` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Removes user variables from a system. Deletes the specified user variables from the system's user parameter collection. Params: `system, variablesToRemove` |
| `epic_set_emitter_data(emitter?:o, emitterData:o, emitterRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara Emitter. Applies new values to emitter-level properties based on the provided data structure. Params: `emitter?, emitterData, emitterRef?` |
| `epic_set_module_enabled(moduleRef:o, bEnabled:b)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets whether a module is enabled. Disabled modules remain in the stack but don't execute. Current state is visible in module topology. Params: `moduleRef, bEnabled` |
| `epic_set_niagara_script_description(objectPath, newDescription, versionTarget)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Assets] Sets the Description field on a Niagara script's FVersionedNiagaraScriptData. Does not checkout or save the asset but will update the asset registry tags. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `objectPath, newDescription, versionTarget` |
| `epic_set_renderer_data(renderer?:o, rendererData:o, rendererRef?:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara Renderer. Applies new values to renderer properties based on the provided data structure. Payload shape varies with the concrete renderer class; call GetRendererSchema for the renderer's class to inspect valid properties before writing. Params: `renderer?, rendererData, rendererRef?` |
| `epic_set_stack_input_data(stackInputRef:o, inputData:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets the value of a stack module input and returns the resulting stored value. Updates the value and configuration for a specific module input parameter. Params: `stackInputRef, inputData` |
| `epic_set_system(niagaraComponent:ref, system:ref, bResetExistingOverrideParameters:b)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Sets the Niagara System for a component. Use this instead of setting the Asset property directly to ensure proper initialization. Params: `niagaraComponent, system, bResetExistingOverrideParameters` |
| `epic_set_system_data(system:ref, systemData:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System] Sets property values on a Niagara System. Applies new values to system-level properties based on the provided data structure. Params: `system, systemData` |
| `epic_set_variable(component:ref, variable:o)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Component] Sets the value of a user variable on the component. This overrides the default value of a user-exposed parameter on a specific component instance. Params: `component, variable` |
| `epic_uenum_info(enum:ref)` | [Epic NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_Info] Returns information about a UEnum and all its values. ALWAYS call this when working with a UEnum type to see valid values. Params: `enum` |

---

## audio

*Audio: sound assets, playback, MetaSound + SoundCue graph authoring, submixes/effects, sound classes/mixes, attenuation, concurrency, spatialization.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list(directory?, recursive?:b, offset?:n, cursor?, limit\|maxResults?:i)` | List sound assets (SoundWave, SoundCue, MetaSoundSource) under a directory, cursor-paginated (#730). Every page carries count, total, hasMore and a nextCursor to pass back. The row offset this used to page with is refused, because a row number cannot report that the library changed underneath it. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit and sizes the page when limit is omitted. Params: `directory?, recursive?, offset?, cursor?, limit? (or maxResults)` |
| `extract_pcm(soundPath\|assetPath, maxSeconds?:n, downmixMono?:b)` | Decode a USoundWave's imported audio to in-memory PCM (no intermediate file, no reliance on the original source path) for semantic sound search / analysis (#729). Returns sampleRate, numChannels, numFrames, durationSeconds, and 16-bit PCM samples base64-encoded (interleaved). Params: `soundPath (or assetPath), maxSeconds?, downmixMono?` |
| `import_audio(filePath\|filename, name\|assetName?, packagePath\|destinationPath?, looping?:b, replaceExisting?:b)` | Import a WAV/OGG/FLAC file as a USoundWave. Returns durationSeconds, numChannels, looping. Params: `filePath (or filename), name? (or assetName), packagePath? (or destinationPath), looping?, replaceExisting?` |
| `play_at_location(soundPath\|assetPath\|path, location?:v, volumeMultiplier\|volume?:n, pitchMultiplier\|pitch?:n)` | Play a sound in the editor world. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath, or path), location?, volumeMultiplier? (or volume), pitchMultiplier? (or pitch)` |
| `spawn_ambient(soundPath\|assetPath\|path, location?:v, label?, onConflict?, volumeMultiplier\|volume?:n)` | Place an AmbientSound actor playing a sound. A sound that does not load is refused rather than placing a silent actor. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath, or path), location?, label?, onConflict?, volumeMultiplier? (or volume)` |
| `metasound_author(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, format?, oneShot?:b, inputs?:[o], outputs?:[o], nodes?:[o], connections?:[o])` | PREFERRED: stamp a whole MetaSound graph in ONE call from a declarative spec (avoids dozens of add_node/connect round-trips). Creates the asset through UMetaSoundSourceFactory, which is the only route that produces a document with interfaces and a graph page, then writes every element straight into that asset's own document and saves at the end. Each element reports its own ok/error. Read the result back with metasound_read_document. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, format?, oneShot?, inputs?, outputs?, nodes?, connections?` |
| `create_metasound(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, format?, oneShot?:b)` | Create a MetaSoundSource through its own asset factory (which installs the UE.Source, one-shot and output-format interfaces and mints the default graph page) ready for INCREMENTAL authoring with add_node/connect/... For a whole graph at once prefer metasound_author. The incremental actions do NOT depend on this call: they attach a builder to whatever asset they are pointed at, so a MetaSound already on disk, or one from an earlier editor run, is editable without it. Returns the asset path. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, format?, oneShot?` |
| `metasound_list_node_classes(filter?)` | List common MetaSound node classes to add (name, namespace, variant, notes). Params: `filter?` |
| `metasound_get_graph(assetPath\|metasoundPath)` | SUPERSEDED for graph contents by metasound_read_document; kept for the one fact it still answers plainly: whether a builder is attached to this asset's document right now (hasActiveBuilder), plus audioOutputs and oneShot when this editor run has created or written to the asset. An attached builder does not mean unsaved work: the write actions edit the asset's own document and save it, and they attach a builder on demand, so this reports whether one is open rather than whether anything is pending. Asks only, and never attaches one itself. For nodes, pins, connections, variables, defaults and problems use metasound_read_document / metasound_list_connections / metasound_inspect_node / metasound_list_node_pins / metasound_search_nodes / metasound_list_variables / metasound_validate. Errors when assetPath names nothing, or names something that is not a MetaSoundSource. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath)` |
| `metasound_add_node(assetPath\|metasoundPath, nodeClassName, nodeNamespace?, nodeVariant?, majorVersion?:i)` | Add a node to a MetaSound graph by registered class name. Works on any MetaSound asset on disk: a builder is attached to the asset's own document on demand, so create_metasound is not a prerequisite and an asset from an earlier editor run is editable. Returns nodeId (+ input/output counts). Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), nodeClassName, nodeNamespace?, nodeVariant?, majorVersion?` |
| `metasound_add_input(assetPath\|metasoundPath, name, dataType, defaultValue?:*)` | Add a graph input to a MetaSound. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), name, dataType, defaultValue?` |
| `metasound_add_output(assetPath\|metasoundPath, name, dataType)` | Add a graph output to a MetaSound. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), name, dataType` |
| `metasound_connect(assetPath\|metasoundPath, fromNodeId, fromOutput, toNodeId, toInput)` | Connect one node's output vertex to another node's input vertex. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), fromNodeId, fromOutput, toNodeId, toInput` |
| `metasound_connect_input(assetPath\|metasoundPath, graphInput, toNodeId, toInput)` | Connect a graph input to a node input vertex. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), graphInput, toNodeId, toInput` |
| `metasound_connect_output(assetPath\|metasoundPath, fromNodeId, fromOutput, graphOutput)` | Connect a node output vertex to a graph output. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), fromNodeId, fromOutput, graphOutput` |
| `metasound_connect_audio_out(assetPath\|metasoundPath, fromNodeId, fromOutput, channel?:i)` | Connect a node output vertex to the source's audio output. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), fromNodeId, fromOutput, channel?` |
| `metasound_set_default(assetPath\|metasoundPath, value:*, dataType?, nodeId?, inputName?, graphInput?)` | Set a default value on a node input vertex (nodeId + inputName), or on a graph input (graphInput). Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), value, dataType?, nodeId?, inputName?, graphInput?` |
| `metasound_read_document(assetPath\|metasoundPath, pageId?, includeNodes?:b, includeConnections?:b)` | Read a MetaSound graph back: document version, declared interfaces, graph inputs and outputs with their defaults, variables, every node and every connection. This is the verification counterpart to metasound_author, and the reason it matters is that the bridge could BUILD a graph and never read it, so it could write but not verify or iterate. Reads the asset's own document, which is the same one the write actions edit, so there is no second unflushed copy that could disagree with it; source and hasActiveBuilder report whether a builder is attached to that document. Reports pageId and readDefaultPage, falling back to the first page the document holds when it declares none under the default page id. Node ids match what metasound_add_node returned. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), pageId?, includeNodes?, includeConnections?` |
| `metasound_list_connections(assetPath\|metasoundPath, pageId?, nodeId?, direction?, dataType?)` | List every edge in the graph, each reported using the exact field names metasound_connect takes (fromNodeId, fromOutput, toNodeId, toInput), so a listed connection can be echoed straight back as a call payload. Use it to see what is already wired before adding more. Malformed edges are counted separately rather than silently dropped. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), pageId?, nodeId?, direction?, dataType?` |
| `metasound_list_variables(assetPath\|metasoundPath, pageId?, filter?)` | List the graph's variables with data type, initial value, the node that sets each one and the node ids that read it, so a variable can be followed to the wiring that consumes it. Most graphs declare none, which is normal rather than a fault. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), pageId?, filter?` |
| `metasound_search_nodes(assetPath\|metasoundPath, pageId?, query?, dataType?, classType?, limit?:i)` | Find node INSTANCES inside one existing graph, by name, class, namespace, variant, data type or class type. This is the step between reading a document and acting on a node. Distinct from metasound_list_node_classes, which lists classes you could add rather than nodes already present. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), pageId?, query?, dataType?, classType?, limit?` |
| `metasound_inspect_node(assetPath\|metasoundPath, nodeId, pageId?)` | Inspect one node in full: its class identity in metasound_add_node's own parameter names, every input and output vertex with data type, default and connection state, and the incoming and outgoing edges named by node. A wrong nodeId comes back with the valid ones rather than a bare failure. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), nodeId, pageId?` |
| `metasound_list_node_pins(assetPath\|metasoundPath, nodeId, pageId?, direction?, dataType?)` | List just a node's input and output vertices with their types, connection state and set defaults, plus a count of unconnected inputs. The lean way to get the exact vertex names metasound_connect and metasound_set_input_default require, without reading the whole document. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), nodeId, pageId?, direction?, dataType?` |
| `metasound_validate(assetPath\|metasoundPath, pageId?)` | Diagnose a MetaSound graph and report actionable problems: undriven graph outputs, orphaned nodes, dead-end nodes, unconnected Trigger and Audio inputs, cross-type edges, dangling edges, and unread or unwritten variables. Returns problems[] naming the node and the call that fixes it, plus runnable. This is what catches the graph that builds successfully and then plays silence. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), pageId?` |
| `metasound_build(assetPath\|metasoundPath)` | SAVE the MetaSound asset to disk. Despite the name this compiles nothing and flushes nothing: every authoring action writes straight into the asset's own document, so what this adds is persistence, and it is what makes edits survive an editor restart. A read does not need it, since the reads see the same document. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath)` |
| `metasound_remove_node(assetPath\|metasoundPath, nodeId, removeUnusedDependencies?:b)` | Remove a node from a MetaSound graph, with every edge that touched it. Attaches a builder to the asset's own document the way the MetaSound editor does, so a MetaSound already on disk, from any editor run, can be edited with no create call first. The edit lands in that document and is saved, so pendingBuild comes back false and metasound_build is not needed after it; source says whether a builder was already attached when the call arrived. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the id is not in the graph, and the miss lists the ids that are. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), nodeId, removeUnusedDependencies?` |
| `metasound_disconnect(assetPath\|metasoundPath, fromNodeId?, fromOutput?, toNodeId?, toInput?, graphOutput?)` | Cut MetaSound edges: the inverse of all four connect actions in one call, because they all reduce to the same two builder handles. Four addressing forms - all of fromNodeId, fromOutput, toNodeId and toInput drops that one edge and is the only form with an exact rollback; toNodeId plus toInput alone clears whatever drives that input; fromNodeId plus fromOutput alone clears every edge leaving that output; graphOutput clears what drives a graph output, which is also how an audio output is cleared since the audio outs are graph outputs named 'Out Mono', 'Out Left' and 'Out Right'. metasound_list_connections reports edges in these exact field names. Works on any MetaSound asset on disk, with no create call first, and saves the document it edited. Idempotent: alreadyDisconnected=true when nothing was connected there. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), fromNodeId?, fromOutput?, toNodeId?, toInput?, graphOutput?` |
| `metasound_remove_member(assetPath\|metasoundPath, memberKind, name)` | Remove a graph input, graph output or variable: the inverse of metasound_add_input and metasound_add_output, and the only removal path for a variable. Works on any MetaSound asset on disk, with no create call first, and saves the document it edited. The miss lists the members that do exist, and the result carries the removed member's dataType so the rollback can restore it. Note that every edge the member drove is cut with it, so read them with metasound_list_connections first if they matter. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the member is absent. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), memberKind, name` |
| `metasound_rename_member(assetPath\|metasoundPath, memberKind, name, newName)` | Rename a graph input or output on any MetaSound asset on disk, with no create call first, saving the document it edited. Not a property write: the rename rewires the template nodes that stand in for the member inside the graph, which a direct document write would leave dangling. Both names are checked first, so renaming onto an existing name is refused with the list rather than colliding, and a replay where the new name is already present reports unchanged=true. The inverse is the same call with the names swapped. Params: `assetPath (or metasoundPath), memberKind, name, newName` |
| `cue_author(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, nodes?:[o], connections?:[o], root?)` | PREFERRED: create a SoundCue and stamp its whole node tree in ONE call. Each element reports ok/error; links + saves at the end. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, nodes?, connections?, root?` |
| `create_cue(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create an empty SoundCue. Add a wave with cue_add_node, or prefer cue_author for a whole graph. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `cue_add_node(cuePath\|assetPath, nodeType, soundWavePath?, properties?:o)` | Add a node to a SoundCue graph. Returns nodeId. Params: `cuePath (or assetPath), nodeType, soundWavePath?, properties?` |
| `cue_connect(cuePath\|assetPath, childNodeId, parentNodeId?, childIndex?:i)` | Connect a SoundCue node as a child of another (or as the cue root). Params: `cuePath (or assetPath), childNodeId, parentNodeId?, childIndex?` |
| `cue_get_graph(cuePath\|assetPath)` | Read a SoundCue node graph: nodes (id, type, children) and root. Params: `cuePath (or assetPath)` |
| `cue_remove_node(cuePath\|assetPath, nodeId)` | Remove a node from a SoundCue: detach it from every parent, drop its paired editor graph node, and clear the cue root if it was the root. Its own children are ORPHANED rather than deleted, because they are separate nodes the caller may still want and an unasked-for cascade is the harder failure to recover from; they come back in orphanedChildren. Warns when the cue is left with no root, since the cue then plays nothing. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when the id is not in the cue, and the miss lists the ids that are. Params: `cuePath (or assetPath), nodeId` |
| `cue_disconnect(cuePath\|assetPath, childNodeId?, parentNodeId?, clearRoot?:b)` | Detach a SoundCue child from its parent: the inverse of cue_connect. With parentNodeId it removes that one link; without, it removes the child from every parent. clearRoot=true unsets the cue root instead, which is the inverse of a cue_connect that named no parent. Idempotent: alreadyDisconnected=true when the link was not there. Params: `cuePath (or assetPath), childNodeId?, parentNodeId?, clearRoot?` |
| `create_submix(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, parentPath?, outputVolume?:n, wetLevel?:n, dryLevel?:n)` | Create a USoundSubmix, optionally parented. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, parentPath?, outputVolume?, wetLevel?, dryLevel?` |
| `set_submix_parent(submixPath, parentPath?)` | Reparent a submix (sets ParentSubmix, updating both ends). Params: `submixPath, parentPath?` |
| `add_submix_effect(submixPath, effectType, name?, packagePath?, settings?:o)` | Append a submix effect preset to a submix's effect chain (creates the preset asset). Params: `submixPath, effectType, name?, packagePath?, settings?` |
| `create_sound_class(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, properties?:o, parentPath?)` | Create a USoundClass, optionally parented, with properties. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, properties?, parentPath?` |
| `set_sound_class_parent(soundClassPath\|assetPath, parentPath?)` | Reparent a sound class on all three sides: ParentClass on the child, ChildClasses on the new parent, and the removal from the old parent's list. Writing ParentClass with a property setter produces a class the audio engine walks up from and the mixer never walks down to, which is why this is a handler. An empty parentPath detaches to the root, and a parent already below this class is refused as a cycle. Reports listedOnParent, read back from the other end. Params: `soundClassPath (or assetPath), parentPath?` |
| `read_sound_routing(soundPath\|assetPath)` | Read where a sound actually goes: its sound class chain up to the root and its submix chain up to the master, each entry with its objectPath, plus submix sends, attenuation, concurrency, and problems[] naming the calls that fix them. This is the verification half of set_sound_submix, add_sound_submix_send, set_sound_class, set_sound_attenuation and set_sound_concurrency, which could all assign routing and none of which could read it back. Catches the cases that make a correctly authored mix silent anyway: a sound class at volume 0, a send at level 0, a duplicate send (add_sound_submix_send appends without checking), an attenuation with a falloff distance and bAttenuate off, a concurrency with MaxCount 0, and a cycle in either chain. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath)` |
| `create_sound_mix(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, fadeInTime?:n, fadeOutTime?:n, adjusters?:[o])` | Create a USoundMix with sound-class adjusters. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, fadeInTime?, fadeOutTime?, adjusters?` |
| `create_concurrency(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, maxCount?:i, limitToOwner?:b, volumeScale?:n, resolutionRule?)` | Create a USoundConcurrency asset. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, maxCount?, limitToOwner?, volumeScale?, resolutionRule?` |
| `create_attenuation(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, settings?:o, falloffDistance?:n, spatialize?:b, enableOcclusion?:b)` | Create a USoundAttenuation asset from a settings struct, with falloffDistance, spatialize and enableOcclusion as shortcuts over it. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, settings?, falloffDistance?, spatialize?, enableOcclusion?` |
| `set_sound_submix(soundPath\|assetPath, submixPath?)` | Set a sound's base submix (routing target). Params: `soundPath (or assetPath), submixPath?` |
| `add_sound_submix_send(soundPath\|assetPath, submixPath, sendLevel?:n)` | Add a submix send to a sound. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath), submixPath, sendLevel?` |
| `set_sound_class(soundPath\|assetPath, soundClassPath)` | Assign a sound class to a sound. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath), soundClassPath` |

| `set_sound_concurrency(soundPath\|assetPath, concurrencyPath?)` | Attach a concurrency asset to a sound. Params: `soundPath (or assetPath), concurrencyPath?` |
| `set_property(assetPath, propertyName, value:*)` | Set any UPROPERTY on an audio asset by (dotted) name, value as JSON. Handles nested structs, arrays, object refs. Params: `assetPath, propertyName, value` |
| `epic_add_graph_inputs(builderName, inputs:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Declares graph inputs. Each becomes a node whose ref is the input's own name. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, inputs, page?` |
| `epic_add_graph_outputs(builderName, outputs:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Declares graph outputs. Each becomes a node whose ref is the output's own name. | `epic_add_graph_page(builderName, page, bDuplicateLastGraph?:b, bSetAsBuildPage?:b)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Adds a paged graph. Page must be declared (FindRegisteredPages) and not already carried (the record's Pages). Duplicating copies topology but not graph-input defaults. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page, bDuplicateLastGraph?, bSetAsBuildPage?` |
| `epic_add_graph_variables(builderName, variables:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Declares graph variables, which carry state across blocks. Referenced by name thereafter. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, variables, page?` |
| `epic_add_nodes(builderName, nodes:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Adds nodes by registered class. Returns each new node's ref in the report's Nodes. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, nodes, page?` |
| `epic_add_variable_nodes(builderName, nodes:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Adds Set / Get / Delayed-Get nodes for already-declared graph variables. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, nodes, page?` |
| `epic_attach_builder_to_asset(assetPath, builderName, page)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Attaches an editable builder to an existing MetaSound under BuilderName, targeting Page. The builder is the engine's singleton for that asset, so anything else editing it in this editor shares the state. BuilderName is independent of the asset; any unused name works. Page is stated, not inherited: the page a builder arrives on differs by whether the asset is open, was opened earlier, or never has been, and those are indistinguishable from here. Pass "Default" unless the asset is paged. Fails without attaching on an unknown page, or one the asset does not carry -- AddGraphPage adopts it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPath, builderName, page` |
| `epic_build_to_asset(builderName, assetName, packagePath, author)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Writes the builder to a NEW asset on disk. Params: `builderName, assetName, packagePath, author` |
| `epic_clear_pins(builderName, pins:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Removes every edge touching the named pins, without knowing what is wired to them. | `epic_commit_builder_to_asset(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Saves an attached builder's edits back to its source asset and re-registers its graph, so the next play of the asset hears them. | `epic_connect(builderName, connections:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Wires outputs to inputs. Every edge is resolved before any is made. | `epic_create_patch_builder(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Creates a Patch builder registered under BuilderName. Persists for the session. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, outputFormat?, bIsOneShot?` |
| `epic_create_source_preset_builder(presetName, referencedSourcePath)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Creates a Source preset over an existing MetaSoundSource. The returned record's inputs are the whole overridable set; topology tools reject this builder. A restricted editor refuses a parent FindMetaSoundAssets would not list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `presetName, referencedSourcePath` |
| `epic_describe_graph(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] The whole document in one call: interfaces, graph I/O with defaults, variables, nodes with their pins and authored values, positions, and edges. The detailed read -- creating or attaching a builder reports the same document with its nodes named but not detailed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_describe_node(builderName, node, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] One node with its pins and the values authored onto them -- the record a document read reports. Errors when the ref names no node; a node that resolves but declares no pins reads back empty. A pin's ValueType is None when the node authored nothing, so the class default applies; DescribeNodeClass reports it. A connected pin uses neither -- the edge feeding it wins. Re-read refs per page: a duplicated page keeps the ids it was copied from. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, node, page?` |
| `epic_describe_node_class(namespace, name, variant)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundDiscoveryToolset] A registered class's default pins, without adding a node. Resolves the highest version.
