| `epic_detach_builder_from_asset(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Unregisters an attached builder and drops its attachment record. Returns BuilderName. Uncommitted edits are lost. Safe to call when the builder was already unregistered externally. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName` |
| `epic_diff_pages(builderName, pageA, pageB)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Compares two pages across topology and paged input defaults. Every array empty means they match. Matches by class, not id, so independently built pages compare usefully. Counts are significant: ten wave players against four reports six extras -- how many differ, not which. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, pageA, pageB` |
| `epic_disconnect(builderName, connections:[o], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Removes specific edges. Takes the same records a read reports. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, connections, page?` |
| `epic_export_wav(soundWave:ref, filePath)` | [Epic EditorToolset.SoundWaveToolset] Exports a SoundWave to a .wav file on disk. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `soundWave, filePath` |
| `epic_find_all_connections(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Every edge on Page, addressed by node ref. Edges whose pin names do not resolve against the document are dropped, not reported. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_find_all_nodes(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Every node on Page, interface and graph-I/O nodes included. Read DisplayName and AssetPath to tell what a node is: a nested patch or source registers its class name off the asset's GUID, so ClassName alone does not name it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_find_builder_interfaces(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Interfaces declared on this builder. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName` |
| `epic_find_data_types(pattern)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundDiscoveryToolset] Registered MetaSound data types matching Pattern, exact name first. TypeName is the spelling every data-type argument on this surface expects. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pattern` |
| `epic_find_graph_input_defaults(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Graph-input defaults on Page. Inputs with no default there are omitted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_find_graph_inputs(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Graph inputs as Name / DataType, with the default set on Page. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_find_graph_outputs(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Graph outputs as Name / DataType. Outputs carry no default, so Default is empty. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName` |
| `epic_find_graph_pages(builderName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Pages this asset carries, naming which one mutations target. For the wider set a page can be added from, call FindRegisteredPages. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName` |
| `epic_find_graph_variables(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Graph variables on Page as Name / DataType / Default. Their Set and Get nodes are in the node listing, named "Variable.Get.<Name>_<id>". Declaring a variable also adds a "Variable.<Name>_<id>" node holding its value, which performs no access. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_find_interface_input_nodes(builderName, interfaceName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Ids of the input nodes an interface contributes on the build page; empty when undeclared. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, interfaceName` |
| `epic_find_interface_output_nodes(builderName, interfaceName)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundInspectionToolset] Ids of the output nodes an interface contributes on the build page; empty when undeclared. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, interfaceName` |
| `epic_find_interfaces()` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundDiscoveryToolset] Every registered MetaSound interface, at its highest registered version. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_find_meta_sound_assets(pattern, maxResults?:i, firstResult?:i)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] MetaSound assets in content, ordered by path. Where preset authoring starts: each can parent a preset, and a preset that is not read-only can be attached and retuned. Lists only what this editor lets the user see. A restricted editor also drops any asset a preset would fail validation from: a preset's chain must end at a built-in MetaSound, not a project's own. The preset creators and AttachBuilderToAsset refuse the same assets there. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pattern, maxResults?, firstResult?` |
| `epic_find_node_classes(pattern, inputs:[s], outputs:[s], bIncludeNonAddable?:b, maxResults?:i, firstResult?:i, maxPerGroup?:i)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundDiscoveryToolset] Registered node classes matching Pattern, best first, one group per node. Highest versions only; no deprecated classes. No pins: describe the chosen class before wiring it. The session's first call waits on the asset scan, so an empty result means nothing matched. Every term must match the class triple, display name, description, keywords or category. Ranked by match strength, an exact name first; ties rank UE before Experimental. Asset MetaSounds are listed loaded or not, and match by asset name. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pattern, inputs, outputs, bIncludeNonAddable?, maxResults?, firstResult?, maxPerGroup?` |
| `epic_find_registered_pages()` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundDiscoveryToolset] Page names the project declares, Default first -- the set AddGraphPage draws from. A name means the same page on every MetaSound. For the pages one asset carries, read Pages off a graph record. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_import_file(folderPath, assetName, sourceFile, bReplaceExisting?:b, bSave?:b)` | [Epic EditorToolset.SoundWaveToolset] Imports an audio file from disk as a SoundWave asset. Accepts the extensions SoundFactory declares: wav, aif, aiff, ogg, flac, opus, mp3. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `folderPath, assetName, sourceFile, bReplaceExisting?, bSave?` |
| `epic_layout_graph(builderName, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Arranges the targeted page left to right by connection depth, discarding manual arrangement. Applied counts the nodes positioned, which is every node on the page, so zero with bOk set means the page held no nodes rather than that layout declined to run. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page?` |
| `epic_remove_graph_page(builderName, page)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Removes a paged graph. Removing the targeted page moves the builder to an adjacent one unreported -- read the next result's BuildPage. Default cannot be removed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page` |
| `epic_remove_graph_variables(builderName, variables:[s], page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Removes graph variables, every Set and Get node bound to them, and the edges those carried. Refs to those nodes are stale afterwards. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, variables, page?` |
| `epic_remove_nodes(builderName, nodes:[s], bRemoveUnusedDependencies?:b, page?)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Removes nodes and every edge touching them. Refs are stale afterwards. Removing an interface-provided node leaves the interface inconsistent. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, nodes, bRemoveUnusedDependencies?, page?` |
| `epic_set_build_page(builderName, page)` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Moves the builder to another page the asset carries. Every later edit lands there. Shared with the MetaSound editor, so an open editor follows. Transacted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, page` |
| `epic_set_defaults(builderName, defaults:[o])` | [Epic MetaSoundToolset.MetaSoundAuthoringToolset] Sets default values on node pins and graph inputs. A node pin on a preset aborts the whole call rather than failing that one item. A value carries no type; each is parsed against the data type of the pin it lands on. Scalars go bare -- "true", "440", "0.5", an object path -- and arrays as JSON. An empty value clears the default rather than setting one. Array values on a node pin do not render in the MetaSound editor. A graph-input default is page-scoped. Each entry's Page names where it lands, empty meaning the targeted page. Unlike the mutators a named page here writes there rather than failing -- the write is addressed, not applied in place. Node-pin defaults ignore Page; there is no paged form. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `builderName, defaults` |

---

## widget

*UMG Widget Blueprints, Editor Utility Widgets, and Editor Utility Blueprints. One parameter contract across every action (#798): the asset is always `assetPath`, an Unreal package path such as `/Game/UI/WBP_Example`; a widget inside the tree is always `widgetName`; its parent panel is always `parentWidgetName`; arguments for any wrapped `epic_*` action go in `input`, and a top-level `assetPath` is folded into the asset reference of the wrapped tool for you. A `.uasset` suffix, an object suffix (`.WBP_Example`), backslashes, and the legacy `path` / `widgetBlueprintPath` / `widgetBlueprint` spellings are accepted and normalized. Create actions take `assetPath` too; `name` plus `packagePath` remains valid and is composed into it. See [Widget parameter contract](widget-parameters.md).*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `read_tree(assetPath\|path)` | Read widget hierarchy. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `check_structure(assetPath\|path)` | Check the object ownership UWidgetBlueprint::ValidateGeneratedClass asserts, the usual suspect when a Widget Blueprint hangs or crashes the editor on compile or load: the designer WidgetTree is outered to the blueprint and every widget in it to that tree, and the generated class's archetype tree (the _C:WidgetTree prototype) is outered to the class and every widget in it to that archetype. Every object comes back with its path, expectedOuter, actualOuter and pass, plus unreachableWidgets (owned by the tree but in no hierarchy), and a pass/failures summary (#1350). Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `get_details(assetPath\|path, widgetName)` | Inspect widget (curated subset). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName` |
| `get_properties(assetPath\|path, widgetName, includeSubtree?:b)` | Full reflected property dump for a widget - every UPROPERTY (RenderOpacity, Visibility, ColorAndOpacity, Border padding/colors, Image brush TintColor/ImageSize, fonts, etc.) plus the slot block, for diagnosing visual bugs get_details omits. Pass includeSubtree to also dump children (#547). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, includeSubtree?` |
| `list_bindings(assetPath\|path, filterWidgetName?, filterProperty?)` | List designer property bindings on a WidgetBlueprint (the UE 5.7 Python API keeps them protected). Returns {widgetName, propertyName, functionName, bindingType}. Optional filterWidgetName/filterProperty (#530). Params: `assetPath (or path), filterWidgetName?, filterProperty?` |
| `clear_binding(assetPath\|path, widgetName, propertyName?)` | Remove designer binding(s) matching widgetName (and optional propertyName) from a WidgetBlueprint without opening the editor. Idempotent (#530). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, propertyName?` |
| `set_property(assetPath\|path, widgetName, propertyName, value\|propertyValue:*)` | Set widget property. Slot struct props take UE struct text that persists every field - `Slot.Size`=`(Value=1.0,SizeRule=Fill)`, `Slot.Padding`=`(Left=8,Top=8,Right=8,Bottom=8)` - or a nested field path like `Slot.Size.Value` / `Slot.Padding.Left`; an invalid value errors instead of silently writing 0 (#532). value may also be a JSON object or array, filled field by field (`Slot.Padding`={Left:8,Top:8,Right:8,Bottom:8}). An enum takes `Bottom`, `VAlign_Bottom`, `EVerticalAlignment::VAlign_Bottom` or an enumerator number; any other value is refused (#1540). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, propertyName, value (or propertyValue)` |
| `set_style(assetPath\|path, widgetName, propertyName, value:*)` | Set a full/nested style struct on a widget from JSON (FButtonStyle, FEditableTextBoxStyle, FSlateFontInfo, FSlateColor and their nested brushes) - what set_property's scalar path can't express. value is a JSON object mirroring the struct; propertyName is the struct property, e.g. WidgetStyle (#563). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, propertyName, value` |
| `reorder_child(assetPath\|path, widgetName, index:n)` | Reorder a widget among its parent panel's children (move to a sibling index) - e.g. insert a new row BETWEEN two existing children. move_widget only reparents (#635). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, index` |
| `bulk_set_properties(assetPath\|path, properties:[o])` | Apply many {widgetName, propertyName, value} style/property writes to a WidgetBlueprint in one call (single compile+save) - font/color/style stylesheet across many widgets (#563). propertyName takes the same paths as set_widget_property: slot.* (any case) on the widget's slot, dotted paths into structs, and its typed names; value is JSON (an object or array fills a struct or array, a string may be UE struct text). Each entry reports its own ok/error, and the rollback replays the previous values through this action (#1632). Params: `assetPath (or path), properties` |
| `list(recursive?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List Widget BPs, sorted by object path. Params: `recursive?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `read_animations(assetPath\|path)` | Read UMG animations. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `create_animation(assetPath\|path, animationName, durationSeconds?:n, displayRate?:n, displayLabel?)` | Create a UMG animation on a Widget Blueprint, with its MovieScene, display rate and playback range. Idempotent by animationName: a second call reports existed and leaves the timing alone. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, durationSeconds?, displayRate?, displayLabel?` |
| `delete_animation(assetPath\|path, animationName)` | Delete a UMG animation from a Widget Blueprint, including its bindings. The rollback recreates an empty animation of the same name and rate, so the tracks and keys are NOT restored. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName` |
| `get_animation(assetPath\|path, animationName)` | Read one UMG animation in full: display rate, tick resolution, playback range, and per bound widget every track, section, channel and key time/value in SECONDS, plus the event tracks. read_animations reports the shape, this reports the values, which is what verifies a key actually landed. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName` |
| `add_animation_track(assetPath\|path, animationName, widgetName, propertyName)` | Add a property track to a UMG animation, binding the widget into the animation first if it is not bound yet. The track class is chosen from the property's own reflected type; a property Sequencer cannot key is refused by name with the keyable types listed. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, widgetName, propertyName` |
| `remove_animation_track(assetPath\|path, animationName, widgetName, propertyName)` | Remove a property track from a UMG animation. The rollback re-adds the empty track, so its keys are NOT restored. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, widgetName, propertyName` |
| `add_animation_key(assetPath\|path, animationName, widgetName, propertyName, time:n, value:*, channel?, channelIndex?:i, interpolation?)` | Set a key on an animation track channel at a time in SECONDS, creating the track and the section if needed. Pick the channel by name (R/G/B/A, Left/Top/Right/Bottom, Translation.X) or by channelIndex; a miss lists the channels the section actually has. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, widgetName, propertyName, time, value, channel?, channelIndex?, interpolation?` |
| `remove_animation_key(assetPath\|path, animationName, widgetName, propertyName, time:n, channel?, channelIndex?:i)` | Remove the key at a time in SECONDS from an animation track channel. Removing a key that is not there reports unchanged rather than failing. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, widgetName, propertyName, time, channel?, channelIndex?` |
| `add_animation_event_key(assetPath\|path, animationName, functionName, time?:n, trackName?)` | Add an event key that calls a Widget Blueprint function at a time in SECONDS, creating the event track and its trigger section if needed. trackName defaults to Events. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, functionName, time?, trackName?` |
| `remove_animation_event_key(assetPath\|path, animationName, time?:n, trackName?)` | Remove the event key at a time in SECONDS from an animation event track. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, time?, trackName?` |
| `bind_animation_event(assetPath\|path, animationName, event?, userTag?)` | Bind an animation lifecycle event (Finished or Started) on a Widget Blueprint to a handler graph, creating the K2Node_WidgetAnimationEvent if it is not there. userTag scopes a Started binding. Idempotent: an existing binding reports existed. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, event?, userTag?` |
| `unbind_animation_event(assetPath\|path, animationName, event?, userTag?)` | Remove an animation lifecycle event binding from a Widget Blueprint. Params: `assetPath (or path), animationName, event?, userTag?` |
| `set_navigation(assetPath\|path, one(rules:[o]; widgetName), direction?, rule?, widgetToFocus?)` | Write UMG navigation rules on a widget: rule is Escape, Explicit, Wrap, Stop, Custom or CustomBoundary, direction is Up, Down, Left, Right, Next or Previous, and widgetToFocus names the target for Explicit. Creates the UWidgetNavigation subobject that set_property cannot make. Pass one write as widgetName + direction + rule, or many as rules[] of {widgetName, direction, rule, widgetToFocus}; the whole batch is validated before anything is written. Params: `assetPath (or path), rules OR widgetName, direction?, rule?, widgetToFocus?` |
| `clear_navigation(assetPath\|path, widgetName, direction?)` | Reset navigation rules on a widget back to Escape. Omit direction to clear all six. Clearing what is already clear reports unchanged. Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, direction?` |
| `restore_navigation(assetPath\|path, previous:[o])` | Restore navigation rules from a captured snapshot - the `previous` array that set_navigation and clear_navigation put in their rollback payload, so a failed flow can be undone by hand as well as by the runner. Params: `assetPath (or path), previous` |
| `audit_focus_chain(assetPath\|path)` | Read-only report over the whole widget tree: which widgets can take focus, their explicit navigation edges, widgets reachable from none of them, edges pointing at a missing/invisible/unfocusable target, and directions whose opposite does not lead back. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `audit_accessibility(assetPath\|path, minFontSize?:n, minHitSize?:n)` | Read-only accessibility report over the whole widget tree: font sizes under minFontSize, interactive widgets whose authored hit area is under minHitSize, and what could not be checked from authored values alone. Params: `assetPath (or path), minFontSize?, minHitSize?` |
| `get_runtime_focus_path(userIndex?:i)` | Read the live Slate focus path for a user index in PIE - which widget holds focus and the chain of widgets above it. Requires a running PIE or Game world; the editor's own focus is never reported. Params: `userIndex?` |
| `set_runtime_focus(widgetName, userIndex?:i, className?)` | Give keyboard focus to a named child of a live PIE widget, so a navigation chain can be walked and verified rather than predicted. Locate the host with className when more than one instance is up. Setting focus where it already is reports unchanged. Params: `widgetName, userIndex?, className?` |
| `create(any(assetPath\|path; name), packagePath?, parentClass?, onConflict?)` | Create Widget BP. assetPath is the full destination, e.g. /Game/UI/WBP_Example; name + packagePath is the older spelling of the same thing. Idempotent by path. Params: `at least one of assetPath (or path)/name, packagePath?, parentClass?, onConflict?` |
| `create_utility_widget(any(assetPath\|path; name), packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create editor utility widget. assetPath is the full destination; name + packagePath is the older spelling. Idempotent by path. Params: `at least one of assetPath (or path)/name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `run_utility_widget(assetPath\|path)` | Open editor utility widget. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `create_utility_blueprint(any(assetPath\|path; name), packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create editor utility blueprint. assetPath is the full destination; name + packagePath is the older spelling. Idempotent by path. Params: `at least one of assetPath (or path)/name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `run_utility_blueprint(assetPath\|path)` | Run editor utility blueprint. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `add_widget(assetPath\|path, widgetClass\|typeName, widgetName\|name?, parentWidgetName?)` | Add widget to widget tree. Idempotent by assetPath + widgetName: passing widgetName makes a retry safe, and the result carries requestedWidgetName/persistedWidgetName/renamed plus compileStatus. Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetClass (or typeName), widgetName? (or name), parentWidgetName?` |
| `build_tree(assetPath\|path, tree:o, parentWidgetName?)` | Build a nested widget subtree in one call (#1300). tree is one node {widgetClass, widgetName?, properties?, children?}, children nesting the same shape; properties take set_widget_property names, slot.* included, with JSON values (a string, number or bool goes through set_widget_property's routes, an object or array through the JSON setter). The whole spec is validated (classes, panels, unique and unused names) before anything is built, any failure undoes every widget it built, and the blueprint is compiled and saved once. Lands under parentWidgetName, else the root panel, else becomes the root. The one rollback is remove_widget on the subtree root, which removes everything under it. Wrap several siblings in a panel node. Params: `assetPath (or path), tree, parentWidgetName?` |
| `remove_widget(assetPath\|path, widgetName)` | Remove widget from tree. Idempotent, and clears the widget's Widget Blueprint GUID metadata so later compiles stop reporting a deleted variable (#799). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName` |
| `rename_widget(assetPath\|path, widgetName, newName)` | Rename a widget in place (#1679). It keeps its object, slot, sibling position and properties; the variable GUID, designer bindings, animation bindings, navigation rules, desired focus and graph get/set nodes move to the new name. Refuses a name another widget, variable or function holds, unless it is a BindWidget name on the native parent for a widget of the bound class, which is how a copied widget is fitted to a BindWidget contract. Reports referencesUpdated; idempotent by the new name; the rollback renames it back. Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, newName` |
| `move_widget(assetPath\|path, widgetName, newParentWidgetName\|parentWidgetName)` | Reparent widget. Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName, newParentWidgetName (or parentWidgetName)` |
| `set_root(assetPath\|path, widgetName)` | Replace WBP root with an existing widget by name (#365). Params: `assetPath (or path), widgetName` |
| `wrap_root(assetPath\|path, wrapperClass\|widgetClass, wrapperName?)` | Wrap the current root in a new panel widget (UMG 'Wrap With'). wrapperClass must be a UPanelWidget subclass (#365). Params: `assetPath (or path), wrapperClass (or widgetClass), wrapperName?` |
| `list_classes(filter?, module?, includeAbstract?:b, includeBlueprint?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List the UWidget classes this editor has loaded, grouped by the module that defines them, each with its full path, parent class, whether it is a panel that accepts children, and the slot properties its children take. This is how a CommonUI or project-C++ widget is discovered: pass a row's `name` to add_widget as widgetClass, or its `path` when two modules share a name. Loaded classes only, so a Widget Blueprint nothing has opened is absent (use list) and a class from a disabled plugin does not exist until project(enable_plugin) and a restart. Params: `filter?, module?, includeAbstract?, includeBlueprint?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_bind_widget_contract(any(className; assetPath\|path))` | Report the BindWidget contract a native UserWidget parent imposes: every UPROPERTY marked BindWidget, BindWidgetOptional, BindWidgetAnim or BindWidgetAnimOptional, with the exact widget name it demands, the class that name must be, whether it is optional, and which ancestor declares it. Metadata is not a property value and reflect_class does not report these keys, so this is the only way to learn the contract short of a failed compile. Pass className for the contract alone, or assetPath to also check one Widget Blueprint's own tree against its parent and get back satisfied/missing/wrongType. Params: `at least one of className/assetPath (or path)` |
| `audit_commonui(assetPath\|path?)` | Read-only CommonUI wiring report. Checks the rules that fail silently at runtime rather than at compile time: the plugin being enabled at all, GameViewportClientClass being a CommonGameViewportClient (without it gamepad navigation and Back do nothing), CommonInputSettings.InputData being set (without it no input action resolves and bound action bars render empty) and, when assetPath names a Widget Blueprint, an activatable widget with no DesiredFocusWidget, a CommonBoundActionBar with no ActionButtonClass, and CommonUI widgets with no Style. Every problem carries the exact call that fixes it. Params: `assetPath? (or path)` |
| `extract_subtree(sourceAssetPath\|sourcePath, sourceWidgetName\|widgetName, destinationAssetPath\|destinationPath, destinationParentClass?, destinationRootName?, dryRun?:b)` | Lift an authored designer subtree out of one WidgetBlueprint into a standalone one, using UMG's own clipboard serializer so hierarchy, child order, editable properties, panel slot data and named-slot content survive. The selected widget becomes the destination root. dryRun defaults to true and only returns the name mapping - pass dryRun=false to actually write the asset. The destination must be absent or empty; an exact-shape replay returns existed. The source is never compiled or saved. Params: `sourceAssetPath (or sourcePath), sourceWidgetName (or widgetName), destinationAssetPath (or destinationPath), destinationParentClass?, destinationRootName?, dryRun?` |
| `list_viewmodels(assetPath\|path)` | List the viewmodels a Widget Blueprint declares: viewModelName, viewModelId, viewModelClass, creationType (Manual, CreateInstance, GlobalViewModelCollection, PropertyPath, Resolver, Context), the global identifier or property path it is fetched by, the optional/setter/getter flags and how many bindings use it. Needs the UMG Viewmodel plugin (ModelViewViewModel) enabled. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `add_viewmodel(assetPath\|path, viewModelClass, viewModelName?, creationType?:{Manual,CreateInstance,GlobalViewModelCollection,PropertyPath,Resolver,Context}, globalViewModelIdentifier?, viewModelPropertyPath?, optional?:b, createSetter?:b, createGetter?:b, viewModelId?)` | Add a viewmodel to a Widget Blueprint. viewModelClass is a native MVVMViewModelBase subclass or a Blueprint viewmodel asset path; viewModelName defaults to the class name; creationType must be one the class allows, with globalViewModelIdentifier for GlobalViewModelCollection and viewModelPropertyPath for PropertyPath. Idempotent by viewModelName (same class reports existed). Saved, not compiled: run compile_viewmodels. The rollback removes it. Params: `assetPath (or path), viewModelClass, viewModelName?, creationType?, globalViewModelIdentifier?, viewModelPropertyPath?, optional?, createSetter?, createGetter?, viewModelId?` |
| `remove_viewmodel(assetPath\|path, viewModelName)` | Remove a viewmodel from a Widget Blueprint by viewModelName. Bindings that use it are left in place and listed as bindingsLeftDangling. The rollback re-adds it with the same id, so those bindings resolve again. Removing one that is not there reports alreadyDeleted. Params: `assetPath (or path), viewModelName` |
| `list_viewmodel_bindings(assetPath\|path)` | List a Widget Blueprint's viewmodel bindings: bindingId, displayName, sourcePath and destinationPath (ViewModelName.Field, WidgetName.Property or Self.Member), bindingMode, executionMode (Default when not overridden), enabled, includeInCompile, the conversion function with its direction and arguments ({path} or {literal} per input), and the errors and warnings the last compile recorded on it. Every row is also valid add_viewmodel_binding input. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `add_viewmodel_binding(assetPath\|path, sourcePath?, destinationPath?, bindingMode?:{OneTimeToDestination,OneWayToDestination,TwoWay,OneWayToSource}, executionMode?:{Default,Immediate,Delayed,Tick,Auto}, conversionFunction?, conversionArguments?:o, conversionDirection?:{sourceToDestination,destinationToSource}, enabled?:b, includeInCompile?:b)` | Add a viewmodel binding. Paths start with a viewmodel name, a widget name or Self and walk fields: sourcePath PlayerVM.Health to destinationPath HealthBar.Percent. bindingMode defaults to OneWayToDestination. conversionFunction (Class.Function, /Script/Module.Class:Function, or a function on the blueprint) converts the value; conversionArguments set its inputs by pin name to a literal or {path}, and sourcePath goes to the first input no argument names. Idempotent: the same destination, mode and source (or conversion) reports existed. Saved, not compiled. The rollback removes it. Params: `assetPath (or path), sourcePath?, destinationPath?, bindingMode?, executionMode?, conversionFunction?, conversionArguments?, conversionDirection?, enabled?, includeInCompile?` |
| `update_viewmodel_binding(assetPath\|path, bindingId, sourcePath?, destinationPath?, bindingMode?:{OneTimeToDestination,OneWayToDestination,TwoWay,OneWayToSource}, executionMode?:{Default,Immediate,Delayed,Tick,Auto}, conversionFunction?, conversionArguments?:o, conversionDirection?:{sourceToDestination,destinationToSource}, enabled?:b, includeInCompile?:b)` | Change an existing viewmodel binding by bindingId: any of sourcePath, destinationPath, bindingMode, executionMode (Default clears the override), conversionFunction (empty string removes it) with conversionArguments, enabled, includeInCompile. A call that changes nothing reports unchanged. The rollback restores the previous values. Params: `assetPath (or path), bindingId, sourcePath?, destinationPath?, bindingMode?, executionMode?, conversionFunction?, conversionArguments?, conversionDirection?, enabled?, includeInCompile?` |
| `remove_viewmodel_binding(assetPath\|path, bindingId)` | Remove a viewmodel binding by bindingId. The rollback re-adds it from its captured paths, mode, flags and conversion (under a new id). Removing one that is not there reports alreadyDeleted. Params: `assetPath (or path), bindingId` |
| `compile_viewmodels(assetPath\|path)` | Compile a Widget Blueprint and report its viewmodel bindings with the errors and warnings the viewmodel compiler recorded on each (bindingErrorCount), plus compileStatus. Saved when the compile succeeds. Params: `assetPath (or path)` |
| `list_runtime(classFilter?, namePrefix?, viewportOnly?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)` | (#160) List live UUserWidget instances in the PIE world, sorted by object path. Params: `classFilter?, namePrefix?, viewportOnly?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_runtime(any(widgetName; className), childName?, maxDepth?:i, includeLayout?:b)` | (#160) Inspect a live PIE widget tree with text/visibility/brush/percent plus style values: renderOpacity (all), colorAndOpacity (TextBlock/Image), Border brushColor/contentColorAndOpacity (#592). includeLayout adds read-only layout diagnostics to every node - geometry (desired/local/absolute size, layout and render bounds), render transform, effective opacity, reflected slot properties including structured Canvas anchors/offsets/alignment, derived clipping, parent and viewport overlap, and a diagnostics array - plus the host UserWidget node under `host`, a `layoutCapture` summary, and per-node `deltaSincePreviousCapture` against the previous includeLayout call on that instance, so capture / reproduce / capture again isolates position-dependent sizing. Off by default: it is a much larger payload. A given widgetName and className must both match. Params: `at least one of widgetName/className, childName?, maxDepth?, includeLayout?` |
| `inspect_runtime_instances(widgetName?, classFilter?, propertyNames?:[s], includeSubtree?:b, childName?, childClassFilter?, viewportOnly?:b, world?, pieInstance?:i, maxInstances?:i, maxNodesPerInstance?:i)` | Inspect every matching live widget instance (never an implicit first match), with stable identity/owning-player metadata and selected reflected properties on the widget or subtree. Requires a running PIE/Game world and errors instead of falling back to the editor world. Passing childName or childClassFilter implies includeSubtree. Provide widgetName or classFilter. Params: `widgetName?, classFilter?, propertyNames?, includeSubtree?, childName?, childClassFilter?, viewportOnly?, world?, pieInstance?, maxInstances?, maxNodesPerInstance?` |
| `get_runtime_delegates(widgetName?, className?)` | (#161) Read delegate binding state on a live PIE widget, located by widgetName or className. Returns array of {delegateName, isBound, numBindings}. Params: `widgetName?, className?` |
| `add_to_viewport(assetPath\|path\|widgetBlueprintPath, zOrder?:n)` | (#602) Instantiate a WidgetBlueprint and add it to the live PIE viewport for visual verification. Requires PIE running. Params: `assetPath (or path, or widgetBlueprintPath), zOrder?` |
| `invoke_runtime_function(any(widgetName; className), functionName?, childName?, value?:*, commitMethod?)` | (#559/#812) Fire a UI interaction on a live PIE widget: a parameterless UFUNCTION (functionName) on the located UserWidget, OR drive an interactive child via childName - Button (click), CheckBox (value true/false/toggle), Slider and SpinBox (numeric value), EditableText/EditableTextBox/MultiLineEditableText/MultiLineEditableTextBox (string value), ComboBoxString (option string or index), CommonButtonBase (click through its HandleButtonClicked; OnPressed/OnReleased via functionName). The matching delegate is broadcast so bound Blueprint logic runs. functionName alongside childName picks the delegate (e.g. OnPressed, OnTextChanged). Locate the widget with widgetName or className. Params: `at least one of widgetName/className, functionName?, childName?, value?, commitMethod?` |
| `epic_activate_widget(widgetName, localPlayerIndex?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Activate a live activatable widget, as if the game had activated it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetName, localPlayerIndex?` |
| `epic_add_uicomponent(widgetBlueprint:ref, widgetName, componentClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Adds a UI component of the given class to the named widget. Params: `widgetBlueprint, widgetName, componentClass` |
| `epic_add_view_condition(widgetBlueprint:ref, sourceContext:ref, sourcePropertyPath, destinationContext:ref, destinationPropertyPath, operation, value:n, maxValue?:n)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Adds a condition to the WidgetBlueprint's View: when the source value changes and compares true against Value (Value to MaxValue for a Between operation), the destination is called or set. The widget blueprint is then compiled; compile errors do not fail the call and are reported in the condition's CompileErrors. Not supported during PIE. Values are compared as 32-bit floats. A destination function is called with default parameter values, and a destination property is set to its type's default value, not to the source value. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, sourceContext, sourcePropertyPath, destinationContext, destinationPropertyPath, operation, value, maxValue?` |
| `epic_add_view_model_property(viewModel:ref, propertyName, propertyType, defaultValue)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Add a property to an existing ViewModel. The ViewModel is compiled automatically when it is next added to a widget or used in a binding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `viewModel, propertyName, propertyType, defaultValue` |
| `epic_add_view_model_to_widget(widgetBlueprint:ref, viewModelClass:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Adds a ViewModel to the WidgetBlueprint Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, viewModelClass` |
| `epic_add_widget(widgetBlueprint:ref, widgetClass:ref, widgetDisplayName, parentWidget?:ref, childIndex?:i)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Adds a widget to the tree at the specified position. Returns full widget info including Slot pointer. When ParentWidget is null and no root exists, the new widget becomes the root of the tree. Use ObjectTools.list_properties on the returned Widget and Slot to get property names before calling set_properties. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `widgetBlueprint, widgetClass, widgetDisplayName, parentWidget?, childIndex?` |
| `epic_add_widget_to_animation(widgetBlueprint:ref, animation:ref, objectToBind:ref)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Add a UWidget (or a UPanelSlot with non-null content) as a possessable binding on a widget animation. Returns a FMovieSceneBindingProxy usable with every SequencerScripting method that takes a binding (MovieSceneBindingExtensions.AddTrack, etc.). ObjectToBind must be either: - A UWidget inside the Widget Blueprint's tree (typical case: animate a child widget's properties). - A UPanelSlot whose Content is non-null (animate slot properties like padding/anchors). The Widget Blueprint must have a compiled GeneratedClass. The implementation compiles the blueprint if needed before binding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, animation, objectToBind` |
| `epic_analog_input(key, value:n, userIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Send an analog axis value along the target user's focus path; 1D axes only, send 0 afterwards to release. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `key, value, userIndex?` |
| `epic_bind_to_event_property(widgetBlueprint:ref, eventName, propertyName, propertyClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Adds a Blueprint event handler graph node bound to a widget's multicast delegate event, Typical events: UButton::OnClicked / OnPressed / OnReleased / OnHovered / OnUnhovered, UCheckBox::OnCheckStateChanged, USlider::OnValueChanged. The matching delegate UPROPERTY must exist on PropertyClass (or a parent of it). Preconditions: - PropertyName must exist in the blueprint. - PropertyClass must be the widget's class (or a parent class) that declares the delegate. Params: `widgetBlueprint, eventName, propertyName, propertyClass` |
| `epic_clear_conversion_function_argument_path(widgetBlueprint:ref, bindingId, argumentName, bSourceToDestination?:b)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Removes the property path bound to an input pin of a binding's conversion function, resetting the pin to its default literal, then recompiles the WidgetBlueprint. The compiler does not warn if the cleared pin carried the binding's source value. If the recompile fails the edit is kept; use CompileWidgetBlueprint to read the errors. Not supported during PIE. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, bindingId, argumentName, bSourceToDestination?` |
| `epic_clear_focus_log()` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] Clears all recorded events. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_clear_highlight()` | [Epic WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem] Remove any highlight overlay drawn by Highlight. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_clear_widget_lifetime_log()` | [Epic UMGEditor.UMGDebuggerSubsystem] Discards all captured events. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_click(ref, button?, doubleClick?:b, modifiers?:o, params?:o)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Click a Slate widget identified by its ref. Returns false without clicking when the target point would not receive the event -- something is on top of it, the widget has no arranged size, or MouseDown still holds the button. The log and LastRefusal() name the reason. True means the event was delivered to the widget's branch, not that the widget handled it. Params: `ref, button?, doubleClick?, modifiers?, params?` |
| `epic_compile_widget_blueprint(widgetBlueprint:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Compiles a widget blueprint. Returns false with error details if compilation fails. Errors include missing BindWidget bindings, type mismatches, and graph errors. Call after all widgets and properties are set. Save separately via AssetTools.save_asset. Params: `widgetBlueprint` |
| `epic_create_and_add_widget(widgetBlueprint:ref, widgetClass:ref, widgetDisplayName, parentWidget?:ref, childIndex?:i)` | [Epic UMGEditor.WidgetBlueprintEditorSubsystem] Adds a widget to the tree at the specified position. When ParentWidget is null and no root exists, the new widget becomes the root of the tree. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, widgetClass, widgetDisplayName, parentWidget?, childIndex?` |
| `epic_create_view_binding(widgetBlueprint:ref, sourceContext:ref, sourcePropertyPath, destinationContext:ref, destinationPropertyPath, conversionName)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Creates a View Binding from the SourceProperty to the Destination property. If ConversionName is given, that conversion function is used, even if the property types already match (e.g. to format a FText). Otherwise, if there is a type mismatch, an existing conversion function will try to be used. Property paths resolve against each segment's declared type, so a field that only exists on a subclass of an intermediate object's declared type won't resolve. Bind to the intermediate object and cast inside a conversion function instead. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, sourceContext, sourcePropertyPath, destinationContext, destinationPropertyPath, conversionName` |
| `epic_create_view_event_binding(widgetBlueprint:ref, eventContext:ref, eventPropertyPath, destinationContext:ref, destinationPropertyPath)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Creates a View Event Binding from the EventProperty to the Destination property. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, eventContext, eventPropertyPath, destinationContext, destinationPropertyPath` |
| `epic_create_view_model(viewModelName, packagePath, parentClass:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Creates a new ViewModel asset Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `viewModelName, packagePath, parentClass` |
| `epic_create_widget_animation(widgetBlueprint:ref, animationName, lengthSeconds?:n)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Create a new UWidgetAnimation on a Widget Blueprint and return its summary. The empty FWidgetAnimationInfo return signals failure (Animation == nullptr). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, animationName, lengthSeconds?` |
| `epic_create_widget_blueprint(folderPath, assetName, parentClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Creates a new Widget Blueprint asset. Returns the blueprint or nullptr on failure. Params: `folderPath, assetName, parentClass` |
| `epic_deactivate_widget(widgetName, localPlayerIndex?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Deactivate a live activatable widget. Same addressing rules as ActivateWidget, but matches only currently-active widgets. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetName, localPlayerIndex?` |
| `epic_describe_widget(widgetBlueprint:ref, startWidget?:ref, maxDepth?:i, propertyNameFilter?, bSkipDefaultValues?:b, bIncludeFullDescription?:b, bIncludeComposedColors?:b)` | [Epic WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset] Full structured description of every widget in the tree (or the subtree rooted at StartWidget). Values are the designer-time state stored in the asset. Anything set at runtime (for example a Blueprint graph changing a slot through SlotAsCanvasSlot, or style state that is not a UPROPERTY) does not appear; use TraceWidgetPropertyOverrides for graph writes. ComposedColors reports the composed pre-display **linear** tint only -- never a display-space value, and never for URichTextBlock/CommonRichTextBlock (a fundamentally different per-inline-tag-run model, excluded from v1 coverage). It does not model the contrast setting, DisplayGamma, retainer boxes, Button's DisabledEffect, or widget animations. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, startWidget?, maxDepth?, propertyNameFilter?, bSkipDefaultValues?, bIncludeFullDescription?, bIncludeComposedColors?` |
| `epic_drag(startRef, endRef, modifiers?:o, params?:o)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Drag from one Slate widget to another (mouse down, stepped move, release). Both ends are hit-tested first; returns false without dragging if either is covered or unarranged. The pointer is stepped along the path, so drag detection fires partway and the target receives OnDragOver, including once at the drop point. Waypoints bend that path, for gestures a straight line would not produce. Start and end positions are normalized within each widget and default to the center. Use them to aim at edge-band drop zones, e.g. EndPosition.Y = 0.1 to drop against the target's top edge. Leave EndRef empty and pass MoveBy or Waypoints to drag StartRef by a distance instead of onto another widget, e.g. splitters, sliders, scrollbars and divider grips. EndPosition is then ignored, and a path that never leaves the press point is refused since the drag would not move. Params: `startRef, endRef, modifiers?, params?` |
| `epic_fill_form(fields:[o])` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Fill multiple Slate form fields at once. Params: `fields` |
| `epic_find_widget_animation(widgetBlueprint:ref, animationName)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Find an animation by internal name. Returns empty info (Animation == nullptr) when not found. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, animationName` |
| `epic_fixup_mvvmdata(widgetBlueprint:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Attempts to fixup MVVM data. This function can be called if the MVVM Generated Blueprint graphs like conversion functions report compilation errors. It regenerates the graphs to ensure parity with view binding data. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint` |
| `epic_focus(ref, userIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Set Slate keyboard/navigation focus to a widget, e.g. before gamepad navigation in PIE. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `ref, userIndex?` |
| `epic_get_action_bindings(localPlayerIndex?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] All UI action bindings currently active (reachable by input) for a player. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `localPlayerIndex?` |
| `epic_get_activatable_tree(localPlayerIndex?:i, bIncludeFullDump?:b)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Snapshot of the CommonUI activatable tree: root nodes, action-domain roots with children and bindings, active root, leafmost active widget, and optionally the full-depth indented tree dump text. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `localPlayerIndex?, bIncludeFullDump?` |
| `epic_get_container_widget_navigation_doc(widgetClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGEditor.WidgetBlueprintEditorSubsystem] Returns navigation/focus documentation for a container widget class - both layout panels (UScrollBox, UVerticalBox, ...) and list views (UListView, UTileView, ...). Reads from the class's Navigation* UCLASS meta and its ancestors', so it needs only a class, not a widget instance. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetClass` |
| `epic_get_current_focus(userIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] What has focus RIGHT NOW for a user, queried live from Slate, with its full widget path. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `userIndex?` |
| `epic_get_event_logging_status()` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] The current status of the logger: on/off, event count, dropped count, time span, subscribed players. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_event_timeline(maxCount?:i, eventTypeFilter?, localPlayerIndex?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Chronological digest of logged events, oldest first. Never carries callstacks; use GetLoggedEvents when those are wanted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `maxCount?, eventTypeFilter?, localPlayerIndex?` |
| `epic_get_focus_event_detail(seq:i)` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] The full causal chain for ONE event, located precisely by its sequence number (from any GetFocusEvents/GetFocusTimeline row). FocusReceived -> full path + symbolicated callstack + context + linked input/nav; other event types -> that record bare. bFound=false if evicted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `seq` |
| `epic_get_focus_events(widgetNameFilter, eventTypeFilter, focusCauseFilter?, userIndex?:i, maxCount?:i, bIncludePath?:b)` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] Recent events (newest first), filtered. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetNameFilter, eventTypeFilter, focusCauseFilter?, userIndex?, maxCount?, bIncludePath?` |
| `epic_get_focus_log_status()` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] Recording status: on/off, record count, dropped count, time span. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

| `epic_get_umginfo(ref)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Resolve a Slate widget ref back to the UMG UWidget that created it (for UMG and PIE UIs). "resolvedVia" is "self" when the widget itself carries UMG metadata, or "parent" when an ancestor did. On failure Error is set and Widget is null: either the widget is pure Slate with no UMG owner, or its authoring UWidget has since been destroyed. The remaining metadata fields are still filled in for the latter case. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `ref` |
| `epic_get_view_model_connection_map(viewModelClass:ref, scopeFilter?)` | [Epic WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset] Reverse-searches every Widget Blueprint whose MVVM View references ViewModelClass, and returns each one's own connection map grouped per widget. Each widget's rows are narrowed to just the VMFieldBinding bindings to that exact ViewModelClass; call GetWidgetConnectionMap directly for a widget's whole map. Native (non-Blueprint) ViewModel classes never surface here, since they have no on-disk package identity for the reverse search to find. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `viewModelClass, scopeFilter?` |
| `epic_get_widget_animation_bindings(animation:ref)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Get all bindings on a widget animation as FMovieSceneBindingProxy entries. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `animation` |
| `epic_get_widget_class_info(widgetClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Returns the Category, Description and if it's a Panel for a single widget class. Same per-entry data as ListWidgetClasses, but lets callers query a class they already have without scanning every UClass. Returns an empty entry if WidgetClass is null. Can be used to get more information on the class from the Description and Category. Params: `widgetClass` |
| `epic_get_widget_connection_map(widgetBlueprint:ref, scopeFilter?)` | [Epic WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset] Maps every connection on WidgetBlueprint (MVVM field bindings, event bindings, delegates, and legacy property bindings) into one pre-sorted checklist, Unconnected/Misconfigured rows first. Misconfigured only applies to VMFieldBinding rows: Fixable if a conversion function can bridge the types, Unbridgeable if none is allowlisted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, scopeFilter?` |
| `epic_get_widget_description(widgetBlueprint:ref, startWidget?:ref, maxDepth?:i)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Full property dump of every widget in the tree. Each line: [N] Type Name Prop:Value ... slot:(SlotProp:Value ...) N is the 0-based index into result.Widgets -- use result.Widgets[N] to get the widget ref without text parsing. Same indentation format as GetTaggedWidgetDescription; richer per-widget detail. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `widgetBlueprint, startWidget?, maxDepth?` |

| `epic_get_widget_tree_depth(widgetBlueprint:ref, startWidget?:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Returns the maximum depth of the widget tree. Depth: root with no children = 0; root + children = 1; etc. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `widgetBlueprint, startWidget?` |

| `epic_get_widgets(widgetBlueprint:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Returns blueprint info and all widgets in depth-first order. | `epic_highlight(request:o)` | [Epic WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem] Outline every match in the live UI with the Widget Reflector's debug border, to see what a query selects. | `epic_hit_test(ref, params?:o)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Report whether a widget is reachable by pointer input, without changing anything. Returns JSON {reached, samples, reachedSamples, x, y, reason}, using the same hit test Click, Hover, Drag and Scroll refuse on; `reason` names the obstruction. Grid > 1 samples a Grid x Grid lattice inset inside the widget instead of a single point. `reachedSamples` counts the samples that hit, and x/y locate the first sample that missed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `ref, params?` |
| `epic_hover(ref, params?:o)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Hover over a Slate widget, triggering any hover state or tooltip. Unlike the other action tools, Hover moves the OS cursor, since hover state only lasts while the pointer stays over the widget. On Mac, Click, Drag and Scroll move it too and leave it on the target, because Mac only routes pointer input to the window under the real cursor. A button held by MouseDown stays held. Params: `ref, params?` |
| `epic_key_down(key, userIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Press a key and leave it held; pair with KeyUp. Same key specs and gamepad routing as PressKey. A held modifier key (LeftShift, RightControl, LeftAlt, LeftCommand, ...) is down for every later key event of the same Slate user until released, by KeyUp or by a PressKey of the same key. It does not apply to pointer tools, which take their own Modifiers, nor to the platform modifier state FSlateApplication::GetModifierKeys reports. KeyUp or ReleaseHeldInput releases it, as does the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call. Returns true once the press is sent, whether or not a widget handled it, as a held modifier is normally unhandled. False means nothing was sent because the key or user is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `key, userIndex?` |
| `epic_key_up(key, userIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Release a key held by an earlier KeyDown for the same Slate user. Same key specs and gamepad routing as PressKey. Returns true once the release is sent, whether or not a widget handled it, as most widgets act on the press. False means nothing was sent because the key or user is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `key, userIndex?` |
| `epic_last_refusal()` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Why the last action tool refused, as JSON {seq, tool, target, reason}; seq is 0 when nothing has refused this session. seq increments on each refusal, so sample it before an action and compare afterwards to tell a new refusal from one already read. Click, Hover, Scroll, Drag, Type, Focus, SelectOption, PressKey, KeyDown and KeyUp record refusals, and they record one every time they return false unless Slate is not running. For PressKey that includes a key that was sent but that nothing handled. Read-only tools such as Snapshot and HitTest never change it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_bindable_widget_properties(widgetBlueprint:ref, widget:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Lists the bindable property paths available on a widget (binding source/destination candidates). Names aren't filtered by direction -- a read-only property can't be used as a destination and a write-only one can't be used as a source; CreateViewBinding reports that mismatch if it's tried. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, widget` |
| `epic_list_binding_conversion_options(widgetBlueprint:ref, sourceContext:ref, sourcePropertyPath, destinationContext:ref, destinationPropertyPath)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Reports whether SourcePropertyPath and DestinationPropertyPath bind directly, and/or which conversion functions bridge them. Parameters mirror CreateViewBinding's Source-/Destination-prefixed parameters. A function-backed leaf field on either side resolves as unbridgeable. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. | `epic_list_conversion_functions(widgetBlueprint:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] List Available Conversion functions for a WidgetBlueprint that bind a Source Property to a Destination Property Includes Pure and Const functions on the WidgetBlueprint itself once it has been compiled. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint` |

| `epic_list_widget_view_models(widgetBlueprint:ref)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] List all view models used by a widget Blueprint Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint` |

| `epic_observe(ref, maxDepth?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Register an observer on a widget subtree so its refs are continuously kept up to date (~100ms tick). | `epic_press_key(key, userIndex?:i, repeatCount?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Press and release a key on the focused Slate widget; gamepad keys route as controller input for the target user. Modifier keys held by KeyDown are down for the press, as with "Ctrl+" prefixes. True means some handler consumed the press, an auto-repeat, its char event or the release, not that the UI changed as intended. Any focusable widget handles Tab, arrow and D-pad keys as a navigation request, so true for them does not mean focus moved; compare Snapshot or HitTest before and after. False means nothing handled the key, or that nothing was sent because the key, user or RepeatCount is invalid; LastRefusal() names the reason, including which widget had focus. In PIE, false can also mean the game viewport passed the key to the game and the game did not consume it. Only BackSpace, Tab, Enter and Escape send a character; use Type to enter text. Pass each result's `Ref` to the SlateInspectorToolset tools to act on the widget. Prefer Query and WaitForQuery over the SlateInspectorToolset Snapshot/Observe/Screenshot tools. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `request` |

| `epic_replace_widget_with_template(widgetBlueprint:ref, widgetToReplace:ref, templateClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Replaces a widget instance in the blueprint's widget tree with a new instance created from a different template widget class. | `epic_screenshot(ref)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Screenshot a Slate widget or an editor window. Params: `widgetBlueprint, event, argumentName, value` |
| `epic_set_input_type_lock(inputType, reason?, localPlayerIndex?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Lock the effective input type for a player until the lock is removed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `inputType, reason?, localPlayerIndex?` |
| `epic_set_named_slot_content(widgetBlueprint:ref, hostWidget:ref, slotName, widgetClass:ref, widgetName)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Sets content for a named slot. Returns full widget info including Slot pointer. Params: `widgetBlueprint, hostWidget, slotName, widgetClass, widgetName` |
| `epic_set_tree_visualization(bEnabled:b, bIncludeInactive?:b, bShowLabels?:b, bLeafmostOnly?:b, bShowLegend?:b)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Toggle an in-viewport overlay that outlines activatable widgets, color-coded by activation/focus state: green bold with a black halo = leafmost active node, green dashed = activated in the active-root chain, yellow dashed = activated outside the active root, dim grey = deactivated (only with bIncludeInactive), cyan = the leafmost widget's desired focus target, orange = the widget actually holding Slate focus, white dashed = active root boundary. Outlines are stacked by Slate paint layer, so the widget CommonUI treats as topmost is drawn on top. Each activatable's label ends in [ActivationFocus] or [NoActivationFocus]; labels of widgets that opt out of activation focus are drawn in magenta. A legend with the active input mode and type is drawn top-left. The overlay is hit-test-invisible, so it does not perturb the input being debugged; it is PIE-only and auto-disables on PIE end. A multi-client session gets one overlay per client window, each showing only the players that window owns. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bEnabled, bIncludeInactive?, bShowLabels?, bLeafmostOnly?, bShowLegend?` |
| `epic_set_view_condition_operation(widgetBlueprint:ref, condition:ref, operation, value:n, maxValue?:n)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Sets the comparison of an existing condition, then compiles the widget blueprint; compile errors do not fail the call and are reported in the condition's CompileErrors. Not supported during PIE. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, condition, operation, value, maxValue?` |
| `epic_set_widget_animation_display_label(animation:ref, displayLabel)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Set the user-facing display label shown in the Animations panel. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `animation, displayLabel` |
| `epic_set_widget_animation_length(animation:ref, lengthSeconds:n)` | [Epic WidgetAnimationToolset.WidgetAnimationToolset] Set the animation playback length in seconds. Updates the MovieScene playback range to [0, LengthSeconds] in tick resolution. LengthSeconds must be > 0. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `animation, lengthSeconds` |
| `epic_set_widget_preview_active(widgetBlueprint:ref, bActive:b)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Turns the View Bindings design-time preview on or off for a WidgetBlueprint, exactly like the eye toggle on the View Bindings panel toolbar. The WidgetBlueprint's designer must be open for the canvas to update; the state is stored either way. No-ops while the per-user Enable Design-Time View Model Preview editor preference is off. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, bActive` |
| `epic_set_widget_view_binding_enabled(widgetBlueprint:ref, bindingId, bEnabled?:b, bCompile?:b)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Changes the enabled and compile flag for an existing widget view binding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, bindingId, bEnabled?, bCompile?` |
| `epic_set_widget_view_config(widgetBlueprint:ref, configuration:o)` | [Epic MVVMToolset.MVVMToolset] Writes the MVVM View configuration on the WidgetBlueprint's View. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, configuration` |
| `epic_show_widget_lifetime_log_window()` | [Epic UMGEditor.UMGDebuggerSubsystem] Opens or focuses the Widget Lifetime Log editor tab, which shows the same recording. Returns false without a Slate UI. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_snapshot(ref, maxDepth?:i, bIncludeSourceLocations?:b)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Capture a Slate UI accessibility snapshot. Use this to read the current widget tree and discover refs for action tools (Click, Type, Hover, etc.). A shallow root observer (depth 0) covers top-level windows automatically. Before interacting with a specific window or panel, call Observe() on it to get deep coverage, then Snapshot that subtree to see its contents. Refs discovered by a previous Snapshot remain usable. You do NOT need to call Snapshot again before every action. Each [pos=X,Y size=W,H] is the widget's on-screen bounds in desktop pixels, whatever the DPI scale or rotation, the same space as the pointer and touch tools' screen positions and offsets. Params: `ref, maxDepth?, bIncludeSourceLocations?` |
| `epic_start_event_logging(bCaptureCallstacks?:b, bufferSize?:i)` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Begin logging CommonUI events (widget activation/deactivation/rebuild, input mode/config changes, input method changes, container displayed-widget/transition changes) into an in-memory ring buffer. Restarting clears the buffer. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bCaptureCallstacks?, bufferSize?` |
| `epic_start_focus_recording(bCaptureCallstack?:b, bCaptureContext?:b, bufferSize?:i)` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] Starts recording Slate focus and navigation events into an in-memory buffer, discarding events already captured. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bCaptureCallstack?, bCaptureContext?, bufferSize?` |
| `epic_start_service()` | [Epic WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem] Begin mirroring the live Slate widget tree into the store, so Query/Highlight/WaitForQuery can work. The service is off by default. Call this once before locating widgets and leave it running for the session. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_start_widget_lifetime_logging(bufferSize?:i, bCaptureInvalidations?:b)` | [Epic UMGEditor.UMGDebuggerSubsystem] Starts recording Constructed, Destructed and Rebuilt events for every user widget, discarding events already captured. Query them with GetWidgetLifetimeEvents. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bufferSize?, bCaptureInvalidations?` |
| `epic_stop_event_logging()` | [Epic CommonUIToolset.CommonUIToolset] Stop logging; the buffer is retained for querying. Does nothing when not logging. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_stop_focus_recording()` | [Epic SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem] Stops recording. The buffer is retained for querying. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_stop_service()` | [Epic WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem] Stop mirroring and empty the store, ending the scanning cost. Pending WaitForQuery calls fail at once, and the query tools fail until StartService. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_stop_widget_lifetime_logging()` | [Epic UMGEditor.UMGDebuggerSubsystem] Stops recording. Captured events stay queryable until ClearWidgetLifetimeLog or the next start. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_toggle_widget_as_variable(widgetBlueprint:ref, widget:ref, bIsVariable:b)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Sets the bIsVariable flag. Params: `widgetBlueprint, widget, bIsVariable` |
| `epic_touch_end(x:n, y:n, touchIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Lift a finger held by an earlier TouchStart at an absolute screen position. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `x, y, touchIndex?` |
| `epic_touch_move(x:n, y:n, touchIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Move a finger held by an earlier TouchStart to an absolute screen position. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `x, y, touchIndex?` |
| `epic_touch_start(ref, x?:n, y?:n, touchIndex?:i)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Put a finger down and leave it there; it shares the left mouse button with the cursor, so do not mix it with a held MouseDown. TouchEnd or ReleaseHeldInput lifts it, as does the hold watchdog after SlateInspectorToolset.HeldInputTimeoutSeconds without a pointer, touch, KeyDown or KeyUp call. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `ref, x?, y?, touchIndex?` |
| `epic_trace_widget_property_overrides(widgetBlueprint:ref, propertyNameFilter?, widgetNameFilter?)` | [Epic WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset.WidgetStaticAnalysisToolset] Traces every statically-discoverable write to a widget property across the whole tree, merging Blueprint-graph writes with static origins (class defaults, archetype overrides, bindings). Results are grouped per (widget, property) pair. The highest-Order Applied entry is the Winner; earlier entries are Redundant, later ones Conflict. With no Applied entry, the highest-Order entry is an uncertain best guess and all are Conflict. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `widgetBlueprint, propertyNameFilter?, widgetNameFilter?` |
| `epic_type(ref, text, submit?:b)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Type text into a Slate text input widget, focusing it first; use PressKey for keys that are not characters. Params: `ref, text, submit?` |
| `epic_unobserve(identifier)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Remove an observer by its identifier. Params: `identifier` |
| `epic_wait_for(text?, textGone?)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] Check once whether text is present or absent in the Slate widget tree (substring match); poll to wait. Params: `text?, textGone?` |
| `epic_wait_for_query(request:o)` | [Epic WidgetFinder.WidgetFinderSubsystem] Wait, without polling, until a query's raw match count meets Comparison/Threshold, then return the matches. Prefer it over repeated Query calls and over the SlateInspectorToolset Snapshot/Observe/Screenshot tools. Completes once, with bConditionMet, or with bTimedOut after TimeoutSeconds, which still counts as success. A bad query, a stopped service, or stopping the service mid-wait fails the call. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `request` |
| `epic_windows(index?:i, width?:i, height?:i, ref?, input?:o)` | [Epic SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset] List, select, close or resize top-level Slate editor windows. "list" returns a JSON array of {index, ref, title, active, regular, x, y, width, height}. Pass the ref to Screenshot or Snapshot to target that window; the index is positional and changes as windows open and close, the ref does not. "resize" and "maximize" also work under -RenderOffScreen. Params: `index?, width?, height?, ref?, input? (carries action, which cannot be sent at the top level)` |
| `epic_wrap_widgets(widgetBlueprint:ref, widgets:[ref], wrapperClass:ref)` | [Epic UMGToolSet.UMGToolSet] Wraps one or more widgets in a new panel widget of the specified class. Only the root-most widgets in the selection are wrapped - children of other selected widgets are skipped because their parent will be wrapped. Returns info for each newly created wrapper. Use ObjectTools.list_properties on each returned Widget and Slot to discover property names before calling set_properties (padding, alignment, anchors, etc. vary per panel class). Params: `widgetBlueprint, widgets, wrapperClass` |

---

## editor

*Editor commands, Python execution, PIE, undo/redo, hot reload, viewport, performance, sequencer, build pipeline, logs, editor control.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `get_shader_compile_status(waitUntilIdle?:b)` | Read outstanding shader jobs, compiling state, pending material and shader-map counts, and manager availability. waitUntilIdle polls short game-thread snapshots between ticks, leaving the editor free to finish compiling. timeoutMs bounds the wait (default 60000); a timeout returns success=false and state=timed_out with the last counters. Params: `waitUntilIdle?` |
| `start_editor(dialogPolicy?, extraArgs?, ide?, timeout?:n, window?)` | Launch Unreal Editor and BLOCK until it is fully ready (not merely until the socket answers), rendering a startup progress bar in the terminal. Returns the phase timeline it waited through. Do NOT poll get_engine_state or get_status afterwards: this call already waited, and a ready editor is the only way it returns success. An editor already running for this project is reported as a failure, because this call launched nothing, with alreadyRunning=true, bridgeReady, and the port it published, so a caller can tell "there was nothing to do" from "the launch broke" without parsing the sentence. A flow step that expects that outcome sets ignore_failure: true on itself rather than asking this action to call a non-launch a launch. dialogPolicy answers startup prompts before they can wedge the game thread, which is how the post-crash "Restore Packages" modal used to stall a launch (#968). Params: `timeout? (seconds, default 300), dialogPolicy? ("pattern=response;pattern=response", responses as set_dialog_policy takes them), window? (normal (default) or offscreen, which passes -RenderOffScreen so no editor window appears), ide? (allow or none; none passes the NullSourceCodeAccessor ini override so the editor opens no IDE; defaults to editor.ide from ue-mcp.yml, then none for an offscreen editor and allow otherwise), extraArgs? (extra editor command-line arguments, appended after editor.launchArgs from ue-mcp.yml)` |
| `get_engine_state(probeWindows?:b)` | What the engine is REALLY doing, read from outside the game thread: startup phase from the editor's own log, every process holding this project's .uproject open (PID, command line, responding), the plugin's status snapshot (slow-task name and percent, active modal dialog, game-thread stall), and native dialog windows. `running` follows the strongest evidence: an editor that answered over the bridge is running whatever the process table saw, and a probe that could not run is reported as processProbeFailed rather than as an absent editor (#965). Call this ONCE when something is already wrong (handlers timing out, an editor that will not come up). Never call it in a wait loop: start_editor blocks until ready on its own, and polling this during startup burns tokens re-reading state that is already tracked. Params: `probeWindows? (default true; scans native windows, costs ~2s)` |
| `stop_editor(discardTransient?:b)` | Close Unreal Editor gracefully (asks the editor to quit itself via the bridge; never an OS kill of an editor). Acts only on the editor for the loaded project, resolved from the port lockfile that editor published at <project>/Saved/UE_MCP_Bridge/port.json. With no lockfile there is no port to aim at and the call refuses, naming the file it checked, rather than probing a default port that another project's editor could answer on (#819). With no editor of this project running there is nothing to quit, and the call fails saying so, with alreadyStopped=true marking that reason apart from a running editor that cannot be reached or refuses on unsaved work. A flow that stops the editor before building sets ignore_failure: true on the stop step. With more than one editor of this project open it closes the one the lockfile names and reports the rest under remainingInstances, so plain success never has to be read as 'no editor of this project is running' (#1072). Unsaved work: the quit is sent and the EDITOR decides. It refuses inside the engine and names every dirty package without scheduling a close, so nothing is lost and no quit is left pending; save them with editor(save_dirty), or close the editor yourself and answer its save prompt by hand. There is deliberately no flag that discards real content. discardTransient=true clears, before the quit, only packages nobody can save (the transient package and /Engine maps such as the /Engine/Maps/Entry startup map, as editor(discard_dirty) judges them), so a prompt that would ask only about those never comes up; anything else still reaches the editor's save prompt, and what was cleared is reported under discarded. This action has no dialog behaviour of its own: a modal blocks it exactly as it blocks every other action, refused by the same gate with the same fields. Read the dialog with editor(list_dialogs) and answer it with editor(respond_to_dialog). On Windows, once no editor of this project is left running (after the stop, or when there was nothing to stop), it ends any CrashReportClient process a crashed editor of this project left behind, because it keeps the project's module DLLs open and the next build_project fails with LNK1104; each one is reported under crashReporters with its pid and the reason it was judged this project's (a path under the project on its command line, or a project binary it holds open). A reporter still watching a live editor, or one of another project, is never touched. A success names the editor it quit under stopped {project, pid}, and an editor name that matches no registered session refuses rather than stopping the active editor (#1278). Params: `discardTransient?` |
| `restart_editor(extraArgs?, ide?, window?)` | Stop then start the editor for the loaded project. Editors for other projects are left alone: the stop is aimed by this project's port lockfile, and the decision to start is made from the process holding this project's .uproject open, never from whether some editor is running (#819). The stop half is editor(stop_editor) exactly as it behaves on its own, so a restart refuses on unsaved packages and reports them rather than acting on them, and an editor that was already down is not a reason to refuse the start. Like the stop half it has no dialog behaviour of its own: a modal blocks it through the same gate as every other action. Params: `window? (normal or offscreen; defaults to editor.window from ue-mcp.yml, then normal, not to the mode of the editor being stopped), ide? (allow or none; none passes the NullSourceCodeAccessor ini override so the editor opens no IDE; defaults to editor.ide from ue-mcp.yml, then none for an offscreen editor and allow otherwise), extraArgs? (extra editor command-line arguments, appended after editor.launchArgs from ue-mcp.yml)` |
