| `build_project(clean?:b, configuration?, platform?)` | Build the project's C++ out of process with UnrealBuildTool. Works with the editor STOPPED, which a full rebuild requires (UBT cannot link while an editor holds the module DLLs). Blocks until the build finishes and returns the compiler output. A link that fails because another process holds an output open names the file and the holder under lockedOutputs, with the remedy in the message. Params: `configuration? (default Development), platform? (default the host platform), clean? (#958)` |
| `execute_command(command, world?, pieInstance?:n, playerIndex?:n)` | Run a console command. world=editor (the default) runs it against the editor world, where Open is refused because it does nothing there; switch maps with level(load) (#1393). world=pie runs it as a PIE player through that player's console (PlayerController::ConsoleCommand, in that instance's context), so cheat-manager and game commands such as slomo, pause or ToggleDebugCamera reach the running game; pieInstance and playerIndex pick the instance and player, a dedicated server with no player runs it against its world, and the command's console output comes back as output. This is the safe route for PIE console commands; calling ExecuteConsoleCommand through invoke_object_function is a known editor crash (#1250). Params: `command, world?, pieInstance?, playerIndex?` |
| `execute_python(code, taskSummary, captureLog?:b, maxLogChars?:n, resultVariable?, ruledOut?:[o])` | GATED LAST RESORT. execute_python is unreachable until a semantic tool search over your taskSummary has been run AND every candidate it returns is EXPLICITLY ruled out with a stated reason. Flow: (1) call with taskSummary (+code) - it returns the candidate actions AND the exact ruledOut array to send back; (2) re-call with the same taskSummary/code PLUS that ruledOut=[{action, reason}], each reason at least 12 characters saying why that candidate does not fit. The action field accepts the bare name, tool(action) or tool.action, and rulings are remembered for the session so rewording the taskSummary never asks you to justify the same action twice. A candidate the running plugin does not register cannot do the task, so it needs no ruling: it is listed under notInRunningPlugin with the upgrade command instead. Python runs only once every candidate is ruled out. Candidates are the search hits that bear on the summary: when it names a subsystem (PCG, Niagara, MetaSound), another subsystem's actions that only share a word are not candidates, nor is a hit scoring under half the best one. Params: `code, taskSummary (required), ruledOut?, resultVariable? (name of a top-level variable to return as `result`, separate from print()/log; #732) (#704, #938, #960, #1167)` |
| `run_python_file(filePath\|path, entryPoint?, runName?, asMain?:b, args?:o/[s]/[o]/s, kwargs?:o, resultVariable?, captureLog?:b, maxLogChars?:n)` | Run a Python file from disk with __file__/__name__ populated (#142). Pass entryPoint to load the file WITHOUT firing its `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard and then call one named function in it, which is how a Tools/ script holding several stages behind a main() is driven a stage at a time; `args` are then that call's positional arguments rather than sys.argv, `kwargs` its keyword arguments, and its return value comes back as `result` with no resultVariable needed. Pass asMain=true (or runName="__main__") to run the file through runpy as __main__ with sys.argv set to the file plus args, so a main guard that starts a tick callback does fire; runName also sets the module name an entryPoint load uses. captureLog=false drops everything the script logged except its errors, and maxLogChars keeps only the tail: a script that prints a few hundred lines otherwise returns tens of KB to a caller that wanted one value. A script that needs a line trace against the PIE world calls unreal.MCPTraceLibrary.line_trace(start, end, 'pie', pie_instance, 'WorldStatic', trace_complex), which returns hit, impact_point, impact_normal, distance, actor_path, component_name and physical_material without a round trip; the engine's SystemLibrary traces take a TraceTypeQuery, not a CollisionChannel (#1283). (#142/#732/#995) Params: filePath (or path), entryPoint?, runName?, asMain?, args?, kwargs?, resultVariable?, captureLog?, maxLogChars? |
| `purge_python_modules(prefix)` | Purge cached embedded-Python modules whose name starts with a prefix, so the editor drops stale code after you edit a Python tool on disk. Returns the purged module names + count (#719). Params: `prefix` |
| `close_sequence()` | Close the currently open Level Sequence editor (Sequencer). Do this before bulk-deleting actors a sequence may possess - open sequences re-resolve possessables by name during destruction and can mis-bind. Returns wasOpen + closedSequence (#718). Params: `none` |
| `open_tab(tabId)` | Open a registered editor tab by ID so its UI can be screenshotted as evidence (e.g. 'ProjectSettings', 'OutputLog', 'ContentBrowserTab1') (#727). Params: `tabId` |
| `open_settings(container?, category?, section?)` | Open (and navigate) a settings viewer for visual settings evidence. section takes a bare name with category, or a combined 'Engine.Physics' (#727). Params: `container?, category?, section?` |
| `show_notification(text, subText?, durationS?:n(1..600), severity?:{info,success,warning,error}, hyperlinkText?, hyperlinkUrl?)` | Show a toast in the editor's notification area (bottom right), the way the editor reports a finished build or a failed save. severity picks the icon and colour (info default, success, warning, error); durationS is how long it stays before fading (default 8). hyperlinkText with hyperlinkUrl adds a link that opens the URL in the default browser; only http and https URLs are accepted. Returns onScreen, read back from the notification windows, so a toast Slate accepted but never drew is visible as onScreen=false. Params: `text, subText?, durationS?, severity?, hyperlinkText?, hyperlinkUrl?` |
| `set_property(objectPath\|path\|assetPath, propertyName, value:*, save?:b)` | Set UObject property. Saves the package to disk by default; pass save=false to leave it dirty in-memory (batch many writes, then editor(save_dirty)/asset(save)) (#674). TMap values take either { "Key": value } or, for struct keys, [{ key: {...}, value: ... }] - exactly what get_property/describe_object return under `value`. A write that cannot store every entry it was given fails and leaves the old value in place; containers report elementCount on success (#820). SkeletalMeshAsset/SkinnedAsset on a skinned mesh component go through SetSkinnedAssetAndUpdate, since a raw write crashes the next pose evaluation; for a placed actor use level(set_component_skeletal_mesh) (#1099). An Instanced or EditInlineNew object property takes {instanceClass, properties}: a new subobject of that class is created with the owning object as its outer and its fields set from properties, e.g. RootMotionModifier = {instanceClass: "RootMotionModifier_Scale", properties: {Scale: {x:0,y:0,z:0}}} (#1292). propertyName accepts dotted paths, array indices and field-value selectors (`Items[Id=Foo].Field`); resolvedPropertyName and the rollback carry the numeric index matched, with indexedPath also returned for keyed paths. A config property on a settings class default (objectPath=/Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings and other Project Settings classes) is written to its ini instead of a package, and the result carries configFile, configSection, configKey and storedValue read back from that file (#1566). Params: `objectPath (or path, or assetPath), propertyName, value, save?` |
| `get_property(objectPath\|path\|assetPath, propertyName)` | Read UObject property. propertyName takes the dotted, indexed (`Rules[1]`) and keyed (`Rules[Id=Axe]`) paths asset(set_property) does. `value` is structured JSON and is always safe to write straight back with set_property; `valueText` is UE export text and for a struct-keyed TMap does not read back, so valueTextRoundTrips reports whether it can be reused (#820). resolvedPropertyName reports the numeric path matched; indexedPath is also returned for keyed paths. Params: `objectPath (or path, or assetPath), propertyName` |
| `describe_object(objectPath\|path\|assetPath, includeProperties?:b, includeValues?:b, propertyNames?:[s])` | Describe a UObject and optionally list/read properties. Per property, `value` is the round-trippable structured form and valueTextRoundTrips flags export text that is not (#820). Params: `objectPath (or path, or assetPath), includeProperties?, includeValues?, propertyNames?` |
| `play_in_editor(pieAction?, waitForAssetRegistry?:b, assetRegistryTimeoutSeconds?:n)` | PIE control. A start with a session already active fails with alreadyRunning, and a stop with none active fails with alreadyStopped: neither call changed anything, and the marker names the reason. A flow step that expects either outcome carries ignore_failure: true. pieAction defaults to status. A start waits for the AssetRegistry initial scan by default, since PIE silently no-ops during it on a cold editor (#406). Params: `pieAction?, waitForAssetRegistry?, assetRegistryTimeoutSeconds?` |
| `play_in_editor_ignore_blueprint_errors(assetRegistryTimeoutSeconds?:n, waitForAssetRegistry?:b)` | Start PIE for one launch with the editor's unresolved-Blueprint-error prompt suppressed. PIE then runs whatever bytecode those Blueprints last compiled to, so the launch is authorized per call: set ue-mcp.pie.allowIgnoreBlueprintErrors to true in your ue-mcp config to pre-authorize it, otherwise the user answers an MCP approval prompt. The bridge refuses the launch when a Blueprint would have to be recompiled first (dirty non-data Blueprints, errored Level Blueprints) and lists every errored Blueprint it suppressed in loadedErroredBlueprints. Params: `waitForAssetRegistry? (default true), assetRegistryTimeoutSeconds? (default 180)` |
| `get_runtime_value(actorLabel?, actorPath?, propertyName, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Read PIE actor property. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. propertyName supports dotted paths (component.field or component.struct.field) for nested reads on component subobjects (#344/#381). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, propertyName, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `get_pie_pawn(playerIndex?:n, pieInstance?:n)` | Resolve the controlled pawn in a PIE world: pieInstance, else the primary world, or the first client world when the primary is a dedicated server. Returns actorLabel/class/path/location/rotation, the controller's controlRotation, velocity, pieInstance, netMode and the map it is in now, so a read after a level change names the new level (#228/#229/#1565). Params: `playerIndex?, pieInstance?` |
| `list_pie_instances()` | List the running PIE worlds with their instance id, net mode (standalone\|listenServer\|dedicatedServer\|client), player count and whether they own a game viewport. In a multiplayer PIE session every other runtime action resolves the primary world (the server) unless you pass pieInstance, so this is how you discover that a client exists and what id addresses it (#778). Params: `none` |
| `invoke_object_function(functionName, objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?:n, propertyPath?, args?:o/[s]/[o]/s, modify?:o, world?, pieInstance?:n, deferToNextTick?:b)` | Call a UFUNCTION on any UObject, not just a placed actor. Target it with objectPath, or target=gameinstance\|gamemode\|gamestate\|playercontroller\|playerpawn\|subsystem (subsystem also needs subsystemClass, and resolves world, game instance, LocalPlayer, engine and editor subsystems; a LocalPlayer subsystem such as EnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem is taken from the local player at playerIndex in the selected PIE instance; playercontroller/playerpawn accept playerIndex). The GameInstance, GameMode and subsystems have no actor label, so invoke_function could never reach them. Returns output and return params under returnValues, with a TArray/TSet/TMap return as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885); an unknown function name lists the available ones, and an args name that is not an input of the function is refused with the inputs listed, rather than being dropped and the call run with that parameter at its default (#1548). propertyPath follows a dotted chain of object-reference properties from the selected root to the object actually called, e.g. target=gameinstance with propertyPath='GameSettings.Game Settings' (Details-panel spellings, array indexes and actor component names are accepted) (#1215). Enum arguments take the enumerator or display name. modify={argument, getter, patch} reads a struct from a zero-argument getter on the same object, applies patch (field names or dotted paths to structured JSON, including TMap fields) and passes it as that struct argument, so read-modify-write of a component's settings struct is one call; the result echoes modifiedArgument and modifiedValue (#1203). A target in a running PIE instance is called in that instance's context (callContext=playInstance, callPieInstance), so a client object's UFUNCTION(Server) is sent through that client's net driver instead of running locally (#1217); netCallspace reports the routing. An editor-world target runs under the editor script-execution guard, which forces every actor callspace to Local; the result warns when that happened, and deferToNextTick=true queues the call for the next engine tick where it routes normally, at the cost of returning before it runs (#973). To click a UMG button in PIE, use widget(invoke_runtime_function) (#1140). (#739) Params: functionName, objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?, propertyPath?, args?, modify?, world?, pieInstance?, deferToNextTick? |
| `invoke_object_functions(calls:[o], world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Call 1-64 UFUNCTIONs in order without yielding to the editor tick loop. Each call independently targets a UObject using the same fields as invoke_object_function, so one sequence can span an actor and its components. Calls stop at the first failure; earlier calls are not rolled back. Returns results[] in call order plus completedCalls/requestedCalls, and failedIndex when it stops early, so a retry can resume instead of replaying mutations. Params: `calls, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `read_bone_transforms(actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, bones?:[s], relativeTo?, space?, limit?:n, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Read live skeletal bone and socket transforms off an actor, once. This is a point-in-time read, NOT a time series - for per-frame capture over a window use a plugin listed in the plugin registry that provides PIE observation. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Pass bones (bone OR socket names) or omit for every bone up to limit. space=world (default) or component; component space is independent of where the actor is standing. Pass relativeTo (bone OR socket name) to express every sample in that live reference frame; relativeTo supersedes space and is calculated in component space. world defaults to auto. Also reports the AnimInstance class/path (#756/#757/#761/#764). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, bones?, relativeTo?, space?, limit?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `get_object_properties(objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?:n, propertyPath?, propertyNames?:[s], world?, pieInstance?:n, limit?:n, maxValueLength?:n)` | Read reflected properties off any UObject, with the same targeting as invoke_object_function: objectPath, or target (plus subsystemClass or playerIndex), then propertyPath to follow object references from there (#1215). Blueprint-declared variables are reflected properties, so they read the same way as native ones. Pass propertyNames to filter; entries may use the Details-panel spelling ('World Context Object' finds WorldContextObject, 'Is Active' finds bIsActive), and an entry with a dot or index is a path read into a struct, subobject or, on an actor, a component ('StashWorld.KickRadiusCm', 'CharacterMovement.GroundFriction'), reported under properties and values by the path as written, with pathErrors naming why a path did not resolve (#1212). Names that do not exist come back under missingProperties instead of silently returning nothing. Properties holding a TMap are also reported under `values` in the structured form set_property accepts, because export text cannot carry a struct-keyed map back (#820). world defaults to auto (#739/#802). Params: `objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?, propertyPath?, propertyNames?, world?, pieInstance?, limit?, maxValueLength?` |
| `set_movement_mode(actorLabel?, actorPath?, mode?, customMode?:i, velocity?:v, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Set a live PIE character's movement mode and/or velocity on its CharacterMovementComponent. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Modes are named (none\|walking\|navwalking\|falling\|swimming\|flying\|custom) rather than raw enum numbers, because a wrong number reads as success and then behaves as None. Reports previousMode/previousVelocity and reads the mode back afterwards, since SetMovementMode can refuse a mode the character cannot enter (flying with bCanFly off, swimming outside a volume). world defaults to pie (#757). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, mode?, customMode?, velocity?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `set_object_property(propertyName, value:*, objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?:n, propertyPath?, postEditChange?:b, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Write a reflected property on a live UObject instance, with the same targeting as invoke_object_function: objectPath, or target (plus subsystemClass or playerIndex), then propertyPath to follow object references from there (#1215). Use this for a PIE actor, a spawned widget or any runtime instance: editor(set_property) is the asset path and marks the package dirty and saves it, which a live instance has no business doing. propertyName accepts dotted/indexed/keyed paths and the Details-panel spelling. Reports previousValue plus the value read back after the write, so a coerced or clamped write is visible. Export text naming a struct member the target does not have fails the call and leaves the value as it was. Nothing is saved; pass postEditChange=true to fire PostEditChangeProperty. An object inside a saved package (a Widget Blueprint's WidgetTree template, a Blueprint, an editor level actor) is part of that asset: the write marks it dirty, owner reports asset or level, and package, blueprint, compileRequired and saveRequired say what keeps it (#1544). world defaults to auto (#802). Params: `propertyName, value, objectPath?, target?, subsystemClass?, playerIndex?, propertyPath?, postEditChange?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `find_object(any(objectPath; className; nameContains), outerPath?, exactClass?:b, includeDefaults?:b, world?, pieInstance?:n, cursor?, limit?:n)` | Resolve or search for a live UObject instance and report the objectPath that addresses it, which is what invoke_object_function / get_object_properties / set_object_property need. Pass objectPath to check one path (returns found/isValid rather than failing when it is gone), or className and/or nameContains to search every loaded object. className takes a short name (StaticMeshActor), a /Script path, a generated class name (WBP_Hud_C) or a Blueprint asset path. This is how you get the path of something spawned at runtime, an editor utility widget or a UMG widget, which no naming convention predicts. The search is paged: pass back nextCursor as cursor to read the next page (#802). Params: `at least one of objectPath/className/nameContains, outerPath?, exactClass?, includeDefaults?, world?, pieInstance?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `teleport_runtime_actor(actorLabel?, actorPath?, location?:v, rotation?:r, stopMovement?:b, sweep?:b, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Move a live PIE actor and have it STAY moved. A plain SetActorLocation on a Character is undone by CharacterMovement on the next tick, so this stops the movement component, teleports, and stops it again. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Reports actualLocation read back from the actor rather than what was requested. sweep=true moves along the way and stops at the first blocking hit, reported as blocked and hit. world defaults to pie (#770/#777). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, location?, rotation?, stopMovement?, sweep?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `set_runtime_visibility(hidden:b, one(actorLabels:[s]; actorPaths:[s]; actorClass), componentNames?:[s], componentClasses?:[s], affectActor?:b, affectComponents?:b, propagateToChildren?:b, matchSubclasses?:b, maxTargets?:i, dryRun?:b, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Hide or show live PIE actors and their scene components, capturing an exact rollback snapshot. PIE-only: world must be 'pie' (the default) and pieInstance picks the world when several are running (see list_pie_instances). Provide exactly ONE actor selector - actorLabels[], actorPaths[] (the unambiguous one) or actorClass; a label matching several actors is refused rather than resolved at random. hidden=true hides, hidden=false shows. componentNames[]/componentClasses[] narrow to matching SceneComponents and imply affectComponents; with no component filter the actor itself is the target. affectActor/affectComponents override that split, propagateToChildren (default true) also takes each matched component's descendants, matchSubclasses (default true) widens class matching, and maxTargets bounds how far the expansion may go. dryRun defaults to TRUE: the call reports what it would change and mutates nothing until dryRun=false. Returns hidden, dryRun, mutationPerformed, matchedActors, targetCount, changed, alreadyDesired, worldPath, pieInstance, netMode, targets[], and on a real mutation a rollbackToken to hand to restore_runtime_visibility. Params: `hidden, actorLabels OR actorPaths OR actorClass, componentNames?, componentClasses?, affectActor?, affectComponents?, propagateToChildren?, matchSubclasses?, maxTargets?, dryRun?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `restore_runtime_visibility(rollbackToken, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Put back the exact visibility state set_runtime_visibility captured, addressed by the rollbackToken from its response. Run set_runtime_visibility with dryRun=false first; a dry run issues no token. The token belongs to one PIE session and expires with it, so restore before play ends. world, if passed, must be 'pie', and pieInstance must match the token's session. Returns restored, rollbackToken, targetCount, changed, alreadyRestored, worldPath, pieInstance, netMode. Params: `rollbackToken, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `invoke_static_function(className, functionName, args?:o/[s]/[o]/s, actorArgs?:o, worldContextParam?, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Call a project static BlueprintCallable editor UFUNCTION by className, functionName and args, returning its result in returnValues. Works on any reflected class, including actor component classes and UBlueprintFunctionLibrary subclasses (no actor instance). invoke_function needs an actor/component target; this targets the library class CDO instead, so it reaches static *_BlueprintOnly libraries (Voxel sculpt/query/stamp), GeometryScript, Kismet math, any function library. world/pieInstance pick WHICH world fills the context param, so a static that looks a GameInstance subsystem up off its context can be exercised against a live PIE session (#971); the result names the world it ran against and the parameter that carried it. Returns return/out params under returnValues, with a TArray/TSet/TMap return as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885). A project library works the same way: className takes the short name with or without its U (or /Script/Module.Class), args are keyed by parameter name, and every non-const reference out-param comes back under its own name in returnValues, an FString unquoted and whole. Example: void UMyLibrary::PlanZone(const FString& ZoneId, bool bDryRun, FString& OutManifestJson, FString& OutError) is className='MyLibrary', functionName='PlanZone', args={ZoneId:'A1', bDryRun:true}, read returnValues.OutManifestJson and returnValues.OutError. Discover libraries + functions with list_function_libraries. Params: `className, functionName, args?, actorArgs?, worldContextParam?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `invoke_function(functionName, any(actorLabel; actorPath), component?, args?:o/[s]/[o]/s, actorArgs?:o, world?, pieInstance?:n, deferToNextTick?:b)` | Call a BlueprintCallable / Exec UFUNCTION on a target actor or one of its components. world=editor (the default) runs the function on the actor placed in the level, no PIE session needed, and reports which instance ran it as resolvedActorLabel/resolvedActorPath. actorLabel is matched against placed actors by editor label first, then internal object name, then full object path; a miss is an error naming what was searched (#806). Returns out/return params under returnValues; a TArray/TSet/TMap return comes back as real JSON and everything else as export text (#885). A PIE target is called in its own instance's context with normal RPC routing (callContext=playInstance, #1217). An editor-world target runs under the editor script-execution guard, which forces every actor callspace to Local, so a UFUNCTION(Server) executes locally instead of being sent; the result warns when that happened, and deferToNextTick=true queues the call for the next engine tick where it routes normally, at the cost of returning before it runs (#973). A component redirects the call to that subobject (#382), and actorArgs fills UObject* parameters from actor labels (#383). An args name that is not an input of the function is refused with the inputs listed (#1548). See #228/#229. Params: `functionName, at least one of actorLabel/actorPath, component?, args?, actorArgs?, world?, pieInstance?, deferToNextTick?` |
| `list_function_libraries(pattern?, includeFunctions?:b)` | Enumerate UBlueprintFunctionLibrary subclasses on this build. Filter by name with pattern (case-insensitive substring, e.g. 'GeometryScript' / 'Kismet' / 'Animation'). Returns name, pythonName (the unreal.* class from ScriptName, e.g. unreal.GeometryScript_List for GeometryScriptLibrary_ListUtilityFunctions), module, and (by default) every static BlueprintCallable function on the library with its pythonName, pythonMethod when it is also a ScriptMethod, and tooltip. pattern also matches the Python name. Use to discover what's available for editor.invoke_function (#455). Params: `pattern?, includeFunctions?` |
| `set_pie_time_scale(factor:n)` | Fast-forward PIE game time. Raises WorldSettings caps and calls SetGlobalTimeDilation. Params: `factor` |
| `set_pie_paused(paused:b, mode?, force?:b, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Pause or resume a running PIE instance. mode=game (default) is the game's own pause (UGameplayStatics::SetGamePaused, run in that instance's context), so it resumes a game a startup menu paused, which execute_command 'pause' cannot reach because it runs against the editor world. mode=debug is the editor's Pause/Resume play buttons and applies to every PIE world. A refused unpause names the cause; force=true clears the world's pauser. Reports gamePaused/debugPaused read back after the call plus their previous values, and a rollback to the previous state (#1215). Params: `paused, mode?, force?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `hot_reload()` | Hot reload C++. Params: `none` |
| `undo()` | Undo last transaction. Params: `none` |
| `redo()` | Redo last transaction. Params: `none` |
| `get_perf_stats()` | Editor performance stats. Params: `none` |
| `run_stat(command?, name?)` | Run a stat overlay. name is a bare stat name (e.g. 'unit','fps','game','gpu') prefixed with 'stat '; command is a full console command and wins over name (#722). Params: `command?, name?` |
| `set_scalability(level?)` | Set rendering quality via the Scalability system (actually applies + persists, not just sg.* cvars). Returns appliedLevels (#591). Params: `level?` |
| `get_cvars(name?, names?:[s], pattern?, limit?:n)` | Read console variables from the running editor by name, names, or pattern (substring match over every registered variable). Each row carries value, defaultValue, isDefault, type, whether it is a cheat, and `setBy`: the priority the current value was written at, which is what separates a variable sitting at its default from one a scalability group or device profile drove there. A variable set at a higher priority ignores later writes from lower ones. Names that do not resolve come back under notFound rather than as an error (#1006). Params: `name?, names?, pattern?, limit?` |
| `set_cvars(cvars:[o]/o)` | Bulk-set console variables, from a {name: value} object or a [{name, value}] array. Returns per-cvar old/new values and any notFound names. Use get_cvars to read one back, including which priority its value was set at (#591). Params: `cvars` |
| `capture_screenshot(filename\|outputPath, target?, pieInstance?:n, worldPath?, inline?:b/i)` | Screenshot. target=pie synchronously captures the selected PIE client game viewport with UMG/Slate UI; target=editor captures the level viewport; target=window synchronously captures a whole Slate window via FSlateApplication::TakeScreenshot - pixel-true for ALL Slate/UMG UI, returns after the PNG is written, and works while the window is unfocused. target=pie and target=window refuse a window Slate is not drawing (hidden, minimized, off screen) with the reason, so no readback is left queued (#1450). Multi-instance PIE automatically prefers a world with a game viewport; pass pieInstance or worldPath to select explicitly, which for target=window is what picks the PIE client window instead of the active editor window. Every mode captures at the source viewport/window size - use capture_scene_png for a chosen output size. outputPath is accepted for filename, so the two capture actions take the same name (#966). Returns the resolved PIE instance/world and image dimensions (#226/#724). target=editor reports cameraLock and a warning when the viewport is piloting an actor or locked to a Sequencer camera, since the image then comes from that actor rather than from a pose set_viewport wrote (#1361). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `filename (or outputPath), target?, pieInstance?, worldPath?` |
| `capture_screenshot_sequence(filename, frameCount?:i, intervalMs?:n, pieInstance?:n, target?, worldPath?, inline?:b/i)` | Capture a numbered frame sequence on a fixed interval, through capture_screenshot (default target=pie, the running game viewport). Frame k is scheduled at k * intervalMs from the first; one that starts after its slot is reported with lateMs rather than shifting the rest, so the sequence keeps its cadence. Frames are written as <filename>_0000.png, <filename>_0001.png and so on, under Saved/Screenshots for a relative path. Stops at the first failed frame and returns the frames already written. Returns frames [{index, filename, scheduledAtMs, capturedAtMs, durationMs, lateMs, width, height}] and maxLateMs (#1645). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the first 8 written images as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `filename, frameCount? (default 10, at most 600), intervalMs? (default 500), target? (pie\|editor\|window\|auto, default pie), pieInstance?, worldPath?` |
| `capture_scene_png(outputPath\|filename?, captureId?, cancel?:b, warmupFrames?:n, warmupTimeoutSeconds?:n, location?:v, rotation?:r, captureTransform?:o, focusActorLabel?, focusActorPath?, focusDirection?:v, focusMargin?:n, world?, pieInstance?:n, width?:n, height?:n, fov?:n, fullyLoadTextures?:b, inline?:b/i)` | Headless PNG via a transient SceneCapture2D (RGBA8 LDR). Returns captureMetadata with the actual camera transform/basis, FOV, resolution, world/PIE identity and resolved focus actor/bounds. Pair this data with this image; get_viewport_state and hit_test_viewport_pixel refer to a different, live editor camera. Without warmupFrames the capture is synchronous and its actor is destroyed before return; old stray capture actors are swept and reported. warmupFrames=1-240 starts one bounded asynchronous capture using normal streaming from the capture camera, then returns captureId and status=warming. Query this same action with captureId only until complete=true, or add cancel=true. Only the latest warm job is retained; another start while it is active is refused. warmupTimeoutSeconds defaults to 60 (1-120), checked between frames and before export. A completed job reports fileWritten, actual warmupFramesRendered, camera metadata, streaming enablement and textureResidencyVerified=false: warmup does not guarantee highest mip residency. Warm captures require fullyLoadTextures omitted or false, retain temporal rendering state, and leave viewport/config/streaming settings alone. Cancel, timeout, world cleanup and module shutdown release the transient rig. focusActorLabel or focusActorPath auto-frames the camera on that actor's bounds (#599/#662). Pending render updates are flushed before the capture so components created at runtime (BeginPlay attachments, retargeted meshes) are drawn, and for immediate PIE captures captureMetadata.runtimeComponents counts the visible runtime primitives and names any the capture still cannot draw (no render state, or bOnlyOwnerSee, which a capture owned by its own actor never shows) (#1203). A synchronous capture keeps a view state and renders settling passes before the exported frame, so Lumen lighting and auto exposure are converged; exposure is metered from the capture camera itself, not copied from the live view, and captureMetadata.exposure reports it (#1549). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the written image as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `outputPath? (or filename), captureId?, cancel?, warmupFrames?, warmupTimeoutSeconds?, location?, rotation?, captureTransform?, focusActorLabel?, focusActorPath?, focusDirection?, focusMargin?, world?, pieInstance?, width?, height?, fov?, fullyLoadTextures?` |
| `get_viewport_state(viewportIndex?:n)` | Full readout of a level viewport: viewMode, viewportType, fov, nearClip, farClipOverride, exposure (fixed or auto, with the EV100), cameraSpeed, gameView, realtime, location and rotation, plus the view modes this engine build supports. get_viewport reports location, rotation and fov only. Call this before a capture to record the conditions it was taken under, so two captures can be compared honestly. Params: `viewportIndex?` |
| `set_view_mode(viewMode, viewportIndex?:n)` | Pin the viewport's shading mode (Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, LightingOnly, DetailLighting, ShaderComplexity and the rest this build supports). The single biggest determinism lever for screenshot comparison: Unlit takes lighting out of the picture, Wireframe takes shading out. An unknown name is refused with the full list this engine supports rather than silently ignored. Idempotent: setting the mode it already has reports unchanged, and the previous mode comes back as a rollback. Params: `viewMode, viewportIndex?` |
| `set_buffer_visualization(buffer, target?:{editor,pie}, viewMode?, viewportIndex?:n, pieInstance?:n)` | Show one scene buffer full screen: Velocity (motion vectors), SceneDepth, BaseColor, WorldNormal, Roughness and the rest this engine's BufferVisualizationMaterials define. target=editor (default) sets a level viewport's buffer; target=pie sets r.BufferVisualizationTarget, which every PIE game viewport reads each frame, and puts the game viewport (or the pieInstance one) in VisualizeBuffer, so capture_screenshot(target=pie) records the buffer. buffer=Overview shows the grid of all buffers; buffer=off returns to viewMode (default Lit). An unknown name is refused with availableBuffers. Reports previousBuffer and previousViewMode with a rollback to them (#1645). Params: `buffer, target?, viewMode?, viewportIndex?, pieInstance?` |
| `render_mesh_studio(captures:[o], outputDir, resolution?:i(64..4096), viewDirection?:v, lightingPreset?:{studio}, cubemapPath?, captureMode?:{beauty,matte,both}, fullyLoadTextures?:b, inline?:b/i)` | Render a list of static or skeletal meshes and assemblies under isolated studio lighting. Uses a disposable preview world, three broad rectangular lights, a cubemap skylight, fixed exposure and no bloom. Fits the camera to union bounds and optional inventory aspect. Waits across real editor frames for registration, shaders and requested texture mips; both combines beauty with an inverse-opacity matte into RGBA. Writes <id>.png and a job-specific outcome manifest. Returns per-item rendered/blocked/error with file, bounds and camera, cleanupComplete and verified dirtyPackagesUnchanged. Refuses PIE and concurrent runs. Cancels on map changes or PIE start. A changed dirty-package set fails the job without clearing dirty flags or saving. Overwrites matching PNG names in outputDir. The call waits for completion; get_mesh_studio_render reads a known job and cancel_mesh_studio_render stops it. inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the first 8 written images as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `captures, outputDir, resolution?, viewDirection?, lightingPreset?, cubemapPath?, captureMode?, fullyLoadTextures?` |
| `get_mesh_studio_render(jobId)` | Read a studio render's progress or final manifest by jobId. Retains the last 16 jobs; no preview objects remain after a job finishes. Params: `jobId` |
| `cancel_mesh_studio_render(jobId)` | Cancel a studio render, destroy its preview scene and write outcomes for unfinished items. Returns completed jobs unchanged. Params: `jobId` |
| `set_viewport_exposure(ev100?:n, fixed?:b, mode?, viewportIndex?:n)` | Pin the editor viewport to a fixed EV100 instead of auto eye-adaptation. Targets the viewport CLIENT, so it is transient, editor-only and does not dirty the level. This does not pin capture_scene_png's separate SceneCapture2D exposure. Post-process volumes remain asset(set_property) territory. Pass ev100 for a fixed value, or mode='auto' to return to eye adaptation. Params: `ev100?, fixed?, mode?, viewportIndex?` |
| `set_viewport_view(fov?:n, nearClip?:n, farClip?:n, viewportType?, cameraSpeed?:n, viewportIndex?:n)` | Set fov, nearClip, farClip, viewportType and cameraSpeed in one call. set_viewport writes only location and rotation and does not write the fov it reads back, which is the gap this fills. Reports a per-field changed flag and the previous values, and rolls back to them. nearClip's rollback is marked lossy because the engine reports the effective plane rather than the override. Params: `fov?, nearClip?, farClip?, viewportType?, cameraSpeed?, viewportIndex?` |
| `set_game_view(enabled?:b, viewportIndex?:n)` | Toggle game view, which hides editor-only overlays (grid, gizmos, actor icons, volume wireframes) so a viewport capture shows what the game shows rather than what the editor shows. Idempotent: setting the state it already has reports unchanged. Params: `enabled?, viewportIndex?` |
| `redraw_viewport(allViewports?:b, invalidateHitProxies?:b, viewportIndex?:n)` | Force the viewport to repaint. A bridge write marks the viewport dirty but does not repaint it, so a capture taken immediately afterwards can show the state from before the write. Use set_realtime instead when a ticking simulation also has to advance. Params: `allViewports?, invalidateHitProxies?, viewportIndex?` |
| `begin_transaction(description\|label?)` | Open an undo transaction so a run of writes collapses into ONE undo step. General-purpose, unlike material(begin_transaction) which is material-scoped. Nesting is reported rather than refused. Pair with end_transaction to commit or cancel_transaction to discard. Params: `description? (or label)` |
| `end_transaction()` | Commit the open undo transaction and return its index in the undo buffer. Ending with nothing open reports that rather than erroring, so a flow that already closed one is safe to replay. Params: `none` |
| `cancel_transaction(index?:n)` | Discard the open transaction and restore every object it touched. This is what makes 'do several writes, detect a failure partway, abort, leave the editor unchanged' possible at all; material's begin/end pair had no cancel, so an aborted flow could only ever commit. Cancelling with nothing open reports that rather than erroring. Params: `index?` |
| `get_undo_state()` | Report canUndo and canRedo plus the DESCRIPTION strings of what an undo or redo would actually apply, the queue length, the undo count and the current index. Look before you undo, instead of undoing and reading back a bare boolean. Params: `none` |
| `undo_redo_steps(steps?:i, direction?)` | Undo or redo several steps at once, returning appliedDescriptions: the titles of the transactions actually reversed or reapplied, which is how you confirm you undid what you meant. Stops early with a stated reason rather than silently doing fewer steps, and refuses while a transaction is open. Params: `steps?, direction?` |
| `get_transaction_history(maxEntries?:n)` | Read the undo buffer itself, newest first: per entry the index, title, id, record count, byte size and primary object, and whether it is applied or undone. currentIndex splits the applied entries from the undone ones. Use it to find the transaction a later cancel or undo should target. Params: `maxEntries?` |
| `start_trace(channels?:[s]/s, traceTarget?, file?, host?, truncate?:b, excludeTail?:b)` | Start an Unreal Insights trace. Writes a .utrace and REPORTS WHERE IT LANDED (traceFile, plus the exact UnrealInsights command that opens it); editor(analyze_trace) reads it back once the trace is stopped. Defaults to a timestamped file under <Project>/Saved/Profiling so the path is deterministic rather than invented by the engine. Idempotent in the way that matters here: a trace that is ALREADY running is reported as alreadyTracing rather than quietly starting a second one, because only one connection exists per process. A channels list where nothing resolves is refused with the closest channel names. Rollback: stop_trace. Params: `channels?, traceTarget?, file?, host?, truncate?, excludeTail?` |
| `stop_trace()` | Stop the running trace and report the finished file: absolute path, byte size, and the UnrealInsights command line that opens it. The destination is only readable while connected, so it is captured before the stop rather than lost by it. Stopping when nothing is running reports wasTracing=false rather than erroring, so a replayed flow is safe. Warns when profiling regions were still open, since those have no end event in the file. The rollback is LOSSY and says so: restarting writes a NEW .utrace and cannot reopen this one. Params: `none` |
| `pause_trace(paused?:b)` | Pause or resume the running trace by muting every active channel, without closing the file. Idempotent: pausing an already-paused trace reports changed=false. Rollback restores the previous state. Params: `paused?` |
| `get_trace_status()` | Read the whole trace system: tracing, paused, systemStatus, connectionType, destination, activeChannels, byte and memory statistics, the channel presets start_trace accepts, whether UnrealInsights is on disk, every profiling region still open, and whether a bridge-launched standalone run is alive. Params: `none` |
| `list_trace_channels(filter?, enabledOnly?:b)` | Every trace channel this build registers, with its enabled state and, on UE 5.7+, its description, id and read-only flag. This is what makes start_trace's channels parameter discoverable instead of guesswork. Params: `filter?, enabledOnly?` |
| `set_trace_channels(enable?:[s]/s, disable?:[s]/s)` | Turn named trace channels on and off, including mid-trace. Validates the WHOLE request before applying any of it, so a typo cannot leave a half-configured trace recording something other than what was asked for, and an unknown name comes back with the closest real ones. Each channel reports wasEnabled, enabled and changed read back from the trace system rather than assumed, so a read-only channel refusing at runtime is visible instead of silent. Rollback restores exactly the channels that moved. Params: `enable?, disable?` |
| `begin_profile_region(regionName, regionCategory?)` | Open a named bracket around an operation so it can be measured. Times wall clock unconditionally and, on UE 5.7+ with a trace running, also emits an Insights timing region; when it cannot emit one it says so in tracedReason rather than pretending. The name is the key: opening the same name twice reports the existing region rather than nesting two begins under one end. Rollback: end_profile_region. Params: `regionName, regionCategory?` |
| `end_profile_region(regionName)` | Close a named bracket and return what it measured: durationMs and the number of rendered frames it spanned. A region spanning zero frames says so, because a CPU-versus-GPU verdict cannot describe work that ran inside one tick. Ending a region that is not open reports wasOpen=false and lists the ones that are, rather than erroring. No inverse exists and the response says why. Params: `regionName` |
| `add_trace_bookmark(bookmarkName)` | Drop a named marker on the Insights timeline. Reports recorded=false with the reason when no trace is running or the Bookmark channel is off, instead of returning a success for an event that was dropped. Deliberately NOT idempotent: a bookmark is a point event, so two calls write two markers and the response says so. Params: `bookmarkName` |
| `get_frame_timing(cpuGpuMarginPercent?:n)` | Frame timings WITH A VERDICT: gameThreadMs, renderThreadMs, rhiThreadMs, swapBufferMs, per-thread wait time, frameMs and fps, and GPU min/avg/max drained from the RHI's own history, then bound = gpu \| cpu-game \| cpu-render \| cpu-rhi \| balanced \| unknown with the arithmetic that produced it spelled out in verdict. Says unknown when the RHI published no GPU timing rather than guessing. warnings[] names the conditions that make the numbers meaningless and the exact call that fixes each, including the unfocused-editor CPU throttle, which is a plain UPROPERTY and is therefore REPORTED here with its objectPath for editor(set_property) instead of getting a typed setter that would duplicate a working path. sampleWindow states what was actually measured: a handler runs inside one tick and cannot advance frames to build a window. Params: `cpuGpuMarginPercent?` |
| `trigger_hitch(hitchMilliseconds?:n, bookmark?:b)` | Stall the game thread for a known number of milliseconds, so hitch-detection logic can be tested against a hitch whose size is known in advance. Brackets the stall with a trace region and a bookmark so it is findable in the capture. Capped at 5000ms because this blocks the same thread the bridge answers on. Sleeping consumes no CPU, so it reads as a long frame rather than as game-thread work. No inverse: time does not come back. Params: `hitchMilliseconds?, bookmark?` |
| `analyze_trace(file?, startSeconds?:n, endSeconds?:n, hitchThresholdMs?:n, worstFrames?:i, topTimers?:i, timersPerFrame?:i, maxHitches?:i, maxBookmarks?:i, threads?:{game,all}, timerSort?:{inclusive,exclusive}, frameType?:{game,rendering}, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?)` | Read a recorded .utrace back and summarise it, through the engine's TraceServices analysis (the module Unreal Insights is built on). Returns frames {count, avgMs, p50Ms, p95Ms, p99Ms, minMs, maxMs, avgFps, framesInTrace}, hitches over hitchThresholdMs (default 50) in time order, worstFrames each with its top CPU timers by exclusive time, topTimers over the window by inclusive (default) or exclusive time with per-frame figures, gpu busy time per frame when the trace carries GPU timing (present=false with the reason otherwise, e.g. a -nullrhi editor), and bookmarks with their time and frame. file defaults to the newest .utrace under Saved/Profiling; startSeconds/endSeconds narrow the window; threads=game (default) aggregates the game thread only, all every CPU thread. Lists are bounded and say when they were cut; dumpToFile writes the whole analysis to JSON and returns the headline numbers with outputPath. A trace still being written is refused: stop it first. Long traces analyse on worker threads and report progress while the call waits. Needs UE 5.7+. Params: `file?, startSeconds?, endSeconds?, hitchThresholdMs?, worstFrames?, topTimers?, timersPerFrame?, maxHitches?, maxBookmarks?, threads?, timerSort?, frameType?, dumpToFile?, outputPath?` |
| `start_csv_profile(captureName?, maxFrames?:n, folder?)` | Start a named CSV profiler capture (the per-frame stat recorder behind csvprofile start) and wait for it to begin, then return csvPath, the file it is writing. captureName names the file (default <Project>_<timestamp>), folder defaults to Saved/Profiling/CSV, maxFrames ends it by itself after that many frames. A capture already running is reported as alreadyCapturing with its file instead of being queued behind it. Rollback: stop_csv_profile. Params: `captureName?, maxFrames?, folder?` |
| `stop_csv_profile()` | End the running CSV capture and wait for the profiler to finish writing it, then return csvPath, csvBytes and capturedFrames. Stopping when nothing runs reports wasCapturing=false (and the last capture's file) rather than erroring. Read the file with editor(summarize_csv_profile). The rollback starts a NEW capture; a finished CSV cannot be reopened. Params: `none` |
| `summarize_csv_profile(csvPath?, hitchThresholdMs?:n, maxEvents?:i, maxStats?:i, sortBy?, stats?:[s]/s)` | Summarise a CSV profiler capture on the server, without the editor: frameCount, per-stat avg/min/max/p50/p95/p99 and the frame each peak happened on, frameTime with hitches over hitchThresholdMs (default 50) and avgFps, the events the capture recorded with their frames, and the metadata block. csvPath defaults to the newest capture in <Project>/Saved/Profiling/CSV (a relative path is tried there first); .csv.gz is read too. stats filters columns by case-insensitive substring; sortBy is avg (default), max, p95 or name; maxStats (default 50) and maxEvents (default 50) bound the lists, with totals reported. complete=false (with a warning) means the file had no closing metadata row: the capture was still running. Params: `csvPath?, stats?, sortBy?, maxStats?, maxEvents?, hitchThresholdMs?` |
| `launch_standalone(mapName?, channels?:[s]/s, traceFile?, windowed?:b, resX?:n, resY?:n, extraArgs?)` | Launch the project as a separate -game process, optionally tracing, so frame times come from a real game process rather than from the editor. Passing channels (or traceFile) adds -trace and -tracefile, and the response carries the .utrace path plus the UnrealInsights command that opens it. Idempotent: a bridge-launched run that is still alive is reported as alreadyRunning rather than joined by a second. When the editor runs offscreen, the game is launched offscreen too. The process is detached and its output is not read; poll get_standalone_status. Rollback: stop_standalone. Params: `mapName?, channels?, traceFile?, windowed?, resX?, resY?, extraArgs?` |
| `get_standalone_status()` | Is the bridge-launched standalone run still alive: running, processId, commandLine, uptimeSeconds, the exit code once it has ended, and its .utrace path with the command that opens it. Only reports runs this bridge started; one launched another way is not tracked. Params: `none` |
| `stop_standalone()` | Terminate the standalone run this bridge launched, killing its process tree so nothing is left holding the .utrace open. Stopping when nothing is running reports wasRunning=false rather than erroring. Termination is not a graceful quit and the response says what that costs. No inverse: relaunching is a new run. Params: `none` |
| `set_realtime(enabled?:b)` | Toggle realtime update on the level editor viewports so the editor-world sim (Niagara, anims) ticks - otherwise capture_scene_png renders an unticked, empty sim (#537). Params: `enabled?` |
| `get_viewport()` | Get viewport camera. Params: `none` |
| `hit_test_viewport_pixel(x:n, y:n, width?:n, height?:n, maxDistance?:n, ignoreActors?:[s])` | Ray-cast from a screen pixel through the active editor viewport and return the first hit. Builds the ray from the live viewport's projection matrix (no FOV/aspect guessing). width and height override the viewport size when picking from a different-resolution screenshot. Returns hit + actorLabel/actorClass/componentName/componentClass/materialPath/location/impactPoint/normal/distance/faceIndex/boneName/physicalMaterial (#418). Params: `x, y, width?, height?, maxDistance?, ignoreActors?` |
| `get_runtime_values(classFilter?, componentName?, paths:[s], world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Bulk runtime read across the active world. For each actor/component matching classFilter, resolves every path against the (actor\|component) root and returns rows of {actorLabel, actorClass, componentName?, componentClass?, values, errors?}. Paths support property hops, sub-object hops, and BlueprintCallable getter calls at any segment (e.g. 'PowerConnector.GetRequired' reaches a UFUNCTION on a UObject sub-object). A getter that takes arguments is written with them inline, 'GetMirroredTallyWeight(overclock)' or 'GetBalance(gold, 2)', which is what makes a keyed accessor readable across every matched instance in one call; the literals are coerced by the same rules invoke_object_function's args use, so FName/FString/int/float/bool/enum all read (#969). classFilter matches actor class OR component class - omit to match everything. An actor whose own class does not match answers with one row per matching component, so two InstancedStaticMeshComponents on one actor are two rows; matched counts rows and matchedActors the actors. componentName roots every path at the component with that instance name (case-insensitive) and skips actors without one, so two components of the same class are addressable apart (#1113). The first segment of a path may also name a component by instance name (case-insensitive) or by class when only one component has it ('CharacterMovementComponent.GroundFriction'); a segment that resolves to nothing lists the actor's components with their classes and the properties it could have been (#1204). To enumerate a live actor's components, use level(query_components, world='pie', actorLabelContains=...). A path whose result is a TArray/TSet/TMap comes back as real JSON rather than one string (#885). World defaults to PIE if running, else editor (#414). Params: `classFilter?, componentName?, paths, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `set_viewport(location?:v, rotation?:r, projection?, viewportType?, orthoZoom?:n)` | Set the viewport camera, its projection and its orthographic zoom. The projection is switched BEFORE the requested pose is applied, because the viewport keeps a separate transform cache per projection and writing the pose first would hand back the camera from the mode you just left. Every value is validated before anything is written, and the rollback restores the projection and zoom as well as the location and rotation. Acts on the active level viewport (#1029). When the viewport is piloting an actor or locked to a Sequencer camera the pose snaps back on the next tick, so the result carries cameraLock {kind: pilot\|cinematic, actorLabel, actorPath} and a warning (#1361). Params: `location?, rotation?, projection?, viewportType?, orthoZoom?` |
| `focus_on_actor(actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Focus on actor. Pass actorLabel or actorPath (#983). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `create_sequence(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, displayRate?:*)` | Create Level Sequence. displayRate sets its display rate up front (#1641). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, displayRate?` |
| `get_sequence_info(assetPath\|path, includeSectionDetails?:b)` | Read sequence: bindings (possessable/spawnable) with their Sequencer tags (#556), each possessable's parentGuid, each spawnable's template class and transform, and each binding's and root tracks with class, name and displayName (the label Sequencer shows, such as the rig on a Control Rig track) and every section's class, range, isActive and rowIndex (#1644), plus a SkeletalAnimation section's animation: clip, offsets and play rate (#1641). includeSectionDetails adds blendType, attach sockets and each channel's key times and default value, which is what a constant transform with zero keys evaluates to. UNITS: playbackRange is reported in TICKS (tick resolution, commonly 24000/s), while MovieSceneScripting*Channel.add_key defaults its time_unit to DISPLAY_RATE. Keys authored with a tick number under the default unit land roughly 800x past the range and the track evaluates to its first key, which presents as transforms that do not work on a structurally perfect sequence (#881). Params: `assetPath (or path), includeSectionDetails?` |
| `add_sequence_track(assetPath\|path, trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, materialParameterCollection?)` | Add an empty track. actorLabel or actorPath binds it to an actor; omit both for a master track (#983). trackType MaterialParameterCollection (MPC) needs materialParameterCollection, the collection asset the track animates (#1407). Params: `assetPath (or path), trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, materialParameterCollection?` |
| `add_sequence_section(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, startSeconds?:n, endSeconds?:n, cameraActorLabel?, cameraActorPath?, materialParameterCollection?, animation?, startFrameOffset?:i, endFrameOffset?:i, playRate?:n)` | Add a section to a track (creating the track if needed), set its start/end in seconds, and for a CameraCut track bind it to a camera. actorLabel or actorPath scopes the track to an actor binding. Returns the section index, its range, the channel names to key, and trackCreated. A track that is created with a section of its own gets that section rather than a second overlapping one (reusedDefaultSection) (#548/#983/#1232). On a SkeletalAnimation track, animation sets the clip, startFrameOffset/endFrameOffset trim it in ticks, and playRate scales it; without endSeconds the section spans the clip after those, and the result's animation object reads them back (#1641). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, startSeconds?, endSeconds?, cameraActorLabel?, cameraActorPath?, materialParameterCollection?, animation?, startFrameOffset?, endFrameOffset?, playRate?` |
| `set_sequence_keyframes(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?:i, channel, keyframes:[o], interpolation?)` | Add keyframes to a section channel. Transform channels: Location.X/Y/Z, Rotation.X/Y/Z (or friendly x/y/z, yaw/pitch/roll); Fade/Float: the float channel (#548). interpolation is cubic, linear or constant, and a keyframe's own interpolation field wins (#1232). For any other channel use set_sequence_channel_keys. Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), trackType, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?, channel, keyframes, interpolation?` |
| `get_sequence_channel_keys(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?:i, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?:i, channel?, sampleStartFrame?:n, sampleEndFrame?:n, sampleStep?:n)` | Read a section's channels through its channel proxy: every key (tick, displayFrame, seconds, value, interpolation) and the channel default, for one channel or all of them. Works on any section, including the MovieSceneParameterSection of an MPC track, whose channels are named Intensity, Tint.R/G/B/A and so on. The track is chosen by trackType and/or trackName (trackIndex when several match) among the root tracks, or within a binding via bindingGuid, bindingName or actorLabel/actorPath; nothing is created. sampleStartFrame/sampleEndFrame/sampleStep also evaluate the curve at display frames, which replaces baking the channel through Python (#1407). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?, channel?, sampleStartFrame?, sampleEndFrame?, sampleStep?` |
| `set_sequence_channel_keys(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?:i, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?:i, channel, keyframes?:[o], interpolation?, clearExisting?:b, defaultValue?:*, clearDefault?:b, parameterType?)` | Write keys and the default value of one named channel on any section, through its channel proxy. keyframes take seconds, frame (display) or tick, a number or boolean value, and an optional per-key interpolation (cubic, linear, constant). clearExisting replaces the whole key set; defaultValue/clearDefault set or remove the default. On an MPC track a name the section does not animate yet is added first, its type read from the collection (parameterType overrides it, and names it on other MovieSceneParameterSection tracks). Validates every key before writing, reads the channel back, and reports keysVerified plus any mismatches. Rollback rewrites the channel with its previous keys and default (#1407). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex?, channel, keyframes?, interpolation?, clearExisting?, defaultValue?, clearDefault?, parameterType?` |
| `remove_sequence_section(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?:i, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex:i)` | Remove one section from a track by sectionIndex, using the same track selector as get_sequence_channel_keys. Reports the removed section's class and range and the section count before and after. The rollback is the editor undo of the removal's transaction, valid while it is still the latest on the undo stack (#1232). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), trackType?, trackName?, trackIndex?, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, sectionIndex` |
| `resolve_sequence_bindings(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, bindingGuid?, bindingName?)` | What every binding of a Level Sequence resolves to in the editor world right now: bound objects with world transforms, possessedClass, parentGuid, and stale=true for a possessable that resolves to nothing. Filter with bindingGuid or bindingName. Use it to find bindings whose actors were re-created (#1356). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), bindingGuid?, bindingName?` |
| `rebind_possessable(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, includeChildren?:b, componentMap?:o, renameBinding?:b)` | Retarget an existing possessable binding to a current level actor without destroying it: the binding guid is kept, so its tracks and every reference to it (camera cuts, attach sections) stay valid. Child component possessables follow the matching components on the new actor (by binding name, then componentMap, then a unique component of the possessed class). Verifies by resolving the binding again and fails when it does not resolve to exactly that actor; children report verified per child. renameBinding renames it to the actor label. The sequence is marked dirty, not saved. Rollback rebinds the previous actor when there was one (#1356). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), bindingGuid?, bindingName?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, includeChildren?, componentMap?, renameBinding?` |
| `get_sequence_runtime_bindings(world?, pieInstance?:n, sequencePath?, actorLabel?)` | Every LevelSequenceActor in a world (auto: PIE when running, else editor) with its sequence, playback state (isPlaying, isPaused, currentTime), overrideInstanceData and instance-data transform origin, and for each binding of its player the bound objects with world transforms. This maps a PIE actor to the player and binding that own it, which tells it apart from the duplicates an open Sequencer editor spawns (#1232). Params: `world?, pieInstance?, sequencePath?, actorLabel?` |
| `get_sequence_binding_components(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, bindingGuid?, bindingName?, componentClass?, propertyNames?:[s])` | The components of every Level Sequence binding with their property values, without opening or evaluating the sequence. A spawnable is read off its object template (legacy spawnable or custom binding), a possessable off the actor or component it resolves to in the editor world; a Blueprint class contributes the construction script templates the template holds no instance of. Each component reports name, class, path, source (instance, blueprintClassTemplate, bound) and properties. propertyNames takes C++ or Python spelling and dotted paths, ["*"] reads every editable property, and the default is the primitive rendering flags (CastShadow, bAffectDynamicIndirectLighting, bAffectDistanceFieldLighting, bVisibleInRayTracing, bHoldout, LightingChannels, custom depth and stencil, visibility). Names a component lacks go to missingProperties when asked for. Filter with bindingGuid, bindingName and componentClass (#1640). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), bindingGuid?, bindingName?, componentClass?, propertyNames?` |
| `set_sequence_playback_range(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, startSeconds:n, endSeconds:n)` | Set a Level Sequence's playback range in seconds (#548). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), startSeconds, endSeconds` |
| `set_sequence_display_rate(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, displayRate:*)` | Set a Level Sequence's display rate, the frame grid Sequencer shows, frame-based scrubbing reads and bakes sample at. displayRate is frames per second (23.976, 29.97 and 59.94 map to the NTSC rates) or {numerator, denominator}. Keys and ranges are stored in ticks and keep their times. Returns the new and previous rate; rollback restores the previous one (#1641). Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), displayRate` |
| `play_sequence(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path?, sequenceAction?)` | Play/stop/pause a Level Sequence in Sequencer. Pass sequencePath (or assetPath) to target a specific sequence - it is opened first, because the underlying Sequencer commands act on whatever is currently open. Omit it and the call applies to the open sequence and says so. sequenceAction defaults to play. Params: `sequencePath? (or assetPath, or path), sequenceAction?` |
| `scrub_sequence(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path?, seconds?:n, frame?:n, timeUnit?)` | Park the Sequencer playhead on an exact time and evaluate there, then return. This is what makes scrub-then-capture_scene_png deterministic: play_sequence only offers play/pause/stop and realtime playback races the capture. Pauses first, scrubs, and forces the evaluation before answering, because the playhead move alone does not write possessed-actor transforms. Pass exactly one of seconds or frame. frame is read in timeUnit: display (default, the frame numbers Sequencer shows) or tick (the units get_sequence_info's playbackRange reports). Returns the evaluated time in all three units plus displayRate/tickResolution/playbackRange, and warns when the time is outside the playback range (#881). Params: `sequencePath? (or assetPath, or path), seconds?, frame?, timeUnit?` |
| `render_sequence_frames(sequencePath\|assetPath\|path, startFrame?:n, endFrame?:n, startSeconds?:n, endSeconds?:n, frameStep?:n, maxFrames?:n, width?:n, height?:n, outputDir?, format?, cameraActorLabel?, cameraActorPath?, location?:v, rotation?:r, fov?:n, fullyLoadTextures?:b, inline?:b/i)` | Render a Level Sequence to a PNG image sequence in ONE call: for each frame it scrubs, forces the evaluation, and captures through a transient SceneCapture2D (RGBA8 LDR, real PNG), instead of scrub_sequence + capture_scene_png per frame. Camera: the sequence's camera cuts by default (frames with no active cut are skipped and reported), or cameraActorLabel/cameraActorPath for one camera actor, or location/rotation/fov for a fixed camera. The camera's own FOV and post process are used. Range is in display frames: startFrame and endFrame (inclusive), or startSeconds and endSeconds (end exclusive); default is the playback range. frameStep skips frames. More frames than maxFrames is refused. Files are written to outputDir (absolute or project-relative, default Saved/SequenceFrames/<sequence>) as <sequence>.<frame>.png. Refused while PIE runs. The playhead is restored afterwards and playback is left paused. A run that nears the 600s timeout stops, returns truncated=true and nextStartFrame. Returns files[], frames[] with per-frame evaluateMs/captureMs/exportMs/totalMs, and timing totals (#1098). inline=true, or a longest-edge size in pixels, also returns the first 8 written images as image content, scaled down when larger. Params: `sequencePath (or assetPath, or path), startFrame?, endFrame?, startSeconds?, endSeconds?, frameStep?, maxFrames?, width?, height?, outputDir?, format?, cameraActorLabel?, cameraActorPath?, location?, rotation?, fov?, fullyLoadTextures?` |
| `mrq_create_job(sequence, map?, jobName?, preset?, graph?, outputDirectory?, fileNameFormat?, width?:n, height?:n, format?, startFrame?:n, endFrame?:n)` | Add a job to the editor's Movie Render Queue (needs the Movie Render Pipeline plugin): sequence to render, map to render in (default the open level, which must be saved), and either a preset (a MoviePipelinePrimaryConfig copied into the job) or a graph (a MovieGraphConfig, Movie Render Graph). For a preset job, outputDirectory, fileNameFormat, width+height, format (png \| jpg \| exr \| bmp, replacing the job's other image outputs) and startFrame+endFrame (display frames, end exclusive) are applied to the job's own configuration copy, never the preset asset; a deferred render pass is added when it has none and existing output is overwritten on rerun. A graph job takes those from its graph, so they are refused with a graph. A job name already in the queue reports existed=true and changes nothing. Rolls back through mrq_delete_job. Params: `sequence, map?, jobName?, preset?, graph?, outputDirectory?, fileNameFormat?, width?, height?, format?, startFrame?, endFrame?` |
| `mrq_list_jobs()` | List the Movie Render Queue's jobs: name, sequence, map, enabled, consumed, status and progress, configMode (preset or graph) with the graph or preset origin, and for preset jobs the output folder, file name format, resolution, custom range, output formats, render passes and every setting class. isRendering says whether the queue is rendering now. Params: `none` |
| `mrq_delete_job(jobName?, jobIndex?:i)` | Delete a Movie Render Queue job by jobName or jobIndex. Refused while the queue renders. A name no job has reports alreadyRemoved=true. Rolls back through mrq_create_job with the job's sequence, map, name, preset or graph and output folder, marked lossy since other edits to its configuration copy are not in the record. Params: `jobName?, jobIndex?` |
| `mrq_render(jobNames?:[s], wait?:b)` | Render Movie Render Queue jobs in the editor through the PIE executor: jobNames, or every enabled job. The chosen jobs render even when consumed by an earlier render, and the queue's enabled flags are put back afterwards. wait=true (default) answers when the render ends, reporting progress while it runs, with render.outputs (the image and video files written since it started), the Movie Render Pipeline's warnings and errors, rendered and cancelled; cancelling the call cancels the render. wait=false answers once it starts; follow it with mrq_get_render_status and mrq_list_outputs. Refused while PIE runs or another render is in progress. No inverse: delete the files listed to undo it. Params: `jobNames?, wait?` |
| `mrq_get_render_status()` | Status of the Movie Render Queue render in flight (render) or of the last one (lastRender): jobs with their progress and status message, overall progress, elapsedSeconds, the pipeline's warnings and errors, and once finished its outputs, rendered and cancelled. isRendering reads the queue subsystem directly. Params: `none` |
| `mrq_cancel_render()` | Cancel the Movie Render Queue render in progress; every job in it stops after the frame in flight and frames already written stay on disk. alreadyStopped=true when nothing was rendering. No inverse: mrq_render starts it again. Params: `none` |
| `mrq_list_outputs(jobName?, outputDirectory?, limit?:n)` | List the image and video files under a Movie Render Queue output folder, newest first: a job's output folder (jobName), any folder (outputDirectory), or by default the folders of the last render, else of every queued job. Tokens other than {project_dir} and {engine_dir} cut the scan at the folder before them. Each file has path, sizeBytes and modifiedUtc. Params: `jobName?, outputDirectory?, limit?` |
| `build_all()` | Build all (geometry, lighting, paths, HLOD). Params: `none` |
| `build_geometry()` | Rebuild BSP geometry. Params: `none` |
| `build_hlod()` | Build HLODs. Params: `none` |
| `validate_assets(directory?, assetPath?, assetPaths?:[s])` | Run data validation over a directory (default /Game/) or over exact assets named by assetPath or assetPaths, one selector per call. Params: `directory?, assetPath?, assetPaths?` |
| `get_build_status()` | Get build/map status. Params: `none` |
| `cook_content(platform?)` | Cook content. Params: `platform?` |
| `get_log(maxLines\|lastN?:i, filter?, category?, cursor?, limit?:n)` | Read output log. maxLines selects how far back into the ring buffer to read (default 100, or the whole buffer when filter or category is given); limit pages the lines that match filter/category within that window, and each line carries the sequence number that anchors a cursor. Params: `maxLines? (or lastN), filter?, category?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `search_log(query, maxResults?:i, cursor?, limit?:n)` | Search the captured log. Every match in the 4096-line ring buffer is collected and paged, so a busy log reports how many matched instead of stopping at the first hundred. maxResults caps the search itself and reports cappedAtMaxResults when it was what ended the collection. Params: `query, maxResults?, cursor?, limit?` |
| `run_map_check(maxMessages?:i, severity?)` | Run Map Check on the open level, the same pass as Build > Map Check without its results window, and return the messages it wrote: severity, text, the objects each names and the actorLabel of the first actor, with errors, warnings and total counts. Each run starts a fresh MapCheck page, so the messages are this run's (#1828). Params: `maxMessages?, severity?` |
| `log_map_check_message(severity, message, actorLabel?, actorPath?)` | Add an error, warning or info message to the MapCheck listing, optionally linked to an actor (UMapCheckSubsystem::LogMapCheckError, LogMapCheckWarning and LogMapCheckInfo on UE 5.9, the same FMessageLog write before it). Read it back with get_message_log logName=MapCheck; the next run_map_check starts a fresh page (#1828). Params: `severity, message, actorLabel?, actorPath?` |
| `add_python_path(path, owner?, mountPointRoot?)` | UE 5.9: put an existing absolute folder on the editor Python's sys.path, optionally under an owner name and with a mountPointRoot that gives generated types stable names (UPythonScriptLibrary::AddAdditionalPath). A path already registered is reported as existed; the rollback removes it. Refused when the path is already on sys.path from another source (#1828). Params: `path, owner?, mountPointRoot?` |
| `remove_python_path(any(path; owner))` | UE 5.9: take a registered additional path off sys.path (UPythonScriptLibrary::RemoveAdditionalPath), or with only owner every path that owner registered (RemoveAdditionalPaths). Modules already imported stay loaded. Reports removedPaths, or alreadyRemoved when nothing was registered (#1828). Params: `at least one of path/owner` |
| `list_python_paths(owner?)` | UE 5.9: the additional Python paths registered to every owner (UPythonScriptLibrary::GetAllAdditionalPaths), or to one owner (GetAdditionalPaths, with ownerRegistered) (#1828). Params: `owner?` |
| `get_message_log(logName?, maxLines?:i, severity?)` | Read a Message Log listing (MapCheck, AssetCheck, PIE, LoadErrors, LightingResults...). Call with NO logName to list the registered listings with their error/warning counts, then read one. Counts come from the listing itself; message bodies come from the current page and honour the Message Log tab's severity checkboxes, so when fewer are readable than exist the response says so instead of reading clean. An unknown logName is an error, not an empty log. Blueprint COMPILE results are not here - the compiler makes a listing per Blueprint; use blueprint(compile). Params: `logName?, maxLines?, severity?` |
| `list_crashes(cursor?, limit?:n)` | List crash reports, sorted by folder name, which is chronological. Params: `cursor?, limit?` |
| `get_crash_info(crashFolder)` | Get crash details. Params: `crashFolder` |
| `check_for_crashes()` | Check for recent crashes. Params: `none` |
| `set_dialog_policy(pattern, any(response; buttonLabel))` | Arm an answer, in advance, for dialogs whose title or message contains a pattern. READ THIS BEFORE USING IT: an armed policy presses the button for you, so from then on a matching prompt is answered and dismissed and the user never sees the question. On a save prompt that means unsaved work can be discarded without anyone reading the warning. Nothing arms a policy on your behalf - the plugin ships none and no other action arms one - so every policy in effect is one somebody typed here deliberately, and this is the only way the bridge ever answers a dialog by itself. Covers the Slate modal windows the editor raises itself (the shutdown "Save Content" prompt among them, whose buttons are Save Selected / Don't Save / Cancel). A response keyword (yes/no/ok/cancel/retry/continue/yesall/noall) resolves to whichever of the dialog's buttons carries that meaning, so response='no' presses "Don't Save"; pass buttonLabel to name a button literally instead. On a plain message dialog buttonLabel answers with the button it names (buttonLabel="Yes" answers Yes); where that dialog has no such button, a label or response answers with the nearest one it offers (yes is OK on an OK/Cancel dialog, no is Cancel), and one with no equivalent there leaves the dialog for a person (#1334). A policy set here answers a matching dialog whoever raised it, and answers one that is already on screen. To read a dialog instead of pre-answering it, use editor(list_dialogs) and then editor(respond_to_dialog). Params: `pattern, at least one of response/buttonLabel` |
| `clear_dialog_policy(pattern?)` | Clear dialog policies. Params: `pattern?` |
| `get_dialog_policy()` | Get the dialog policies currently armed, each with its response and literal buttonLabel. Every one was armed by a caller through set_dialog_policy: the plugin arms none of its own, so an empty list means nothing will answer any dialog on its own. Params: `none` |
| `list_dialogs()` | Read the modal dialog blocking the editor, in full: its exact title, its COMPLETE message text (never truncated - messageTruncated is always false), every button label in the order the dialog lays them out, and a `choices` array pairing each button with the exact editor(respond_to_dialog) call that presses it.
