When the dialog asks a question per row (the "Save Content" prompt is a checkbox per unsaved package), an `items` array reports each tickable row: its index, its label, its cells (asset name, package path, class path) and whether it is currently ticked. `blocks` is the same body in reading order without the title or button labels: paragraphs, and each list as a table {columns, rows, checked, items} (#1891). No button is marked recommended and none is reordered; choosing is yours. Also reports which armed policy matches and which button that policy would press, if any. `blocksGameThread` says whether the editor is actually held: true only for a window on Slate's modal stack, which is what parks the game thread and refuses every other action. A prompt the editor raised without AddModalWindow comes back with `blocksGameThread` false and `detectedBy` parentedWindow - it is reported, because an unanswered question must not be quit out from under, and nothing is refused for it (#1118). `notTreatedAsDialogs` names any window the walk considered and rejected, with the reason: a standalone Message Log or an undocked Output Log is a regular parented window like a dialog is, and used to block every action for the life of the session with no button that could answer it (#1078). A window in that list is NOT blocking anything. Also reports `windows`: every open modal and floating window with the windowId editor(list_windows), press_window_button and close_window take. Runs even while a dialog is blocking the editor, when every other handler times out, so this is the way to see what the editor is asking. Params: `none` |
| `respond_to_dialog(any(buttonLabel; buttonIndex:n; dialogAction), items?:[o])` | Press one named button on the active modal dialog, releasing the game thread. This is the deliberate way to answer a dialog: read it with editor(list_dialogs) first, then name the button you chose. Runs even while the dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE. The dialog handling mode decides who answers, and it is enforced here: under interactive the question is put to the person in an elicitation form (raised on the call AFTER the one that hands the dialog back, so its text is read somewhere nothing truncates it) and only their button is pressed, under defer they answer it in the Unreal Editor window, and in both this call is refused with the dialog named. editor(list_dialogs) stays available in every mode, so the dialog can always be READ. Pass dialogAction='close' (or 'escape') to destroy the dialog window when no button label fits, which ends the modal without answering the question. It is NOT called 'action': that name is this tool's own dispatch field, so a call writing action='close' selects a nonexistent editor action and never reaches the dialog (#1078). Pass items to tick or untick the dialog's own rows before the button is pressed, which is what makes "Save Selected" mean something: read them from editor(list_dialogs) and send [{index, checked}] for the ones you want changed. The ticks and the press happen in this one call, so a modal is never left holding a selection nobody pressed anything on. Params: `at least one of buttonLabel/buttonIndex/dialogAction, items?` |
| `list_windows(windowId?:i, maxTexts?:i, maxTextChars?:i, maxButtons?:i)` | Every open modal and floating editor window except the main window, each with a windowId, its title, isModal, isActiveModal, receivesInput, hasParentWindow, hostsDockTabs, isVisible, gatesBridge (true for the window the dialog gate is refusing calls for), its visible texts, and its buttons with index, label, toolTip and enabled state. Reaches what list_dialogs does not: a second prompt behind the first, a floating Message Log or asset editor, a window behind a notification. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. Pass windowId to describe one window (#1231). Params: `windowId?, maxTexts?, maxTextChars?, maxButtons?` |
| `press_window_button(windowId:i, one(buttonLabel; buttonIndex:n))` | Press one button of an open window, by buttonLabel or buttonIndex from editor(list_windows). Refuses a disabled button, a label matching more than one button, and a window that does not receive input while another window is modal. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE, like respond_to_dialog (#1231). Params: `windowId, buttonLabel OR buttonIndex` |
| `close_window(windowId:i)` | Close an open window the way its own close box does: a floating dock area asks its tabs first, and a modal ends unanswered. Served while a dialog is blocking the editor. ONLY IN auto MODE, like respond_to_dialog (#1231). Params: `windowId` |
| `open_asset(assetPath\|path, saveFirst?:b, discardUnsaved?:b)` | Open asset in its editor. A map opens as the editor world through level(load), so it refuses while the open map has unsaved changes unless saveFirst or discardUnsaved is passed (#1259). Params: `assetPath (or path), saveFirst?, discardUnsaved?` |
| `get_open_asset_editors()` | What the user currently has open in the editor, and which of it holds focus. Returns every open asset editor with its asset path/class, its window and major tab label, and its own tabs - so an open PCG Graph, the Blueprint graph documents someone has open, and the Details panel they are looking at all come back by name. Unreal publishes no single answer to this: the asset editor subsystem knows what is open, the global tab manager knows the active tab, and each tab knows when it was last activated, and nothing joins them. focusedAssetEditor is the editor holding Slate's active tab, activeTab.context says whether that tab is in an asset editor, the Level Editor or elsewhere, and mostRecentlyActiveAssetEditor is where the user last was. Read editorApplicationFocused before trusting the word focused: an agent driven from a terminal has taken OS focus away from Unreal, so Slate's active tab is a record of where the user was rather than where their cursor is, and focusNote says which of the two this answer is. Reads only - it never focuses or opens anything, which editor(open_asset) is for (#1112). Params: `none` |
| `reload_bridge()` | Hot-reload Python bridge handlers from disk. Params: `none` |
| `save_dirty(includeMaps?:b, includeContent?:b, commitDeletes?:b)` | Flush every dirty package and return a per-package saved/failed map. Use after multi-step CDO/component edits when set_class_default leaves the asset dirty without persisting (#378). The emptied external package of a deleted World Partition or one-file-per-actor actor is deleted from disk rather than failed, and listed under deleted (#1301). The bridge keeps that package loaded from the delete until a save commits it, so a garbage collection in between no longer loses the delete (#1545). With commitDeletes=true it uses the editor's own dirty-package save instead, which deletes the external package of a deleted World Partition actor rather than failing with 'SavePackage returned false', and reports written, deleted and stillDirty per package (#1156). Params: `includeMaps?, includeContent?, commitDeletes?` |
| `configure_pie(numClients?:n, netMode?, runUnderOneProcess?:b, launchSeparateServer?:b, newWindowWidth?:n, newWindowHeight?:n, clientWindowWidth?:n, clientWindowHeight?:n, newWindowPosition?:o, centerNewWindow?:b, playMode?)` | Set ULevelEditorPlaySettings - multi-client PIE, net mode, single-process flag, Play-in-New-Window resolution (#384/#671), and multiplayer client window placement: clientWindowWidth/clientWindowHeight size each additional client window, newWindowPosition {x,y} places new PIE windows and turns centerNewWindow off unless it is passed too (#1235). playMode viewport \| new_window \| standalone sets where the Play button and every bridge PIE launch play; the default is the active level viewport (#1526). Reports every setting read back after the write with its previous value, and a rollback to the previous values. get_pie_config reports the same fields. Params: `numClients?, netMode?, runUnderOneProcess?, launchSeparateServer?, newWindowWidth?, newWindowHeight?, clientWindowWidth?, clientWindowHeight?, newWindowPosition?, centerNewWindow?, playMode?` |
| `get_pie_config()` | Read current ULevelEditorPlaySettings (numClients, netMode, single-process, separate-server) (#384). Params: `none` |
| `pose_debug_camera(enabled?:b, location?:v, rotation?:r, lookAtActorLabel?, lookAtActorPath?, playerIndex?:n, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Eject and aim the PIE debug camera (ToggleDebugCamera free camera) for verification shots. Moving the DebugCameraController actor is overridden by its free camera, so this poses what the camera follows: the spectator pawn (moved with its velocity stopped) and the control rotation. location and rotation set the pose, lookAtActorLabel/lookAtActorPath aim at an actor's bounds center, enabled=false returns control to the player. Reports the camera location and rotation read back from the camera manager and a rollback to the previous state (#1250). Params: `enabled?, location?, rotation?, lookAtActorLabel?, lookAtActorPath?, playerIndex?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `set_pie_view_target(any(actorLabel; actorPath), playerIndex?:n, blendTime?:n, world?, pieInstance?:n)` | Make an actor the running PIE player's view target (PlayerController SetViewTargetWithBlend, run in that instance's context), so a spawned CameraActor frames capture_screenshot(target=pie) even in a map with no possessed pawn, which pie_set_player_view cannot do. Select the actor with actorLabel or actorPath in the PIE world; playerIndex picks the player, blendTime blends instead of cutting. Reports the view target read back, pendingViewTarget while blending, the previous target, and a rollback to it (#1203). Params: `at least one of actorLabel/actorPath, playerIndex?, blendTime?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `pie_set_player_view(pitch?:n, yaw?:n, roll?:n)` | Point the running PIE player's view (control rotation) at a pitch/yaw/roll so a capture frames the intended direction. Requires PIE (#671). Params: `pitch?, yaw?, roll?` |
| `stage_game_input(inputMode?, showMouseCursor?:b)` | Stage input for the running game: set input mode (gameOnly\|gameAndUI\|uiOnly) and mouse cursor so injected/simulated input reaches the pawn. This only sets the mode; pie(inject_input) injects the input. Requires PIE (#671). Params: `inputMode?, showMouseCursor?` |
| `run_automation_tests(filter?, maxTests?:n, latentTimeoutSeconds?:n)` | Run registered Automation tests matching a filter and return per-test pass/fail plus error lines. Runs them synchronously through the test framework rather than the console queue, and suspends the editor's unfocused-CPU throttle for the duration - otherwise an unfocused editor drops to a few FPS and the framework's interactive-frame-rate gate never opens, leaving tests queued forever (#765). A test whose latent commands are still queued when latentTimeoutSeconds runs out is reported as abandoned, with the reason: latent work needs engine frames, and this runs on the game thread, so a test that starts PIE (CQTest multi-client network tests, for instance) belongs in the editor's Automation window or -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests <name>" at launch. Such a test used to terminate the editor outright (#993). Afterwards it clears the dirty flag on /Temp world packages the run dirtied that no world context still uses, so a test that left its world behind does not block level(load) or prompt on shutdown, and lists them in tempWorldsCleared; nothing is saved or deleted (#1488) (#693). Params: `filter?, maxTests?, latentTimeoutSeconds?` |
| `list_dirty_packages()` | Enumerate currently-dirty content + map packages, read from the editor's own dirty-package lists (the same ones Save All uses). Includes a never-saved /Temp world, because an unsaved new map is exactly the unsaved work a caller needs to see before closing or reloading (#340). Params: `none` |
| `discard_dirty(packages:[s], dryRun?:b, allowContent?:b)` | Clear the dirty flag on the packages named, so closing the editor does not stop on unsaved state nobody wants. Only packages in packages are touched, all or nothing: one refusal clears none. Transient packages and /Engine maps (their built data and external actors too), such as the /Engine/Maps/Entry startup map that cannot be saved, are always allowed. Project and plugin content, never-saved /Temp maps and engine content outside a map are refused unless allowContent=true, because their unsaved edits are lost when the editor closes; code and PIE packages are always refused. Each package is reported as cleared, notDirty, refused (with a reason) or, under dryRun, wouldClear, with its kind, and remainingDirty lists what the editor's close prompt would still ask about. The edits stay in memory until the editor closes. editor(stop_editor, discardTransient=true) runs this for every disposable package before the quit. Params: `packages, dryRun?, allowContent?` |
| `get_world_state()` | One atomic read of which world is open and what is unsaved. Returns editorWorldName, editorWorldPackage, persistentLevelPackage, worldPackageDirty, a sorted dirtyPackages list with counts, and the editor/play/simulate mode. level(get_current) plus editor(list_dirty_packages) is two calls, so the editor can change between them and neither result proves which world the other described; this answers both in one game-thread dispatch. Read-only, and fails closed rather than reporting an empty world as a clean one (#920/#921). Params: `none` |
| `request_editor_shutdown(allowContent?:b, dirtyPackages?, endPIE?:b, packages?:[s], requireClean?:b)` | Ask the editor to close itself from inside the engine, after it has checked that closing is safe. Refuses by default when any content or map package is dirty (including an unsaved /Temp world) and reports which ones, so nothing is lost to a silent discard. Ends an active PIE/SIE session first and closes only once play has actually stopped. The response is returned before the process exits. Aimed at the same editor stop_editor aims at, through the same ownership check, so the two can never disagree about which editor belongs to the loaded project (#967), including what happens when none is running: both fail with alreadyStopped=true rather than one succeeding and the other refusing. This IS what stop_editor sends: stop_editor calls it with requireClean=false, so the editor schedules its own close and raises its own save prompt for anything dirty rather than the server refusing in its place. Called directly it defaults to requireClean=true, which refuses and names the dirty packages without scheduling anything. To close without the save prompt, say up front what happens to the dirty packages: dirtyPackages=save writes each one (every package is checked for writability first; any failure refuses the close and names it in failedPackages), dirtyPackages=discard clears transient or engine map dirty flags; project or plugin content additionally requires allowContent=true, and code or PIE packages are refused. DISCARD IS IRREVERSIBLE: the changes were never written and nothing keeps a copy. Both act in this call on the dirty list read in this call and report savedPackages or discardedPackages, with skippedPackages for missing or already-clean packages and deletedPackages for committed empty external packages; pass packages to name exactly which ones you expect, and any other dirty package refuses the call (unexpectedDirtyPackages) with nothing saved or discarded. Both refuse while PIE is running. If something is dirty again when the close runs, the close is called off rather than prompting. Use editor(stop_editor) for the full stop-and-confirm flow; this action is the in-engine half of it. Params: `requireClean? (default true), dirtyPackages? (default refuse), packages?, allowContent? (default false), endPIE? (default true)` |
| `batch(ops:[o], onError?, transactionDescription?)` | Run several actions as ONE game-thread job in the editor, so no call from any other session can land between them. This is the fix for multi-step edits that other agents interleave with: add a variable, add a node and connect its pins arrive as one unit, and a rename from another session cannot slip in between. ops is an ordered list of {category, method, args}, each prepared exactly as a direct call to that action would be (paths repaired, the action's own parameter contract checked) BEFORE anything is sent, and a batch with one bad step is refused whole. Every step must be an action the editor runs: an action served by this server process (start_editor, execute_python, flows, another batch), the asset lock actions, the undo and transaction actions, and the dialog actions are refused with the reason. The steps share one editor transaction, so what they changed that is transactional is ONE Undo entry; transactionDescription names it. The dialog guard checks the batch once, and when locking is enabled the locks taken are the union of every step's asset paths, held for the whole batch. onError=stop (default) ends the batch at the first failing step; continue runs every step and reports each verdict. NO ROLLBACK: the editor has no reliable inverse for every action, so a step that fails leaves the steps before it applied, and the result says exactly which ran (completedCalls, failedIndex, per-step success). Each step's answer comes back under results[i].result, including any rollback descriptor that action reports on its own. The wait is the sum of what each step would get alone, or the batch's timeoutMs; a batch that outlives the wait reports how many steps had finished, and keeps running. Params: `ops:[{category, method, args?}] (1-256), onError? (stop\|continue), transactionDescription?` |
| `checkpoint(label?)` | Record a checkpoint in this project's shadow history (Saved/UE_MCP_Bridge/shadow.git, separate from the project's own source control): the current bytes of every path written through ue-mcp since the last one, packages saved in the editor included. Returns its id, the paths it recorded as changed, and dirtyPackages: unsaved packages the history does not cover, which the editor's transactions do; save them first to record them. Bracket each group of edits (a chat turn) with one before and one after. Checkpoints are off unless ue-mcp.yml sets checkpoints: on or the daemon turned them on for the session. Params: `label?` |
| `list_checkpoints(limit?:n)` | Whether checkpoints are on for this session and why (config or session override), the shadow repository's path, and its checkpoints newest first with id, label, createdAt, trigger (client, restore-before, restore-after) and the number of files each recorded. Params: `limit? (default 50)` |
| `list_changes(from, assetDiffs?:b, blueprintDiffs?:b, to?)` | Every file that differs between checkpoint `from` and checkpoint `to`, or the project now when `to` is omitted. Each entry has path, status (added, modified, deleted), kind (package, config, source, other), and a unified text diff for config and source. Each package carries assetDiff: both versions loaded in the editor with DiffUtils::LoadPackageForDiff and Unreal's own diff code run on them, serialized per record (property differences from DiffUtils::CompareUnrelatedObjects with both values, graph differences from FGraphDiffControl::DiffGraphs with the engine's DisplayString, component differences from DiffUtils::CompareUnrelatedSCS), grouped under the engine's categories, with facts about each version, a thumbnail of each (url on the daemon), a one-line summary, and an explicit error with its reason when a package cannot be diffed. The first 25 packages are diffed; the rest are listed in assetDiffs.deferred and diffed one at a time with diff_checkpoint_asset. A modified Blueprint also keeps blueprintDiff. untracked marks a path changed outside the bridge and outside package saves, which restore will not overwrite without force. Params: `from, to?, assetDiffs? (default true), blueprintDiffs? (default true)` |
| `diff_checkpoint_asset(changedPath, from, to?)` | One package's assetDiff between checkpoint `from` and `to` (omitted: the project now), as list_changes gives it: for a package list_changes deferred past its limit, or to diff one again. Needs the editor. Params: `from, to?, changedPath (project-relative, as list_changes gives it)` |
| `open_checkpoint_diff(changedPath, from, to?)` | Open Unreal's own diff of a package between checkpoint `from` and `to` (omitted: the asset as loaded now) and bring the editor to the front: the Blueprint diff for a Blueprint, the material and material instance diffs, the details diff for other assets, or the text diff tool Editor Preferences names for a level or DataTable (refused with the reason when none is set). For an added or deleted package, the asset editor opens on the one version there is. Returns opened (window, editor or external) and windowTitle. Params: `from, to?, changedPath` |
| `restore(checkpoint, force?:b, paths?:[s])` | Put every path, or only `paths`, back to its state at a checkpoint and reload it in the editor: packages are reloaded (or unloaded and dropped from the asset registry when they did not exist then), restored config files reload their GConfig branch, and open asset editors on them are closed and reopened. Source is restored as bytes; rebuilding is yours to call. Restoring a subset is a cherry pick: the rest of the turn stays. The restore is itself bracketed by checkpoints, `before` and `after`, so restore(before) undoes it. A path edited outside the agent since the checkpoint is refused and named unless force; a path nothing recorded is refused as not-recorded. Refused during PIE. Unsaved in-memory edits are not in the history: cancel the turn's editor transaction first when reverting a whole turn. Params: `checkpoint, paths? (project-relative), force?` |
| `clear_checkpoints()` | Delete this project's checkpoint history: the shadow repository, its plain copies of large files and anything pending. Turning checkpoints off keeps the history; this is how to remove it. Params: `none` |
| `journal_group(journalGroup?)` | Name the group every later call that may change state is journaled into, until another group is named; omit journalGroup to stop journaling. Use one group per chat turn. Each journaled call records its rollback descriptor when its handler returned one, and with checkpoints on (checkpoints: on in ue-mcp.yml) a checkpoint before and after it, so the files it wrote can be put back. The journal is Saved/UE_MCP_Bridge/journal.jsonl in the project and survives restarts; the current group does not, so name it again after one. Returns the journal state. Params: `journalGroup?` |
| `list_journal(journalGroup?)` | The journal: the current group, whether checkpoints are on, and every group with its entry, revertible and reverted counts in the order they were first recorded. With journalGroup, also that group's entries: task, effect, the rollback descriptor or checkpoint snapshot that restores it, and for one that cannot be restored, the reason. Params: `journalGroup?` |
| `revert_group(journalGroup)` | Revert every call journaled into journalGroup that is not reverted yet, newest first: a rollback descriptor is replayed through the bridge (falling back to the files when it fails and a snapshot exists), otherwise the call's files are restored to the checkpoint taken before it and reloaded in the editor. Returns one result per entry: reverted, failed with the error, or not-revertible with the reason, so nothing is skipped silently. Works after an editor or server restart. Params: `journalGroup` |
| `revert_after_group(journalGroup)` | Revert every call of every group first journaled after journalGroup, newest first, the same way revert_group does; journalGroup itself is kept. Params: `journalGroup` |
| `epic_add_assets_to_collection(collection:o, assetPaths:[s])` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Adds assets to the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `collection, assetPaths` |
| `epic_call_cheat(cheatName, args)` | [Epic CheatsToolset.CheatsToolset] Runs a cheat on the local player, exactly as if it were typed into the console. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `cheatName, args` |
| `epic_capture(world:ref, camera:o, mode, options:o)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Renders offscreen from the given world and camera using the specified mode. Use ListModes for names available in this build and session; DescribeMode supplies interpretation and sub-modes. Unknown or unavailable modes raise a script error. Mode names are case-sensitive. Availability does not validate scene content or every pass prerequisite. Uses world post-process volumes, with no temporal history or camera-specific post-process overrides. This is not a live viewport screenshot. PNG output is an opaque, display-encoded 8-bit visualization, not a raw or HDR buffer export. Capture timings are not representative game-frame timings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `world, camera, mode, options` |
| `epic_capture_active_editor_view(mode, options:o)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Captures the active editor camera offscreen using the requested mode, without changing the viewport. Repeated calls follow viewport movement; use GetActiveEditorView plus Capture for a fixed camera. Mode, Options, output format and rendering limits are the same as Capture. Does not reproduce temporal history, editor overlays or camera-specific post-processing. This is not a viewport screenshot. Use DescribeMode for diagnostic guidance. Raises a script error if no active editor level viewport is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `mode, options` |
| `epic_capture_asset_image(assetPath)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Renders a thumbnail for the specified asset (e.g. static meshes, skeletal meshes, skeletons, animations, montages, materials, textures). Params: `assetPath` |
| `epic_capture_editor_image()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Captures an image of the entire editor application as the user sees it. Params: `none` |
| `epic_capture_editor_viewport(captureTransform?:o, annotations?:o, bShowUI?:b, viewportId?)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Redraws and captures an editor viewport with its view and post-process state: a level viewport or an asset editor viewport such as the Static Mesh or Skeletal Mesh Editor's. Restores camera and show flags on return; temporal history may advance or be affected by camera overrides. Asymmetric projections return the image with a warning and no camera snapshot or image FOV. Raises a script error for an unavailable/unreadable viewport or unsupported HDR encoding. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `captureTransform?, annotations?, bShowUI?, viewportId?` |
| `epic_capture_game_viewport(world:ref, maxResolution:i)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Captures the current Game or PIE viewport as Slate draws it, with UMG and any other UI over the viewport, such as the recording border. In PIE it redraws the window that holds the viewport; if that fails, the image shows the scene only, with a warning. Metadata records the world and request time, not the originating GPU frame, camera, mode or internal resolution. Output is an opaque 8-bit PNG, not a raw or HDR buffer export. PQ/scRGB HDR uses the engine screenshot decoder and sRGB8 image conversion. Conversion clips highlights and out-of-gamut channels without an additional tone curve. A warning identifies this conversion. Other HDR output encodings are rejected. Raises a script error if the host cannot render, or if no initialized, readable Game/PIE framebuffer is available. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `world, maxResolution` |
| `epic_capture_viewport(captureTransform?:o, annotations?:o, bShowUI?:b)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Captures the level viewport with optional annotations. Annotations rendering overlays a projected 3D world-space grid plus name + position labels on visible actors. The grid is drawn at a configurable ground-plane Z and projected through the camera, with coordinate numbers at intersections (shown in meters). Each labeled actor gets a crosshair at its projected screen position with a leader-line callout placed to avoid overlap. This gives a vision-capable agent spatial awareness: it can reference grid coordinates to direct placement and identify scene contents by label. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `captureTransform?, annotations?, bShowUI?` |
| `epic_center_view(time:n)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Re-centres the Rewind Debugger visible view range on Time, preserving the current view width. Independent of the scrub cursor: pair with SetScrubTime when you want to both move the cursor and bring it into the centre of the visible timeline. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `time` |
| `epic_close_editor_for_asset(assetPath, unsavedChanges)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Closes every asset editor open for the specified asset. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPath, unsavedChanges` |
| `epic_create_collection(collectionName, shareType)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Creates a new static collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `collectionName, shareType` |
| `epic_describe_mode(mode)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Describes a mode's purpose, interpretation, limits, registered sub-modes and default. Accepts the same names and aliases as Capture. Unknown names raise a script error. Availability covers capture-path and session prerequisites, not per-world content or pass activation. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `mode` |
| `epic_destroy_collection(collection:o)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Deletes the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `collection` |
| `epic_execute_python(script:o)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Runs a Python script in the editor's interpreter on the game thread. IMPORTANT: Call `read_me` once per conversation before using this tool, for full usage instructions -- including how to compose other tools and yield control during long-running work. Look up each `unreal` API with search_symbols or get_symbol before calling it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `script` |
| `epic_exit_editor(bDiscardUnsavedChanges?:b)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Requests a shutdown of the editor application. The request is queued for the next editor tick so this call can return first; the process then exits and no further tool calls are possible. Errors if any level or content package has unsaved changes and bDiscardUnsavedChanges is false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bDiscardUnsavedChanges?` |
| `epic_focus_on_actors(actors:[ref])` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Repositions the level editor camera to focus on the specified actors. Cannot be called while PIE is active. Params: `actors` |
| `epic_get_active_editor_modes()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the IDs of the currently active editor modes. More than one mode can be active at once; the default placement mode ("EM_Default") is usually present. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_active_editor_view(viewportId?)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Snapshots a level editor viewport's world, camera and clipping planes: ViewportId's, or the active one. Asset editor viewports are refused, since Capture cannot render their preview worlds. Pass World and Camera to Capture. Match SourceDimensions' aspect ratio to retain framing; letterboxing is excluded. The snapshot does not follow viewport movement. Requires an interactive editor session and an active level viewport. Raises a script error if the viewport is unavailable, has zero size or uses an unsupported projection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `viewportId?` |
| `epic_get_asset_editor_selection(asset:ref)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets what is selected inside the asset editor for the given asset (e.g. selected graph nodes in a Blueprint or Material editor, selected widgets in a UMG editor, and objects shown in the editor's details panels). This is distinct from level-actor selection (GetSelectedActors) and content-browser selection (GetSelectedAssets). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `asset` |
| `epic_get_asset_thumbnails(assetPaths:[s])` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the assets' existing cached thumbnails (the images the Content Browser shows) without loading or rendering the assets. On success the result's value holds one image per requested path, in request order; an entry is an empty image when the asset has no saved thumbnail or its thumbnail could not be decoded. The call completes with an error instead if any requested path cannot be found. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPaths` |
| `epic_get_camera_transform()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the position and rotation of the level viewport camera. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_collection_assets(collection:o)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Returns the assets in the specified collection. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `collection` |
| `epic_get_content_browser_path()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the current path of the active content browser. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_csv_info(path, statNameFilter?, bIncludeAllMetadata?:b, groupDepth?:i)` | [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Surveys a capture without returning per-frame values. StatGroups (the group histogram) is always populated; individual stat names only when StatNameFilter is set. GroupDepth groups the histogram by the first N segments of the '/'-delimited stat tree: depth 1 buckets under "Exclusive", depth 2 under "Exclusive/GameThread". Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, statNameFilter?, bIncludeAllMetadata?, groupDepth?` |
| `epic_get_cvar_value(name)` | [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Reads the current value of a console variable as its canonical string representation (e.g. "true"/"false" for bools, "1.5" for floats). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `name` |
| `epic_get_frame_timings()` | [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Reads the engine's per-frame timing globals once (no smoothing - usually the previous frame). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_frame_tree(minInclusiveMs:n, maxDepth:i, pathFilter)` | [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Captures the latest stat frame as a nested tree. Siblings sorted most-expensive first. Top-level entries are typically thread roots (GameThread, RenderThread). On leaves, ExclusiveMs equals InclusiveMs. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `minInclusiveMs, maxDepth, pathFilter` |
| `epic_get_log_categories(filter)` | [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns a sorted list of registered log categories. Params: `filter` |
| `epic_get_log_entries(category?, pattern, maxEntries?:i)` | [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns log entries from the current session's log file. Params: `category?, pattern, maxEntries?` |
| `epic_get_object_events(objectId:i, startTime:n, endTime:n)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns all events that fired on a recorded object within a time range. Events represent discrete occurrences such as Linguine prompt executions. Returns {"Events": []} when no session is active or no events exist in the range. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `objectId, startTime, endTime` |
| `epic_get_object_properties(objectId:i, time:n)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the recorded property state of an object at or before a given time. Uses closest-before semantics: returns the most recent snapshot at or before Time. Returns {} when no session is active or no snapshot exists before Time. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `objectId, time` |
| `epic_get_open_assets()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the list of assets currently open in asset editors. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_pivot_location()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the current location of the editor's transform-gizmo pivot. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_recent_transactions(count?:i, offset?:i)` | [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns transactions from the undo history, newest first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `count?, offset?` |
| `epic_get_selected_actors()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the currently selected actors in the level editor. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_selected_assets()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the list of assets selected in the content browser. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_selected_object()` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the object currently selected in the Rewind Debugger outliner, if any. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_selected_outliner_folders()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Gets the folder paths selected across all open scene outliners. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_session_info()` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the current Rewind Debugger session state. Call this first to confirm a session is active before querying object data. Always returns all fields; IsActive is false when no session is loaded. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_show_flag(flagName)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Reads whether a named engine show flag is currently enabled on the active level editor viewport. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `flagName` |
| `epic_get_stat_counters(groupName, bIncludeZero:b)` | [Epic PerfToolset.StatsToolset] Samples every non-cycle counter in a stat group for a single frame: integer/float counters and memory pool sizes (draw calls, primitive counts, LLM tags, etc). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `groupName, bIncludeZero` |
| `epic_get_symbol(name)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Returns the documentation of a registered tool, or of a type, function, method, or property in the `unreal` Python API. Pass a toolset or full tool name, a top-level name ('EditorActorSubsystem', 'log'), or a qualified 'Class.member'. A toolset returns its description and the signature of each of its tools. A tool returns its signature, description, and parameters. A function or member returns its signature and full documentation. A type returns its description, then one line for each editor property (inherited ones included), enum value, and method it declares, and how many methods it inherits from each base; get_symbol on 'Type.member' or on a base gives the details. A struct only tools use returns its fields and the tools that use it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `name` |
| `epic_get_trace_event_details(source, eventId)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Returns the full decoded JSON for a single trace event from a named source. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `source, eventId` |
| `epic_get_transaction_details(transactionId, maxObjects?:i)` | [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns detailed information about a single transaction Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `transactionId, maxObjects?` |
| `epic_get_transaction_recency_index(transactionId)` | [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Returns how far back a transaction is in the undo history, counted newest-first: 0 is the most recent transaction, 1 the next, and so on. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `transactionId` |
| `epic_get_verbosity(category?)` | [Epic EditorToolset.LogsToolset] Returns the current verbosity level for a log category. Params: `category?` |
| `epic_get_video_info(path)` | [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Reads container metadata. Windows Media Foundation is required. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path` |

| `epic_is_pierunning()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] True for active PIE or simulation, including online login before world creation. A queued start alone returns false. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_cheats(nameFilter?)` | [Epic CheatsToolset.CheatsToolset] Lists the cheat commands available on the local player. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `nameFilter?` |
| `epic_list_collections()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists all collections in the content browser. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_editor_modes()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists the IDs of all registered editor modes (e.g. "EM_Default", "EM_Landscape", "EM_Foliage"), ordered by mode priority. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

Only a viewport with bIsVisible set presents frames, so ask the user to bring any other to the front first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

At most Count events (the first in frame order) are returned. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, count?, frameStart?, frameEnd?` |
| `epic_list_modes(bIncludeUnavailable:b)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists canonical names of modes that can capture in this build and session. Aliases are not listed separately. Availability reflects capture-path, build, session and project prerequisites, not scene content. Buffer-visualization targets incompatible with the capture output format are omitted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `bIncludeUnavailable` |
| `epic_list_object_trace_events(objectId:i, startTime:n, endTime:n, sourceFilter, includedNameFilter, excludedNameFilter, limit:i, offset:i)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Lists trace events attributed to ObjectId within [StartTime, EndTime], aggregated across every registered IRewindDebuggerToolsetEventDecoder. | `epic_list_objects(className?)` | [Epic RewindDebuggerToolset.RewindDebuggerToolset] Lists all objects recorded in the current session, optionally filtered by class name. Each entry includes an ObjectId for use with GetObjectEvents and GetObjectProperties. Returns {"Objects": []} when no session is active or no objects match the filter. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `className?` |
| `epic_list_show_flags()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Lists every engine show flag with its display name and editor group. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

Preserves custom perspective near planes and explicitly configured orthographic clip planes. A player view whose transform, active lens and clipping match a listed view marks that entry as a player view instead of adding one. Lists player views first, then the remaining actor cameras. Returns empty when no views exist; an invalid world raises a script error. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `world` |
| `epic_list_worlds()` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Lists Editor, PIE and Game worlds in the engine's world contexts, including non-renderable worlds. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

| `epic_read_me()` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Usage instructions for execute_python. Call this once per conversation before using execute_python. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_read_stat_values(path, statName, frameStart?:i, count?:i)` | [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Returns up to Count per-frame values of one stat, starting at FrameStart. An over-large Count clamps to the stat's own length rather than erroring; Count = -1 reads to the end of the column. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. | `epic_record_viewport(options:o, durationSeconds:n)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Records a viewport for DurationSeconds, then completes with the finalized file. | `epic_run_console_command(command)` | [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Executes an arbitrary UE exec command. Output is written to the session log. | `epic_screen_coords_to_world(coords:o, traceDistance?:n)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Finds the world position of the nearest solid object at a given set of normalized view space coords. Params: `coords, traceDistance?` |
| `epic_search_console_commands(name)` | [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Returns exec commands whose name contains the search string (case-insensitive). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `name` |
| `epic_search_cvars(name)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Finds all console variables that contain a given name. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `name` |
| `epic_search_cvars__console_toolset(name)` | [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Finds all console variables that contain a given name. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `name` |
| `epic_search_symbols(pattern?, max_results?:i, match?, kinds?:[s], accepts?, returns?)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.python_scripting.PythonScriptingTools] Searches the registered tools and the `unreal` Python API for types, functions, methods, and properties. Searches what this editor session provides, so every result exists here. Feed a result's qualified_name to get_symbol to read it. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. | `epic_search_transactions(query, count?:i, offset?:i)` | [Epic EditorToolset.UndoHistoryToolset] Searches the undo history by transaction label using a fuzzy (edit-distance) match, closest match first. When two transactions match a query equally well the more recent one is returned first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `query, count?, offset?` |
| `epic_select_actors(actors:[ref])` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Selects the specified actors in the current scene. Params: `actors` |

| `epic_set_camera_transform(transform?:o, translation?:o, rotation?:o)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets the position and/or rotation of the level viewport camera. Anything not provided keeps its current value. Params: `transform?, translation?, rotation?` |

| `epic_set_cvar_value(name, value)` | [Epic ConsoleToolset.ConsoleToolset] Sets the value of a console variable. The value is parsed according to the variable's declared type. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `name, value` |
| `epic_set_editor_mode(modeId)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Activates the specified editor mode. Pass "EM_Default" (or an empty string) to return to the default placement/select mode. Cannot be used during PIE. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `modeId` |
| `epic_set_pivot_location(location:o, bSnapToGrid?:b)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Sets the location of the editor's transform-gizmo pivot. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `location, bSnapToGrid?` |

| `epic_show_notification(message, state?, expireDuration?:n)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Shows a transient editor notification (Slate toast, bottom-right). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `message, state?, expireDuration?` |
| `epic_skim_video(path, maxFrames?:i, maxEdge?:i)` | [Epic MediaToolset.MediaToolset] Samples midpoint-spaced frames over the video's known duration. Windows only. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, maxFrames?, maxEdge?` |
| `epic_start_pie(options?:o)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Starts PIE or simulation in the current level, then waits for warmup. | `epic_stop_pie()` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Stops PIE or simulation and waits for shutdown. Normally handled on an editor tick; pending online login defers shutdown until a world exists. Errors if no session is active. Params: `none` |
| `epic_stop_viewport_recording(recordingId)` | [Epic SceneCaptureToolset.SceneCaptureToolset] Stops a recording and completes once its file is finalized. A recording that already ended returns its result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `recordingId` |
| `epic_top_stats(path, count?:i, rankBy?, statNameFilter?, frameStart?:i, frameEnd?:i)` | [Epic PerfToolset.CsvProfilerToolset] Ranks the capture's stats by a reduced aggregate (average, max, total, or a P50/P90/P95/P99 percentile) over a frame range and returns the top Count, each already reduced. A StatNameFilter wildcard restricts the ranking to a group (e.g. "GPU*"); empty ranks all stats. FrameEnd -1 runs to the end; the defaults rank the whole run. Ranking is by raw aggregate value with no unit normalisation, so an unfiltered ranking mixes unit domains (byte counters rank alongside millisecond timings). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `path, count?, rankBy?, statNameFilter?, frameStart?, frameEnd?` |
| `epic_trigger_gpuprofile(minInclusiveMs:n)` | [Epic PerfToolset.GpuProfilerToolset] Captures the next rendered frame's GPU work as a nested tree (2-3 frame latency). Top-level entries are GPU queues (Graphics, Async Compute); each contains its passes as a recursive subtree. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `minInclusiveMs` |
| `epic_world_pos_to_screen_coords(position:o)` | [Epic EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset] Converts a world-space position into normalized screen space based on the editor viewport camera. Params: `position` |

## pie

*PIE testing: record, replay and observe Play-In-Editor sessions, diff runs, inject input, drive remote players, and run test scripts with auto and manual steps. Starting PIE itself is editor(play_in_editor).*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `view_trace(playerIndex?:i, pieInstance?:i, distance?:n, channel?, sweepRadius?:n, traceComplex?:b, ignoreActors?:[s], ignorePawn?:b)` | Trace the live PIE player viewpoint. Returns viewLocation, viewRotation, viewDirection and line; sweepRadius also returns a sphere sweep. Each hit includes component collision state, channel response, blocksVisibility and owner label/class. Ignores the viewing pawn by default; requires running PIE. Params: `playerIndex?, pieInstance?, distance?, channel?, sweepRadius?, traceComplex?, ignoreActors?, ignorePawn?` |
| `inject_input(action_path, value_x?:n, value_y?:n, value_z?:n, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), client?:i(0..))` | Inject one frame of an Enhanced Input action into a PIE player. client 1..N relays to a remote player. Params: `action_path, value_x?, value_y?, value_z?, client_id?, pie_instance?, client?` |
| `inject_input_start(action_path, value_x?:n, value_y?:n, value_z?:n, injection_id?, duration_seconds?:n(0..), control_rotation?:r, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), client?:i(0..))` | Start holding an input action every frame until inject_input_stop, PIE end, or duration_seconds of game time; control_rotation pins the controller's aim every frame while it runs. Hold several actions at once with one call each. Returns injection_id. Rolls back with inject_input_stop. Params: `action_path, value_x?, value_y?, value_z?, injection_id?, duration_seconds?, control_rotation?, client_id?, pie_instance?, client?` |
| `inject_input_update(injection_id, value_x?:n, value_y?:n, value_z?:n, control_rotation?:r)` | Change the value or control_rotation of a running hold. Params: `injection_id, value_x?, value_y?, value_z?, control_rotation?` |
| `inject_input_stop(injection_id)` | Stop a hold or tape by id; alreadyStopped when it had ended. Params: `injection_id` |
| `inject_input_tape(action_path, values:[*], hz?:n, injection_id?, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), client?:i(0..))` | Play a per-frame value array through an input action; returns injection_id. Params: `action_path, values, hz?, injection_id?, client_id?, pie_instance?, client?` |
| `drive_pawn(one(direction:v; targetLocation:v), mode?:{input,navigate}, durationSeconds?:n(0..600), scale?:n(-1..1), sampleEvery?:n(0..), acceptanceRadius?:n(0..), planar?:b, stopOnMapChange?:b, playerIndex?:i, pieInstance?:i, driveId?, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n(0..))` | Walk the PIE player's pawn: movement input every frame along direction or toward targetLocation, or mode=navigate for a navmesh move to targetLocation. Ends as completed, arrived, timeout, no_path, nav_ended, map_changed (stopOnMapChange), stopped or pie_ended. The pawn is found again every frame, so a drive carries on through a level change. With wait (default true) answers once it ends with a sampled track of location, rotation, controlRotation, velocity and map, plus mapChanges, distanceTravelled and the navPath taken; wait=false returns driveId at once. Params: `direction OR targetLocation, mode?, durationSeconds?, scale?, sampleEvery?, acceptanceRadius?, planar?, stopOnMapChange?, playerIndex?, pieInstance?, driveId?, wait?, timeoutSeconds?` |
| `drive_status(driveId?, includeSamples?:b)` | A pawn drive's state and sampled track; includeSamples=false for the summary only. Params: `driveId?, includeSamples?` |
| `drive_stop(driveId?)` | End a pawn drive now and return its track; alreadyStopped when it had ended. Params: `driveId?` |
| `clients()` | List a networked PIE session's players: client 0 is the editor's own player, 1..N remote players in join order with ready and log_file. Params: `none` |
| `console(command, client:i(1..))` | Run a console command in a remote player's own process (client 1..N). The editor's own PIE player is editor(execute_command, world="pie"). Params: `command, client` |
| `remote_result(request_id\|injection_id)` | Whether a request relayed to a remote player ran: reported, ok, finished, error. Params: `request_id (or injection_id)` |
| `uat_run(one(scenario:o; path))` | Run a multiplayer acceptance scenario unattended: opens its map, starts PIE with its players, drives each step, judges it from the host and client logs, stops PIE and writes report.md and report.json. Poll uat_status. Params: `scenario OR path` |
| `uat_status()` | State of the current or last acceptance run: per-step results, verdict and report_dir. Params: `none` |
| `uat_abort(reason?)` | End the acceptance run early; it stops PIE and reports what it reached. Params: `reason?` |
| `record_arm(actions?:[s], track_values?:[s], track_actors?:[s], axis_threshold?:n, sample_hz?:i(1..), pin_fps?:i, capture_pawn_state?:b, capture_montage?:b, take_record?:b, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), rng_seed?:n, run_gap_frames?:i, recording_dir?, id?)` | Arm the PIE recorder; it starts on BeginPIE and finalizes on EndPIE into Saved/MCPRecordings/<id>. Rolls back with record_disarm. Params: `actions?, track_values?, track_actors?, axis_threshold?, sample_hz?, pin_fps?, capture_pawn_state?, capture_montage?, take_record?, client_id?, pie_instance?, rng_seed?, run_gap_frames?, recording_dir?, id?` |
| `record_disarm()` | Cancel an armed recording. Params: `none` |
| `record_stop()` | Finalize the recording in flight. Params: `none` |
| `record_status()` | Recorder state, id, frame, elapsed time and pie_active. While waiting_for_pawn: waiting_for (what is missing) and pie_worlds (each PIE world's pie_instance, net_mode, players and pawns). Params: `none` |
| `record_list(recording_dir?, limit?:i(1..), offset?:i(0..))` | List recordings. Params: `recording_dir?, limit?, offset?` |

| `record_delete(id, confirm?:b, recording_dir?)` | Delete a recording folder (confirm=true). Params: `id, confirm?, recording_dir?` |

| `replay_arm(recording_id?, sequence_path?, recording_dir?, steps?:[o], settle_ms?:i(0..), sample_hz?:i(1..), rng_seed?:n, pin_fps?:i, apply_rng_seed?:b, record_drift?:b, auto_stop_pie?:b, eject?:b, time_scale?:n, mode?:{replay,monitor}, capture_frame_every?:i(0..), encode_gif?:b, fixed_timestep?:b, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), drift_thresholds?:o, start_when?:o)` | Arm the replayer for the next PIE session: re-injects a recording's input and records drift. Rolls back with replay_disarm. Params: `recording_id?, sequence_path?, recording_dir?, steps?, settle_ms?, sample_hz?, rng_seed?, pin_fps?, apply_rng_seed?, record_drift?, auto_stop_pie?, eject?, time_scale?, mode?, capture_frame_every?, encode_gif?, fixed_timestep?, client_id?, pie_instance?, drift_thresholds?, start_when?` |
| `replay_run(recording_id?, sequence_path?, recording_dir?, steps?:[o], settle_ms?:i(0..), sample_hz?:i(1..), rng_seed?:n, pin_fps?:i, apply_rng_seed?:b, record_drift?:b, auto_stop_pie?:b, eject?:b, time_scale?:n, mode?:{replay,monitor}, capture_frame_every?:i(0..), encode_gif?:b, fixed_timestep?:b, client_id?:i(0..), pie_instance?:i(0..), drift_thresholds?:o, start_when?:o)` | Unattended replay: arm and start PIE in one call, auto-stop PIE and write drift.json. Poll replay_status until pie_active=false. Params: `recording_id?, sequence_path?, recording_dir?, steps?, settle_ms?, sample_hz?, rng_seed?, pin_fps?, apply_rng_seed?, record_drift?, auto_stop_pie?, eject?, time_scale?, mode?, capture_frame_every?, encode_gif?, fixed_timestep?, client_id?, pie_instance?, drift_thresholds?, start_when?` |

| `replay_analyze(recording_id?, recording_dir?, limit?:i(0..), offset?:i(0..))` | Read a finalized drift.json as a lead: first divergence, top channels, errors during the run, bracketing images. Params: `recording_id?, recording_dir?, limit?, offset?` |

Always saves, returning what the check finds as warnings [{step, field, message, candidates}]: an expect.value the level, player pawn and profile do not resolve, an op or target the value's type cannot meet, an actor, actor class or Input Action arrange and act name that does not exist, or no auto step without manual_only=true. resolve_in_pie=true on a step defers a value that only exists in PIE. Refused (INVALID_SCRIPT_STEPS, errors in the same shape) only when the script cannot be written: no steps, a step that does not parse, or a map (e.g. /Game/Maps/L_Arena) that is not a level. Params: `name, package_path?, steps, description?, profile?, map?, default_within_ms?, manual_only?, onConflict?` |

Checks the result like script_create when steps, profile, map or manual_only change, and saves with its findings as warnings; refuses only what cannot be written. Params: `path, steps?, description?, profile?, map?, default_within_ms?, manual_only?` |
| `script_validate(steps:[o], profile?, map?, manual_only?:b)` | Check steps the way script_create does without saving anything: valid, and errors [{step, field, message, candidates}] for every finding script_create would return as a warning or refuse. Params: `steps, profile?, map?, manual_only?` |
| `script_values(target?, profile?, limit?:i(1..))` | What a script can name in the open level: the player pawn's readable value paths with kind and type, pawn_channels read off the sampled pawn with no profile (pos_x, vel_z, rot_yaw, speed2d, ...), level actors, classes the game mode spawns, Widget Blueprints and the profile's tracked values. target adds which actors are of that class and whether it is the player pawn. Params: `target?, profile?, limit?` |
| `script_delete(path, confirm?:b)` | Delete a test script (confirm=true). Params: `path, confirm?` |
| `script_list(directory?)` | List test scripts, each with map and last_run: its newest run's run_id, state, started_at, ended_at, summary and results_path, or null. Params: `directory?` |
| `script_run(one(script; steps:[o]), name?, profile?, map?, record?:b, start_pie?:b, block_on_manual?:b, mode?:{full,manual}, default_within_ms?:i(1..), pie_instance?:i(0..), client_id?:i(0..), wait?:b, timeout_seconds?:n(0..))` | Run a test script in PIE: opens the script's map first when another level is open, refusing when that level has unsaved changes or PIE is running elsewhere; arms the observer and, unless record=false, the recorder; mode=manual instead starts no PIE, observer or recording, leaves auto steps unchecked and puts every manual step up for its verdict at once; evaluates auto steps live and marks each pass or fail; waits on manual steps for verdicts, asked through an elicitation form when the client supports one, otherwise through verdict. Writes results.json beside the observation. wait=true returns once the run finishes. Params: `script OR steps, name?, profile?, map?, record?, start_pie?, block_on_manual?, mode?, default_within_ms?, pie_instance?, client_id?, wait?, timeout_seconds?` |
| `script_status(run_id?, since_seq?:i(0..), wait?:b, timeout_seconds?:n(0..))` | A script run's state, steps and events since since_seq. wait=true blocks until it finishes or needs a verdict. Params: `run_id?, since_seq?, wait?, timeout_seconds?` |
| `script_stop(run_id?, reason?)` | End a script run now; unsettled steps stay pending and results.json is written. Params: `run_id?, reason?` |
| `verdict(step:i(0..), verdict:{pass,fail,skip}, note?, run_id?, source?:{human,agent,elicitation,action}, evidence?:o)` | Record a manual step's verdict: pass, fail or skip, with a note. source=agent marks the calling agent's own judgement and needs evidence {note, captures?}; a step with agent_judgeable=false takes only a person's verdict. Params: `step, verdict, note?, run_id?, source?, evidence?` |
| `script_results(run_id?, results_path?)` | Read a finished run's results.json. Params: `run_id?, results_path?` |
| `script_runs(script?, limit?:i(1..), include_steps?:b)` | List script runs newest first, the active one included: run_id, script, started_at, ended_at, state, summary, per-step results and results_path. script narrows to one script's runs. Params: `script?, limit?, include_steps?` |
| `script_replay(run_id?, results_path?, time_scale?:n(0..), auto_stop_pie?:b, pie_instance?:i(0..), client_id?:i(0..), wait?:b, timeout_seconds?:n(0..))` | Replay a finished run's recording in the level it ran in and re-evaluate its auto steps at their recorded offsets; manual steps keep their verdicts. Reports regressions. Params: `run_id?, results_path?, time_scale?, auto_stop_pie?, pie_instance?, client_id?, wait?, timeout_seconds?` |
