## gas

*Gameplay Ability System: abilities, effects, attribute sets, cues.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `add_asc(blueprintPath, componentName?)` | Add AbilitySystemComponent. Params: `blueprintPath, componentName?` |
| `create_attribute_set(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create AttributeSet BP. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `add_attribute(attributeSetPath, attributeName)` | Add attribute to set. Params: `attributeSetPath, attributeName` |
| `create_ability(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create GameplayAbility BP. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `set_ability_tags(abilityPath, ability_tags?:[s], cancel_abilities_with_tag?:[s], block_abilities_with_tag?:[s], activation_required_tags?:[s], activation_blocked_tags?:[s])` | Set tags on ability. Each container passed is written whole, so the inverse is this same call carrying the tags that were in it; containers you do not pass are left alone and are not in the record. unchanged=true means the tags a written container ended up holding are the same set it already held, compared both ways, not merely that the caller passed nothing. Params: `abilityPath, ability_tags?, cancel_abilities_with_tag?, block_abilities_with_tag?, activation_required_tags?, activation_blocked_tags?` |
| `create_effect(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, durationPolicy?, durationMagnitude?:n)` | Create GameplayEffect BP. durationPolicy (Instant, Infinite or HasDuration) and durationMagnitude are written onto the effect's class defaults and read back in the result. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, durationPolicy?, durationMagnitude?` |
| `add_effect_component(effectPath, componentClass, properties?:o)` | Add a GameplayEffectComponent (TargetTagsGameplayEffectComponent, AssetTagsGameplayEffectComponent, AdditionalEffectsGameplayEffectComponent and so on) to a GameplayEffect Blueprint, outered to its class defaults the way the editor's Components list does it, and optionally write properties onto it. Idempotent on the class: a component of that class already on the effect reports existed and takes the property writes. A component this call added rolls back through remove_effect_component. Params: `effectPath, componentClass, properties?` |
| `remove_effect_component(effectPath, componentClass)` | Remove the GameplayEffectComponent of a class from a GameplayEffect Blueprint, the inverse of add_effect_component. Idempotent: a class the effect does not carry reports alreadyRemoved=true. Rolls back by adding a component of that class again, marked lossy because its property values are not recorded. Params: `effectPath, componentClass` |
| `set_effect_granted_tags(effectPath, tags:[s], removedTags?:[s])` | Set the tags a GameplayEffect grants its target, through its Grant Tags to Target Actor component (added when missing). tags is written whole as the component's added tags; removedTags drops tags inherited from a parent effect. Unregistered tags are refused. Returns the effect's granted tags read back, warns when the effect is Instant (an Instant effect grants nothing), and rolls back to the previous tags. Params: `effectPath, tags, removedTags?` |
| `set_effect_modifier(effectPath, attribute, operation?, magnitude?:n)` | Add or update a modifier on a GameplayEffect, matched on attribute + operation. Overwriting an existing static magnitude rolls back to the value it held, qualified as SetName.Attribute so the inverse cannot land on another set's same-named attribute, and marked lossy because it comes back as a plain ScalableFloat constant. A magnitude that CHANGES WITH EFFECT LEVEL gets no record: it is probed at levels 1, 2 and 10, and one that moves is curve-table-backed, so writing a single constant would destroy the binding. APPENDING a new modifier has no inverse either, because no action removes a modifier from an effect; the response says rollbackPossible=false rather than offering a magnitude of zero as an undo. Params: `effectPath, attribute, operation?, magnitude?` |
| `create_cue(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, cueType?)` | Create GameplayCue. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?, cueType?` |
| `get_info(blueprintPath)` | Inspect GAS setup. On a GameplayEffect the effect field carries its durationPolicy, components and granted tags. Params: `blueprintPath` |
| `set_asc_defaults(blueprintPath, attributeSet\|attributeSetPath, componentName?, initDataTable?)` | Wire an AttributeSet onto a Blueprint's ASC component (DefaultStartingData) so attributes exist at runtime. Idempotent: a set already wired reports existed. No inverse - nothing removes an entry from DefaultStartingData, and removing the whole component would undo more than this did, so the response says rollbackPossible=false. Run add_ability_system_component first. Params: `blueprintPath, attributeSet (or attributeSetPath), componentName?, initDataTable?` |
| `apply_effect(actorLabel?, actorPath?, effectClass\|effectPath, level?:n, setByCaller?:o, world?)` | Apply a GameplayEffect to a live actor's ASC (agnostic stat/damage stimulus - uses the game's own effect). A duration or infinite effect comes back with an effectHandle and rolls back through gas(remove_effect) on that handle. When the effect STACKS - its StackingType is not None and one of its class was already on the ASC - no new active effect is created, the existing handle comes back with a higher stackCount, and the record removes exactly one stack so the stacks that predate the call survive (reported as stackedOntoExisting, marked lossy because the duration refresh does not come back). an instant effect executes into the attribute base values, leaves no handle, and says so through rollbackPossible=false. An effect the ASC refuses reports unchanged=true rather than a bare success. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, effectClass (or effectPath), level?, setByCaller?, world?` |
| `remove_effect(actorLabel?, actorPath?, effectHandle?, effectClass\|effectPath?, stacksToRemove?:i, world?)` | Take an active GameplayEffect back off a live actor's ASC - the inverse of apply_effect. Address it by effectHandle (what apply_effect returned, and the only way to remove exactly the effect one call added) or by effectClass, which removes every active effect of that class on the actor. Idempotent: a handle whose effect has already expired reports alreadyRemoved=true rather than failing, so a replayed rollback is safe. Removing exactly one effect rolls back to apply_effect at the level it held, marked lossy because duration, stack count and SetByCaller magnitudes do not survive removal. Instant effects have no handle and cannot be removed - their modifiers are already in the attribute base. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, effectHandle?, effectClass? (or effectPath), stacksToRemove?, world?` |
| `set_attribute(actorLabel?, actorPath?, attribute, value:n, world?)` | Set a gameplay attribute's base value on a live actor's ASC (recalculates CurrentValue through the aggregator). Reports unchanged=true when the base value did not move, including when the set's own clamping refused the write. Rolls back by writing the previous base value through the same path, which restores the current value with it because the modifiers are never touched; the record names the attribute QUALIFIED as SetName.Attribute, because a bare name resolves to whichever attribute set the class iterator reaches first and two sets can both declare Health. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, attribute, value, world?` |
| `get_attribute(actorLabel?, actorPath?, attribute?, world?)` | Read gameplay attribute base + current values on a live actor's ASC. Omit attribute to list all. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, attribute?, world?` |
| `init_asc(actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet?, world?)` | Initialize a live actor's ASC (InitAbilityActorInfo) and optionally instantiate an AttributeSet so attributes are live - the runtime setup step for testing a bridge-authored GAS actor. Reports unchanged=true when the ASC was already initialized for this actor and every set it needs was already registered. No inverse: nothing returns an ASC to uninitialized, and this is what BeginPlay would have done anyway, so the response says rollbackPossible=false and names any AttributeSet it had to CONSTRUCT. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet?, world?` |
| `get_asc_state(actorLabel?, actorPath?, world?)` | Introspect a live actor's ASC: granted ability specs (class, level, inputID, active, dynamicTags) + owned gameplay tags. Pass actorLabel or actorPath (#587). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, world?` |
| `get_live_attribute_value(actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet, attribute, registerOwnerSets?:b, world?)` | Read the live value of one FGameplayAttributeData on the attribute set instance actually REGISTERED on an actor's AbilitySystemComponent - equivalent to ASC->GetSet<T>(), not the actor's own subobject pointer. Works in the editor world, where no set is registered yet, by first registering the actor's own sets the way BeginPlay would (set registerOwnerSets=false for a strict read). Returns currentValue and baseValue off the instance plus the aggregator's view of both, and the instance's object path so you can prove which object was read. Gated as a mutation because registering those sets changes the live world; the response reports unchanged=true when it registered nothing, and rollbackPossible=false either way, since nothing un-registers a set the engine would register again at BeginPlay. Pass actorLabel or actorPath (#956). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet, attribute, registerOwnerSets?, world?` |
| `set_live_attribute_value(actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet, attribute, value:n, valueType?, registerOwnerSets?:b, world?)` | Write the live value of one FGameplayAttributeData on the REGISTERED attribute set instance on an actor's AbilitySystemComponent. valueType="current" (default) writes the attribute data in place, which is what staging a mid-combat state needs; valueType="base" writes through the ASC so the aggregator recomputes the current value, which is what a durable change needs. The set's PreAttributeChange may clamp, so the result reports what was actually stored alongside the previous values and the instance's object path. Reports unchanged=true when neither the value moved nor a set was registered, reading the stored value back because PreAttributeChange can clamp a write to what was already there. The inverse writes the overwritten value back through the same valueType, and is marked lossy when the call also had to register the actor's own attribute sets to reach the value, since that registration stays. Pass actorLabel or actorPath (#956). Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, attributeSet, attribute, value, valueType?, registerOwnerSets?, world?` |
| `grant_ability(actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, level?:n, inputId?:i, world?)` | Grant a GameplayAbility to a live actor's ASC, which is what makes an authored ability activatable at all - an ability the ASC has never been given does nothing and logs nothing worth reading. Idempotent: granting a class that is already granted returns the existing spec with existed=true rather than a second handle for what the caller thinks of as one ability. Refused on a non-authoritative ASC, because GiveAbility only runs on the authority and would otherwise look like it worked. Returns the spec (handle, level, inputID, active) and a rollback that revokes it. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, level?, inputId?, world?` |
| `revoke_ability(actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, world?)` | Remove a granted GameplayAbility from a live actor's ASC. Idempotent: revoking one that is not granted reports alreadyRevoked=true rather than failing, so replaying a rollback is safe. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, world?` |
| `get_active_effects(actorLabel?, actorPath?, world?)` | List every GameplayEffect currently active on a live actor's ASC: effect class, stack count, level, total duration, time remaining, whether it is inhibited, the instigator that applied it, and the tags it grants. Plus the ASC's owned tags. Unfiltered on purpose - the caller is diagnosing, and a filter that hid the effect they were looking for would be the whole problem. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, world?` |
| `add_loose_gameplay_tag(actorLabel?, actorPath?, tag, count?:i, world?)` | Add a loose gameplay tag to a live actor's ASC, so a test can arrange exactly one piece of tag state. count adds that many references, matching AddLooseGameplayTag. The tag must already be registered (reflection(create_tag) makes one). Loose tags are local to the ASC they are added on and are not replicated. Returns tagCount (the ASC's count for the tag afterwards) and previousTagCount; the rollback removes exactly the references this call added. Read the owned tags back with gas(get_asc_state). Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, tag, count?, world?` |
| `remove_loose_gameplay_tag(actorLabel?, actorPath?, tag, count?:i, world?)` | Remove references to a loose gameplay tag from a live actor's ASC, never more than it holds. Loose and effect-granted tags share one counter, so the result reads the count back: tagCount above 0 means the tag is still owned. Idempotent: a tag the ASC does not own reports alreadyRemoved=true rather than failing, so a replayed rollback is safe. The rollback adds back exactly what was removed. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, tag, count?, world?` |
| `trace_ability_activation(actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, activate?:b, world?)` | Answer why an ability will not activate, which GAS otherwise reports only to the log in a form nothing can read back. Checks in order: is it granted at all (the most common cause, and silent), is it already active without bRetriggerInstancedAbility, which tags it was refused over (the engine reports one relevant-tag set rather than separating 'blocked by' from 'missing', so neither does this - compare them against the returned ownedTags), is it on cooldown (with seconds remaining), and is its cost unmet. Returns wouldActivate plus a blockedBy[] naming each reason. Pass activate=true to also call TryActivateAbility and prove it rather than predict it; a refusal with no blocker found means the ability's own CanActivateAbility override refused. Reports unchanged=true on every path where nothing fired. An activation has no inverse - the ability has already committed its cost, applied its cooldown and run its effects - so the response says rollbackPossible=false. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, activate?, world?` |
| `bind_ability_input(actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, inputId:i, world?)` | Bind a granted ability to an input id, which is how anything other than a direct TryActivateAbility call ever fires it. GAS addresses input by integer: UAbilitySystemComponent::AbilityLocalInputPressed(id) activates every granted spec whose InputID matches, and the Enhanced Input asset side (gameplay(create_input_action) plus gameplay(add_imc_mapping)) is what turns a key into that call in the game's own input component. Idempotent: re-binding the same id reports unchanged=true. Refused on a non-authoritative ASC, because an ability spec is replicated from the authority and a local write would be overwritten while looking like it worked. Reports sharedWith[] when another granted ability already uses that id, since sending the input then activates all of them. The rollback restores the exact previous id, which is not always -1. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, inputId, world?` |
| `clear_ability_input(actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, world?)` | Unbind a granted ability from its input id, setting InputID back to -1 so no input event can reach it. Idempotent: an already-unbound ability reports unchanged=true rather than failing, so replaying a rollback is safe. The rollback re-binds the id that was there. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, abilityClass, world?` |
| `send_ability_input(actorLabel?, actorPath?, inputEvent?, inputId?:i, abilityClass?, world?)` | Deliver an input event to a live ASC, which fires a bound ability the way the game fires it rather than through a direct activation call. inputEvent=pressed\|released calls AbilityLocalInputPressed / AbilityLocalInputReleased for an inputId (or for the id abilityClass is bound to); inputEvent=confirm\|cancel calls InputConfirm / InputCancel, which reach targeting actors and take no id. Returns the specs that matched the id with their pressed and active state before and after, so the result says what happened rather than what was asked for. An id nothing is bound to is reported as matchedSpecCount 0, not as an error. pressed and released are a genuine inverse pair and roll back to each other; confirm and cancel have no inverse and say so. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, inputEvent?, inputId?, abilityClass?, world?` |
| `add_effect_cue(effectPath\|effectClass, cueTag, minLevel?:n, maxLevel?:n, magnitudeAttribute?)` | Link a GameplayCue tag to a GameplayEffect, so applying the effect fires the cue. Refuses a tag the tag manager does not know (writing one would store an invalid tag and the cue would never fire; create it first with reflection(create_tag)) and a tag outside the GameplayCue root (the cue system routes nothing else). Reports whether any GameplayCueNotify actually answers the tag, matching a parent tag the way the cue system does, and warns when none does. Idempotent on the tag: re-adding reports existed, changing the level range reports updated. Params: `effectPath (or effectClass), cueTag, minLevel?, maxLevel?, magnitudeAttribute?` |
| `remove_effect_cue(effectPath\|effectClass, cueTag)` | Unlink a GameplayCue tag from a GameplayEffect. Accepts a tag that is no longer registered, because cleaning up after a deleted tag is exactly what this has to be able to do. Drops a cue entry left with no tags rather than leaving a blank row. Idempotent: a tag that is not linked reports alreadyRemoved=true. Params: `effectPath (or effectClass), cueTag` |
| `validate_cue_coverage(directory?, effectPath\|effectClass?, maxEffects?:i)` | Audit every GameplayEffect against every GameplayCueNotify in the project and report which cue links fire nothing. Resolves each cue tag the way the cue system does, falling back to a parent tag, so a notify on GameplayCue.Damage counts as covering GameplayCue.Damage.Fire and is reported as a parent match rather than a false positive. Problems it names: a cue tag with no notify on it or any parent, a cue entry with no tag at all, a cue tag outside the GameplayCue root (inert), a notify with no GameplayCueTag (unreachable), and duplicate tags across notifies. Also reports orphan notifies that no effect references, which is usually a rename done on one side only. Reads the asset registry rather than the cue manager index, so a cold index does not read as 'no cues exist'; the manager's own counts come back alongside. Params: `directory?, effectPath? (or effectClass), maxEffects?` |
| `audit_attributes(attributeSet?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, probeClamping?:b, world?)` | Report what is provable about an AttributeSet: whether it can clamp at all, which attributes replicate and carry an OnRep, which have a paired Max attribute, and which look like meta attributes. There is deliberately no configure_attribute_clamping counterpart, because UE 5.8 has no data-driven clamp: PreAttributeChange and PreAttributeBaseChange are plain C++ virtuals rather than UFUNCTIONs, so a Blueprint AttributeSet can never clamp and this says so outright instead of pretending to configure one. On a native set, pass probeClamping=true with a live actor to MEASURE an existing clamp by driving PreAttributeChange with extreme values rather than guessing from the class; the probe runs the project's own code so it needs a registered live set, never a class default object. A strict read: unlike get_live_attribute_value it never registers the actor's own sets, so an actor whose ASC has none is told which call registers one. Everything about an attribute set that IS a property stays reachable through asset(set_property) on its Blueprint CDO. Pass attributeSet, actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `attributeSet?, actorLabel?, actorPath?, probeClamping?, world?` |
| `capture_gas_state(actorLabel?, actorPath?, snapshotId?, compareWith?, registerOwnerSets?:b, world?)` | Capture an actor's whole ability-system state as one snapshot: granted abilities with level, input id, active count and dynamic tags; every active effect with its stack count, level, duration, time remaining, inhibition and instigator; every attribute with BOTH its base and current value; owned gameplay tags with their counts; and the tags currently blocking activation. Stores it under snapshotId (generated when omitted) and also returns it, so a caller that needs it to outlive the editor session keeps the object; the store holds the 64 most recent and is emptied by a restart. Pass compareWith to diff this capture against an earlier snapshot id in the same call, which is the whole capture-act-compare loop in two calls. The diff lives here rather than on compare_gas_states because capturing registers the actor's attribute sets on its ASC where a world has not begun play, so it is gated as the mutation it is. Pass actorLabel or actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, snapshotId?, compareWith?, registerOwnerSets?, world?` |
| `compare_gas_states(beforeId?, beforeSnapshot?:o, afterId?, afterSnapshot?:o)` | Diff two GAS snapshots and name each change rather than handing back two blobs. Every entry in changes[] carries a kind (ability_granted, ability_revoked, ability_level_changed, ability_input_changed, ability_activated, ability_ended, effect_applied, effect_removed, effect_stack_changed, effect_level_changed, effect_inhibition_changed, attribute_changed, attribute_added, attribute_removed, tag_gained, tag_lost, tag_count_changed, ability_block_added, ability_block_removed, asc_initialized), the subject it happened to, the before and after rows, and a sentence saying what it means - an attribute whose current value moved while its base did not is reported as a modifier rather than as a failed write. Time is not counted as a change: effects present in both come back under stillActiveEffects with their remaining time on each side, and the gap is reported once as timeElapsedSeconds. Comparing two different actors is allowed and flagged. A pure read over snapshots you already have; to take the later reading and diff it in one call use capture_gas_state with compareWith. Pass beforeId or beforeSnapshot, and afterId or afterSnapshot. Params: `beforeId?, beforeSnapshot?, afterId?, afterSnapshot?` |
| `list_gas_snapshots(actorPath?, includeSnapshots?:b)` | List the GAS snapshots this editor session holds, oldest first, with the actor, world, capture time and per-section counts. Pass actorPath to narrow to one actor, or includeSnapshots to get the full bodies back. Params: `actorPath?, includeSnapshots?` |
| `delete_gas_snapshot(snapshotId)` | Drop one stored GAS snapshot, returning its contents first so nothing is lost: the returned object can be passed straight back to compare_gas_states as beforeSnapshot. Idempotent: an id that is not stored reports alreadyDeleted=true. Params: `snapshotId` |
| `epic_add_cue_tag(cueTag, comment?)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Adds a new gameplay cue tag to the project. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Params: `cueTag, comment?` |
| `epic_create_cue_notify_asset(cueTag, packagePath, assetName, bIsActor:b)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Creates a new GameplayCueNotify Blueprint asset at the specified content browser location. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Params: `cueTag, packagePath, assetName, bIsActor` |
| `epic_create_gameplay_ability(folderPath, assetName, parentClass:ref)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayAbilityToolset] Creates a new Gameplay Ability Blueprint asset, the same as the Content Browser's Gameplay Ability Blueprint factory. Unlike a plain Blueprint with a GameplayAbility parent, its root ability has a "Gameplay Ability Graph" in place of the default "EventGraph". This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `folderPath, assetName, parentClass` |
| `epic_execute_cue_on_selected_actor(cueTag, normalizedMagnitude:n, location:o, normal:o)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Executes a gameplay cue non-replicated on the currently selected actor in the editor. Useful for previewing cue effects without network replication. Requires a PIE session or a configured GameplayCueManager to produce visible results. Params: `cueTag, normalizedMagnitude, location, normal` |
| `epic_find_attribute_set_classes()` | [Epic GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset] Returns all AttributeSet subclasses found in the project, including their attributes. Covers both native C++ subclasses and Blueprint subclasses discovered via the asset registry. Params: `none` |
| `epic_find_cue_notify_assets(parentTag)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Returns all GameplayCueNotify assets found in the project via the asset registry. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `parentTag` |
| `epic_find_cue_tags_without_notifies()` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Returns gameplay cue tags that have no GameplayCueNotify of their own. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_active_effects(actor:ref)` | [Epic GASToolsets.AbilitySystemInspectorToolset] Returns all gameplay effects currently active on the actor's AbilitySystemComponent. Params: `actor` |
| `epic_get_active_tags(actor:ref)` | [Epic GASToolsets.AbilitySystemInspectorToolset] Returns the gameplay tags currently owned by the actor's AbilitySystemComponent (includes loose tags, effect-granted tags, etc.). Params: `actor` |
| `epic_get_attribute_values(actor:ref)` | [Epic GASToolsets.AbilitySystemInspectorToolset] Returns the current base and modified values of all gameplay attributes on the actor's AbilitySystemComponent. Params: `actor` |
| `epic_get_cue_info(cueTag)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Returns information about a specific gameplay cue, including its notify asset. Only notifies in the project's gameplay cue notify paths are known. Params: `cueTag` |
| `epic_get_granted_abilities(actor:ref)` | [Epic GASToolsets.AbilitySystemInspectorToolset] Returns all abilities granted to the actor's AbilitySystemComponent. Params: `actor` |
| `epic_list_attributes(className)` | [Epic GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset] Returns the gameplay attributes defined on a specific AttributeSet class. Params: `className` |
| `epic_list_cues(parentTag)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Returns gameplay cue tags registered in the project. Params: `parentTag` |
| `epic_remove_cue_tag(cueTag)` | [Epic GASToolsets.GameplayCueToolset] Removes a gameplay cue tag from the project. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Params: `cueTag` |

## networking

*Networking and replication: actor replication, property replication, net relevancy, dormancy.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `set_replicates(blueprintPath, replicates?:b)` | Enable or disable actor replication on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value. Rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, replicates?` |
| `set_property_replicated(blueprintPath, variableName\|propertyName, replicationType?, replicated?:b, repNotify?:b)` | Mark a Blueprint variable as replicated. replicationType is 'None' \| 'Replicated' \| 'RepNotify'; repNotify=true is shorthand for RepNotify and replicated=true for Replicated (#768). Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the variable already had that type. Rolls back through this same action with the type it had; marked lossy when the variable carried a ReplicationCondition other than COND_None, because making a variable replicated resets that and this action has no parameter to restore one. Params: `blueprintPath, variableName (or propertyName), replicationType?, replicated?, repNotify?` |
| `configure_net_frequency(blueprintPath, netUpdateFrequency?:n, minNetUpdateFrequency?:n)` | Set update frequency. Reports unchanged=true when both frequencies already held these values, and otherwise rolls back to the pair that was there - the record carries both regardless of which one was asked for, so an inverse cannot leave the two inconsistent. Params: `blueprintPath, netUpdateFrequency?, minNetUpdateFrequency?` |
| `set_dormancy(blueprintPath, dormancy)` | Set net dormancy on a Blueprint's CDO: DORM_Never \| DORM_Awake \| DORM_DormantAll \| DORM_DormantPartial \| DORM_Initial. An unrecognised spelling is REFUSED and the valid five are named, where it used to leave the value alone and still report success. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had that dormancy. Rolls back through this same action with the previous one, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, dormancy` |
| `set_net_load_on_client(blueprintPath, loadOnClient?:b)` | Control whether the actor is loaded on clients (bNetLoadOnClient). A class with no such property reports a warning and unchanged=true rather than the existed it used to claim for a write that never happened. Reports existed=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag. Params: `blueprintPath, loadOnClient?` |
| `set_always_relevant(blueprintPath, alwaysRelevant?:b)` | Set bAlwaysRelevant on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, alwaysRelevant?` |
| `set_only_relevant_to_owner(blueprintPath, onlyRelevantToOwner?:b)` | Set bOnlyRelevantToOwner on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, onlyRelevantToOwner?` |
| `configure_cull_distance(blueprintPath, netCullDistanceSquared?:n)` | Net cull distance. Reports unchanged=true when the value is already set, and otherwise rolls back to the previous NetCullDistanceSquared read off the CDO before the write. A class with no writable NetCullDistanceSquared reports a warning rather than a silent success. Params: `blueprintPath, netCullDistanceSquared?` |
| `set_priority(blueprintPath, netPriority?:n)` | Set NetPriority on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the value is already nearly equal to the one asked for, and otherwise rolls back to the float the property held, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, netPriority?` |
| `set_replicate_movement(blueprintPath, replicateMovement?:b)` | Set replicated movement on a Blueprint's CDO. Reports existed=true and unchanged=true when the class already had this value, and otherwise rolls back through this same action with the previous flag, with nothing lost. Params: `blueprintPath, replicateMovement?` |
| `get_info(blueprintPath)` | Get networking info. Params: `blueprintPath` |
| `audit_replication(path?, className?, includeNative?:b, includeBlueprints?:b, includeEngine?:b, requireServerValidation?:b, onlyWithFindings?:b, maxBlueprints?:i, limit?:i, dumpToFile?:b, outputPath?)` | Project-wide replication audit over native and Blueprint classes. Each class row lists its replicated properties (lifetime condition, push-based, RepNotify function and its REPNOTIFY condition, read from the class's own GetLifetimeReplicatedProps), its RPCs (Server / Client / NetMulticast, reliable, validated) and, for actors and components, the replication settings on its defaults (replicates, netDormancy, netCullDistanceSquared, update frequencies, priority, relevancy). findings name each problem visible from the class alone: repNotifyFunctionMissing, onRepWithoutReplicatedProperty, replicatedPropertyNotRegistered, replicatedPropertyOnNonReplicatingClass, reliableMulticast, and serverRpcWithoutValidation when requireServerValidation=true. Native scope is the project's modules and project plugins unless includeEngine=true; Blueprints come from path (default /Game). Classes with findings sort first; totals stay complete when rows are cut at limit, and dumpToFile writes every row to a JSON file. Params: `path?, className?, includeNative?, includeBlueprints?, includeEngine?, requireServerValidation?, onlyWithFindings?, maxBlueprints?, limit?, dumpToFile?, outputPath?` |

## demo

*Neon Shrine demo scene builder and cleanup.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `step(step\|stepIndex?:i)` | Execute demo step. Steps are NOT idempotent: each one spawns unconditionally, so a replay leaves a second set of Demo_ actors, and the result says created rather than a bare success. No inverse is emitted. No step records what it individually created, and demo(cleanup) is not a substitute: it removes the whole demo scene, and on the way it creates /Game/MCP_Home if missing and switches the editor to it, then deletes by label prefix in whatever level is then open. The response names it as guidance with rollbackPossible=false, so the flow runner never invokes it as an undo. Params: `step? (or stepIndex)` |
| `get_steps()` | List every demo step up front: index, id and description, plus a count. Use this to see what the 19 steps build before running any of them. Params: `none` |
| `cleanup()` | Remove demo assets and actors. Switches editor to /Game/MCP_Home before deleting so the editor is never left on an Untitled map, dropping unsaved changes to the demo level (which it deletes) and refusing, with nothing deleted, when any other open map has unsaved changes. unchanged=true only when nothing was deleted AND the home level already existed AND the editor was already in it, because anchoring to that level is itself a change this call makes. No inverse of its own - rebuilding means running step 1 through 19 again. Params: `none` |
| `go_home(discardUnsaved?:b)` | Switch the editor to /Game/MCP_Home (creating it on first use). Use this before any operation that would leave the editor on an Untitled map. When the open map has unsaved changes (an Untitled map someone edited included) it refuses and names them in dirtyPackages, and the editor stays where it is; pass discardUnsaved=true to drop them, and discardedPackages lists what was dropped. Succeeds only when the home level is the open map afterwards. Reports alreadyOpen=true when the home level was already the open one, and otherwise rolls back by reopening the level that WAS open through level(load) - marked lossy when the home level had to be created, since that package stays on disk. A previously open map with no content path (unsaved or Untitled) has no inverse and the response says so. Params: `discardUnsaved?` |

## feedback

*Submit feedback when a native tool falls short: a missing action, a wrong result, a crash, or a gap you had to work around with execute_python. A python workaround is a common trigger but is not required. Reports are routed to the tracker that owns the surface - ue-mcp core, or the plugin listed in the plugin registry that provides it - by consulting the published plugin registry.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `submit(summary, title, author?, confirmToken?, idealTool?, pythonWorkaround?, repo?)` | Submit feedback about a tool gap (missing action, wrong behavior, crash, or a case you had to work around). Provide a specific title and a summary; pythonWorkaround and idealTool are optional enrichment, not prerequisites. Checks the plugin registry first and files against the owning plugin's repo when one matches, then blocks on an MCP elicitation prompt that asks the USER (not the agent) to approve or decline the exact payload - and to override the tracker - before anything is posted to GitHub. If the client cannot show that form (it never advertised elicitation, it throws, or it auto-answers in milliseconds without rendering anything), nothing is lost: the report is written to disk and the result carries a prefilled GitHub issue URL for the user to click. Params: `title, summary, pythonWorkaround?, idealTool?, author?, repo?, confirmToken?` |
| `route(summary, title, idealTool?, repo?)` | Dry run the tracker routing for a report without posting anything. Returns the repo the issue would be filed against, the matched plugin (if any), and why. Params: `title, summary, idealTool?, repo?` |

## statetree

*StateTree asset editing: read, modify states/tasks/conditions/transitions/bindings/evaluators/global tasks/colors/state parameters/root parameters, compile and validate.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `read(assetPath)` | Full dump of a StateTree asset: state hierarchy (with description, tag, customTickRate, color), tasks, conditions, transitions, evaluators, global tasks, root params, bindings, and editor data extensions (class + objectPath, editable with editor(set_property)). Params: `assetPath` |
| `list_states(assetPath, cursor?, limit?:i)` | List all states with IDs and paths, depth-first in the tree's authored order, cursor-paginated. Params: `assetPath, cursor?, limit?` |
| `add_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, name, stateType?, selectionBehavior?, insertIndex?:i, linkedSubtree?)` | Add a child state under the parent named by stateId or statePath, or a root state when neither is given. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, name, stateType?, selectionBehavior?, insertIndex?, linkedSubtree?` |
| `remove_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)` | Remove a state by ID. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?` |
| `set_state_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on a state (name\|type\|selectionBehavior\|bEnabled\|weight\|linkedAsset\|description\|tag\|customTickRate\|color). For tag: gameplay tag string or empty to clear. For customTickRate: number in seconds or empty to disable. For color: palette color display name, GUID, or empty to clear. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, propertyName, value` |
| `clear_state_nodes(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)` | Remove all tasks/conditions/transitions from a state. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?` |
| `add_task(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o)` | Add a task to a state. structType is a C++ struct name, e.g. FMyStateTreeTask or an engine-shipped task like FStateTreeRunParallelStateTreesTask. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?` |
| `add_enter_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)` | Add an enter condition to a state. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?, operand?` |
| `remove_enter_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, conditionIndex:i)` | Remove an enter condition by index. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, conditionIndex` |
| `remove_task(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i)` | Remove a task by index. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex` |
| `set_task_instance_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on a task's instance data. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex, propertyName, value` |
| `set_task_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on the task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level: bConsideredForCompletion, bTaskEnabled, bShouldStateChangeOnReselect). Distinct from set_task_instance_property which targets instance data. value is string-encoded, e.g. 'true'/'false'. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex, propertyName, value` |
| `add_transition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, trigger, transitionType, eventTag?, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, priority?, delayDuration?:n, bDelayTransition?:b)` | Add a transition to a state. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, trigger, transitionType, eventTag?, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, priority?, delayDuration?, bDelayTransition?` |
| `add_transition_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)` | Add a condition to an existing transition. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex, structType, instanceProperties?, operand?` |
| `remove_transition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i)` | Remove a transition by index. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex` |
| `add_binding(assetPath, sourceStructId, sourcePath, targetStructId, targetPath)` | Add a property binding. Params: `assetPath, sourceStructId, sourcePath, targetStructId, targetPath` |
| `remove_binding(assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath)` | Remove a property binding. Params: `assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath` |
| `list_bindings(assetPath, structId?)` | List all property bindings, optionally filtered to one struct. Params: `assetPath, structId?` |
| `list_bindable_sources(assetPath, cursor?, limit?:i)` | Enumerate the context/bindable sources in a StateTree (context objects, parameters, evaluators, global tasks, per-state nodes) with their structId + struct type - what a property can bind FROM, sorted by structId, cursor-paginated (#681). Params: `assetPath, cursor?, limit?` |
| `add_evaluator(assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?:o)` | Add an evaluator to the StateTree (tree-level). Params: `assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?` |
| `remove_evaluator(assetPath, nodeId)` | Remove an evaluator by node ID. Params: `assetPath, nodeId` |
| `set_evaluator_instance_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on an evaluator's instance data. Params: `assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value` |
| `set_evaluator_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on the evaluator's node struct (FStateTreeEvaluatorBase-level). Params: `assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value` |
| `add_global_task(assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?:o)` | Add a global task to the StateTree (tree-level). Params: `assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?` |
| `remove_global_task(assetPath, nodeId)` | Remove a global task by node ID. Params: `assetPath, nodeId` |
| `set_global_task_instance_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on a global task's instance data. Params: `assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value` |
| `set_global_task_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)` | Set a property on a global task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level). Params: `assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value` |
| `list_colors(assetPath)` | List all color palette entries for a StateTree. Returns: colors[] with id, displayName, color. Params: `assetPath` |
| `add_color(assetPath, displayName, color?)` | Add a new color to the StateTree palette. Params: `assetPath, displayName, color?` |
| `list_state_parameters(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)` | List parameters defined on a state. Returns: parameters[] with name, id, type, value; also bFixedLayout. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?` |
| `add_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, paramType)` | Add a parameter to a state's property bag. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, paramType` |
| `remove_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName)` | Remove a parameter from a state's property bag by name. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName` |
| `set_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, value)` | Set the value of an existing state parameter. On fixed-layout states, also marks the parameter as overridden. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, value` |
| `set_root_parameters(assetPath, parameters:[o])` | Define root parameters (property bag). Params: `assetPath, parameters` |
| `set_schema(assetPath, schema?)` | Attach or replace the StateTree schema, then compile. The schema is what makes a tree compilable: without one the compiler logs "does not have a schema" and stops, and everything that loads the asset reports it as failed to link. Repairs a tree that has no editor data at all (what asset(create_asset_by_class) writes) by creating the editor data, the schema and a root state. Omit schema to take StateTreeComponentSchema, then StateTreeAIComponentSchema, then whatever concrete schema this editor has, and read schemaSource / schemaNote to see which was used (#833). Params: `assetPath, schema?` |
| `compile(assetPath)` | Compile a StateTree asset. Returns success, errors[], warnings[]. Params: `assetPath` |
| `validate(assetPath)` | Validate a StateTree asset without compiling. Params: `assetPath` |
| `list_node_types(assetPath, nodeType?, filter?, includeInstanceProperties?:b, schemaAllowedOnly?:b)` | Enumerate every task, condition, evaluator and utility consideration THIS tree's schema allows, with the exact structType string add_task / add_enter_condition / add_transition_condition / add_consideration / add_evaluator / add_global_task take, and the property names their instanceProperties map accepts. Every add_* action takes a C++ struct name and nothing listed them, so authoring meant guessing. Also reports the schema's own capability flags (allowEnterConditions, allowUtilityConsiderations, allowEvaluators, allowMultipleTasks, allowGlobalParameters), which is what decides whether an add would be refused, and the context data a binding can come from. Blueprint-authored nodes are listed separately with the wrapper struct and the two calls that author one, because a Blueprint node needs set_node_class after the wrapper is added. Params: `assetPath, nodeType?, filter?, includeInstanceProperties?, schemaAllowedOnly?` |
| `read_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)` | Read ONE state whole, including everything the tree-wide read omits: utility considerations, the LinkedSubtree link, RequiredEventToEnter, TasksCompletion, Weight, and every transition's priority, enabled flag, delay variance and reactivation rule. Returns the state's objectPath, which is how the fields with no typed setter are written - editor(set_property) at that path reaches Transitions[0].Priority and the rest. problems[] names the faults a state cannot report about itself: utility selection with no scoring considerations anywhere below it, considerations whose parent never reads them, a Linked type pointing at nothing, and a transition targeting a deleted state. Pass stateId OR statePath. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?` |
| `add_consideration(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)` | Add a utility consideration to a state, which is what produces the score a parent uses when its selectionBehavior is TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility or TrySelectChildrenAtRandomWeightedByUtility. Those behaviours were already settable and nothing could add the scoring half, so the setting could be written and never did anything. Refuses when the tree's schema does not allow considerations, and warns when the PARENT does not select by utility, because that is the silent failure. Pass stateId OR statePath. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?, operand?` |
| `remove_consideration(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, considerationIndex:i)` | Remove a utility consideration from a state by index. The rollback captures the struct type, operand and instance values, and says plainly that a replay appends at the end with a new nodeId rather than restoring its position or its bindings. Pass stateId OR statePath. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, considerationIndex` |
| `remove_transition_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i, conditionIndex:i)` | Remove one condition from a transition by index. add_transition_condition shipped without it, so a mistyped condition could only be undone by deleting the whole transition. Pass stateId OR statePath. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex, conditionIndex` |
| `set_state_link(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, linkType, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, linkedAsset?)` | Link a state to a Subtree state in THIS asset, or to another StateTree asset, or clear both. UStateTreeState carries two separate link fields and only the asset one had any route: add_state documented a linkedSubtree parameter and assigned LinkedAsset with it, so in-asset subtree reuse was impossible. Goes through SetLinkedState / SetLinkedStateAsset rather than assigning the field, which is what pulls the linked target's parameters into this state - without that a linked state has an empty fixed-layout parameter list and set_state_parameter has nothing to override. Pass stateId OR statePath; for linkType subtree pass targetStateId OR targetStatePath, for asset pass linkedAsset. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, linkType, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, linkedAsset?` |
| `move_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, newParentStateId?, newParentStatePath?, toRoot?:b, insertIndex?:i)` | Reparent or reorder an existing state. add_state takes an insertIndex for a NEW state and nothing could move one afterwards, so wrong order meant delete and rebuild - and order is load-bearing, since TrySelectChildrenInOrder walks it and NextState and NextSelectableState transitions resolve through it. Refuses to move a state under its own descendant, which would detach the branch. insertIndex is the final position among siblings; omit it to append. Reports unchanged when the state is already there, and rolls back to its previous parent and index. Pass stateId OR statePath, and newParentStateId OR newParentStatePath OR toRoot. Params: `assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, newParentStateId?, newParentStatePath?, toRoot?, insertIndex?` |
| `set_node_class(assetPath, nodeId, nodeClass)` | Point a Blueprint node wrapper at its Blueprint class AND reallocate its instance data. This is the step with no property-write equivalent: the wrapper reports the Blueprint class AS its instance data type, so a node added before the class is set has no instance data at all, and writing the class afterwards does not go back and allocate it. Works on any task, condition, transition condition, consideration, evaluator or global task, addressed by the nodeId every add_* action returns. Returns instanceObjectPath, where the Blueprint's own variables live for editor(set_property). Params: `assetPath, nodeId, nodeClass` |
| `read_runtime(actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?:i, includeDebugStrings?:b)` | Read a RUNNING StateTree in depth: run status, last tick status, the state change count, the active states, the execution frames and the pending event queue. gameplay(get_state_tree_runtime) answers the same question with active state names only, which cannot tell you whether the tree succeeded, failed or stopped, nor whether an event you sent is still waiting to be consumed. Needs a game world, so run it in PIE. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?, includeDebugStrings?` |
| `send_event(actorLabel?, actorPath?, eventTag, componentName?, origin?, world?, pieInstance?:i)` | Send a gameplay event to a running StateTree, which is how an event-driven tree is meant to be driven from outside and had no route at all. The event is QUEUED and consumed on the tree's next tick, so the snapshot returned still shows the state before it is handled; read it again with read_runtime after a tick. Refuses an unregistered tag, since no transition could ever match one. Has no inverse: once queued it is consumed and whatever it triggered has run. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, eventTag, componentName?, origin?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `request_transition(actorLabel?, actorPath?, targetStateId?, targetStateTag?, priority?, fallback?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?:i)` | Force a running StateTree to transition to a named state, resolved through the COMPILED data - so a state added since the last compile is reported as missing rather than silently ignored. Queued like an event and resolved on the next tick against every other pending request by priority. Refuses when the tree is not Running, naming the status it is in. targetStateTag needs UE 5.8 or later; targetStateId works everywhere. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath, and targetStateId OR targetStateTag. Params: `actorLabel?, actorPath?, targetStateId?, targetStateTag?, priority?, fallback?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?` |
| `move_node(assetPath, nodeId, newIndex:i)` | Reorder a task, enter condition, consideration, transition condition, evaluator or global task within the list it is in, found by its nodeId. Tasks run in list order and conditions combine in list order through their operand and indent, so order is load-bearing; the node keeps its ID, so bindings into and out of it survive. The rollback moves it back. Params: `assetPath, nodeId, newIndex` |
| `read_node(assetPath, nodeId)` | Read ONE node by nodeId wherever it lives: where it is (container, state, transition, index), its node struct properties, instance data (struct or Blueprint object), execution runtime data, the struct ID bindings into it use (instanceStructId), its editor description, and the typed flags taskEnabled, consideredForCompletion, canEditConsideredForCompletion and evaluationMode. Params: `assetPath, nodeId` |
| `set_node_flags(assetPath, nodeId, taskEnabled?:b, consideredForCompletion?:b, evaluationMode?)` | Set the typed node flags the editor exposes, with the editor's rules: taskEnabled and consideredForCompletion on tasks (state or global; a Blueprint task's completion flag lives on its instance), evaluationMode (Evaluated, ForcedTrue, ForcedFalse) on enter or transition conditions. consideredForCompletion is refused on a disabled task or one that does not allow the edit. Params: `assetPath, nodeId, taskEnabled?, consideredForCompletion?, evaluationMode?` |
| `set_node_data(assetPath, nodeId, target?, propertyName?, value)` | Write a node's data by nodeId: target node (the node struct), instance (default; struct or Blueprint object) or executionRuntime. Pass propertyName to write one property, or omit it to replace the whole struct with value in Unreal text format. Works on conditions and considerations, which the index-addressed set_*_property actions do not reach. Params: `assetPath, nodeId, target?, propertyName?, value` |
| `list_bindable_properties(assetPath, structId, targetPath?, exactOnly?:b, maxDepth?:i)` | Binding discovery for one bindable struct (structId from list_bindable_sources or read_node's instanceStructId). Without targetPath: every property of it with type, category and current binding. With targetPath: every compatible source in that property's scope, exact matches before numeric promotions (exactOnly drops promotions; maxDepth limits descent into value structs). UE 5.7 and later. Params: `assetPath, structId, targetPath?, exactOnly?, maxDepth?` |
| `check_binding(assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath?, sourceStructId?, sourcePath?)` | Check a proposed binding without writing it: resolve the target (and the source, when given) against the structs' current values, report each end's type, whether the source is in the target's scope, the compatibility (compatible, promotable, incompatible), canBind and the reasons. Omit the source to only resolve a path. UE 5.7 and later. Params: `assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath?, sourceStructId?, sourcePath?` |
| `promote_to_parameter(assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath, parameterName?, stateId?, statePath?)` | Promote to Parameter: create a parameter with the target property's type and current value, on the given state (the target's state or an ancestor, not linked) or on the tree parameters when no state is given, and bind the target to it. The name defaults to the property name and is made unique. UE 5.7 and later. Params: `assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath, parameterName?, stateId?, statePath?` |
| `diagram(assetPath, depth?:i, focus?, format?, maxNodes?:i, outputPath?)` | Draw a StateTree as a stateDiagram-v2: the state hierarchy as nested states (a parent entered through its first child), each state's tasks and enter conditions, and every transition labelled with its trigger, event tag, conditions and delay. Succeeded and Failed transitions end at Tree succeeded / Tree failed; NextState goes to the next sibling. Evaluators and global tasks are listed in notes. format: mermaid (default; Mermaid text), svg (an image file drawn by ue-mcp, its path returned), png (the same image rasterised, returned inline as image content and written to a file), json (the normalised nodes and edges). focus: a node title, id or state name to centre on, with depth hops either way (default 3). maxNodes caps the drawing (default 80, max 500); what is cut is named in a note node and in notes. outputPath: where svg, png or mermaid is written (default <Project>/Saved/UE_MCP/Diagrams/). Params: `assetPath, format?, focus?, depth?, maxNodes?, outputPath?` |
| `epic_add_blueprint_consideration(state_tree:ref, state:ref, consideration_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a Blueprint-based utility consideration to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, consideration_class` |
| `epic_add_blueprint_enter_condition(state_tree:ref, state:ref, condition_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a Blueprint-based enter condition to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, condition_class` |
| `epic_add_blueprint_evaluator(state_tree:ref, evaluator_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a Blueprint-based evaluator to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, evaluator_class` |
| `epic_add_blueprint_global_task(state_tree:ref, task_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a Blueprint-based global task to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, task_class` |
| `epic_add_blueprint_task(state_tree:ref, state:ref, task_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a Blueprint-based task to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, task_class` |
| `epic_add_child_state(state_tree:ref, parent:ref, name, state_type?)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a new child state under the given parent state. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, parent, name, state_type?` |
| `epic_add_consideration(state_tree:ref, state:ref, consideration_struct:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based utility consideration to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, consideration_struct` |
| `epic_add_enter_condition(state_tree:ref, state:ref, condition_struct:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based enter condition to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, condition_struct` |
| `epic_add_evaluator(state_tree:ref, evaluator_struct:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based evaluator to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, evaluator_struct` |
| `epic_add_global_task(state_tree:ref, task_struct:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based global task to the asset. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, task_struct` |
| `epic_add_sub_tree(state_tree:ref, name, state_type?)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a new top-level subtree to the asset. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, name, state_type?` |
| `epic_add_task(state_tree:ref, state:ref, task_struct:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Adds a struct-based task to a state. Returns the new node's ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, task_struct` |
| `epic_compile(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Compiles a StateTree. Returns whether it succeeded and the compiler's messages. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_all_states(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns every state in the tree (root + descendants), in hierarchy order. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_children(state:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns child states of a state. Params: `state` |
| `epic_get_considerations(state:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the utility considerations on a state. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state` |
| `epic_get_editor_data(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns the editor data for a StateTree asset. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_enter_conditions(state:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns enter conditions on a state. Params: `state` |
| `epic_get_evaluators(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns global evaluators. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_extension(state_tree:ref, extension_class:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the first editor-data extension of the requested type, or None. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, extension_class` |
| `epic_get_global_tasks(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns global tasks that run across all states. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_node_description(state_tree:ref, node:o)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns a human-readable description for a node. Params: `state_tree, node` |
| `epic_get_node_execution_runtime_data(state_tree:ref, node_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the node's Execution Runtime struct (per-execution scratch data). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id` |
| `epic_get_node_execution_runtime_object(state_tree:ref, node_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the node's Execution Runtime UObject. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id` |
| `epic_get_node_instance_data(state_tree:ref, node_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the node's Instance struct (per-state-tree-instance data, struct-typed). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id` |
| `epic_get_node_instance_object(state_tree:ref, node_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the node's Instance UObject (per-state-tree-instance data, UObject-typed). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id` |
| `epic_get_node_template_data(state_tree:ref, node_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Returns the node's Template struct (the type-defining, shared data). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id` |
| `epic_get_root_states(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns top-level states of a StateTree. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_get_tasks(state:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns tasks on a state. Params: `state` |
| `epic_get_transitions(state:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns transitions on a state. Params: `state` |
| `epic_mark_as_modified(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Marks the asset as dirty so a recompile and UI refresh happen on the next tick. Call this when you've mutated the asset outside the wrappers below (the wrappers below already call this for you on every write). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_move_child_state(state_tree:ref, parent:ref, child:ref, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves a child state to a specific index in its parent's children list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, parent, child, index` |
| `epic_move_consideration(state_tree:ref, state:ref, consideration_id, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves a consideration to a specific index in the state's consideration list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, consideration_id, index` |
| `epic_move_enter_condition(state_tree:ref, state:ref, condition_id, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves an enter condition to a specific index in the state's enter-condition list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, condition_id, index` |
| `epic_move_evaluator(state_tree:ref, evaluator_id, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves an evaluator to a specific index in the asset's evaluator list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, evaluator_id, index` |
| `epic_move_global_task(state_tree:ref, task_id, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves a global task to a specific index in the asset's global-task list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, task_id, index` |
| `epic_move_sub_tree(state_tree:ref, sub_tree:ref, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves an existing subtree to a specific index in the subtree list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, sub_tree, index` |
| `epic_move_task(state_tree:ref, state:ref, task_id, index:i)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Moves a task to a specific index in the state's task list. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, task_id, index` |
| `epic_remove_child_state(state_tree:ref, parent:ref, child:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes a child state from its parent. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, parent, child` |
| `epic_remove_consideration(state_tree:ref, state:ref, consideration_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes a consideration from a state by ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, consideration_id` |
| `epic_remove_enter_condition(state_tree:ref, state:ref, condition_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes an enter condition from a state by ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, condition_id` |
| `epic_remove_evaluator(state_tree:ref, evaluator_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes an evaluator by ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, evaluator_id` |
| `epic_remove_global_task(state_tree:ref, task_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes a global task by ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, task_id` |
| `epic_remove_sub_tree(state_tree:ref, sub_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes a subtree from the asset. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, sub_tree` |
| `epic_remove_task(state_tree:ref, state:ref, task_id)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Removes a task from a state by ID. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, state, task_id` |
| `epic_request_ui_refresh(state_tree:ref)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Requests a full refresh of the open StateTree editor (no-op if no editor is open). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree` |
| `epic_set_node_execution_runtime_data(state_tree:ref, node_id, runtime_data:o)` | [Epic state_tree_toolset.state_tree.StateTreeToolset] Sets the node's Execution Runtime struct. The struct types must match. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `state_tree, node_id, runtime_data` |
