## chooser

*Author ChooserTable assets (the data-driven selection layer behind Motion Matching): signature and parameters, columns and their input bindings, rows and their results, cells, the fallback result, auto populate, and nested choosers.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `create(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create an empty ChooserTable asset. Add input columns with add_column, then rows with add_row (#685). Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `describe(table\|assetPath, nested?)` | Introspect a ChooserTable: row count, result type, whether it is nested, each column (index, name, columnType, cellType, disabled, randomize, autoPopulates, hasFallbackValue, inputType and its binding) and the fallback result. Read this first to learn the cell text format each column expects (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?` |
| `add_column(table\|assetPath, columnType, inputStruct?, boundProperty?, enumPath?, nested?, insertIndex?:i)` | Add an input column to a ChooserTable (so rows have a condition to fill). columnType is a Chooser column struct short name, e.g. EnumColumn, BoolColumn, FloatRangeColumn, GameplayTagColumn, ObjectColumn, or an Output* column. Optionally bind its input: inputStruct (parameter struct e.g. EnumContextProperty/BoolContextProperty), boundProperty (context property name to read), enumPath (for enum columns). Placed where the editor places it (before a trailing randomize column) unless insertIndex says otherwise. Sizes the new column's cells to the current rows (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), columnType, inputStruct?, boundProperty?, enumPath?, nested?, insertIndex?` |
| `list_rows(table\|assetPath, nested?)` | List every row: index, disabled flag, output object (resultType + referenced asset path), and each column's cell value as round-trippable text (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?` |
| `add_row(table\|assetPath, output?, outputType?, cells?:[*], inputs?:o, nested?, resultType?, insertIndex?:i)` | Add a row (appended, or before insertIndex). Set the output via `output` (asset path) + outputType ('asset' hard ref default \| 'soft_asset' \| 'evaluate' for a nested ChooserTable), or a default result of any type via resultType. Set input-column conditions via `cells` (array aligned to column order) and/or `inputs` (object keyed by column index or name). Cell values are struct text like '(Value=2)' - partial fields are allowed and unspecified ones keep defaults; a bare number/bool works for scalar columns (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), output?, outputType?, cells?, inputs?, nested?, resultType?, insertIndex?` |
| `set_row(table\|assetPath, index:i, output?, outputType?, disabled?:b, cells?:[*], inputs?:o, nested?, resultType?)` | Edit an existing row by index: optionally replace the output (output + outputType) or the result type (resultType, keeping the cells), toggle disabled, and/or update column cells (cells / inputs, same format as add_row) (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), index, output?, outputType?, disabled?, cells?, inputs?, nested?, resultType?` |
| `delete_row(table\|assetPath, index:i, nested?)` | Delete a row by index (removes its output plus the per-row cell from every column). The rollback puts it back at the same index (#685). Params: `table (or assetPath), index, nested?` |
| `list_object_references(assetPath\|path, classFilter?, pathFilter?)` | List every leaf object reference reachable from a chooser, descending through nested chooser tables. list_rows renders those as an opaque resultType:NestedChooser with an empty output, so the actual PoseSearchDatabase/asset paths were invisible. Each entry reports the owning table, the exact location (e.g. ResultsStructs[3].Asset), the struct type and the current object path. classFilter matches the referenced object's class, pathFilter is a substring on the path (#754). Params: `assetPath (or path), classFilter?, pathFilter?` |
| `remap_object_references(assetPath\|path, from?, to?, fromPrefix?, toPrefix?, dryRun?:b, allowMissing?:b)` | Repoint object references throughout a chooser's nested structure. Either an exact swap (from + to) or a folder rewrite (fromPrefix + toPrefix), which is the 'adopt vendor choosers into our namespace' case. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT - pass dryRun=false to apply. Object-typed targets are class-checked before assignment; the chooser is recompiled and left dirty rather than saved (#754). Params: `assetPath (or path), from?, to?, fromPrefix?, toPrefix?, dryRun?, allowMissing?` |
| `list_types(kind:{column,result,parameter,input}, table?, nested?, column?:i)` | List the type names an authoring call accepts: kind 'column' (add_column), 'result' (resultType on add_row/set_row/set_fallback), 'parameter' (add_parameter), or 'input' (the input types one column accepts for set_column inputType; needs table + column). Full paths, sorted; short names work too. Params: `kind, table?, nested?, column?` |
| `get_signature(table\|assetPath, nested?)` | Read a chooser's signature: result type (ObjectResult \| ClassResult \| NoPrimaryResult), result class, the ChooserSignature asset it inherits from (UE 5.9), and every parameter with its type, class or struct, and full value text. Works on a ChooserTable or a ChooserSignature asset; a nested chooser reports its root's. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?` |
| `set_signature(table\|assetPath, nested?, resultType?:{ObjectResult,ClassResult,NoPrimaryResult}, resultClass?, signatureAsset?)` | Set a chooser's result type and/or result class, or point it at a ChooserSignature asset to inherit them and the parameters from (UE 5.9; empty clears the reference). Refused while the signature is inherited, except for clearing the reference. Bindings recompile against the new signature. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, resultType?, resultClass?, signatureAsset?` |
| `add_parameter(table\|assetPath, nested?, parameterType, properties?:o)` | Add a parameter (the object or struct a chooser reads from or writes to) of parameterType, e.g. ContextObjectTypeClass with properties {Class: '/Script/Engine.Character'} or ContextObjectTypeStruct with {Struct: ...}. Returns its index, which column bindings use. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, parameterType, properties?` |
| `remove_parameter(table\|assetPath, nested?, index:i)` | Remove a parameter by index. Column bindings name parameters by index and are not renumbered, so bindings to later parameters need set_column afterwards. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, index` |
| `get_property(table\|assetPath, nested?, target:{column,row,fallback,parameter}, index?:i, propertyPath?)` | Read any property by path from a column (target 'column'), a row's result ('row'), the fallback result ('fallback') or a parameter ('parameter'), in Unreal text format. Paths are '.' separated with [index], stepping into instanced structs, e.g. 'InputValue.Binding.DisplayName', 'DefaultRowValue', 'Asset'. An empty path reads the whole struct. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, target, index?, propertyPath?` |
| `set_property(table\|assetPath, nested?, target:{column,row,fallback,parameter}, index?:i, propertyPath?, value)` | Write any property by path on a column, a row's result, the fallback result or a parameter (same targets and paths as get_property), in Unreal text format. The value is parsed in full before anything changes. A result change refreshes auto populating columns, as the editor does. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, target, index?, propertyPath?, value` |
| `delete_column(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i)` | Delete a column and its cell in every row. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column` |
| `move_column(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i, newIndex:i)` | Move a column so it ends up at newIndex. A randomize column stays last and cannot be moved, and nothing moves after it. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column, newIndex` |
| `duplicate_column(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i)` | Duplicate a column with its cells, inserting the copy right after it. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column` |
| `copy_column(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i, targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?:i)` | Copy a column with its cells (matched to rows by index) into another table, a nested chooser, or the same table, before insertIndex. The copy's binding keeps its parameter index, so the target needs compatible parameters. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column, targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?` |
| `set_column(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i, disabled?:b, inputType?, parameterIndex?:i, propertyChain?:[s])` | Change a column: disable or enable it, change its input type (list_types kind 'input'), and/or bind its input to a parameter (parameterIndex) through a property chain, e.g. ['Speed'] or ['MyStruct','MyFloat']; an empty chain binds the parameter itself. The chain is checked under the editor's binding rules before anything changes. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column, disabled?, inputType?, parameterIndex?, propertyChain?` |
| `delete_rows(table\|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i])` | Delete several rows at once, with their cells. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, rows` |
| `move_rows(table\|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i], targetIndex:i)` | Move rows, keeping their order, so they sit before targetIndex (a row index from before the move; rowCount moves them to the end), like dragging rows in the editor. Returns the new index of the first moved row. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, rows, targetIndex` |
| `duplicate_rows(table\|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i])` | Duplicate rows (results, disabled flags and cells), inserting the copies after the last of them. A nested chooser result is deep copied. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, rows` |
| `copy_rows(table\|assetPath, nested?, rows:[i], targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?:i, includeFallback?:b)` | Copy rows into another table, a nested chooser, or the same table, like copy and paste in the editor: cells go into columns matching by type and input name, and a column is added for cells with no match. Nested choosers are deep copied. includeFallback also copies the fallback result and fallback cells. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, rows, targetTable?, targetNested?, insertIndex?, includeFallback?` |
| `get_cell(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i, row?:i, fallback?:b)` | Read one cell (column + row) or a column's fallback cell (fallback=true, output columns only), with its cell type. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column, row?, fallback?` |
| `set_cell(table\|assetPath, nested?, column:i, row?:i, fallback?:b, value)` | Write one cell (column + row) or a column's fallback cell (fallback=true). The value is struct text like '(Min=0,Max=100)' or a bare scalar, parsed in full before anything changes. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column, row?, fallback?, value` |
| `set_fallback(table\|assetPath, nested?, resultType?, output?, outputType?, remove?:b)` | Set the fallback result (used when no row passes every filter) from an asset (output + outputType) or a default result of resultType, or remove it (remove=true; output columns keep their fallback cells). Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, resultType?, output?, outputType?, remove?` |
| `auto_populate(table\|assetPath, nested?, column?:i, rows?:[i], includeFallback?:b)` | Fill auto populating columns' cells from each row's result: one column (column), some rows (rows, optionally includeFallback), or everything. UE 5.7 and newer. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, column?, rows?, includeFallback?` |
| `create_nested(table\|assetPath, nested?, row?:i, name?)` | Create a nested chooser inside the table's asset and make it a row's result (row), or add a new row for it. Address it afterwards with `nested` on any table action. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?, row?, name?` |
| `list_nested(table\|assetPath)` | List the nested objects of a chooser's asset (nested choosers and column-owned objects) with name, path, class and parent. Params: `table (or assetPath)` |
| `delete_nested(table\|assetPath, name)` | Delete a nested chooser or other nested object from the asset, clearing every row's reference to it. Params: `table (or assetPath), name` |
| `rename_nested(table\|assetPath, name, newName)` | Rename a nested chooser or other nested object; the name must be unique among the asset's nested objects. Params: `table (or assetPath), name, newName` |
| `restore_snapshot(table\|assetPath, snapshot:o)` | Put a chooser asset back as a snapshot records it: every table's columns, rows, disabled flags and fallback, recreating nested choosers that were deleted. The snapshot is the rollback payload of the edits that drop data no other action restores (delete_column, delete_rows, a scattered move_rows, auto_populate, delete_nested, remove_disabled). Params: `table (or assetPath), snapshot` |
| `remove_disabled(table\|assetPath, nested?)` | Delete every disabled row and column (and any column whose type is not loaded), as the editor's Remove Disabled Data does. Params: `table (or assetPath), nested?` |

## plugins

*Introspect npm-distributed plugins that contribute actions into other categories. Read-only.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list()` | Every plugin loaded from ue-mcp.yml: name, version, prefix, status, and injected actions. Params: `none` |
| `describe(name)` | Full detail for one plugin including knowledge files and flows. Params: `name` |
| `epic_add_additional_plugin_directory(directory)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds a directory the project searches for plugins, saves the .uproject file, and rescans so plugins in the directory are discovered without a restart. No-ops if the directory is already listed. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `directory` |
| `epic_add_disallowed_plugin(pluginName, disallowedPluginName, comment)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds an entry to a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file, or updates its comment if the entry already exists. The disallowed plugin does not need to be currently discovered. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, disallowedPluginName, comment` |
| `epic_add_plugin_dependency(pluginName, dependencyName, bOptional:b, bEnabled:b, bActivate?:b)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Adds a dependency entry to a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. No-ops if a dependency with that name already exists with matching settings. The dependency plugin does not need to be currently discovered. Params: `pluginName, dependencyName, bOptional, bEnabled, bActivate?` |
| `epic_create_plugin(pluginName, relativePluginLocation, bPlaceInEngine:b, templateInfo:o, description, pluginVersePath?, pythonScriptAdditionalArgs?)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Creates a new plugin from a template and loads it into the editor. Use GetPluginTemplateDescriptions to obtain a valid TemplateInfo. Params: `pluginName, relativePluginLocation, bPlaceInEngine, templateInfo, description, pluginVersePath?, pythonScriptAdditionalArgs?` |
| `epic_get_additional_plugin_directories()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the extra directories the project searches for plugins (the .uproject's AdditionalPluginDirectories). Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_capabilities(capabilityIds:[s])` | [Epic AgentPluginToolset.AgentPluginToolset] Returns details for specific capabilities. Discovery fails after 60 seconds. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `capabilityIds` |
| `epic_get_configured_additional_metadata_keys()` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists the additional metadata keys the GameFeatures subsystem is configured to read from each .uplugin (UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys), sorted. These are the only keys SetGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue and RemoveGameFeaturePluginMetadataValue will accept. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_disallowed_plugins(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the entries from a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_game_feature_plugin_details(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Reads the editable metadata on a Game Feature Plugin's .uplugin descriptor. Returns the BuiltInInitialFeatureState and the configured additional metadata keys (UGameFeaturesSubsystemSettings::AdditionalPluginMetadataKeys) with their values rendered as JSON literals. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_game_feature_state(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Gets the current state of a Game Feature Plugin. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_plugin_dependencies(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the dependency entries from a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_plugin_dependents(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the names of all discovered plugins that declare a dependency on the given plugin. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_plugin_descriptor(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Gets the editable descriptor fields for a discovered plugin. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_plugin_for_asset(assetPath)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the name of the enabled plugin whose content mount point contains the given asset path. Accepts full asset paths or mount point prefixes (e.g. /PluginName/ or /Game/Path/To/Asset). Params: `assetPath` |
| `epic_get_plugin_info(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Gets metadata for a discovered plugin, including description, version, base directory, content directory, descriptor path, and mounted asset path. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_get_plugin_template_descriptions()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Returns the list of available plugin templates. Pass one of the results to CreatePlugin to create a new plugin from that template. Params: `none` |
| `epic_is_enabled(pluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether a discovered plugin is currently enabled. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_is_game_feature_active(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Checks whether a Game Feature Plugin is active. Raises an error if the subsystem is unavailable or the plugin is not found. Use GetGameFeatureState if you need the current state when the plugin is not active. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_is_game_feature_plugin(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Return whether or not a plugin is a Game Feature Plugin. Will error if no plugin of this name can be found by the Plugin Manager. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_is_plugin_creation_allowed()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether the editor settings permit plugin creation from the plugin browser. Params: `none` |
| `epic_is_plugin_modification_allowed()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Checks whether the editor settings permit modifying plugins from the plugin browser. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_capabilities()` | [Epic AgentPluginToolset.AgentPluginToolset] Lists available capabilities from the current agent plugin directories and working directory. Discovery fails after 60 seconds. Warnings report rejected sources and discovery limits. Treat capability IDs as opaque values and pass them unchanged to GetCapabilities. Use an agent's Reference, not its ID, when a skill asks for a 'subagent_type'. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_discovered_game_feature_plugins()` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists all discovered Game Feature Plugins sorted by name. This includes disabled plugins and plugins the Game Features system has not registered, which the other tools cannot resolve. Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_discovered_plugins()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the names of all discovered plugins (enabled and disabled), sorted alphabetically. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_enabled_game_feature_plugins()` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Lists enabled Game Feature Plugins that the Game Features system has registered, sorted by name. The project's policy can keep an enabled plugin from registering; ListDiscoveredGameFeaturePlugins still includes those. Use the Plugins toolset to do general plugin enable/disable tasks. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_enabled_plugins()` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Lists the names of all enabled plugins, sorted alphabetically. Params: `none` |
| `epic_remove_additional_plugin_directory(directory)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes a directory the project searches for plugins, saves the .uproject file, and rescans. Plugins from the directory that are enabled stay loaded until the editor restarts. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `directory` |
| `epic_remove_disallowed_plugin(pluginName, disallowedPluginName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes an entry from a plugin's DisallowedPlugins array in its .uplugin file. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, disallowedPluginName` |
| `epic_remove_game_feature_plugin_metadata_value(pluginName, key)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Removes one of the configured additional metadata keys from the GFP's .uplugin. After removal the key round-trips through AdditionalMetadata as an empty string -- that is the engine parser's default for missing keys, surfaced honestly. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, key` |
| `epic_remove_plugin_dependency(pluginName, dependencyName)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Removes a dependency entry from a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. Params: `pluginName, dependencyName` |
| `epic_request_activate_game_feature(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests activation of a Game Feature Plugin, loading it first if it is not already loaded. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_request_deactivate_game_feature(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests deactivation of a Game Feature Plugin, which leaves it loaded. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_request_load_game_feature(pluginName)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests load of a Game Feature Plugin without activating it. Use RequestActivateGameFeature instead to make the plugin's features live. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName` |
| `epic_request_unload_game_feature(pluginName, bKeepRegistered?:b)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Requests unload of a Game Feature Plugin, taking it out of the Loaded state. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, bKeepRegistered?` |
| `epic_set_game_feature_plugin_built_in_auto_state(pluginName, newState)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Sets the BuiltInInitialFeatureState on the GFP's .uplugin descriptor and writes the descriptor back to disk. EPluginToolsetGFPAutoState::Invalid is not accepted. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, newState` |
| `epic_set_game_feature_plugin_metadata_value(pluginName, key, jsonValueLiteral)` | [Epic GameFeaturesToolset.GameFeaturesToolset] Writes a value for one of the configured additional metadata keys to the GFP's .uplugin. JsonValueLiteral must be a valid JSON literal (e.g. true, 42, "hello", {"Major":1}); booleans and numbers are stored as native JSON types rather than strings. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, key, jsonValueLiteral` |
| `epic_set_plugin_enabled(pluginName, bEnabled:b)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Enables or disables a plugin in the project and saves the .uproject file, checking it out via source control if enabled. Params: `pluginName, bEnabled` |
| `epic_update_plugin_dependency(pluginName, dependencyName, bOptional?:b, bEnabled?:b, bActivate?:b)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Changes the settings of an existing dependency entry in a plugin's Plugins array in its .uplugin file. Anything not provided keeps its current value, as do fields the plugin editor doesn't show, such as platform lists. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `pluginName, dependencyName, bOptional?, bEnabled?, bActivate?` |
| `epic_update_plugin_descriptor(pluginName, newDescriptor:o)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Updates a plugin's descriptor fields and writes them to its .uplugin file. Checks out the file via source control if source control is enabled. No-ops if the serialized descriptor is unchanged (file is not touched). Params: `pluginName, newDescriptor` |
| `epic_validate_new_plugin_name_and_location(pluginName, relativePluginLocation, bPlaceInEngine:b, templateInfo:o)` | [Epic PluginToolset.PluginToolset] Validates that PluginName and RelativePluginLocation are acceptable for a new plugin. Params: `pluginName, relativePluginLocation, bPlaceInEngine, templateInfo` |

## epic

*Unreal's AI Toolset Registry itself: discovery (status/list_toolsets/describe_toolset), turning toolsets off and on (get_toolset_states/set_toolset_enabled), direct dispatch (call_tool), and the registry's own meta-tooling (agent skills, programmatic tool batching). Also Epic's Unreal MCP plugin's own tools and resources (list_mcp_tools/call_mcp_tool, list_mcp_resources/read_mcp_resource). Toolsets that map to a real editor domain are NOT here - unless nativeTools withholds them, they appear as epic_* actions on that domain's category (GAS in gas, Sequencer in animation, Dataflow in dataflow, and so on), so reach for the domain tool first and use this one to introspect or call the registry directly. A toolset no recorded catalog has (one a launcher plugin adds, such as the Fab plugin's FabToolset that searches Fab and imports listings, or a newer engine's) has no epic_* action but is still listed by list_toolsets and runs through call_tool: check here before concluding the editor cannot do something. Requires UE 5.8+ with the ToolsetRegistry plugin enabled - call epic(status) first to check availability. The ai_assistant_* actions drive Epic's in-editor AI Assistant (UE 5.9+ with the AI Assistant plugin): send a message and get the reply, read a conversation, and read its update events; check ai_assistant_status first.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `status()` | Report whether Epic's ToolsetRegistry is available and how many toolsets are registered. Never errors (reports available=false with a reason when the plugin is absent). Params: `none` |
| `list_toolsets(nameFilter?, includeSchemas?:b)` | List registered toolsets: name, version, description, tool names + count. Strips the verbose per-tool input/output schemas to stay small - use describe_toolset for those (or includeSchemas). Params: `nameFilter?, includeSchemas?` |
| `describe_toolset(toolset)` | Full schema for one toolset: every tool with its input/output JSON schema. Params: `toolset` |
| `get_toolset_states(nameFilter?)` | Every registered toolset with its enabled state, including the disabled ones list_toolsets leaves out: for each, the block and allow patterns that match its name (blockedBy, allowedBy), outsideAllowList, disabledBy (blockList, allowList or noVisibleTools) and toggledHere when set_toolset_enabled wrote its pattern. Also the registry's live blockedNames and allowedNames, the settings' copies, and the config file they are saved to. UE 5.8+ with the ToolsetRegistry plugin, Win64 editor. Params: `nameFilter?` |
| `set_toolset_enabled(toolsets:[s], enabled:b)` | Turn registered toolsets off or on by exact name, effective at once: a disabled toolset leaves list_toolsets and its epic_* actions, and call_tool refuses its tools. Off adds the pattern /^\Qname\E$/ to the registry's block list; on removes it, and adds the same pattern to a non-empty allow list that does not match. Applied to the live registry and saved to UToolsetRegistrySettings (Config/DefaultGame.ini on 5.9, DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini on 5.8), so the next session starts the same way. Unknown names are refused with validNames; a toolset blocked by a pattern this action did not write is refused rather than edited. A toolset already in the asked state reports unchanged. Rollback restores the previous state. Params: `toolsets, enabled` |
| `call_tool(toolset, tool, input?:o, inputJson?)` | Execute a registered Epic tool exactly as its MCP server would. tool takes the qualified name from describe_toolset, e.g. GASToolsets.AttributeSetToolset.ListAttributeSets; pass the arguments as input, or as inputJson to send raw JSON. Returns the tool's JSON result; images its output schema marks (FToolsetImage) come back as MCP image content. A tool that answers later reports progress while it runs. Params: `toolset, tool, input?, inputJson?` |
| `list_mcp_tools(nameFilter?, includeSchemas?:b, includeRegistryAdapters?:b)` | List the tools Epic's Unreal MCP plugin serves beside the registry: legacy MCP Tool Library Blueprints (source toolLibrary) and tools other plugins register (source plugin). Its adapters onto the registry are counted, not listed, since list_toolsets covers them; includeRegistryAdapters lists them too. available=false and no tools when the plugin is not enabled. Params: `nameFilter?, includeSchemas?, includeRegistryAdapters?` |
| `call_mcp_tool(tool, input?:o, inputJson?)` | Run a tool from list_mcp_tools exactly as Epic's MCP server would: input as an object, or inputJson. Text and structuredContent come back as JSON, images and audio as MCP content. A long tool reports progress, and cancelling the call reaches the tool's CancelAsync. Params: `tool, input?, inputJson?` |
| `list_mcp_resources()` | List the resources registered with Epic's Unreal MCP plugin: uri, name, title, description, mimeType. Empty when no provider is registered or the plugin is off. This server also serves them as MCP resources. Params: `none` |
| `read_mcp_resource(uri)` | Read one resource from list_mcp_resources by uri: contents with its text, or its blob as base64. Params: `uri` |
| `ai_assistant_status()` | Report whether Epic's AI Assistant API (UAIAssistantInstance, UE 5.9+ with the experimental AI Assistant plugin) is loaded: engineVersion, available, and when it is not, errorCode unsupported_engine_version or PLUGIN_NOT_AVAILABLE with the reason. When available, lists its UFUNCTIONs, whether the singleton exists, whether conversation updates are being recorded, and pendingRequests. Never errors. Params: `none` |
| `ai_assistant_send_message(message, conversationId?, hiddenContext?, reply?:b, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)` | Send a user message to Epic's AI Assistant, as UAIAssistantInstance::SendTextMessageAndGetReply (reply=true, default) or SendTextMessage (reply=false). Empty conversationId starts a new conversation. Opens the assistant panel, which needs the editor's Epic sign-in to answer. Waits (default 300s) and returns state complete with reply (and conversationId: the one the reply names, or on builds whose reply is bare text the first update event's, when none was given) or, with reply=false, the conversationId the message was bound to; wait=false returns state pending and a requestId for get_request. A timeout fails with state timed_out and keeps the requestId. Engines before 5.9 return unsupported_engine_version. Params: `message, conversationId?, hiddenContext?, reply?, wait?, timeoutSeconds?` |
| `ai_assistant_get_conversation(conversationId?, wait?:b, timeoutSeconds?:n)` | Read an AI Assistant conversation as Epic serializes it (UAIAssistantInstance::GetConversationJson): conversation is the parsed JSON (conversationJson when it does not parse). Empty conversationId reads the active conversation. Does not open the assistant panel, and fails while it is closed (send_message opens it). Waits like send_message (default 60s). Params: `conversationId?, wait?, timeoutSeconds?` |
| `ai_assistant_get_request(requestId:i)` | One poll of an AI Assistant request that send_message or get_conversation opened: state pending, complete (with its reply, conversationId or conversation) or failed (errorCode ai_assistant_failed, assistantError). A complete or failed answer releases the request; an unknown or released requestId returns ai_assistant_request_not_found. Params: `requestId` |
| `ai_assistant_get_events(sinceSeq?:i, conversationId?)` | Conversation updates UAIAssistantInstance::OnConversationUpdated reported (Started, MessagesUpdated, Complete, Stopped), each with seq, conversationId and utc, oldest first; pass the last nextSeq as sinceSeq to read only newer ones. Recording starts once the assistant instance exists (after a send_message or get_conversation, or the panel's own use); listening=false says it has not started. Does not open the panel. Params: `sinceSeq?, conversationId?` |
| `epic_create_markdown_knowledge_base(alias, description, relativePath)` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Creates an empty markdown base under the project's Content/KnowledgeBases folder, writes the marker file that lets it be rediscovered on restart, and registers it. An empty base is valid; the first WriteKnowledge creates its first file. Raises an error if the alias is already registered or not a valid identifier, if RelativePath is not one or two plain segments, if the directory already belongs to another base, or if it cannot be written. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `alias, description, relativePath` |
| `epic_create_skill(folderPath, assetName, description, details:o)` | [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Creates a new AgentSkill. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Params: `folderPath, assetName, description, details` |
| `epic_execute_tool_script(script)` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset] Execute a Python script against the toolset APIs. Use this to batch multiple tool calls into a single script execution, reducing round-trips and context usage. IMPORTANT: Available modules and usage instructions are described by the value returned by `get_execution_environment`. You MUST call `get_execution_environment` once in the conversation before using this tool. Read the value in the `instructions` field in the returned environment info prior to calling this function, so that you understand what APIs are available and how to use them. Before writing a script that calls multiple tools, look up the output schemas (if available) for any tools you plan to use. This returns the JSON schema describing each tool's return value, so you know how to parse results and pass data between calls. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `script` |
| `epic_get_docked_context()` | [Epic AIAssistantEditor.AIAssistantToolset] Returns the UE tab layout and editor context in the window hosting the assistant. Tab information is available for tool windows with no asset editor. The result is empty when the assistant is closed or detached from a window. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_execution_environment()` | [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset] Get details about execution environment. This includes instructions on how to write scripts, and constraints, such as what modules may be imported and the script entrypoint and function signature. Available on UE 5.8; absent from UE 5.9. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_knowledge_entry(alias, entryId)` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Returns one entry by id with its full body. Ids are exact, so take them from QueryKnowledgeBase hits rather than composing them; a miss names the nearest ids the base holds. Raises an error if the alias is not registered or no entry has that id. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `alias, entryId` |
| `epic_get_project_context()` | [Epic AIAssistantEditor.AIAssistantToolset] Returns important information about the current project and/or current user. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_get_skills(skillPaths:[s])` | [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Returns detailed information about a specific set of AgentSkills. Params: `skillPaths` |
| `epic_list_knowledge_base_tags(alias, prefix, limit?:i)` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Lists the tags a base's entries carry, most common first, so a Tags filter is spelled from what exists rather than guessed. Tags are exact strings: "simulation" does not match "Simulation". Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `alias, prefix, limit?` |
| `epic_list_knowledge_bases()` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Lists every registered knowledge base. Call this first: aliases are the handle every other tool takes and they vary by project. Choose a base by its Description. A base with a "vocabulary" consumer is the catalogue that tool's input is spelled from, so query it before calling that tool. Builds nothing. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_skills()` | [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Gets a summary of all AgentSkills in the project. Params: `none` |
| `epic_query_knowledge_base(alias, text, tags:[s], limit?:i)` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Searches one base. Text is matched as plain words and ranked; Tags keep only entries carrying all of them; both empty lists the whole base. Bodies are truncated; GetKnowledgeEntry returns a hit's full payload. Raises an error if the alias is not registered or the base fails to build. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `alias, text, tags, limit?` |
| `epic_update_skill(skillPath, description, details:o)` | [Epic ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset] Updates an existing AgentSkill. This should ONLY be called after getting explicit direction or permission from the user. Params: `skillPath, description, details` |
| `epic_write_knowledge(alias, fileId, summary, tags:[s], bodyJson, entryId)` | [Epic KnowledgeBaseToolset.KnowledgeBaseTools] Writes a structured entry into a markdown base as a JSON block, preserving the prose and other blocks in the file. An existing EntryId is replaced in the file that holds it, wherever that is; an empty EntryId appends a new entry to the file FileId names, creating the file if absent. Reuse the stem of a hit's Source as FileId so a topic accumulates rather than sprawls. Only markdown bases are writable; check bWritable in ListKnowledgeBases first. Raises an error if the alias is not registered, the base is read-only, BodyJson is not a JSON object, or the file cannot be written. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `alias, fileId, summary, tags, bodyJson, entryId` |

## fab

*Fab (Epic marketplace) content in the editor. Searching the Fab catalog and importing listings, free ones included, is what Epic's built-in Fab tools do (the Fab plugin's FabToolset, UE 5.9): list_epic_tools lists the ones this editor has and the epic(call_tool) call that runs each. ue-mcp's own actions add: plugin/login status, login/logout, syncing your owned library into the Content Browser, downloading and verifying owned UE packs with pause/resume, inspecting/clearing the native cache, installing verified Content safely, importing local source files, and opening the fab.com search page at a query.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list_epic_tools(includeSchemas?:b)` | List Epic's built-in Fab tools the connected editor has, which search the Fab catalog and import listings (the Fab plugin's FabToolset in Unreal's Toolset Registry, UE 5.9, and any Fab tool registered with Epic's Unreal MCP plugin). Each tool names the call that runs it: epic(call_tool) with its qualified name, or epic(call_mcp_tool). ue-mcp does not replace these tools; use them for catalog search and free-asset import, and fab's own actions for the owned library. includeSchemas returns each tool's input schema. available=false with a note when the editor has none. Params: `includeSchemas? (bool)` |
| `status()` | Report Fab plugin state: authenticated (whether a native Fab session is available), whether the plugin is installed and enabled (pluginDir, pluginVersion), whether the module is loaded, whether the native import/cache API is linked in this build, whether the Fab window has been opened this session, the download cache location/size, and librarySync state with pages, snapshotItems, publishedRows and any sanitized failure. The launcher installs Fab as its own 'Fab UE Plugin' item, so an engine can lack it; then errorCode is PLUGIN_NOT_AVAILABLE and note says what is missing and how to install it, the same reason the other Fab actions refuse with. Call this first. Params: `none` |
| `login()` | Open the native Fab EOS account portal. With a session already active it opens nothing and answers unchanged=true. Returns before authentication completes; finish any prompt, then poll status.authenticated. No inverse: opening a portal does not own the resulting account session. idempotencyObservable=false because this call cannot attribute a later login to itself. Params: `none` |
| `logout()` | Request native Fab logout and clear this editor's owned-library snapshot. EOS completes asynchronously; poll status.authenticated until false. No inverse: cleared credentials require a person to sign back in. Params: `none` |
| `sync_library(batchSize?:i)` | Sync the owned Fab library into the native Content Browser table (UE 5.8+). Requires a native login. Returns immediately; poll status.librarySync until complete or failed. Fetches all pages before replacing the previous snapshot, preserving it on HTTP, JSON, pagination or publication failure. No project files change. Params: `batchSize?` |
| `list_owned(query?, offset?:i, limit?:i)` | Read the current account's synced owned metadata and supported projectVersions, with local title filtering and pagination. Each row adds listingId (what download takes) and availableForThisEditor (this editor's engine and platform are among its projectVersions). Complete sync_library first; before it, errorCode FAB_NOT_SIGNED_IN or FAB_LIBRARY_NOT_SYNCED says which step is missing. Only the owned library: to search the public catalog use Epic's built-in Fab tools (list_epic_tools). Params: `query?, offset?, limit?` |
| `download(listingId, engineVersion?, platform?, outputDirectory?, verifyOnly?:b)` | Start an owned native UE asset-pack download. engineVersion and platform default to this editor's; a listing without that build answers with the versions it offers. Returns job immediately; poll download_status for complete or failed. Native BuildPatchServices verifies SHA hashes and reuses partial staging. Defaults to the native Fab cache. verifyOnly checks an existing tree without repairing it. Repeat the same listing/version/outputDirectory after an editor restart to resume. No project content changes until install_pack. Params: `listingId, engineVersion?, platform?, outputDirectory?, verifyOnly?` |
| `download_status(jobId?)` | Read asynchronous job state, native phase, progress, required/downloaded bytes and failure code; omit jobId to list this editor session's jobs. No tokens or signed URLs are returned. Params: `jobId?` |
| `pause_download(jobId)` | Stop network/assembly work while keeping native verified files and staging. Wait for paused before resuming. Can pause distribution resolution too. Params: `jobId` |
| `resume_download(jobId)` | Resume a paused, failed or cancelled job. Reuses the native Fab session and obtains a fresh distribution signature before native verification and repair. Params: `jobId` |
| `cancel_download(jobId)` | Cancel a job while retaining its verified data for an explicit later resume. Does not delete downloaded or installed content. Params: `jobId` |
| `install_pack(jobId)` | Copy a completed, SHA-verified pack's native Content packages into this project, preserving package paths. Checks every source and collision first; different existing files are refused. Skips identical files and installs no Config, engine plugins or settings. Records exactly which files it created for remove_installation. Params: `jobId` |
| `remove_installation(jobId)` | Remove only unchanged, unloaded project files that this session's install_pack job created. Refuses modified or loaded packages before deleting anything; preserves pre-existing identical files. Params: `jobId` |
| `list_cached()` | List the entries currently in the local Fab download cache (already-downloaded owned assets). Params: `none` |
| `cache_info()` | Report the Fab download cache location, total size, and entry count. Params: `none` |
| `clear_cache()` | Delete the local Fab download cache to reclaim disk. Does not affect assets already imported into the project. Reports unchanged=true when the cache was already empty (where the native Fab API is linked). No inverse: the downloads come back only by downloading them again. Params: `none` |
| `import_file(source\|sourceFile, destination\|destPath)` | Import a source file into the project through the Fab Interchange import pipeline. Use for owned assets that are downloaded/cached locally, or any local source file (fbx, textures). Single files import synchronously and report the created asset paths; pack/quixel workflows may run asynchronously. A synchronous import rolls back by deleting exactly the assets it created, taken from the paths the importer reported (a force delete, because the imported set references itself). An ASYNCHRONOUS import emits no inverse: its paths are not known yet, and a record naming the destination folder would delete whatever else already lives there. Params: `source (or sourceFile), destination (or destPath)` |
| `open_search(query, listingType?, assetFormat?, free?:b, open?:b)` | Open fab.com's own search page at a query in the user's default browser. Builds https://www.fab.com/search?q=<query>&listing_types=<listingType>&asset_formats=<assetFormat>&is_free=1, leaving out unset filters. This action itself sends no request to Fab and returns no listing data; to search the catalog and import listings from the editor, use Epic's built-in Fab tools (list_epic_tools). open=false returns the URL without opening it, for showing as a link. Returns url and opened. Params: `query, listingType?, assetFormat?, free?, open?` |

## datasmith

*Datasmith scenes (Revit, SketchUp, CAD exports): inspect a .udatasmith file's options and element counts, import it into a content folder and the level, reimport a scene asset with actor sync, and query level actors by tag with their Datasmith metadata and bounds.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `status()` | Report whether the DatasmithImporter and DatasmithContent plugins are enabled and loaded, and list the DatasmithSceneActors in the editor level with their scene asset and related actor count. Call this first. Params: `none` |
| `inspect(filePath)` | Open a .udatasmith file without importing it and return the exporter header (host, vendor, product, version), element counts (meshes, mesh actors, lights, cameras, materials, textures) and every import options object with its current values. The option names it returns are what import and reimport take in options. Params: `filePath` |
| `import(filePath, destinationPath, options?:o)` | Import a .udatasmith file into destinationPath and the current level. Returns the DatasmithScene asset path, the spawned DatasmithSceneActor, the scene's asset counts (static meshes, materials, textures) and actor count, and the source element counts. options sets DatasmithImportOptions fields by dotted path, e.g. {"BaseOptions.bIncludeLight": false}. A failed import is an error that points at LogDatasmithImport. No inverse: it creates the asset set and the actors. Params: `filePath, destinationPath, options?` |
| `reimport(sceneAssetPath, filePath?, syncActors?:b, respawnDeleted?:b, options?:o)` | Reimport an existing DatasmithScene asset from its source (or from filePath when the source moved), updating its actors in the level (syncActors, default true) and optionally respawning deleted ones (respawnDeleted). Returns asset counts before and after and the per-actor changes keyed by Datasmith id: added, removed, moved and kept. No inverse. Params: `sceneAssetPath, filePath?, syncActors?, respawnDeleted?, options?` |
| `query_actors(tagPrefix?, tags?:[s], metadataKey?, metadataValue?, includeMetadata?:b, includeBounds?:b, limit?:i)` | Find level actors by tag prefix (e.g. Revit.Element.Id.), exact tags, or a Datasmith metadata key/value, and return each one's matched tags, UDatasmithAssetUserData metadata and world bounds, plus the union bounds. Tags and bounds work without the Datasmith plugin; metadata needs it. Params: `tagPrefix?, tags?, metadataKey?, metadataValue?, includeMetadata?, includeBounds?, limit?` |

## metahuman

*MetaHuman Creator characters: create a MetaHumanCharacter, read its body constraints, wardrobe and texture state, set parametric body constraints, dress wardrobe slots, request the cloud auto-rig and texture sources, and assemble it into skeletal meshes and a blueprint.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `status()` | Report whether the MetaHumanCharacter plugin is enabled and its editor subsystem loaded, and list the MetaHumanCharacter assets under /Game. The Epic cloud login state is reported as unknown with the reason: no reflected API exposes it. Call this first. Params: `none` |
| `create_character(name, packagePath?, onConflict?)` | Create a MetaHumanCharacter asset through the plugin's own factory. Idempotent by name (onConflict skip). Rollback deletes the asset. Params: `name, packagePath?, onConflict?` |
| `read_character(assetPath\|characterPath, includeBody?:b)` | Read a MetaHumanCharacter: template type, texture state (hasHighResolutionTextures, synthesized face and body texture counts, hasFaceDNABlendshapes), and with includeBody (default) the body constraints (name, active, target, min, max), wardrobe slot selections and canBuild. Opens the character for editing to read those and closes it again if it was not open. The rig state is not reflected and is reported as unknown with the reason. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), includeBody?` |
| `set_body(assetPath\|characterPath, constraints:o)` | Set parametric body constraints by name, {Height: 180, Muscularity: 0.9} or {Height: {target: 180, active: true}}, and commit the body state. Writes the whole constraint array back, so edits are not lost to the copy the engine hands out, refuses unknown names with the list of real ones, and returns each constraint before and after. Rollback restores the previous targets and active flags. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), constraints` |
| `set_wardrobe(assetPath\|characterPath, items:o)` | Dress wardrobe slots: {"Top Garment": wardrobeItemPath}. Each item is added to the character's collection and selected in its slot, then the preview is rebuilt. Returns per-item applied/error and the slot selections before and after. No inverse. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), items` |
| `request_rig(assetPath\|characterPath, rigType?, blocking?:b)` | Request auto-rigging from the MetaHuman cloud service (rigType JointsOnly or JointsAndBlendshapes), blocking by default. This is the step that opens the Epic login, so run it before request_textures. A refusal for want of a login is an error with loginState not-logged-in. Returns the texture/rig state and canBuild afterwards plus the MetaHuman log warnings. No inverse. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), rigType?, blocking?` |
| `request_textures(assetPath\|characterPath, blocking?:b)` | Request high-resolution texture sources from the MetaHuman cloud service, blocking by default. Needs the Epic login request_rig opens; a refusal for want of it is an error with loginState not-logged-in. Returns texture state before and after. No inverse. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), blocking?` |
| `assemble(assetPath\|characterPath, pipelineType?, quality?, nameOverride?, commonFolderPath?)` | Assemble the character (pipelineType Cinematic, Optimized or UEFN; quality such as Medium) as one tracked long call of up to 15 minutes. Checks CanBuildMetaHuman first and returns its logged reason when it refuses. Returns the created skeletal meshes, blueprints and other asset paths, the elapsed seconds and the MetaHuman log warnings. No inverse. Params: `assetPath (or characterPath), pipelineType?, quality?, nameOverride?, commonFolderPath?` |

## dataflow

*Dataflow graphs: node and pin authoring, variables, comment boxes, templates, and creation of Dataflow-compatible assets (Chaos geometry and simulation graphs). Requires UE 5.8+ with the Dataflow toolsets available.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `epic_add_comment(dataflow:ref, graphPath, comment, position:o, size:o, color:o)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] AddComment Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, graphPath, comment, position, size, color` |
| `epic_add_comment_box(graph:ref, nodes:[ref], comment?, color?:o)` | [Epic DataflowAgent.DataflowAgentToolset] Adds a comment box around the given nodes. Params: `graph, nodes, comment?, color?` |
| `epic_add_graph(dataflow:ref, graphName, bIsForEach:b)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Adds a sub-graph. Add its "FDataflowSubGraphInputNode" and "FDataflowSubGraphOutputNode" nodes with AddNode, its signature with AddGraphBinding, and run it with a "SubGraph/<Name>" node. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, graphName, bIsForEach` |
| `epic_add_graph_binding(dataflow:ref, graphPath, direction, bindingName, dataType)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Adds a binding to the signature of a sub-graph: an output pin of its input node (Direction "Input") or an input pin of its output node (Direction "Output"). The nodes running the sub-graph get the matching pin. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, graphPath, direction, bindingName, dataType` |
| `epic_add_link(dataflow:ref, outputPinPath, inputPinPath)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Links an output pin to an input pin, replacing the input pin's existing link if any, as the graph editor does: a pin of any type takes the type of the pin it is linked to, and a conversion node is added when the types need one. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, outputPinPath, inputPinPath` |
| `epic_add_link_with_new_pin(dataflow:ref, sourcePinPath, targetNodePath)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Adds a pin to a node that supports it (e.g. the input or output node of a sub-graph) for the type of SourcePinPath, and links the two, as dropping a link on the node in the graph editor does. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, sourcePinPath, targetNodePath` |
| `epic_add_node(graph:ref, typeName, nodeName, jsonParams?, x?:i, y?:i)` | [Epic DataflowAgent.DataflowAgentToolset] Adds a node of the given type to the Dataflow graph. Params: `graph, typeName, nodeName, jsonParams?, x?, y?` |
| `epic_add_node__dataflow_scripting_subsystem(dataflow:ref, graphPath, nodeType, nodeName, position:o)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Adds a node. Use AddComment for comments. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, graphPath, nodeType, nodeName, position` |
| `epic_add_node_pins(dataflow:ref, nodePath, count:i)` | [Epic DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem] Adds pins to a node whose FDataflowNodeInfo::bCanAddPins is true, as its "Add Pin" menu does. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `dataflow, nodePath, count` |
| `epic_add_variable(graph:ref, name, type)` | [Epic DataflowAgent.DataflowAgentToolset] Adds a new variable to the Dataflow graph. Supported type strings: Primitives : "Bool", "Int32", "Int64", "Float", "Double", "Name", "String" Structs : UScriptStruct name with or without the "F" prefix e.g. "Vector", "FVector", "Transform", "FTransform", "Rotator", "LinearColor" Objects : "Object:<ClassName>" where ClassName is with or without the "U"/"A" prefix e.g. "Object:StaticMesh", "Object:USkeletalMesh" Dataflow types, as pins show them: e.g. "float", "FVector", "TObjectPtr<UStaticMesh>", "TArray<int32>" Params: graph, name, type |

## conversation

*Conversation graphs (UConversationDatabase): dialogue nodes, node connections, sub-nodes, speakers, and entry points. Requires UE 5.8+ with the Conversation toolsets available.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `epic_get_all_nodes(conversation:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns all reachable nodes in the conversation. Use ObjectTools.get_class and get_properties on each node to inspect type and properties. Each node's GUID is available via its compiled_node_guid attribute. Params: `conversation` |
| `epic_get_node_by_guid(conversation:ref, guid)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns a conversation node by its GUID. Params: `conversation, guid` |
| `epic_get_node_connections(node:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns output connection GUIDs for a conversation node. Params: `node` |
| `epic_get_node_guids(conversation:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns GUIDs of all reachable nodes, in map iteration order. Use with get_node_by_guid to look up specific nodes. Params: `conversation` |
| `epic_get_sub_nodes(node:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns sub-nodes (requirements, choices) attached to a task node. Params: `node` |
| `epic_list_entry_points(conversation:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns entry points (FConversationEntryList structs). Params: `conversation` |
| `epic_list_speakers(conversation:ref)` | [Epic conversation_toolset.toolsets.conversation.ConversationTools] Returns speaker/participant information. Params: `conversation` |
