## source_control

*Source control through the editor's own provider (Perforce, Git, Unity Version Control, Subversion): provider, connection and supported operations, file status, history, the project's pending changes, checkout, add, mark for delete, revert, sync, diff, submit, and whether bridge writes check out read-only files automatically. Provider-specific actions (shelves, streams, branches) come from provider plugins injected here under their own prefix, such as p4_*.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `get_provider()` | The active provider, whether it is enabled and connected, its status fields (port, user, client or workspace, branch, repository, where the provider reports them), what it supports (checkout, changelists, diff against the depot), which source_control actions the provider can run (operations, asked of the provider where the engine supports it) and the bridge's checkout mode. Call this first. With no provider configured it reports enabled=false rather than failing. Params: `none` |
| `get_status(paths:[s], limit?:i)` | State of named assets, files or folders, refreshed from the provider: checked out, added, deleted, modified, conflicted, out of date, checked out by another user (otherUser), what can be done next (canCheckout, canAdd, canRevert, canSubmit) and unsavedInEditor for a loaded package. A folder reports every file the provider knows under it, up to limit. Params: `paths, limit?` |
| `list_changes(paths?:[s], limit?:i, includeUntracked?:b)` | Every changed, added, deleted, opened or untracked file under the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders (or the paths given), with its state. Where the provider uses changelists (Perforce) each file names its changelist and changelists lists them with descriptions. Capped at limit with total and truncated; a failed refresh is reported as a warning over the cached list rather than an error. Params: `paths?, limit?, includeUntracked?` |
| `checkout(paths:[s])` | Check out (open for edit) files so they can be saved. Reports checkedOut, alreadyCheckedOut and failed with a reason per file (locked by another user, out of date, not under source control). On a provider without checkout (Git) the files are reported as checkoutNotRequired. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call checked out. Params: `paths` |
| `add(paths:[s])` | Mark new files for add. A file must exist on disk, so save a new asset first. Reports added, alreadyControlled and failed per file. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call added. Params: `paths` |
| `revert(paths:[s], dryRun?:b, discardUnsaved?:b, restoreFrom?:o)` | Revert files to the repository revision, discarding local edits. dryRun=true lists what would be reverted (wouldRevert) and changes nothing. Unsaved editor edits to a named package are reported (unsavedInEditor) and refuse the call unless discardUnsaved=true. Loaded packages are unloaded and reloaded around the revert; a loaded map must be closed first. No inverse: the discarded edits are gone. Params: `paths, dryRun?, discardUnsaved?, restoreFrom?` |
| `diff(path, revision?, openEditor?:b, contextLines?:i, maxLines?:i)` | Diff one file against a repository revision: head, or revision (the provider's id, a unique prefix of 7 or more characters, its number, or head, as history lists them). A text file (config, source, .uproject) returns a unified diff with addedLines and removedLines, capped at maxLines. A package returns its status and the revision it would be compared with; openEditor=true opens the editor's asset diff window against that revision, with the revision loaded into a /Temp package that is unloaded when the window closes (unloadsOnClose). Params: `path, revision?, openEditor?, contextLines?, maxLines?` |
| `submit(paths:[s], description)` | Submit (Perforce, Subversion, Unity Version Control) or commit (Git) the named files with a description. Only the named files are submitted, never implicitly. Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Reports submitted and failed per file. No inverse: a submit is in the repository history, and undoing it is a new change. Params: `paths, description` |
| `mark_for_delete(paths:[s])` | Mark files for delete in the repository. Where the provider removes the file from disk on delete (Git, Perforce) it is gone locally too. Reports markedForDelete, alreadyDeleted and failed per file (marked for add, not under source control, locked). Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call; a clean loaded package is listed under loadedInEditor. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call marked. Params: `paths` |
| `sync(paths?:[s])` | Sync (Perforce get latest, Git pull) the named paths, or the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders, to the latest repository revision. Packages under the paths with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Loaded packages whose file changed are reloaded (reloaded); changedFiles lists the named files and loaded packages the sync rewrote. No inverse: going back is another sync. Params: `paths?` |
| `history(path, limit?:i)` | Revision history of one asset or file, newest first: revision, user, date, action, description, changelist (checkInIdentifier) and file size per revision, capped at limit with total and truncated. Params: `path, limit?` |
| `connect(password?)` | Connect, or reconnect, the editor's configured provider, with an optional password or ticket for providers that log in. Reports wasConnected and connected, and the provider's own error text when it fails. The password is never echoed. Params: `password?` |
| `set_checkout_mode(mode:{manual,auto})` | Choose what a bridge write does with a read-only file under source control for the rest of the editor session. manual (the default) refuses and names source_control(checkout); auto checks the file out first and lists it on the result as autoCheckedOut. UE_MCP_CHECKOUT_MODE=auto at editor startup turns it on from the start. Rolls back to the previous mode. Params: `mode` |
| `epic_add(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Adds files to source control; they are added on the next submit. Async: await the result. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is already tracked, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_check_out(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Checks files out, so they can be edited and submitted. Async: await the result. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that is not tracked or is checked out exclusively by another user, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_create_branch(branchName, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Creates a branch off the current branch. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. Providers may refuse while there are pending changes, and may push the new branch to the server. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branchName, repository?` |
| `epic_create_changelist(assetPaths:[s], description)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Creates a new pending changelist and moves the specified files into it. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPaths, description` |
| `epic_delete(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Marks files for delete and removes them from disk, discarding any unsaved changes in their loaded packages. Unloads the assets of the deleted files and reloads the open level when its map or external packages change, so a deleted actor of a level that stores its actors in separate files disappears from that level. Blocks until the delete and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not tracked; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_delete_branch(branch, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Deletes a branch for every user. Providers that keep history may archive it instead. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it accepts, for example it may refuse the current branch. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch, repository?` |
| `epic_download(file, revision?, destination?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Downloads a revision of a file to a local path, without changing the workspace. Async: await the result. Refreshes the history of the file first. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `file, revision?, destination?` |
| `epic_edit_changelist_description(changelistId, description)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Replaces the description of a pending changelist. Async: await the result. The default changelist's description cannot be edited; to give its files a description, create a changelist with CreateChangelist and move the files into it with MoveFilesToChangelist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `changelistId, description` |
| `epic_get_asset_source_control_state(assetPath)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the source-control state for an asset. Blocks until the provider answers. Does not write to the message log. Raises when the asset does not exist or when the state cannot be read, for example when source control is disabled or unavailable. A file that is not tracked by source control is not an error: bIsSourceControlled is false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPath` |
| `epic_get_changelist_files(changelistId)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the files in a pending changelist, including files that are not content. Raises when source control is unavailable or the changelist does not exist. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `changelistId` |
| `epic_get_checked_out_assets()` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the content paths of all assets you currently have open in source control (checked out, marked for add, or marked for delete). Non-content files (source, config, etc.) and anything that doesn't map to a mounted content root are omitted. Files marked for delete are still listed. Raises when source control is not enabled or the status refresh fails. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_asset_revisions(assetPath)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Returns the source-control revision history for an asset, newest first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPath` |
| `epic_list_branches(repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the branches of a repository. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `repository?` |
| `epic_list_changelists()` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists the pending changelists, including the default changelist. Raises when source control is unavailable, the provider does not use changelists or the refresh fails. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |
| `epic_list_submitted_changelists(revision?, length?:i, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Lists submitted changelists, one page at a time, in the order the provider reports them, typically newest first. Async: await the result. To get the next page, pass the last identifier of a page as Revision. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `revision?, length?, repository?` |
| `epic_load_asset_revision(assetPath, revision?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Loads a historical revision of an asset alongside the currently loaded one. Async: await the result. Treat the loaded package as read-only. It stays in memory until garbage collection runs. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `assetPath, revision?` |
| `epic_merge_branch(branch, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Merges the head of another branch into the current branch and reloads the loaded packages the merge changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the merge and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the merge first to find the affected files. Files changed on both branches may become conflicted: resolve them before submitting. Providers may push the merge result to the server. Raises when the branch is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without merging, when a loaded package the merge changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch, repository?` |
| `epic_move_files_to_changelist(changelistId, files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Moves files into an existing pending changelist. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `changelistId, files` |
| `epic_push_branch(branch, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Pushes a branch to the server. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch, repository?` |
| `epic_query_branch(branch?, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the details of a branch. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch?, repository?` |
| `epic_query_changelist_details(revision, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the details of a submitted changelist, such as its description, author and date. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `revision, repository?` |
| `epic_query_history(file)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the revision history of any file, such as a Verse file, a project file or an asset, newest first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `file` |
| `epic_query_provider(repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the status the provider reports for a repository, for example the current branch, user and workspace. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `repository?` |
| `epic_query_states(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Gets the current source control states of files, refreshing them from the provider first. Async: await the result. A file that is not tracked is not an error: its state reports bIsSourceControlled as false. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_resolve(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Marks conflicted mergeable files, such as text or Verse files, resolved once their conflict markers have been removed from the files on disk. Edit and save the files first. Async: await the result. Does not change the files. For files that are not mergeable, use ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs instead. The provider decides which files it accepts; a file it refuses, for example one that still has conflict markers, fails the call with its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_resolve_complete(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Completes the resolution of conflicts, once every conflicted file has been resolved with Resolve, ResolveMine or ResolveTheirs. Async: await the result. Providers may record the resolved files locally, for example by committing them to a personal branch. The provider decides when it accepts this; for example it fails while conflicts remain or when the repository is not resolving conflicts. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_resolve_mine(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Resolves conflicted files by keeping the local version, and reloads their loaded packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_resolve_theirs(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Resolves conflicted files by taking the incoming version, discarding their local changes, and reloads their loaded packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the resolve and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises, without resolving, when a loaded package of the files has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not conflicted; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_restore_as_latest(description, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Makes the synced revision the latest revision of the current branch again, by submitting a new revision with its content. Blocks until the provider completes. Game thread only. Raises when the description is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises when the branch moved on since the last sync. Raises when files the restore changes are checked out by other users; the error lists them. Raises when the provider fails the operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `description, repository?` |
| `epic_restore_branch(branch, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Restores a branch removed by DeleteBranch. Async: await the result. Does not change local files. The provider decides which branches it can restore. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch, repository?` |
| `epic_revert(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Reverts files, discarding their local changes and any unsaved changes in their loaded packages, and reloads those packages, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the revert and the reload complete. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider refuses a file, for example one that is not checked out; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_revert_unchanged(files:[s])` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Releases the checkout of the given files that are checked out but not modified, so other users can check them out. Refreshes the modified state of the files first. Does not change the files on disk, so their loaded packages are not reloaded. Files that are not checked out or are modified are left alone. Blocks until the revert completes. Game thread only. Raises when no files are given. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when a file cannot be resolved. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `files` |
| `epic_submit_changelist(changelistId)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Submits a pending changelist after validating it, and fails with the validation errors if it does not pass. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Invokes the Submit Tool when one is available, as the Submit action in the Changelists window does; the user completes the submit there, so the changelist is not yet submitted when the result completes. Otherwise submits it directly. Async: await the result. Use this rather than submitting by any other route. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `changelistId` |
| `epic_submit_changes(description)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Submits every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist. Blocks until the submit completes. Game thread only. Refreshes the status of the source control locations, then submits every file there that can be checked in. Invokes the Submit Tool when one is available, as SubmitChangelist does; the user completes the submit there, so the changes are not yet submitted when this returns. Otherwise checks the files in directly, after virtualizing payloads when virtualization is enabled, which may append tags to the description. Does not save, sync or validate first, and does not add files that are not tracked. Raises when the description is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when there is nothing to submit. Raises when the Submit Tool fails to start. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `description` |
| `epic_switch_branch(branch, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Switches to the head of another branch and reloads the loaded packages the switch changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the switch and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the switch first to find the affected files. Raises when the branch is empty. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without switching, when a loaded package the switch changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `branch, repository?` |
| `epic_sync(revision?, repository?)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Syncs to a revision and reloads the loaded packages the sync changes, including the open level when its map or external packages change. Blocks until the sync and the reload complete. Game thread only. Previews the sync first to find the affected files. Raises when source control is unavailable. Raises when the repository does not exist. Raises, without syncing, when a loaded package the sync changes has unsaved changes: save or revert it first. Raises when the provider fails an operation; the error has its reason. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `revision?, repository?` |
| `epic_validate_changelist(changelistId)` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Validates a pending changelist the way the submit check does: the registered validators run on the changelist and on its assets. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `changelistId` |
| `epic_validate_changes()` | [Epic SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers] Validates every pending change under the source control locations, without a changelist, the way the check-in dialog does. Collects the same files SubmitChanges submits, and runs the registered files validator on them. Waits for the asset registry to finish scanning first. Async: await the result. Available on UE 5.9; absent from UE 5.8. Params: `none` |

---

## canvas

*Unreal Canvas (UE 5.9, the UnrealCanvasBridge plugin): Movie Render Graph renders of the viewport, a Level Sequence or an object reposition, the passes and variables of the render preset, scene snapshots, the raw RGBA viewport stream, stencil, depth and annotation capture settings, and Gaussian splat and cutout actors. Each action runs the Bridge's own MCP tool through epic(call_mcp_tool); they are withheld when the editor does not serve that tool, which is the case until UnrealCanvasBridge is enabled in the .uproject. Render paths are on the editor's machine.*

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `status()` | Whether the Canvas Bridge is ready and an MRG preset is configured, with the preset's pass names. Returns ready, presetConfigured, passes? Params: none |
| `list_passes(presetPath?, variables?:o)` | The render passes (output branches) of the MRG preset and the captures each is expected to produce. Returns passes [name] and captures [{branch, subResource}], which match passName, branchName and subResourceName on render results. Params: `presetPath?, variables?` |
| `list_variables(presetPath?)` | The variables the MRG preset defines, with type and default as serialized strings. Pass overrides to the render actions as variables. Returns variables [{name, type, value}]. Params: `presetPath?` |
| `render(cameraSource?:o, captureSceneState?:b, executionMode?, presetPath?, resolution?:o, variables?:o, viewportLook?:o)` | Render the current editor viewport through Movie Render Graph. executionMode PlayInEditor (default) starts a PIE session so physics and Blueprint logic run; EditorWorld renders the loaded editor world at once, as a draft. captureSceneState takes a whole-world Level Snapshot first, for render_reposition and save_scene_snapshot (slow on a large level). Takes 30 to 120 seconds; renders run one at a time. Returns images [{path, passName, branchName, subResourceName, camera}], one PNG per capture under the project's Saved folder; rawDepth [{path, camera}] for a depth capture (float centimetres as .npy); and sceneStateBlobPath when captureSceneState was set. presetPath defaults to the preset in Editor Preferences > Plugins > Unreal Canvas; variables is {name: serialized value} (see list_variables); resolution is {size: preset\|1080p\|1440p\|2160p\|custom, width?, height?, matchAspect?}; cameraSource is {mode: viewport\|sequence\|actor, actorId?, actorName?}; viewportLook is {visibility?, showFlags?, viewMode?}. Params: `presetPath?, variables?, resolution?, cameraSource?, viewportLook?, executionMode? (PlayInEditor\|EditorWorld), captureSceneState?` |
| `render_sequence(cameraSource?:o, presetPath?, resolution?:o, sequencePath?, variables?:o, viewportLook?:o)` | Render a Level Sequence through Movie Render Graph to PNG frames. sequencePath omitted renders the sequence open in Sequencer (only the focused shot when Sequencer is drilled into one); an explicit path renders all of it. cameraSource defaults to the sequence's own Camera Cuts. May take minutes. Returns passes [{directory, passName, branchName, subResourceName, frameCount, fps, filePattern, startFrame, firstFrame, lastFrame, sequenceName}], one directory of PNG frames per capture under Saved/UnrealCanvasSequenceRender. presetPath, variables, resolution, cameraSource and viewportLook are as for render. Params: `sequencePath?, presetPath?, variables?, resolution?, cameraSource?, viewportLook?` |
| `render_reposition(sceneStateBlobPath, cameraPose?:s/o, durationSeconds?:n, fps?:n, presetPath?, resolution?:o, saveSequence?:b, variables?:o)` | Render the move from a captured scene state to the current one: loads the Level Snapshot a render with captureSceneState wrote (sceneStateBlobPath), builds a transient sequence that moves each changed actor from its captured pose to its current one (added actors appear and removed ones disappear at the midpoint) while the camera moves from cameraPose to the current viewport, and renders it. A camera-only change is valid. cameraPose is the camera from the original render's result (object or JSON string). durationSeconds defaults to 4 and fps to 24; saveSequence keeps the sequence for Sequencer. Returns passes as render_sequence does. Params: `sceneStateBlobPath, cameraPose?, durationSeconds?, fps?, saveSequence?, presetPath?, variables?, resolution?` |
| `save_scene_snapshot(sceneStateBlobPath, assetName?, destinationPath?, showDialog?:b)` | Save the Level Snapshot a render captured (its sceneStateBlobPath) as a Level Snapshot asset, which can be inspected or applied to put the captured actor poses back. Saves straight to destinationPath/assetName (default the Canvas generated-content folder's SceneState); showDialog=true opens the editor's save-as dialog instead, which waits for a person. Returns assetPath. Params: `sceneStateBlobPath, destinationPath?, assetName?, showDialog?` |
| `start_viewport_stream(color?:b, depth?:b, exactSize?:b, fps?:n, height?:i, normal?:b, port?:i, sharedMemory?:b, stencil?:b, width?:i)` | Stream the editor viewport over TCP as raw 8-bit RGBA frames, with optional depth, world-normal and stencil matte passes and the annotation JSON per frame. port omitted uses this editor's assigned stream port, or 9880. width and height default to 512, fps to 30; color, depth and normal default on, stencil off. Returns streaming, port, width, height, fps, format, exact_size, shared_memory_name? Params: port?, width?, height?, fps?, color?, depth?, normal?, stencil?, sharedMemory?, exactSize? |
| `set_viewport_stream_fps(fps:n)` | Change the running viewport stream's capture rate (1-120) without restarting it. Refused when no stream runs. Returns fps. Params: `fps` |
| `stop_viewport_stream()` | Stop the viewport stream and disconnect its clients. Returns streaming=false and wasStopped. Params: `none` |
| `assign_stencil(stencilId:i, one(actorPath; actorLabel))` | Turn on custom depth for an actor's primitive components and give them a stencil ID (1-254), which the stencil matte pass and stencil color map key on. Params: `actorPath (or actorLabel), stencilId` |
| `clear_stencil(one(actorPath; actorLabel))` | Turn off custom depth on an actor's primitive components and reset its stencil value. Params: `actorPath (or actorLabel)` |
| `clear_all_stencils(actorLabels?:[s], actorPaths?:[s])` | Turn off custom depth and reset the stencil on the given actors, or on every actor in the editor world that has custom depth on when none are given. Params: `actorPaths?, actorLabels?` |
| `set_stencil_colors(groups:[o])` | Set the stencil-to-color map the viewport stream's matte pass uses: each group maps a stencil ID to an RGB color, and visible=false leaves it out of the matte. At most 32 groups, each {stencilId, r, g, b, visible?}. Params: `groups` |
| `set_depth_range(encoding?, farCm?:n, nearCm?:n)` | Set the depth pass's near and far cutoffs in centimetres (0 or omitted uses each frame's own min or max) and its encoding (ndc, metric or hilbert). Params: `nearCm?, farCm?, encoding?` |
| `set_capture_stage(stage)` | Choose the post-process stage the stream captures scene color and composites stencils at: pre_postprocess, post_tonemap or post_final. A stage whose pass the project does not enable cascades to the one before it. Params: `stage` |
| `set_capture_annotations(enabled:b)` | Turn the 3D annotations pass (the annotations-only image the stream and renders carry) on or off. Params: `enabled` |
| `set_viewport_annotations(enabled:b)` | Show or hide the 3D annotation overlay in the editor viewport. Params: `enabled` |
| `set_annotation_render_mode(edgeThickness:n, fill:b)` | Set how 3D annotations rasterize: filled faces or not, and the edge half-width in cube-local units (0 draws no edges). Params: `fill, edgeThickness` |
| `spawn_splat(plyPath, actorTag?, label?, location?:[n]/o, replaceExisting?:b, rotation?:[n]/o)` | Import a Gaussian splat .ply (a path on the editor's machine) as a new GaussianSplat asset and place a GaussianSplatActor for it. An actor with the same actorTag (default UnrealCanvasSplat) is updated in place unless replaceExisting=false. location is [x,y,z] or {x,y,z}; rotation is [pitch,yaw,roll] or {pitch,yaw,roll}. Returns gsplat_id, actor_path, asset_path, actor_tag, label. Params: `plyPath, location?, rotation?, actorTag?, label?, replaceExisting?` |
| `list_splats()` | List the Gaussian splat actors spawn_splat placed in the editor world. Returns gsplats [{gsplat_id, actor_path, label, location, rotation, asset_path}]. Params: `none` |
| `remove_splat(splatId)` | Delete a Gaussian splat actor spawn_splat placed, by its gsplat_id. The imported asset stays. Returns actor_path. Params: `splatId` |
| `spawn_cutout(location:[n]/o, texturePaths:[s], intensity?:n, labels?:[s], rotation?:[n]/o)` | Place a cutout actor (a textured card) using existing Texture2D assets, one variant per texture, the first active. labels runs parallel to texturePaths; intensity is the emissive multiplier (default 0.3). Returns cutout_id and actor_path. Params: `texturePaths, location, rotation?, labels?, intensity?` |
| `spawn_cutout_from_png(location:[n]/o, intensity?:n, label?, one(pngPath; pngBase64), provenancePath?, rotation?:[n]/o)` | Place a cutout actor from a PNG image, which becomes its first variant. pngPath is read by this server, so it is a path on the machine ue-mcp runs on. provenancePath is a detached C2PA manifest signed for the image. Returns cutout_id and actor_path. Params: `pngPath (or pngBase64), location, rotation?, label?, intensity?, provenancePath?` |
| `list_cutouts()` | List the cutout actors in the editor world. Returns cutouts [{cutout_id, actor_path, location, rotation, variant_count, active_variant_index, labels}]. Params: `none` |
| `remove_cutout(cutoutId)` | Delete a cutout actor by its cutout_id. Params: `cutoutId` |
| `add_cutout_variant(cutoutId, label?, one(pngPath; pngBase64))` | Add an image variant to a cutout actor. Returns variant_index. Params: `cutoutId, pngPath (or pngBase64), label?` |
| `set_cutout_variant(cutoutId, variantIndex:i)` | Show another of a cutout actor's variants, by 0-based index. Params: `cutoutId, variantIndex` |
